problems.name: Zak's modified integer round-down conjecture for the skiving stock problem
problems.field: Skiving stock and bin covering; pattern LP integrality gap
problems.statement: In the one-dimensional skiving stock problem (bin covering), items of given sizes are grouped into as many disjoint groups as possible, each group reaching a threshold $L$; items may be left unused. The pattern linear programming relaxation gives an upper bound $LP_{\mathrm{SSP}}$ on the optimum $OPT_{\mathrm{SSP}}$. The integer round-down property $OPT_{\mathrm{SSP}}=\lfloor LP_{\mathrm{SSP}}\rfloor$ fails, but the largest known gap $LP_{\mathrm{SSP}}-OPT_{\mathrm{SSP}}$ was about $1.18$. The modified integer round-down property (MIRDP) conjectures that every instance satisfies $LP_{\mathrm{SSP}}-OPT_{\mathrm{SSP}}<2$. Is that true?
problems.posedBy: E. J. Zak (2003), as cited by the manuscript; stated as an open conjecture by Martinovic and Scheithauer (Discrete Optimization 2016; Pesquisa Operacional 2019)
problems.ageNote: The manuscript attributes MIRDP to Zak, Int. Trans. Oper. Res. 10 (2003). Martinovic and Scheithauer (2019) state that the SSP is conjectured to possess the MIRDP and give the largest known gap as 325/276. Zak's 2003 paper was not opened here (paywalled).
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1: for every integer $c\ge0$ there is a rational instance with $5B$ items, sizes in $(53/270,11/54)$ for threshold $1$, $LP_{\mathrm{SSP}}=LP_{\mathrm{SSP,prop}}=B$ and $OPT_{\mathrm{SSP}}\le B-c-1$; $c=1$ refutes MIRDP with no rounding ambiguity. Theorem 2 and Corollary 3: fixed additive approximation is NP-hard. The result is conditional on OpenAI's bin-packing theorem (itself a Candidate here). Not shown: any growth rate of the gap in terms of instance size.
problems.model: Anthropic Fable 5.1 and OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol Pro
problems.aiRole: The manuscript's abstract and the repository README say the proof was generated by a combination of Anthropic Fable 5.1 and OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol Pro; its closing note says ChatGPT assisted with drafting, literature organization and analysis of the proofs. The idea is a transfer: complement OpenAI's bin-packing instances (24 September 2026, which disprove the round-up analogue) by $b_i=2-a_i$ with threshold $9$. On $5B$ items with sizes above $1/6$, feasible five-item packing and covering sets coincide, LP saturation carries the LP value $B$ across, and a covering deficit $d$ converts to a packing excess of at most $\lceil 3d/2\rceil$. Result: for every $c\ge0$ an instance with $LP_{\mathrm{SSP}}=B$ and $OPT_{\mathrm{SSP}}\le B-c-1$, also for the proper relaxation, and NP-hardness of every fixed additive approximation.
problems.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here on 7 October 2026: the manuscript's TeX source was read in full. The transfer itself (Proposition 9, Theorems 6 and 7, Corollary 11 and the proof of Theorem 1) was checked by hand and is elementary: four items below $7/30$ always pack and six complemented items always cover, so a covering deficit $d$ gives a packing excess at most $\lceil 3d/2\rceil$; even without the $7/30$ bound, singletons give $24d$, so the conclusion follows from the exported Lean statement of OpenAI's theorem alone. A brute-force computation written here on 60 random 10-item instances (sizes near $1/5$, matching deficiency $0$ to $2$) confirmed the exact formulas $OPT_{\mathrm{BP}}-B=\lceil h/4\rceil$ and $B-OPT_{\mathrm{SSP}}=\lceil h/6\rceil$ in every case. The result depends on OpenAI's unbounded configuration-gap theorem, which is Lean-checked but not independently verified; the transfer is not formalised and nothing was rebuilt here.
problems.significanceNote: A conjecture known within the cutting-and-packing community, open since about 2003 with a published line of partial bounds (divisible case, fixed number of sizes). The covering twin of the Modified Integer Round-Up Conjecture, well below that entry at 32 and below the bin-packing additive question at 45, and obtained by a short transfer from their solution. Just below the Robert trace-cone and Pebody entries at 15.

problems.name: At least five colours for the regular fourteen-gon Minkowski plane
problems.statement: Let $C$ be a centrally symmetric convex curve and let $\chi(\mathbb R^2,C)$ be the least number of colours needed to colour the plane so that no two points at $C$-norm distance one share a colour. Exoo, Fisher and Ismailescu proved $\chi(\mathbb R^2,C)\ge5$ for the regular octagon, decagon and dodecagon and asked (Problem 5.1) whether $\chi(\mathbb R^2,C)\ge5$ for every regular $2n$-gon with $n\ge4$. This entry is the case $n=7$: with $P_{14}=\operatorname{conv}\{z\in\mathbb C:z^{14}=1\}$ as the unit ball, is $\chi(\mathbb R^2,P_{14})\ge5$?
problems.posedBy: Geoffrey Exoo, David Fisher and Dan Ismailescu, The chromatic number of the Minkowski plane: the regular polygon case, Problem 5.1 (arXiv:2108.12861, 2021)
problems.resultNote: We prove $\chi(\mathbb R^2,P_{14})\ge5$ using a graph with 1,540 vertices and 13,755 unit edges. Every edge difference is a rotated point on a side of the unit polygon with an exact algebraic parameter in $[0,1]$. A kernel-checked LRAT refutation of the graph's four-colouring CNF rules out every four-colouring, and restricting a colouring of the plane to these points gives the contradiction. The whole geometric and logical chain is in Lean. With Gehér's upper bound, $5\le\chi(\mathbb R^2,P_{14})\le6$; whether five colours suffice remains open, as does Problem 5.1 for other $n$.
problems.aiRole: An earlier AI-assisted research archive supplied the explicit graph, coordinates, CNF/LRAT certificate and finite logical bridge. OpenAI Codex (GPT-6 Astra) developed the complete geometric Lean proof, connected the obstruction to an actual normed real plane, removed the importer's unsafe term-evaluation calls, rebuilt the finite certificate and audited the final theorem. It also prepared the mathematical exposition and interactive diagrams. The human collaborator selected the result, directed the work, required full geometric formalization and reviewed the presentation. No independent human mathematical audit is claimed.
problems.verificationNote: Checked by this site on 7 October 2026, not rebuilt here. No independent mathematician has checked this yet. The headline theorem at_least_five_colours (formal/Final.lean) was read: any colouring of the plane by n colours that separates every pair at distance one has n at least 5. Plane is the complex numbers as a real vector space with the gauge of the convex hull of the 14th roots of unity as norm, and its distance is that norm of the difference, so the formal statement matches the posed question. The project has no sorry, admit, axiom declarations or native_decide; its SAT importer adds its LRAT steps through addDecl, so the kernel checks them. The public Actions run 37468510724 (commit e0f5e2a, success, on the author's own self-hosted Azure runner) prints propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound for the final theorem and the graph lemma; the formal sources have not changed since that commit. A separate check written here from the graph file: all 13,755 edges have 14-gon norm 1 to within 1e-15 in floating point, and a fresh four-colouring encoding solved by CaDiCaL is unsatisfiable (157 s). Gehér's upper bound six is cited, not formalised.
problems.significanceNote: One case (n = 7) of Problem 5.1 of Exoo, Fisher and Ismailescu (2021), a stated question in the Minkowski-plane variant of Hadwiger-Nelson; the general 2n-gon question stays open. A small specialist audience. Below the unit-distance independence-ratio question (20) and the Pinwheel Kernel Conjecture (12), above Arnosti's greedy-matching conjecture (7), far below the Euclidean five-colour step (55).

problems.name: Wall's D(2) problem
problems.statement: A finite connected CW complex $X$ with fundamental group $G$ satisfies the $D(2)$ condition if $H_i(\widetilde X;\mathbb Z)=0$ for $i>2$ and $H^3(X;M)=0$ for every finitely generated $\mathbb ZG$-module $M$. Wall showed such $X$ has a finite three-dimensional model and asked whether the three-cells can be removed. Stably the answer is yes (Cohen), and it is yes for many finite groups (Johnson, Hambleton, Hofmann-Nicholson); candidate counterexamples (Cohen-Dyer, Bridson-Tweedale) stayed unresolved or conditional on relation-gap assertions. Wall's finite $D(2)$ problem: is every finite $D(2)$ complex homotopy equivalent to a finite CW complex of dimension at most two?
problems.posedBy: C. T. C. Wall
problems.ageNote: Wall, Finiteness conditions for CW-complexes (Annals 1965, Section 2); repeated as Problem D3 in Wall's 1979 problem list. Both are cited by the manuscript.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there is a finite connected three-dimensional CW complex $X$ with $H_i(\widetilde X;\mathbb Z)=0$ for $i>2$ and $H^3(X;M)=0$ for every $\mathbb Z[\pi_1X]$-module $M$ that is not homotopy equivalent to any finite complex of dimension at most two. The obstruction: on a finite 2-complex, a rank-one local system with vanishing twisted $H_2$ is trivial on every finite-order element of $\pi_1$. $\pi_1(X)$ is infinite. It does not settle the D(2) problem for finite fundamental groups, the relation gap problem, or the Eilenberg-Ganea problem.
problems.aiRole: The release README says the vast majority of results, this one included, were produced with one fixed procedure using an unreleased internal OpenAI model, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result, and that some outputs build on earlier model results. This result is not among the README's exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region, whose write-up was human-edited). The manuscript is authored 'OpenAI' and names no human author.
problems.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 was read against Wall's question in the formulation the manuscript takes from Wall (1965, 1979) and Hofmann-Nicholson: finiteness of both complexes, no asphericity hypothesis. The construction is a Quillen plus construction on a five-generator four-relator presentation complex (finite D(2) by Mannan's theorem), with an obstruction from rank-one twisted second homology proved by a Howie-style cyclic tower. The example has infinite fundamental group, so the problem for finite groups, where most work concentrated, remains open. The proof was not refereed. No Lean formalization exists for this family.
problems.significanceNote: Wall's D(2) problem is a classical, sixty-year-old question in low-dimensional homotopy theory, tied to the relation gap and Eilenberg-Ganea problems and famous within that community. Placed below The Borel conjecture for closed aspherical four-manifolds (60), and above Wall's manifold-realization question for Poincare duality groups (42) and The CAT(0) conjecture for Artin groups (40).

problems.name: The Friedgut-Kalai threshold-width conjecture for r-uniform hypergraph properties
problems.field: Random hypergraphs, analysis of Boolean functions
problems.statement: For a nontrivial increasing property of $r$-uniform hypergraphs on $n$ vertices invariant under relabelling, the transitive symmetry of the $\binom nr$ edge coordinates gives threshold width $O(1/\log n)$ by the Friedgut-Kalai method. Friedgut and Kalai (1996, Section 5) conjectured that the vertex symmetry does better: for each fixed $r$ the width from probability $\varepsilon$ to $1-\varepsilon$ should be $O_{r,\varepsilon}((\log n)^{-r/(r-1)})$, the graph case being $r=2$. Bourgain and Kalai reached exponent $r/(r-1)-\delta$ for the influence bound at the uniform measure. For every fixed $r\ge3$, is the threshold width of every such property $O_{r,\varepsilon}((\log n)^{-r/(r-1)})$?
problems.posedBy: Ehud Friedgut and Gil Kalai
problems.ageNote: Friedgut-Kalai, Proc. AMS 124 (1996), Section 5, p. 2999; their formulation counts edge coordinates, equivalent for fixed r.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for each $r\ge3$ there is $C_r$ with $\mathrm{Var}_p(f)\le C_rI_p(f)/(\log n)^{r/(r-1)}$ for every relabelling-invariant Boolean property of $r$-uniform hypergraphs, every $n\ge r$ and every $0<p<1$, without monotonicity. Corollary 4.1: for nontrivial increasing properties the width from $\varepsilon$ to $1-\varepsilon$ is $O_r(\log(1/\varepsilon)/(\log n)^{r/(r-1)})$. Not shown: explicit constants $C_r$ or sharpness examples for each $r$.

problems.name: The Burger-Ozawa-Thom question: does strong Ulam stability characterize amenability?
problems.field: Group theory; stability of approximate representations
problems.statement: A countable discrete group $G$ is strongly Ulam stable if for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $\delta>0$ such that every map $\mu:G\to U(H)$ into the unitary group of any complex Hilbert space, with $\mu(e)=I$ and $\sup_{g,h}\|\mu(gh)-\mu(g)\mu(h)\|\le\delta$, is within $\varepsilon$ uniformly of a genuine unitary representation on the same space. Kazhdan (1982) proved amenable groups are strongly Ulam stable; Burger, Ozawa and Thom (2013) showed groups with a nonabelian free subgroup are not, and Alpeev handled wreath products over nonamenable groups. Burger, Ozawa and Thom asked: is every strongly Ulam stable countable group amenable?
problems.posedBy: Marc Burger, Narutaka Ozawa and Andreas Thom, On Ulam stability, Israel J. Math. 193 (2013), p. 111
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: a countable discrete group is strongly Ulam stable if and only if it is amenable. For every nonamenable countable $G$ and $\delta>0$ there is a separable $H$ and a normalized $\mu:G\to U(H)$ with defect below $\delta$ that stays at uniform distance more than $1/10$ from every unitary representation on $H$. Not shown: anything about finite-dimensional (ordinary) Ulam stability, or uncountable groups.

problems.name: The Ascoli-He-Park-Talagrand graph-decomposition conjecture at the expectation threshold
problems.field: Random graphs; thresholds for subgraph containment
problems.statement: For a graph $H$ on at most $n$ vertices let $p_c(H;n)$ be the least $p$ at which $G(n,p)$ contains a copy of $H$ with probability $1/2$, and $q(H;n)$ its integral expectation threshold. The Park-Pham theorem gives $p_c(H;n)\le Cq(H;n)\log|E(H)|$, and the logarithm cannot be dropped in general. Ascoli, He, Park and Talagrand (2026, Conjecture 8.1) proposed that it can be removed after cutting $H$ into boundedly many pieces, and proved bounded-degeneracy cases. Are there absolute constants $k$ and $L$ such that the edges of every graph $H$ on at most $n$ vertices split into $k$ subgraphs $H_1,\dots,H_k$ with $p_c(H_i;n)\le L\,q(H;n)$ for each $i$?
problems.posedBy: Ruben Ascoli, Xiaoyu He, Jinyoung Park and Michel Talagrand (Conjecture 8.1, arXiv 2608.11183, August 2026)
problems.ageNote: Posed about two months before this manuscript.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there are absolute $k\ge2$ and $L\ge1$ such that for every $n\ge2$ and every graph $H$ on at most $n$ vertices, $E(H)=E(H_1)\sqcup\dots\sqcup E(H_k)$ with $p_c(H_i;n)\le Lq(H;n)$ for each $i$. Pieces may be empty or share vertices, and the partition depends only on $H$ and $n$. It does not give a single copy of $H$ at threshold $Lq(H;n)$ (the separate embeddings need not glue), and $k$, $L$ are not explicit.

problems.name: The Hasenfratz-Maggiore-Niedermayer exact mass gap for the two-dimensional O(4) lattice model
problems.field: Statistical mechanics; asymptotically free sigma models, mass gap
problems.statement: For the nearest-neighbour $O(4)$ model on $\mathbb Z^2$ (spins in $S^3$, weight $\exp(\beta\sum_{x\sim y}\sigma_x\cdot\sigma_y)$), asymptotic freedom predicts a mass $m_{\mathrm{lat}}(\beta)$ of order $\sqrt\beta\,e^{-\pi\beta}$ as $\beta\to\infty$. Hasenfratz, Maggiore and Niedermayer (1990) computed the exact ratio $m/\Lambda_{\overline{\mathrm{MS}}}=\sqrt{32/(\pi e)}$ for $O(3)$ and $O(4)$ by matching the Bethe ansatz with perturbation theory, which fixes the numerical prefactor of the lattice mass. Does the gap of the full lattice transfer operator satisfy the predicted exact asymptotic, with the predicted constant?
problems.posedBy: Peter Hasenfratz, Michele Maggiore and Ferenc Niedermayer (Phys. Lett. B, 1990); extended to all O(n), n >= 3, by Hasenfratz and Niedermayer (1990)
problems.ageNote: The 1990 papers give a physics prediction for the continuum mass in MS-bar units; the manuscript frames proving the corresponding lattice transfer-gap asymptotic as the open step. Polyakov's 1975 renormalization argument fixed only the exponential order.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for the periodic infinite-volume state, the gap of the full Osterwalder-Schrader transfer operator, including rotation-invariant sectors and measured in original lattice time steps, satisfies $\lim_{\beta\to\infty}e^{\pi\beta}\beta^{-1/2}m_{\mathrm{lat}}(\beta)=32\exp(\pi/4-1/2)$. The input companion gives $c\sqrt\beta e^{-\pi\beta}\le m_{\mathrm{lat}}\le C\sqrt\beta e^{-\pi\beta}$ and a positive full gap at every $\beta>0$. Not shown: the corresponding exact constant for $O(3)$ or general $O(n)$, a continuum $O(4)$ theory, or any statement about nonperiodic Gibbs states.

problems.name: The codimension-one bound for singular sets of stationary integral varifolds
problems.shortName: Codimension-one singular set bound for varifolds
problems.field: Geometric measure theory: regularity of stationary varifolds
problems.statement: Let $V$ be a stationary integral $m$-varifold in an open set $U\subset\mathbb R^{m+n}$ and $\mathrm{Sing}\,V$ the support points near which $V$ is not an integer multiple of one smooth embedded minimal submanifold. Two $m$-planes meeting along an $(m-1)$-plane form a stationary varifold whose singular set is $(m-1)$-dimensional, so no better bound is possible. Known cases included two-valued stationary Lipschitz graphs (Hirsch-Spolaor) and classes with controlled density under an epsilon-regularity assumption (Krummel-Minter-Wickramasekera). Brena, Decio and De Lellis (2025, Conjecture 1.1) conjecture the sharp bound, which is stronger than almost-everywhere regularity. Does every stationary integral $m$-varifold satisfy $\dim_{\mathcal H}\mathrm{Sing}\,V\le m-1$, in every dimension and codimension?
problems.posedBy: Camillo Brena, Stefano Decio and Camillo De Lellis, Remarks and conjectures on stationary varifolds dedicated to Enrico Bombieri, Rend. Lincei Mat. Appl. 36 (2025), Conjecture 1.1
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every stationary integral $m$-varifold $V$ in an open $U\subset\mathbb R^{m+n}$, $m,n\ge1$, $\dim_{\mathcal H}\mathrm{Sing}\,V\le m-1$, with no stability, minimizing, orientability, density or codimension hypothesis; crossing planes show it is sharp. This implies $\mathcal H^m(\mathrm{Sing}\,V)=0$. The proof combines the companion paper's signed-excess estimates with a fitting and frequency analysis around a smooth center and a measure-valued blow-up at higher-multiplicity planar tangents. It does not prove rectifiability or finer structure of the singular set, and does not cover Riemannian ambient metrics.

problems.name: Uchida's conjecture on open homomorphisms of Galois groups of solvably closed extensions of number fields
problems.field: Anabelian geometry; Galois groups of number fields
problems.statement: Let $E_i/F_i$ ($i=1,2$) be Galois extensions of number fields with each $E_i$ solvably closed (no nontrivial abelian extension), for example algebraic closures or maximal prosolvable extensions, and write $G_i=\mathrm{Gal}(E_i/F_i)$. The Neukirch-Uchida theorem says that isomorphisms $G_1\cong G_2$ come from field isomorphisms. Uchida (1981) proved the analogous statement for open homomorphisms when the source field is $\mathbb Q$, proved uniqueness in general, and proved existence under a local condition on decomposition groups, and conjectured the general case. Is every continuous homomorphism $\alpha:G_1\to G_2$ with open image induced by a field embedding $j:E_2\hookrightarrow E_1$, i.e. $g\circ j=j\circ\alpha(g)$ for all $g\in G_1$?
problems.posedBy: Koji Uchida, Homomorphisms of Galois groups of solvably closed Galois extensions, J. Math. Soc. Japan 33 (1981), p. 595
problems.resultNote: Claims Uchida's conjecture in full: for number fields $F_1,F_2$ and possibly infinite solvably closed Galois extensions $E_i/F_i$, every continuous open homomorphism $\mathrm{Gal}(E_1/F_1)\to\mathrm{Gal}(E_2/F_2)$ is induced by a unique field embedding $E_2\hookrightarrow E_1$, with no hypothesis on the kernel and no separate cyclotomic-compatibility assumption. problems.name: Small spatial embeddings for one-sided near inclusions of von Neumann algebras
problems.field: Operator algebras; near inclusions, perturbation theory
problems.statement: For von Neumann algebras $M,N\subseteq B(H)$ with common identity let $\gamma(M,N)=\sup_{x\in M,\|x\|\le1}\inf_{y\in N}\|x-y\|$. Christensen showed that an injective $M$ with small $\gamma(M,N)$ embeds into $N$ by a unitary close to the identity. Cameron, Christensen, Sinclair, Smith, White and Wiggins asked the unrestricted one-sided question: for every $\varepsilon>0$ is there a $\delta>0$ such that $\gamma(M,N)<\delta$ always implies $uMu^*\subseteq N$ for some unitary $u$ with $\|u-1\|<\varepsilon$?
problems.posedBy: J. Cameron, E. Christensen, A. M. Sinclair, R. R. Smith, S. White and A. Wiggins, Type II_1 factors satisfying the spatial isomorphism conjecture, PNAS 109 (2012)
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there are $\varepsilon_0>0$ and pairs of von Neumann algebras on separable Hilbert spaces with common identity and $\gamma(M_n,N_n)\to0$ for which spatial embeddings exist but every implementing unitary satisfies $\|u-1\|\ge\varepsilon_0$. So the unrestricted one-sided question has a negative answer, in contrast with Christensen's injective case and with the two-sided strong Kadison-Kastler theorem in the same family. The obstruction is to small unitaries, not to the existence of embeddings.

problems.name: Quasipolynomial-time solution of simple stochastic and turn-based stochastic mean-payoff games
problems.field: Algorithmic game theory; stochastic games; complexity of NP and coNP problems
problems.statement: A simple stochastic game is a finite turn-based reachability game between two players in which some vertices are chance vertices choosing between two successors with probability $1/2$. Condon (1992) showed that deciding whether the value from a start vertex is at least $1/2$ lies in $\mathrm{NP}\cap\mathrm{coNP}$; Ludwig gave a randomized subexponential algorithm, and Andersson and Miltersen showed the problem polynomially equivalent to solving turn-based stochastic mean-payoff and discounted games with binary data. No algorithm subexponential and deterministic, or quasipolynomial, in the binary input length was known. Can simple stochastic games, and turn-based stochastic mean-payoff games, be solved in polynomial time, or at least in quasipolynomial time?
problems.posedBy: Anne Condon, The complexity of stochastic games (1992), as cited by the manuscript; the question is the polynomial-time status of a problem in NP and coNP
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites Condon (1992) for the NP and coNP placement and does not quote a posing sentence; the polynomial-time question for simple stochastic games is commonly attributed to that paper. This entry answers the quasipolynomial form, not the polynomial-time question.
problems.resultNote: Claims a deterministic algorithm with $2^{O((\log(L+2))^2)}$ bit operations that outputs the set of vertices of nonnegative value in finite turn-based stochastic mean-payoff games with signed binary rewards and arbitrary rational chance probabilities, and hence decides the threshold-1/2 problem for Condon's simple stochastic games in deterministic quasipolynomial time. The proof chooses an explicit discount of polynomial bit length and finds the discounted fixed point by a recursive labeling procedure. It does NOT give a polynomial-time algorithm, and it decides the threshold set rather than outputting values or strategies in the stated theorem.

problems.name: Marginal irrelevance of weak bond disorder at the planar Ising critical point: quenched SLE3 interfaces for weak random bonds
problems.field: Disordered systems; two-dimensional Ising model; SLE
problems.statement: For the square-lattice Ising model with independent random couplings $J_e=1+\varepsilon\xi_e$, Harris's criterion is marginal because the pure specific-heat exponent is zero. Dotsenko and Dotsenko (1983) predicted a double-logarithmic specific heat, and Shalaev, Shankar and Ludwig developed the picture that weak disorder is marginally irrelevant: unchanged leading critical exponents with logarithmic corrections, including Shankar's $(\log r)^{1/4}$ growth of the relative second moment of the spin correlation. Rigorously, only vanishing-disorder results were known (Mahfouf). For fixed small disorder, does the critical random-bond Ising model keep the pure model's conformally invariant critical behavior in a typical environment?
problems.posedBy: Vik. S. Dotsenko and Vl. S. Dotsenko (1983); B. N. Shalaev (1984); R. Shankar (1987); A. W. W. Ludwig (1990): renormalization-group predictions of marginal irrelevance
problems.ageNote: The physics predictions concern thermodynamic quantities and correlations; the manuscripts note that a quenched law for a whole interface is not itself predicted there, which is why this entry is a variant.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for any bounded mean-zero nondegenerate law $\rho$ on $[-1,1]$ there is $\varepsilon_0(\rho)>0$ such that for fixed $0<\varepsilon<\varepsilon_0$, at the spontaneous-magnetization threshold $\beta_c^\rho(\varepsilon)=\tfrac12\log(1+\sqrt2)+O(\varepsilon^2)$, the quenched Dobrushin spin interface in any bounded Jordan domain converges to chordal $\mathrm{SLE}_3$ in probability over environments, in the bounded-Lipschitz metric on oriented curves. A companion proves, conditionally on stated deterministic reference estimates, that the relative second moment of the quenched spin correlation grows as $(\log r)^{1/4+o(1)}$ for fair $\pm\varepsilon$ bonds. Not shown: strong disorder, the double-logarithmic specific heat, or unconditional logarithmic corrections.

problems.name: Szabo's Conjecture A on equivariant Jiang-Su stability, in the unital stably finite case
problems.shortName: Szabo's Conjecture A, unital stably finite case
problems.field: Operator algebras; C*-dynamics of amenable group actions
problems.statement: Let $A$ be a separable simple nuclear C*-algebra with $A\cong A\otimes\mathcal Z$ and let $\alpha$ be an action of a countable discrete amenable group $G$ on $A$. Szabo's Conjecture A predicts automatic equivariant Jiang-Su stability: $\alpha$ should be cocycle conjugate to $\alpha\otimes\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal Z}$. Szabo proved it for finite algebras with finitely many rays of extremal traces and very weak comparison; the general case was open, in particular when the action moves traces. Is every amenable action on a separable simple nuclear $\mathcal Z$-stable C*-algebra equivariantly $\mathcal Z$-stable?
problems.posedBy: Gabor Szabo
problems.ageNote: Szabo, Equivariant property (SI) revisited, Anal. PDE 14 (2021), Conjecture A, cited by the manuscript.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for $A$ simple, separable, unital, infinite-dimensional, nuclear, stably finite and $\mathcal Z$-stable, every action $\alpha$ of a countable discrete amenable group is cocycle conjugate to $\alpha\otimes\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal Z}$, with no restriction on how $\alpha$ acts on the trace simplex, and including finite groups and trivial actions. It does not treat nonunital algebras, and stably infinite (purely infinite) algebras are not part of this theorem.

problems.name: Randomized versus quantum query complexity of total Boolean functions: is R(f) = O(Q(f)^3)?
problems.statement: For total Boolean functions the bounded-error randomized query complexity $R$ and quantum query complexity $Q$ are polynomially related: Beals et al. proved $D=O(Q^6)$, and after Huang's sensitivity theorem Aaronson, Ben-David, Kothari, Rao and Tal proved $D(f)=O(Q(f)^4)$, hence $R=O(Q^4)$. The best separations were power $5/2$ (cheat sheets), then $8/3-o(1)$ (Tal) and $3-o(1)$ (Bansal-Sinha; Sherstov-Storozhenko-Wu). Aaronson, Ben-David, Kothari, Rao and Tal conjectured that the cubic relation holds. Is $R(f)=O(Q(f)^3)$ for every total Boolean function, or is the quartic exponent optimal?
problems.posedBy: Scott Aaronson, Shalev Ben-David, Robin Kothari, Shravas Rao and Avishay Tal
problems.ageNote: Conjecture 2 of their STOC 2021 paper, as cited by the manuscript; the preprint appeared on arXiv in October 2020 (2010.12629).
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for each fixed $k\ge2$ there are total Boolean functions $F_{k,m}$ with $Q(F_{k,m})\le C_k\sqrt m(\log m)^{b_k}$ and $R(F_{k,m})\ge c_km^{2-1/k}/(\log m)^2$, a power $4-2/k$ separation up to logarithms, so no bound $R=O((1+Q)^\alpha)$ holds with $\alpha<4$. With the known $R=O(Q^4)$ the optimal exponent is exactly 4, and the cubic conjecture is false. The functions are cheat-sheet-style columns whose certificate cells are addressed by answers to partial-function instances. Not shown: a separation with exponent exactly 4 for a single family, or new results for partial functions.

problems.name: Does the perfect matching polytope have a polynomial-size semidefinite lift?
problems.shortName: SDP lifts of the matching polytope
problems.field: Extended formulations; positive semidefinite rank, lower bounds
problems.statement: A semidefinite lift of size $r$ writes a polytope as an affine image of $L\cap\mathbb S^r_+$ for an affine subspace $L$; by Gouveia-Parrilo-Thomas the least such $r$ equals the PSD rank of a slack matrix. Yannakakis ruled out small symmetric linear programs for the perfect matching polytope, Rothvoss (2014) proved its linear extension complexity is $2^{\Omega(n)}$, and Braun et al. ruled out small symmetric SDPs, noting that it is natural to ask whether matching can be expressed compactly by semidefinite programming. Does the perfect matching polytope of $K_n$ admit an exact semidefinite lift of size polynomial in $n$?
problems.posedBy: G. Braun, J. Brown-Cohen, A. Huq, S. Pokutta, P. Raghavendra, A. Roy, B. Weitz, D. Zink, The matching problem has no small symmetric SDP, SODA 2016 / Math. Program. 165 (2017)
problems.ageNote: Posed in the abstract of arXiv 1504.00703 (April 2015) after Rothvoss's 2014 theorem; the manuscript itself states no posing source and cites this paper for the symmetric case.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there is $c>0$ such that for every fixed $0<\rho<1$ the odd-cut matrix with entries $|M\cap\delta(U)|-1+\rho$ has real PSD rank at least $2^{cn}$ for large even $n$, with no symmetry or precision restriction on the factors. Corollary 1.2: every exact semidefinite lift of the perfect matching polytope has size $2^{\Omega(n)}$. The method follows Lee-Raghavendra-Steurer with a Grigoriev-type parity functional and new averaging lemmas. The endpoint $\rho=1$ has a polynomial factorization, and approximate lifts are not excluded (Kaniewski-Lee-de Wolf give subexponential approximations).

problems.name: The trilinear Hilbert transform conjecture at the L3 x L3 x L3 to L1 point (slopes 1, 2, 3)
problems.statement: The trilinear Hilbert transform with slopes 1, 2, 3 is $T(f_1,f_2,f_3)(x)=\mathrm{p.v.}\int_{\mathbb R}f_1(x-t)f_2(x-2t)f_3(x-3t)\,\frac{dt}{t}$. Its bilinear predecessor was proved bounded by Lacey and Thiele (1997-1999). In the trilinear case quadratic modulations survive in the associated four-linear form (the coefficients $(-1,3,-3,1)$ annihilate polynomials of degree two), so time-frequency analysis does not close the argument; Tao (2015) obtained only sublogarithmic growth for truncations, and Hu and Lie record the straight-line boundedness problem as open. The standard conjecture asks for bounds $L^{p_1}\times L^{p_2}\times L^{p_3}\to L^r$ over a range of exponents. In particular, is $T$ bounded from $L^3(\mathbb R)\times L^3(\mathbb R)\times L^3(\mathbb R)$ to $L^1(\mathbb R)$?
problems.posedBy: Standard conjecture after Lacey and Thiele's bilinear theorem; the manuscript cites it as Conjecture 1.7 of B. Hu and V. Lie, On the curved trilinear Hilbert transform (arXiv:2308.10706, 2023)
problems.ageNote: The manuscript gives only the 2023 statement by Hu and Lie and does not date the conjecture's first appearance. It is older, as the natural continuation of the Lacey-Thiele bilinear theorem (1997-1999), but no earlier source is cited, so the year is left blank.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there is a finite $C$ with $\|T(f_1,f_2,f_3)\|_{L^1}\le C\prod_{j}\|f_j\|_{L^3}$ for Schwartz functions, so $T$ extends uniquely to a bounded trilinear map $L^3\times L^3\times L^3\to L^1$. The proof combines the Leng-Sah-Sawhney inverse theorem with new compression, curvature-localization and sparse counting lemmas that sum the scales without loss. It concerns only the fixed slopes 1, 2, 3 and the single exponent point $(3,3,3;1)$: the rest of the conjectured range, other slopes, maximal or truncation-uniform versions and higher-degree multilinear Hilbert transforms are not treated, as the manuscript itself says.

problems.name: The generalized Ramanujan conjecture for globally generic cuspidal representations of exceptional groups over function fields
problems.field: Automorphic representations over function fields; temperedness
problems.statement: Let $F$ be the function field of a curve over $\mathbb F_q$ and $G$ a split connected reductive group. The generalized Ramanujan conjecture, in its generic form (within Arthur's framework; see Shahidi), predicts that every globally generic cuspidal automorphic representation $\pi=\bigotimes'_v\pi_v$ of $G(\mathbb A_F)$ is tempered at every place $v$. Over function fields this was known for $GL_2$ (Drinfeld), $GL_n$ (L. Lafforgue), and split classical and quasi-split unitary groups (Lomeli); for exceptional groups only conditional unramified results (Sawin-Templier, Ciubotaru-Harris) were available. For split adjoint groups of type $G_2,F_4,E_6,E_7,E_8$ over a global function field, is every globally generic cuspidal automorphic representation tempered at every place?
problems.posedBy: Generic form of the generalized Ramanujan conjecture (Arthur's framework; Shahidi)
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites Arthur (1989) and Shahidi (2011, Arthur packets and the Ramanujan conjecture) for the generic temperedness prediction but gives no original posing date; the Ramanujan-Petersson conjecture itself is far older.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for $G$ split connected adjoint absolutely simple of type $G_2,F_4,E_6,E_7$ or $E_8$ over a global function field, every complex globally generic cuspidal automorphic representation is tempered at every place. The companion (September 24) gives temperedness at unramified places for all split adjoint absolutely simple groups from genericity at one unramified place. Nothing is claimed over number fields, for non-generic representations, or for ramified places of classical groups beyond what Lomeli already proved.

problems.name: The Bogoliubov quantum-depletion law for the dilute Bose gas in the thermodynamic limit
problems.field: Quantum many-body theory; dilute Bose gases
problems.statement: Bogoliubov's theory (1947), carried to the hard-sphere gas by Lee, Huang and Yang (1957), predicts that at zero temperature a dilute three-dimensional Bose gas with scattering length $a$ and density $\rho$ has a fraction $\frac{8}{3\sqrt\pi}\sqrt{\rho a^3}$ of its particles outside the condensate, distributed in momentum by an explicit Bogoliubov profile on the scale $\sqrt{8\pi\rho a}$. The energy to Lee-Huang-Yang order is now proved, but energy bounds do not control occupation of modes whose energy vanishes with the volume, and the depletion had been derived only in Gross-Pitaevskii-type scalings or for approximate equations. In the thermodynamic limit at fixed density, followed by $\rho a^3\to0$, is the ground-state depletion $\frac{8}{3\sqrt\pi}\sqrt{\rho a^3}+o(\sqrt{\rho a^3})$?
problems.posedBy: Prediction of N. N. Bogoliubov (1947) and T. D. Lee, K. Huang and C. N. Yang (1957)
problems.ageNote: Year of the Lee-Huang-Yang hard-sphere calculation, which the manuscript credits with determining the leading depletion; Bogoliubov's 1947 theory gives the momentum profile. The manuscripts present it as a physical prediction to be proved, not as a numbered open problem.
problems.resultNote: For hard spheres (October 5): for every bounded continuous $f$ and $\varepsilon>0$, at all sufficiently small fixed $\rho$, every thermodynamic accumulation value of $\frac{1}{N\sqrt{\rho a^3}}\sum_{k\ne0}f(k/\sqrt{8\pi\rho a})\,n(k)$ is within $\varepsilon$ of $\int f\,d\nu_{\mathrm{Bog}}$, uniformly over ground states; taking $f=1$ gives depletion $\frac{8}{3\sqrt\pi}\sqrt{\rho a^3}+o(\sqrt{\rho a^3})$. A companion proves the same depletion asymptotic for fixed bounded, nonnegative, radial, finite-range potentials with positive scattering length. Not covered: positive temperature, the next-order correction, or unbounded non-hard-core potentials.

This result is not among the README's exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region). The manuscript is authored 'OpenAI' and names no human author. The family has five manuscripts (September 24 to October 5, 2026). The positive-temperature paper says it builds on, and reproduces the needed arguments of, two earlier manuscripts in the same family, so later results rest on earlier model output.
problems.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2 of the hard-sphere depletion manuscript and the main theorem of the bounded-potential companion (both October 5) were read against the Bogoliubov and Lee-Huang-Yang prediction. Not refereed; no Lean formalization for either. The order of limits is thermodynamic first at fixed density, then dilute; the result is uniform over all ground states and does not assume a unique thermodynamic limit. The argument uses the published Lee-Huang-Yang energy upper bound for hard spheres (Basti, Brooks, Cenatiempo, Olgiati, Schlein) and operator estimates from Fournais, Junge, Girardot, Morin, Olivieri and Triay.

problems.name: The index conjecture for semi-log-canonical log Calabi-Yau pairs with finite rational coefficient sets
problems.statement: A projective log Calabi-Yau pair $(X,B)$ has $K_X+B\sim_{\mathbb Q}0$, so some positive multiple $m(K_X+B)$ is Cartier and linearly trivial; the least such $m$ is the index. Gongyo showed such $m$ exists for slc pairs, but it may depend on the pair. The index conjecture asks for uniformity. In its finite-rational-coefficient slc form, fix $d$ and a finite set $\Phi\subset[0,1]\cap\mathbb Q$: is there an integer $a(d,\Phi)$ such that $a(d,\Phi)(K_X+B)$ is Cartier and trivial for every connected projective slc log Calabi-Yau pair of dimension $d$ with coefficients in $\Phi$?
problems.posedBy: Index conjecture for log Calabi-Yau pairs; finite-rational-coefficient slc form stated by C. Jiang and H. Liu (Algebra and Number Theory, 2021), Conjecture 1.5
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites Jiang-Liu (arXiv 2020, published 2021) as one place the conjecture is stated, not as its origin. The normal-pair index conjecture is older; Xu (2019) organized reductions between its forms. Jiang-Liu proved the slc case in dimension at most three.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every $d\ge4$ and finite $\Phi\subset[0,1]\cap\mathbb Q$ there is $a(d,\Phi)>0$ such that $a(d,\Phi)(K_X+B)$ is Cartier with trivial line bundle for every connected projective equidimensional slc log Calabi-Yau pair of dimension $d$ with coefficients in $\Phi$, independently of the number of components. With Jiang-Liu's theorem for $d\le3$ this gives the conjecture in the cited form. Not shown: slc pairs with infinite DCC coefficient sets, or explicit values of $a(d,\Phi)$.

problems.name: Howie's conjecture: every nonsingular system of equations over a group is solvable in an overgroup
problems.field: Combinatorial group theory; equations over groups
problems.statement: Let $G$ be a group and $w_1,\dots,w_m\in G*F(x_1,\dots,x_n)$ a system of equations $w_i=1$ with coefficients in $G$. Its exponent-sum matrix $A\in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb Z)$ records the exponent of each $x_j$ in each $w_i$; the system is nonsingular if $A$ has rank $m$ over $\mathbb Q$. Gerstenhaber and Rothaus (1962) solved nonsingular systems over finite groups and compact Lie groups, Howie (1981) over locally indicable groups, and Nitsche-Thom over hyperlinear groups. The one-equation, one-variable case is the Kervaire-Laudenbach conjecture (a nonzero exponent sum should guarantee solvability). Does every finite nonsingular system over an arbitrary group $G$ have a solution in some group containing $G$, that is, is $G\to(G*F_n)/\langle\langle w_1,\dots,w_m\rangle\rangle$ injective?
problems.posedBy: James Howie (1981), On pairs of 2-complexes and systems of equations over groups; name and formulation as in Klyachko, Mikheenko and Roman'kov (2024)
problems.ageNote: The manuscript takes the name and formulation from Klyachko, Mikheenko and Roman'kov (2024, Introduction) and cites Howie (1981) for the locally indicable case; 1981 is used as the posing year on that basis. Its one-variable case, the Kervaire-Laudenbach conjecture, goes back to the Kervaire problem of 1965.
problems.resultNote: Claims Theorem 1: for every group $G$ and every finite system $w_1,\dots,w_m\in G*F_n$ whose exponent-sum matrix has rank $m$ over $\mathbb Q$, the canonical map $G\to(G*F_n)/\langle\langle w_1,\dots,w_m\rangle\rangle$ is injective, so the system has a simultaneous solution in an overgroup. This contains the Kervaire-Laudenbach conjecture (one equation, one unknown, nonzero exponent sum) and the Kervaire conjecture. It does NOT control the overgroup (no finiteness, solvability or other structure of the solution group), and says nothing about singular systems.
problems.aiRole: The release README says the manuscripts were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model, the vast majority by one fixed procedure using on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result, and that some outputs build on earlier results produced by the models. Its named exceptions to that procedure (the zeta zero-free region work, whose Re(s) > 11/12 write-up was human edited, and the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties) do not concern this family. The manuscript is credited to OpenAI with no human author named. It states that its spectral-phase and planar-surface strategy comes from the family's earlier Kervaire manuscript (24 September 2026), extended by a multi-block fixed-space theorem for products of unitary groups.
problems.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Theorem 1 of the principal manuscript was read against the conjecture as the manuscript formulates it: for any group $G$ and $1\le m\le n$, full rational row rank of the exponent-sum matrix gives injectivity of $G$ into the quotient, with Remark 5.1 extending to infinite systems with independent rows. This manuscript has no Lean formalisation. The family's Lean challenge (ComparatorChallenges/Kervaire.lean) covers only one relator with exponent sum $\pm1$, which is much narrower than this theorem. The release README warns that some unformalised results could have issues.

problems.name: The strong isotropic constant conjecture: simplices maximize the isotropic constant
problems.field: Convex geometry; isotropic constants and the slicing problem
problems.statement: For a convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^n$ with covariance matrix $\Sigma_K$ of the uniform distribution, the isotropic constant is $L_K=(\det\Sigma_K/|K|^2)^{1/(2n)}$, an affine invariant. Bourgain's slicing problem asked for a dimension-free upper bound, recently obtained by Klartag and Lehec. The sharp (strong) form asks for the extremal body: Campi, Colesanti and Gronchi proved it in the plane, Saroglou proved uniqueness there, and Rademacher showed a simplicial polytope maximizer must be a simplex. Klartag showed the sharp bound implies the non-symmetric Mahler inequality, and Fradelizi and Marin Sola recast it as a sharp entropy bound for log-concave densities. Is it true in every dimension $n$ that $L_K\le L_{\Delta_n}$ for every convex body $K$, where $\Delta_n$ is a simplex, with equality only for simplices?
problems.posedBy: Sharp form of Bourgain's slicing problem (1986); no originator named in the manuscript, which cites Campi-Colesanti-Gronchi (1999, planar case) and Fradelizi-Marin Sola (entropy form)
problems.ageNote: The manuscript calls it the strong isotropic constant conjecture without naming who first stated it; the planar case was proved by Campi, Colesanti and Gronchi in 1999, so it predates that. Left null rather than guessed.
problems.resultNote: Claims Theorem 1.1: for every $n\ge1$ and every convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^n$, $L_K\le(n!)^{1/n}/((n+1)^{(n+1)/(2n)}\sqrt{n+2})$, with equality if and only if $K$ is a simplex. Also claims the sharp entropy bound $h(f)\ge m+\tfrac12\log\det\mathrm{Cov}(f)$ for every log-concave density on $\mathbb R^m$, with equality exactly for affine images of products of one-sided exponentials, proved via Gaussian-to-target Brenier transport. Via Klartag (2018) it yields the non-symmetric Mahler inequality $|K||K^\circ|\ge(n+1)^{n+1}/(n!)^2$, already listed from a separate manuscript of the same release. It gives no new information on the symmetric slicing constant or on symmetric Mahler.

problems.name: Gaboriau's fixed price problem: do all essentially free p.m.p. actions of a countable group have the same cost?
problems.field: Measured group theory; cost of measure-preserving actions
problems.statement: For a countable group $\Gamma$ acting by measure-preserving Borel automorphisms on a standard probability space, the cost of the orbit equivalence relation is the infimum of the total measure of generating graphings (Levitt 1995). A group has fixed price if all its essentially free probability-measure-preserving actions have the same cost. Gaboriau showed that free groups $F_n$ have fixed price $n$ and that many groups with commuting or amenable structure have fixed price one, and asked whether every countable group has fixed price. Does every countable group have fixed price, or are there two essentially free p.m.p. actions of one group with different costs?
problems.posedBy: Damien Gaboriau (building on the notion of cost introduced by Gilbert Levitt)
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites Gaboriau, Cout des relations d'equivalence et des groupes, Invent. Math. 139 (2000), for the fixed-price problem, and Levitt (1995) for the definition of cost. The question may have circulated slightly earlier; the manuscript gives no earlier statement.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: let $A=F(a,b_1,\dots,b_{99})$, $w=ab_1ab_2\cdots ab_{99}a$, $J=\langle b_1,\dots,b_{99},w\rangle$ and $\Gamma=A*_J(J\times\langle t\rangle)$. With $K=e^{96}96^{99}/95^{95}$, $0<\alpha<1/200$, $K\alpha^3<1/2$ and $\eta=\alpha/100$, the free part of the Bernoulli action on $[0,1]^\Gamma$ has cost at least $1+\eta$, while the skew action on $X\times\mathbb Z/M$ via $\chi(a)=1$, $\chi(b_i)=\chi(t)=0$ has cost at most $1+99/M$. Taking $M>\max\{100,99/\eta\}$ gives two essentially free p.m.p. actions of one finitely generated group with different costs. It does not address the fixed-price-one question for groups with property (T), the fixed price of any specific classical group, or the rank-gradient consequences of fixed price.

This result is not among the README's exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region, whose write-up was human edited). The manuscripts are authored 'OpenAI' and name no human author. The family is a single manuscript (October 5, 2026). Its INPUTS.md says it was developed from an intermediate source argument and that the available source record does not establish that it was the final revision of that argument; it also says the result is distinct from the fixed-price-one question for property (T) groups.
problems.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 and its proof assembly (the conclusion section) were read against the fixed-price question as Gaboriau posed it. The theorem gives the amalgam $\Gamma=A*_J(J\times\langle t\rangle)$ with $A$ free of rank 100, a Bernoulli action of cost at least $1+\eta$, and finite height extensions of cost at most $1+99/M$; both actions are essentially free, so this is a direct negative answer to the general question. The manuscript's INPUTS.md notes that it was developed from an intermediate argument whose final revision status is not recorded.

problems.name: Critical two-point decay $r^{-1/4}(\log r)^{1/8}$ in the planar XY model
problems.shortName: XY critical decay with log correction
problems.statement: The nearest-neighbor XY model on $\mathbb Z^2$ at inverse temperature $b$ gives angles $\theta_x$ the weight $\exp(b\sum_{x\sim y}\cos(\theta_x-\theta_y))$. Berezinskii, Kosterlitz and Thouless predicted a transition at $b_c$ driven by vortex unbinding, with algebraic decay of the spin correlation $C_b(r)=\langle\cos(\theta_0-\theta_{re_1})\rangle$ for $b\ge b_c$. Kosterlitz's 1974 renormalization-group analysis predicts at criticality the universal exponent $\eta=1/4$ with a multiplicative logarithmic correction, $C_{b_c}(r)\asymp r^{-1/4}(\log r)^{1/8}$ (as recorded, e.g., by Janke for the Villain model). Rigorous work gave power-law bounds (McBryan-Spencer, Frohlich-Spencer, van Engelenburg-Lis) but not the critical exponent. Does $C_{b_c}(r)=B\,r^{-1/4}(\log r)^{1/8}(1+o(1))$ hold with $0<B<\infty$?
problems.posedBy: J. M. Kosterlitz (renormalization-group prediction), building on Berezinskii and Kosterlitz-Thouless
problems.ageNote: Kosterlitz, The critical properties of the two-dimensional XY model, J. Phys. C 7 (1974), cited by the manuscript; it also cites Janke (1997) for the explicit form with the logarithmic factor. Berezinskii (1971) and Kosterlitz-Thouless (1973) predicted the phase.
problems.resultNote: Log-correction paper, Theorem 1.1: $C_{b_c}(r)=B_{XY}r^{-1/4}(\log r)^{1/8}(1+o(1))$ as $r\to\infty$ along the axis, with $B_{XY}\in(0,\infty)$, for the free-box limit. Exponent paper (September 24): $C_{b_c}(r)=r^{-1/4+o(1)}$. The constant is not computed; off-axis directions, other lattices and the Villain model at criticality are not covered here, and the next-order $\log\log r/\log r$ correction is not claimed. Companions prove a Gaussian free field limit for discrete Gaussian heights through the roughening threshold with universal value $8\pi$, and (conditional on stated inputs) the critical center magnetization $n^{-1/8}(\log n)^{1/16}$ and spin-field scaling limit.

problems.name: The Kosterlitz essential singularity of the XY correlation length
problems.statement: For the nearest-neighbor XY model on $\mathbb Z^2$, let $m(b)$ be the exponential decay rate of the spin correlation along an axis and $\xi(b)=1/m(b)$ the correlation length, finite for $b<b_c$. Unlike ordinary critical points, where $\xi$ diverges as a power of $b_c-b$, Kosterlitz's renormalization-group analysis predicts an essential singularity: $\log\xi(b)\sim A/\sqrt{b_c-b}$ as $b\uparrow b_c$. Rigorous work established the transition and the exponential-versus-polynomial dichotomy (Frohlich-Spencer, van Engelenburg-Lis, Aizenman-Harel-Peled-Shapiro, Lammers) but not the rate of divergence. Is there a constant $A\in(0,\infty)$ with $\sqrt{b_c-b}\,\log\xi(b)\to A$ as $b\uparrow b_c$?
problems.posedBy: J. M. Kosterlitz
problems.ageNote: Kosterlitz, The critical properties of the two-dimensional XY model, J. Phys. C 7 (1974), cited by the manuscript as the source of the prediction.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there is $A_{XY}\in(0,\infty)$ with $\lim_{b\uparrow b_c}\sqrt{b_c-b}\,\log\xi(b)=A_{XY}$, for the square-lattice nearest-neighbor cosine model. The constant is expressed through the block construction and is not evaluated. It does not cover other lattices, the Villain model, the behaviour of the susceptibility, or corrections beyond the leading order.

problems.name: The BFSS exclusion of positive-energy normalizable states in the relative SU(2) model
problems.field: Supersymmetric matrix quantum mechanics; embedded eigenvalues
problems.statement: For the relative $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ BFSS Hamiltonian (supersymmetric quantum mechanics of three $9$-vectors with quartic potential $\sum_{a<b}|x^a\wedge x^b|^2$ and sixteen fermions per color), de Wit, Luscher and Nicolai (1989) proved the spectrum is $[0,\infty)$ and left open whether normalizable eigenstates lie inside it. Banks, Fischler, Shenker and Susskind (1997, Section 5, after Equation (5.4)) stated that besides the zero-energy threshold states 'No other normalizable bound states can occur'. Danielsson, Ferretti and Sundborg had found metastable excited states in a Born-Oppenheimer approximation. Does the relative $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ Hamiltonian have normalizable eigenstates of positive energy?
problems.posedBy: T. Banks, W. Fischler, S. H. Shenker and L. Susskind, M theory as a matrix model: a conjecture, Phys. Rev. D (1997), Section 5; open question in de Wit, Luscher and Nicolai (1989)
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: the relative $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ BFSS Hamiltonian has infinitely many positive eigenvalues $E_j\to\infty$ with square-integrable eigenvectors, so $\sigma_p(H)\cap(0,\infty)$ is infinite. This contradicts, for this exact operator at $N=2$, the BFSS paper's sentence excluding other normalizable bound states. It concerns only $N=2$, says nothing about $N\ge3$, and does not bear on the zero-energy state (the companion entry) or on large-$N$ matrix theory.

problems.name: The asymptotically anti-de Sitter Penrose inequality for three-dimensional initial data with spherical conformal infinity
problems.statement: With cosmological constant $-3$, the Schwarzschild-anti-de Sitter relation $M=(r_h+r_h^3)/2$ and Penrose's 1973 argument suggest that asymptotically hyperbolic initial data with a trapped boundary of area $A$ have mass, in the sense of Wang and Chrusciel-Herzlich, at least $\frac12(r_A+r_A^3)$ with $r_A=\sqrt{A/4\pi}$. Even the time-symmetric case was known only for special classes: graphs (Dahl-Gicquaud-Sakovich, de Lima-Girao), small perturbations of Schwarzschild-anti-de Sitter (Ambrozio; Khuri-Kopinski), and Neves showed inverse mean curvature flow cannot be used directly. Does every three-dimensional asymptotically anti-de Sitter initial-data set with spherical conformal infinity, the dominant energy condition and a weakly trapped boundary satisfy $m\ge\frac12(r_A+r_A^3)$ with $A$ the minimal enclosing area, with equality only for Schwarzschild-anti-de Sitter?
problems.posedBy: Penrose's 1973 heuristic in the asymptotically anti-de Sitter setting; studied as a conjecture by Dahl, Gicquaud and Sakovich, Ambrozio, and Khuri and Kopinski, among others
problems.ageNote: The manuscript traces the inequality to Penrose (1973) and the mass of Wang and Chrusciel-Herzlich but cites no single source stating the asymptotically hyperbolic conjecture, so no year is set.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1 (principal): under those hypotheses $m_{AH}\ge\frac12(r_A+r_A^3)$ with $A$ the full enclosing-area infimum, sharp; no maximality, compact topology or connectedness assumption. Equality on the stated horizon subclass identifies the original data as a spacelike hypersurface in Schwarzschild-anti-de Sitter with the same mass. Companions: the maximal case with possibly disconnected boundary, and a local inequality for small maximal vacuum conformal perturbations of Schwarzschild-anti-de Sitter using the horizon's own area. Not shown: higher dimensions, toroidal or higher-genus conformal infinity (the Lee-Neves regime), or timelikeness of the mass as a conclusion.

problems.name: Emerton's dimension conjecture for the full Hecke algebra at p = 2 and odd level
problems.field: p-adic families of modular forms; Hecke algebras
problems.statement: For a prime $p$ and level $N$ prime to $p$, let $\mathbb T_p(N)$ be the inverse limit over $k$ of the $\mathbb Z_p$-Hecke algebras generated by $T_\ell$ and $\ell S_\ell$ ($\ell\nmid pN$) acting on all modular forms of weights $1,\dots,k$ and level $\Gamma_1(N)$, Eisenstein forms included. Emerton, in his 2011 Bourbaki account of $p$-adic families (Conjecture 2.9), conjectured that every irreducible component of $\mathrm{Spec}\,\mathbb T_p(N)$ has Krull dimension four, and proved the lower bound (Corollary 2.28). For $p=2$ and every odd $N$, does every irreducible component have dimension exactly four?
problems.posedBy: Matthew Emerton, p-adic families of modular forms [after Hida, Coleman, and Mazur], Seminaire Bourbaki 2009/2010, Asterisque 339 (2011), Conjecture 2.9
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every odd $N$, every irreducible component of $\mathrm{Spec}\,\mathbb T_2(N)$ has Krull dimension exactly $4$. The upper bound comes from a cuspidal point of weight at least 3 on each component, a tangent bound of 3 from Newton-Thorne Selmer vanishing, and one arithmetic dimension. Only the case $p=2$ is treated; the paper does not claim the conjecture for odd $p$.

problems.name: The permanence conjecture for weakly reversible mass-action systems with fixed rates
problems.field: Chemical reaction network theory: mass-action kinetics
problems.statement: For a weakly reversible reaction network with mass-action kinetics $\dot x=\sum_{y\to y'}k_{y\to y'}x^y(y'-y)$ and fixed positive rates, let $S$ be the span of the reaction vectors $y'-y$ and $P=(c+S)\cap\mathbb R^d_{>0}$ a positive stoichiometric class, which may be unbounded. The system is permanent on $P$ if every solution starting in $P$ is global and positive and one compact $K\subset P$ eventually contains each of them, the entry time but not $K$ depending on the initial point. This is stronger than boundedness plus persistence of each trajectory. Known before: permanence for strongly endotactic networks, including weakly reversible ones with one linkage class (Gopalkrishnan-Miller-Shiu; Boros-Hofbauer), and for two species (Craciun-Nazarov-Pantea). Is every weakly reversible mass-action system with fixed positive rates permanent on every positive stoichiometric class?
problems.posedBy: Permanence conjecture of chemical reaction network theory; the manuscript names it without an originating source and takes the classwise definition from Boros and Hofbauer (2020, Definition 4.1)
problems.ageNote: The manuscript calls this the permanence conjecture but gives no source or date for it, so poser and year are left blank rather than guessed.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for a finite weakly reversible network with fixed positive rates and any positive stoichiometric class $P$, there is a nonempty compact convex forward-invariant $K_P\subset P$ that every solution from $P$ enters in finite time; hence one $\varepsilon_P$ bounds every trajectory in $P$ between $\varepsilon_P$ and $\varepsilon_P^{-1}$ after its entry time, also on unbounded classes. The proof adds strict increase off the trapping set and a passage between scales to the companion's construction. Uniformity holds within one class and one choice of rates; entry times may depend on the initial point, and time-varying rates are not treated.

problems.name: Arnosti's RANDOM-VERTEX versus RANKING conjecture for greedy matching
problems.statement: In Nick Arnosti's random bipartite matching model, each job has a prescribed degree and independently samples a uniform feasible subset of the bins. Every bin has the same positive integer capacity C. RANDOM-VERTEX chooses a uniformly random available feasible bin for each job; RANKING uses one shared random priority order of the bins. Both process jobs in an independent uniform random arrival order. The conjecture following Theorem 2 asks whether RANDOM-VERTEX stochastically dominates RANKING in matching size for every C > 2. The paper proves equality in distribution for C = 1 and stochastic dominance for C = 2.
problems.posedBy: Nick Arnosti, Greedy Matching in Bipartite Random Graphs, conjecture after Theorem 2, p. 136 (online 2021; journal 2022).
problems.resultNote:
For every finite instance in the stated model, every common capacity $C\ge1$ and every threshold $K$, we prove $$\Pr(M_{\mathrm{RV}}\ge K)\ge\Pr(M_{\mathrm{RANKING}}\ge K).$$ The comparison holds for fixed arrival and bin-priority orders independent of the neighborhoods; averaging gives Arnosti's random-order model, including the conjectured $C>2$ regime.

The proof combines capped-load association, a two-bin coefficient identity, a saturation bound, refined histories and coupling at accepted-job counts. The written proof uses Cohen–Sackrowitz (1987), Lemma 4.1; Lean proves the required finite rational association statement directly. The inequality compares matching-size distributions. It does not assert dominance on every run, conditional on an arbitrary fixed graph, or for unequal capacities.
problems.aiRole: OpenAI Codex (GPT-6 Astra) selected and investigated the conjecture, developed the central mathematical argument, simplified the written proof using a published association theorem, and built the Lean formalization, verification tooling and interactive exposition. The human collaborator directed the research, set the requirement for a proof covering all capacities, requested simplification and formal verification, and reviewed the presentation. The contribution label refers to the model developing the central proof; it does not claim publication priority or independent human mathematical verification.

problems.name: The 3SUM hypothesis: is 3SUM solvable in truly subquadratic time?
problems.statement: Given $n$ integers in $[-n^c, n^c]$, decide whether three of them sum to zero. The 3SUM hypothesis asserts that no algorithm on a word RAM with $O(\log n)$-bit words solves this in $O(n^{2-\varepsilon})$ time for any $\varepsilon > 0$. Hundreds of conditional lower bounds in computational geometry and fine-grained complexity rest on it. Is there a truly subquadratic algorithm?
problems.posedBy: Anka Gajentaan and Mark Overmars (3SUM-hardness, 1995); the integer word-RAM form as used today is Patrascu's (2010)
problems.resultNote: Yes: a deterministic $O(n^{1.9992})$ algorithm for 3SUM on polynomially bounded integers on the word RAM, refuting the hypothesis, and a Las Vegas $O(n^{1.998})$ algorithm for real inputs using only additions, subtractions and comparisons. The core is a new algorithm for wanted entries of thin matrix products (a modified Coppersmith rectangular algorithm with a Schönhage identity), which solves Lopsided All-Edges Sparse Triangle; known reductions give 3SUM. The same paper refutes the APSP hypothesis, catalogued separately. The constants are enormous, so the impact is on the theory: the conditional lower bounds built on 3SUM no longer stand as stated. SETH and Orthogonal Vectors are unaffected.
problems.aiRole: From the abstract: "Claude, an AI model developed by Anthropic, discovered the algorithm that refutes the 3SUM, APSP, and Exact Triangle hypotheses." The methodology section adds that an Anthropic employee had set an internal research model to verify and improve cryptographic constructions based on the average-case hardness of Zero-k-Clique; instead it developed this algorithm, first for the average case and then the worst case, in one session of 16 million output tokens with no human input. Anthropic shared it with the authors in September 2026. Alman and Vassilevska Williams simplified, strengthened and extended it, derived further consequences and wrote the paper; an internal model later produced the Lean formalisation.
problems.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Read here on 6 October 2026, not rebuilt. The paper's Theorem 2 was compared with the standard hypotheses as its own introduction states them (word RAM with O(log n)-bit words, integers of absolute value n^O(1)) and matches. The Lean development (anthropics/formal-math, folder 3sum-apsp, commit e1a4e65; Lean 4.33.1 with mathlib, about 102,000 lines) proves correctness and running time of explicit programs on a word-RAM machine defined in Lean, a weaker machine than the standard word RAM, which only strengthens upper bounds. Its five headline claims are stated in a 139-line file with no imports. No sorry outside the deliberate Challenge folder, no axiom declarations, native_decide, implemented_by or unsafe. The statement file was written by the same party as the proof and has not been audited independently, and no Comparator run is recorded. No uninvolved expert has commented yet; the authors are the leading researchers of the area and are not independent reviewers.
problems.significanceNote: The central hardness assumption of computational geometry and one of the three pillars of fine-grained complexity for three decades, with hundreds of conditional lower bounds resting on it. Just below the APSP hypothesis at 55, refuted in the same paper, which carries the older textbook question, and below the matrix-multiplication exponent at 55; far above every other TCS entry, such as the SETH-hardness of furthest pair at 20.

problems.name: The charged spacetime Penrose inequality in upper-area form for Einstein-Maxwell initial data
problems.statement: With electric and magnetic charge, $Q^2=Q_E^2+Q_B^2$, Penrose's heuristic suggests that a black hole of given area cannot have less mass than the Reissner-Nordstrom black hole of that area and charge. For possibly disconnected horizons the lower form $m\ge(r_A+Q^2/r_A)/2$, $r_A=\sqrt{A/4\pi}$, can fail, and the appropriate statement is the upper-area inequality $m\ge|Q|$, $r_A\le m+\sqrt{m^2-Q^2}$; Khuri, Weinstein and Yamada proved it for time-symmetric data with multiple horizons. Does the upper-area inequality hold for general asymptotically flat initial data with arbitrary second fundamental form satisfying the charged dominant energy condition, with $A$ the least area enclosing a weakly trapped boundary, and is equality attained only by Reissner-Nordstrom?
problems.posedBy: Charged extension of Penrose's 1973 heuristic; upper-area form for multiple horizons from Marcus Khuri, Gilbert Weinstein and Sumio Yamada
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites Penrose (1973) and Khuri-Weinstein-Yamada (J. Differential Geom. 106, 2017) but no single source posing the non-time-symmetric charged conjecture, so no year is set.
problems.resultNote: Principal (Theorem 2.3): for one-ended three-dimensional data with arbitrary $K$, nonzero ADM momentum, disconnected weakly future trapped boundary and the stated decay, $m\ge|Q|$ and $r_A\le m+\sqrt{m^2-Q^2}$ with $A$ the minimal enclosing area; positive area and timelike ADM vector are conclusions. Equality (for $m>|Q|$, connected outermost horizon) identifies the data as a slice of dyonic Reissner-Nordstrom. Companions: the purely electric case in every dimension $n\ge4$; a Kerr-Newman Penrose inequality for axisymmetric electrovacuum exteriors with zero ADM momentum that assumes the area condition $A\ge4\pi\sqrt{Q^4+4J^2}$; and counterexamples to the Kerr-Newman bound when $J$ is the bare gravitational angular momentum and fields decay only like $r^{-2}$. problems.name: The stable coordinate conjecture in four variables
problems.statement: A polynomial $f\in\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ is a coordinate if some polynomial automorphism sends it to $x_1$, and a one-stable coordinate if it is a coordinate of $\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_n,w]$. Shpilrain and Yu conjectured that a polynomial which becomes a coordinate after adjoining a variable was already a coordinate. Over $\mathbb C$ it holds in one, two and three variables (Shpilrain-Yu, using Abhyankar-Moh, cancellation for curves and surfaces, and Kaliman's theorem), so four variables is the first possible dimension for a counterexample. Is every one-stable coordinate in $\mathbb C[x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4]$ a coordinate?
problems.posedBy: V. Shpilrain and J.-T. Yu, Affine varieties with equivalent cylinders, J. Algebra 251 (2002), Conjecture 3
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: with $Q=x_2^2-x_4^2+x_1x_3$ and $f=x_1-2Q(Q(x_2+x_4)+x_1x_4)$, a degree-five polynomial in $\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_4]$, some automorphism of $\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_4,w]$ sends $f$ to $x_1$ but none of $\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_4]$ does. Since the conjecture holds in at most three variables, this is the smallest possible dimension, and one added variable suffices. Corollary 1.2: every fibre of $f$ is $\mathbb A^3$ and none is rectifiable. Not shown: anything about dimensions above four, which the release's earlier five-variable example already covered for five; the result is one explicit polynomial, not a classification.

problems.name: The spatial Kadison-Kastler problem for close separable C*-algebras
problems.statement: Kadison and Kastler (1972) initiated the study of close operator algebras. For C*-algebras, Johnson showed implementing unitaries need not be close to the identity and Choi-Christensen gave close non-isomorphic algebras, but only non-separable ones. Christensen, Sinclair, Smith, White and Winter proved that sufficiently close separable nuclear C*-algebras on a separable Hilbert space are spatially isomorphic, and discussed the separable spatial formulation: is there a $\delta>0$ such that any two norm-separable C*-algebras $A,B$ on a separable Hilbert space with Kadison-Kastler distance below $\delta$ satisfy $uAu^*=B$ for some unitary $u$?
problems.posedBy: E. Christensen, A. M. Sinclair, R. R. Smith, S. A. White and W. Winter, The spatial isomorphism problem for close separable nuclear C*-algebras, PNAS 107 (2010)
problems.ageNote: The perturbation program is from Kadison-Kastler (1972); the manuscript cites the 2010 paper as discussing this separable spatial formulation.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every $\varepsilon>0$ there are unital norm-separable C*-algebras $A,B$ on a separable Hilbert space with $\mathrm{KK}(A,B)<\varepsilon$ and $A''=B''$ but no unitary with $uAu^*=B$. The construction uses sequence algebras over a deformation of the free-group regular representation (Pytlik-Szwarc family) and a tensor-norm obstruction. It does not show $A$ and $B$ are non-isomorphic, imposes no nuclearity (the CSSWW positive theorem needs it), and does not affect von Neumann algebras.

problems.name: Gromov's integral scalar-curvature bound for simplicial volume
problems.shortName: Gromov's scalar curvature vs simplicial volume
problems.field: Scalar curvature; simplicial volume and bounded cohomology
problems.statement: For a closed connected oriented $n$-manifold $M$ let $\|M\|$ be its real simplicial volume, and for a Riemannian metric $g$ let $\mathrm{Scal}_g^-=\max\{0,-\mathrm{Scal}_g\}$. In 1986 Gromov (Large Riemannian manifolds, Conjecture 3.A, Remark (B), Equation (8')) proposed bounding simplicial volume by the scale-invariant integral $\int_M(\mathrm{Scal}_g^-)^{n/2}dV_g$; equivalently, $\mathrm{Scal}_g\ge-\kappa^2$ should force $\|M\|\le C_n\kappa^n\mathrm{Vol}_g(M)$. Partial results covered bounded unit-ball volumes in the universal cover (Braun-Sauer), Kahler surfaces (Min-Zheng-Zhu) and qualitative vanishing for spin universal covers. Is there $a_n>0$ with $\int_M(\mathrm{Scal}_g^-)^{n/2}dV_g\ge a_n\|M\|$ for every closed $n$-manifold and every metric?
problems.posedBy: M. Gromov, Large Riemannian manifolds, in Curvature and Topology of Riemannian Manifolds (1986), Conjecture 3.A, Remark (B), Equation (8')
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every $n\ge3$ there is $a_n>0$ with $\int_M(\mathrm{Scal}_g^-)^{n/2}dV_g\ge a_n\|M\|$ for every closed connected oriented smooth $n$-manifold $M$ and smooth metric $g$; e.g. $\mathrm{Scal}_g\ge-n(n-1)$ gives $\mathrm{Vol}_g(M)\ge a_n[n(n-1)]^{-n/2}\|M\|$. The route is a Yamabe reduction to $\mathrm{Scal}=-1$ followed by a bounded-cohomology and graph-deformation estimate. No explicit value of $a_n$ is stated in the theorem, and dimension two is excluded.

problems.name: Bloch's $T^{3/2}$ law for the three-dimensional quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet
problems.statement: Bloch's spin-wave theory (1930) predicts that the spontaneous magnetization of a three-dimensional ferromagnet falls below saturation by an amount proportional to $T^{3/2}$, with a coefficient fixed by the quadratic one-magnon dispersion; for the nearest-neighbour spin-$S$ Heisenberg model the deficit is $\zeta(3/2)(8\pi^{3/2}S^{3/2})^{-1}T^{3/2}$ to leading order. Dyson (1956) analysed spin-wave interactions and the higher-order terms, but not as a rigorous fixed-spin proof, and Correggi-Giuliani-Seiringer (2015) proved the corresponding free-energy asymptotics, which do not control the zero-field derivative. Is it true, for the quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet on $\mathbb Z^3$ at fixed spin, that $S-m(\beta)\sim c\,\beta^{-3/2}$ as $\beta\to\infty$ with Bloch's coefficient, where $m$ is the spontaneous magnetization?
problems.posedBy: Felix Bloch (1930), spin-wave prediction; developed by Holstein-Primakoff (1940) and Dyson (1956)
problems.ageNote: A physical prediction stated precisely in print. The manuscript cites Bloch (1930) and Dyson (1956), notes that Dyson's higher-order estimates were not a rigorous proof, and cites Lieb (1999) and Seiringer (2025) for the ordering problem underneath it.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every fixed spin $S$ and every nonnegative symmetric finite-range coupling $J$ on $\mathbb Z^3$ whose support generates $\mathbb Z^3$, $\lim_{\beta\to\infty}\beta^{3/2}(S-m_{S,J}(\beta))=\zeta(3/2)/(8\pi^{3/2}\sqrt{\det D_{S,J}})$, with $D_{S,J}=\frac S2\sum_z J(z)zz^{\mathsf T}$; nearest-neighbour gives $\zeta(3/2)/(8\pi^{3/2}S^{3/2})$. Companions: the first lattice correction $3\zeta(5/2)(\beta S)^{-5/2}/(128\pi^{3/2})$ for nearest-neighbour couplings, deficit equal to the ideal-magnon density up to $o(\beta^{-5/2})$; and a spherical magnetization law for the symmetric zero-field magnetization on periodic cubes. Not shown: Dyson's $T^4$ interaction term, dimensions other than three, or uniformity in $S$.

problems.name: The Alon-Krivelevich-Sudakov conjecture: graphs with a fixed forbidden subgraph have chromatic number O(Delta/log Delta)
problems.field: Graph coloring: sparse and F-free graphs
problems.statement: Every graph of maximum degree $\Delta$ has $\chi(G)\le\Delta+1$. Johansson (1996) proved $\chi(G)=O(\Delta/\log\Delta)$ for triangle-free graphs, and Alon, Krivelevich and Sudakov (1999) extended this to graphs with sparse neighborhoods. For general fixed $F$, and already for $F=K_4$, the best bounds carried an extra $\log\log\Delta$ factor. Alon, Krivelevich and Sudakov (1999, Conjecture 3.1) conjectured: for every fixed graph $F$ there is $C_F$ such that every $F$-free graph of maximum degree $\Delta$ has chromatic number at most $C_F\Delta/\log\Delta$. Is this true?
problems.posedBy: N. Alon, M. Krivelevich and B. Sudakov, Coloring graphs with sparse neighborhoods, J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 77 (1999), Conjecture 3.1
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every $r\ge4$ there are $C_r$ and $\Delta_r$ such that every $K_r$-free graph of maximum degree $\Delta\ge\Delta_r$ has correspondence (DP) chromatic number at most $\lceil C_r\Delta/\log\Delta\rceil$; Corollary 1.2 gives the same for any fixed forbidden subgraph $F$, which implies the conjecture for ordinary and list coloring. The proof is a round-based random partial coloring with weighted lists, controlled by an entropy potential and local adjustments that offset triangle correlations. Constants and thresholds are not optimized; no explicit leading constant is claimed.

problems.name: The Aaronson-Kuperberg unitary synthesis problem at constant diamond-norm error
problems.field: Quantum query complexity; oracle synthesis of unitaries
problems.statement: Aaronson and Kuperberg (2007) asked whether, for every $n$-qubit unitary $U$, there is a Boolean oracle $A$ such that a polynomial-time quantum algorithm with access to $A$ implements $U$. Aaronson (2021, Problem 6) named it the Unitary Synthesis Problem, called it wide open and conjectured a negative answer. Known results: state synthesis with one query (Irani et al., Rosenthal), a $2^{n/2}$-time upper bound for unitaries (Rosenthal), and one-query and parallel-query lower bounds (Lombardi-Ma-Wright). Is there a polynomial-size quantum oracle circuit family which, for every $n$-qubit $U$ and a suitable Boolean oracle depending on $U$, implements $U$ approximately?
problems.posedBy: S. Aaronson and G. Kuperberg, Quantum versus classical proofs and advice, Theory of Computing 3 (2007), Section 7, Problem (4); restated in Aaronson (2021), Problem 6
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there are a polynomial $p$ and a deterministic algorithm outputting, on $1^n$, an oracle circuit $A_n$ with at most $p(n)$ qubits, gates and oracle calls and oracle input length at most $p(n)$, such that for every $U\in U(2^n)$ some $f$ gives $\|\Phi_{n,f}-\mathcal U\|_\diamond\le1/2$. The method is a recursive dimension reduction using one coherently controlled smaller synthesis per step. It does not achieve arbitrarily small error, does not give an efficient classical procedure for the oracle, and answers positively a question on which Aaronson (2021) had conjectured a negative answer.

problems.name: The Projected Lax Conjecture: is every hyperbolicity cone a spectrahedral shadow?
problems.field: Real algebraic geometry; semidefinite lifts of convex cones
problems.statement: A spectrahedral shadow is a set of the form $\{x\in\mathbb R^d:\exists u\in\mathbb R^a,\ A_0+\sum_i x_iA_i+\sum_j u_jB_j\succeq0\}$ with finitely many real symmetric matrices, that is, a set with a finite semidefinite lift. Netzer and Sanyal (2015) proved that a hyperbolicity cone is a spectrahedral shadow when every nonzero boundary point is a smooth point of its hyperbolic polynomial, and formulated the Projected Lax Conjecture, a weakening of the generalized Lax conjecture. Is every closed hyperbolicity cone a spectrahedral shadow?
problems.posedBy: Tim Netzer and Raman Sanyal, Smooth hyperbolicity cones are spectrahedral shadows, Math. Program. 153 (2015)
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there exists a real homogeneous hyperbolic polynomial whose closed hyperbolicity cone admits no finite semidefinite lift (exact equality, no closure). The cone comes from a positive semidefinite matrix-valued quadratic map $Q$ via an affine section $E_Q=\{(A,t,y):A\succeq0,\ t\ge\mathrm{tr}(A^\dagger Q(y))\}$, and a local sums-of-squares obstruction in the spirit of Scheiderer rules out every lift. This also disproves the generalized Lax conjecture. It is an existence result in high dimension, not an explicit polynomial and not a lower bound on lift size. Note the explicit cone of the September 24 companion does have an exact lift (size 100 pencil, 307 auxiliary variables).

The construction is an existence argument in high dimension; it relies on a finite-field rank certificate given in an appendix.
