problems.name: Flouri et al.'s MSci identifiability conjecture, for clock-JC data with long loci
problems.field: Mathematical statistics; algebraic identifiability; coalescent phylogenetics
problems.statement: Flouri, Jiao, Rannala and Yang ask whether, with multiple sampled sequences and multiple sites per locus, parameters of the multispecies coalescent with introgression are identifiable from sequence alignments exactly when they are identifiable from gene-tree topologies and coalescent times. The present entry makes the observation channel and site-length quantifier explicit: complete labelled contemporaneous haploid alignments, homogeneous stationary molecular-clock JC mutation in mutation-scaled units, and sufficiently long finite loci within each fixed finite MSci model.
problems.posedBy: Flouri, Jiao, Rannala and Yang, MBE 37(4):1211–1223, DOI 10.1093/molbev/msz296 (online 6 Dec 2019; issue 2020). Restated by Yang and Flouri, MBE 39:msac083 (2022).
problems.resultNote:
For every fixed finite admitted MSci model and its unchanged labelled sample panel, a finite site cutoff works uniformly over parameter pairs: complete sequence laws agree exactly when route-marginal timed-genealogy laws agree. All identifiable functionals and all genuine ambiguities transfer. Multiple introgressions, expansions, equal rates, rank-deficient routing and source-allowed inheritance endpoints are covered. The A–D compiler preserves tied ages and current-lineage routing. Trees end at the sample MRCA; route flags are marginalized.

The channel is complete contemporaneous haploid data under homogeneous stationary clock-JC in mutation units. No arbitrary short-locus claim, universal cutoff over unbounded complexity, or general demographic uniqueness is made. Unknown locus-rate mixtures, unphased genotypes and other mutation/clock channels remain separate. No calendar calibration, finite-data accuracy or reliable numerical inference is supplied.
problems.aiRole: Under the user's research direction, dot (OpenAI) developed the mathematical observation bridge, finite-site arguments and source-specific MSci compiler, wrote the proof and exact rational controls, and performed separate AI correctness/source-scope reviews. The finite-generation method builds on classical polynomial-family identifiability and finite exponential recurrence ideas, with attribution in the proof. The biological model and conjecture are existing research. No human expert endorsement is claimed.
problems.verificationNote: Read by this site on 6 October 2026. The source sentence was checked in the 2020 paper (Discussion, Identifiability of MSci models) and in Yang and Flouri's 2022 restatement. The submission's event-compiler check passed when re-run here; it verifies small rational routing compositions, not identifiability. problems.significanceNote: The source states it as a one-sentence speculation (2020), named a conjecture in 2022; real and cited, within phylogenetics. Scored for the variant answered, which fixes the clock-JC channel and allows long loci. Level with the Sun conjectures at 5.

problems.name: Log abundance for threefolds in characteristic $p>3$ in numerical dimension one
problems.shortName: Char p threefold log abundance, nu = 1
problems.field: Birational geometry in positive characteristic; minimal model program
problems.statement: The abundance conjecture predicts that if $(X,B)$ is a projective log canonical pair and $K_X+B$ is nef, then $K_X+B$ is semiample. For threefolds over $\mathbb C$ this is a theorem (Miyaoka, Kawamata, Keel-Matsuki-McKernan). Over algebraically closed fields of characteristic $p>0$ it remains open; Zheng Xu proved nonvanishing for $p>3$, abundance in nef dimension at most two, and abundance in numerical dimension two. Is abundance true for projective log canonical threefold pairs in characteristic $p>3$, in particular when $K_X+B$ is nef of numerical dimension one?
problems.posedBy: The abundance conjecture of the minimal model program (classical; the manuscript names no poser); the remaining numerical-dimension-one case is isolated by Zheng Xu's 2024 and 2026 papers
problems.ageNote: The manuscript does not attribute or date the abundance conjecture; it cites Miyaoka (1988) and Kawamata (1992) for the complex threefold case and Xu (2024, 2026) for the positive-characteristic results that leave numerical dimension one and nef dimension three open. yearPosed is left empty.
problems.resultNote: Principal Theorem 1.1: over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>3$, if $(X,B)$ is a projective log canonical threefold pair with effective $\mathbb Q$-boundary, $K_X+B$ is $\mathbb Q$-Cartier, nef and of numerical dimension one, then $K_X+B$ is semiample; neither terminality nor $\mathbb Q$-factoriality is needed. The companion proves the terminal $\mathbb Q$-factorial case ($K_X$ nef with $\nu=1$ gives $\kappa=1$ and semiampleness). Characteristics 2 and 3, numerical dimension zero and higher dimensions are not addressed.

problems.name: Bose-Einstein condensation of the dilute hard-sphere Bose gas in the thermodynamic limit, at zero and small positive temperature
problems.shortName: BEC for the dilute hard-sphere gas
problems.field: Quantum many-body theory; dilute Bose gases
problems.statement: Consider $N$ bosons on the torus $\Lambda_L=(\mathbb{R}/L\mathbb{Z})^3$ interacting through a repulsive short-range potential, for instance hard spheres of diameter $a$. Condensation in the sense of Penrose and Onsager means that the constant orbital carries a macroscopic fraction of the particles: $\liminf N^{-1}\langle u_0,\gamma^{(1)}u_0\rangle>0$ as $L\to\infty$ with $N/L^3\to\rho$ fixed, for the ground state or the Gibbs state at a fixed temperature. This had been proved only in scaling limits where the box stays comparable to the healing length (Gross-Pitaevskii) or the interaction vanishes, and for a lattice hard-core gas at half filling. Does the dilute three-dimensional interacting Bose gas exhibit Bose-Einstein condensation in the thermodynamic limit at fixed density, in its ground state and at positive temperature?
problems.posedBy: Long-standing, after Penrose and Onsager's 1956 definition of condensation; Solovej's 2025 survey calls condensation in the thermodynamic limit a major open problem
problems.ageNote: The manuscripts trace the notion to Penrose and Onsager (1956) and cite Solovej (C. R. Physique 2025, Section 5) for the problem's status, but none dates when it was first posed as an open problem, so the year is left blank.
problems.resultNote: Positive temperature (October 5): for every $a>0$ there is $\rho_*(a)>0$ such that for each fixed $0<\rho<\rho_*$ some fixed $T(a,\rho)>0$ gives $\liminf N^{-1}\langle u_{0,L},\gamma^{(1)}_{N,L,T}u_{0,L}\rangle>0$ for the exact canonical hard-sphere Gibbs state as $L\to\infty$, $N/L^3\to\rho$. Ground state (September 24 companion): absolute $\varepsilon_0,c_0>0$ with condensate fraction at least $c_0$ in every ground state when $\rho a^3<\varepsilon_0$. A further companion gives a density-uniform bound for bounded nonnegative finite-range potentials at temperatures up to $\rho^2$. Not shown: the transition temperature, condensation at moderate density, two dimensions, or potentials with attractive parts.

problems.name: The APSP hypothesis: are all-pairs shortest paths computable in truly subcubic time?
problems.statement: Given a directed graph on $n$ vertices with integer edge weights in $[-n^c, n^c]$ and no negative cycles, compute all pairwise shortest-path distances. Floyd-Warshall does it in $O(n^3)$ time, and decades of improvements removed only subpolynomial factors. The APSP hypothesis asserts that no algorithm on a word RAM with $O(\log n)$-bit words runs in $O(n^{3-\varepsilon})$ time for any $\varepsilon > 0$; a large class of problems is subcubically equivalent to it. Is there a truly subcubic algorithm?
problems.posedBy: Virginia Vassilevska Williams and Ryan Williams (subcubic equivalences, FOCS 2010); the question of truly subcubic APSP is as old as Floyd-Warshall (1962)
problems.ageNote: Dated from the hypothesis as formulated by Vassilevska Williams and Williams in 2010; whether APSP admits a truly subcubic algorithm had been asked since Floyd-Warshall in 1962. Vassilevska Williams, who co-posed the hypothesis, co-authored the refutation.
problems.resultNote: Yes: deterministic $O(n^{2.9995})$ algorithms for APSP and for the (min,+)-product with polynomially bounded integer weights on the word RAM (the Lean development states $n^{2.99942}$), and Exact Triangle in $O(n^{2.9983})$, refuting the APSP and Exact Triangle hypotheses; a Las Vegas $O(n^{2.998})$ version works for real weights. The core is a new thin-matrix-product algorithm solving Lopsided All-Edges Sparse Triangle, with known reductions giving the rest. The same paper refutes the 3SUM hypothesis, catalogued separately. The constants are enormous; the impact is on the theory of subcubic equivalences, not on practice. SETH and Orthogonal Vectors are unaffected.

problems.name: Ball's extension problem for Lipschitz maps from Hilbert space into $\ell_1$, via the Mendel-Naor metric Markov cotype question
problems.field: Metric geometry; nonlinear Banach space theory, Lipschitz extension
problems.statement: Ball (1992) introduced Markov type and cotype to study Lipschitz extension and asked whether every Lipschitz map $f$ from an arbitrary subset of a Hilbert space $H$ into $L_1$ extends to all of $H$ with $\mathrm{Lip}(F)\le K\,\mathrm{Lip}(f)$ for a universal $K$. Mendel and Naor (2013) formulated metric Markov cotype two in Cesaro form: $X$ has it with constant $C$ if for every reversible stochastic matrix $A$ with stationary $\pi$, every $t$ and points $x_1,\dots,x_n\in X$ there are $y_1,\dots,y_n\in X$ with $\sum_i\pi_i d(x_i,y_i)^2+t\sum_{i,j}\pi_i a_{ij}d(y_i,y_j)^2\le C^2\sum_{i,j}\pi_i(\frac1t\sum_{s=1}^tA^s)_{ij}d(x_i,x_j)^2$. They showed that a positive answer for $\ell_1$ yields the extension, and asked (Question 1.15): is $N_2(\ell_1)<\infty$, that is, does $\ell_1$ have metric Markov cotype two?
problems.posedBy: Keith Ball (1992, extension problem); Manor Mendel and Assaf Naor (2013, Question 1.15)
problems.ageNote: Ball's extension problem dates from his 1992 GAFA paper 'Markov chains, Riesz transforms and Lipschitz maps'. The metric Markov cotype question for l1 was asked explicitly by Mendel and Naor in 2013 (Analysis and Geometry in Metric Spaces, Question 1.15 and Section 7). The paper also cites Naor-Young (Acta Math. 2022) for discussion of the extension problem.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: real $\ell_1$ has metric Markov cotype two with $N_2(\ell_1)\le12\sqrt{21}$, uniformly in the number of points, coordinates and time parameter; complex $\ell_1$ follows with $12\sqrt{42}$. Corollary: there is a universal $K$ such that every Lipschitz $f:S\to\ell_1$, $S$ any subset of a real Hilbert space, extends to $F:H\to\ell_1$ with $\mathrm{Lip}(F)\le K\,\mathrm{Lip}(f)$. The construction is nonlinear (expected coordinatewise medians of geometric-walk endpoints after cut smoothing), consistent with the known failure of Ball's linear Markov cotype for $\ell_1$ and the Kalton-based subspace counterexample. No optimal constant is claimed, and targets other than $\ell_1$ are not treated.

problems.name: The Erdos similarity conjecture for geometric progressions
problems.field: Real analysis; measure theory and affine copies
problems.statement: A set $A\subseteq\mathbb R$ is measure universal if every measurable set of positive Lebesgue measure contains an affine copy $x+sA$ with $s\ne0$. Every finite set is universal. Erdos (1974, Problem 4.33.7*) conjectured that no infinite set is. Falconer and Eigen proved it for sequences $a_n\to0$ with $a_{n+1}/a_n\to1$, and later criteria (Kolountzakis, Humke-Laczkovich, Chlebik) do not apply to geometric progressions, so even the dyadic sequence $\{2^{-n}\}$ remained open. Is it true that for every $q\in(0,1)$ the progression $\{q^n:n\ge1\}$ is not measure universal, that is, some set of positive measure contains no affine copy of it?
problems.posedBy: Paul Erdos (Problem 4.33.7*, Mathematica Balkanica 4, 1974)
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every $q\in(0,1)$ and $\eta\in(0,1)$ there is a compact $E_{q,\eta}\subseteq[0,1]$ with $m(E_{q,\eta})>1-\eta$ such that for all $x\in\mathbb R$, $s\ne0$, some $x+sq^n\notin E_{q,\eta}$. So no geometric progression is measure universal; the dyadic companion first proved $q=1/2$. The construction is probabilistic (random routing tables on a finite tree). It does not prove the conjecture for other infinite sets, and makes no claim of one set avoiding all ratios at once.

problems.name: The stable Morse number as a lower bound for nondegenerate Hamiltonian fixed points
problems.field: Symplectic topology; Hamiltonian fixed points, stable Morse theory
problems.statement: The stable Morse number $\mathrm{SM}(W)$ of a closed manifold is the least number of critical points of a Morse function $F:W\times\mathbb R^k\to\mathbb R$ equal to a nondegenerate quadratic form outside a compact set ($k\ge0$ varying); $\mathrm{SM}(W)\le\mathrm{Morse}(W)$. Dimitroglou Rizell and Golovko proved $\#\mathrm{Fix}_0\ge\mathrm{SM}(M)$ for nondegenerate Hamiltonians when $[\omega]$ and $c_1$ vanish on $\pi_2(M)$. Does the stable Morse bound $\#\mathrm{Fix}_0(\phi_H^1;H)\ge\mathrm{SM}(M)$ hold for every nondegenerate Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of every closed symplectic manifold?
problems.posedBy: Recorded as Conjecture 1.2 in R. Golovko, On variants of Arnold conjecture, Arch. Math. (Brno) 56 (2020); background in Arnold (1986)
problems.ageNote: The stable formulation is cited from Golovko's 2020 survey of variants; Arnold (1986, Section 5) already compared stable and unstable critical-point minima.
problems.resultNote: Principal Theorem 1.1: a simply connected closed Kahler $M$ ($\dim_{\mathbb R}=1412$, $\mathrm{SM}=318968$) and a Hamiltonian with all 318952 fixed points nondegenerate and contractible. Mechanism: a Hamiltonian involution on $X\times Y$ whose fixed components carry Smale-minimal Morse functions, with mixed 2- and 3-primary torsion making $4\lambda(C)<\lambda(M)$; no Floer theory. Companions: in real dimension 22 the deficit is unbounded with ratio $\le127/128$; in dimension 3332 the count attains the cyclic integral Floer bound of Bai-Xu yet is 32 below $\mathrm{SM}$. Since $\mathrm{SM}\le\mathrm{Morse}$ these also refute the Morse-number form in the simply connected setting. The homological bounds remain intact.
problems.claimIssueNote: The release says: 'Ma [Theorem 1.5] asserted that the minimum number of fixed points over all Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms always equals Crit(M). Theorem 1.1 contradicts that assertion' (degenerate paper) and 'Ma's preprint asserts that the minimum number of fixed points of a nondegenerate Hamiltonian diffeomorphism always equals the ordinary Morse number ... Theorem 1.1 contradicts that unrestricted assertion' (Morse-number paper). The other side: R. Ma, Proofs on Arnold conjectures, arXiv 0808.0613v7 (2013), Theorem 1.5, claims these lower bounds hold in general. Ma's preprint is unpublished; no referee has ruled between them. The stable-Morse papers do not cite Ma; the conflict is by implication, since Morse(M) >= SM(M).

problems.name: Uniqueness of DiPerna-Lions renormalized solutions of the hard-sphere Boltzmann equation
problems.field: Kinetic theory; Boltzmann equation, weak solutions
problems.statement: DiPerna and Lions (1989) proved global existence and weak stability of renormalized solutions of the inhomogeneous Boltzmann equation $(\partial_t+v\cdot\nabla_x)F=Q(F,F)$ for any nonnegative initial density with finite mass, energy and entropy, $\int F_0(1+|v|^2+|\log F_0|)<\infty$; these bounds alone do not make the collision term locally integrable. Uniqueness is known only under much stronger control (Maxwellian upper bounds, perturbations of a Maxwellian in weighted Sobolev spaces), and for the spatially homogeneous hard-sphere equation. The uniqueness problem for general renormalized solutions is listed as open, for example in Silvestre's 2022 survey of open problems in kinetic equations, and Gismondi, Golding and Novack (2026) conjectured nonuniqueness. For the hard-sphere kernel on $\mathbb T^3\times\mathbb R^3$, are renormalized (entropy) solutions with finite mass, energy and entropy determined uniquely by their initial datum?
problems.posedBy: Open since the DiPerna-Lions existence theory (1989); cited by the manuscript as open in L. Silvestre, Regularity estimates and open problems in kinetic equations (2022, Section 2)
problems.ageNote: The manuscript does not quote a 1989 statement of the question; it cites Silvestre (2022) for the uniqueness problem and Gismondi-Golding-Novack (2026) for a conjecture of nonuniqueness for a dense class of data. 1989 is the date of the DiPerna-Lions theory that left uniqueness open.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1 (principal): there are $R<\infty$ and a nonnegative $F_0$ with $\mathrm{supp}_vF_0\subset B_R(0)$ and $\int F_0(1+|v|^2+|\log F_0|)<\infty$ on $\mathbb T^3\times\mathbb R^3$ admitting two global entropy solutions with exact local conservation of mass, momentum and kinetic energy, differing on a set of positive measure, both in $C([0,\infty);L^1)$, with $\int_0^T\int\langle v\rangle^k(Q^++Q^-)<\infty$ for all $T,k$. The companion (September 23) proves nonuniqueness in a class with local mass and total momentum conservation. The datum has unbounded amplitudes at shrinking spatial scales. It does not give nonuniqueness for a dense or generic set of data (the Gismondi-Golding-Novack conjecture), nor for other kernels, the whole space, or the Landau equation.

problems.name: C1 regularity of infinity-harmonic functions in dimension three and higher
problems.field: Nonlinear elliptic PDE: the infinity Laplacian
problems.statement: A continuous function $u$ is infinity-harmonic if it is a viscosity solution of $\Delta_\infty u=\sum_{i,j}u_iu_ju_{ij}=0$; by Jensen (1993) and Crandall-Evans-Gariepy (2001) these are the absolutely minimizing Lipschitz extensions studied by Aronsson (1967). Solutions are locally Lipschitz, but the equation controls second derivatives only in the gradient direction, and Aronsson's example $|x_1|^{4/3}-|x_2|^{4/3}$ shows the gradient is at best $C^{0,1/3}$. In the plane, Savin (2005) proved $u\in C^1$ and Evans and Savin (2008) proved $C^{1,\alpha}$; Evans and Smart (2011) proved differentiability at every point in every dimension, which does not give continuity of the gradient. In dimensions $d\ge3$, is every infinity-harmonic function continuously differentiable, with a Holder modulus for the gradient?
problems.posedBy: Open problem of the infinity-Laplacian regularity theory after Savin (2005), Evans and Savin (2008) and Evans and Smart (2011); the manuscript cites no explicit statement of the question
problems.ageNote: The manuscript presents the higher-dimensional case as open after the planar results of 2005 and 2008 and the everywhere-differentiability theorem of 2011, but quotes no source that poses it; poser and year are left blank rather than guessed.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for each $d\ge3$ there are $\alpha_d\in(0,1/3]$ and $C_d$ such that every bounded infinity-harmonic $u$ on $B_1\subset\mathbb R^d$ satisfies $\|\nabla u\|_{L^\infty(B_{1/2})}+[\nabla u]_{C^{0,\alpha_d}(B_{1/2})}\le C_d\,\mathrm{osc}_{B_1}u$; hence infinity-harmonic functions are $C^1_{loc}$ on every open set in $d\ge3$. The proof is by compactness, using the Evans-Savin anisotropic blow-up and a new Liouville theorem for the limiting equation. The exponent $\alpha_d$ is not explicit, and no claim is made about the optimal exponent $1/3$, boundary regularity or the planar endpoint.

problems.name: The Borel conjecture for closed aspherical four-manifolds (homeomorphism form)
problems.statement: A connected manifold is aspherical if its universal cover is contractible, so its fundamental group determines its homotopy type. In a letter to Serre of May 2, 1953, Borel asked whether compact manifolds that are classifying spaces for the same group are homeomorphic. The topological Borel conjecture asks, in every dimension, that every homotopy equivalence between closed aspherical manifolds be homotopic to a homeomorphism; the weaker homeomorphism-existence form asks only that homotopy-equivalent closed aspherical manifolds be homeomorphic. It holds in dimensions at most three, and in dimensions at least five for large classes of groups (Farrell-Jones, Bartels-Lück, including hyperbolic and CAT(0) groups). In dimension four it was known only with extra hypotheses such as a good fundamental group in Freedman's sense. Are homotopy-equivalent closed aspherical four-manifolds always homeomorphic?
problems.posedBy: Armand Borel
problems.ageNote: Borel's letter to Jean-Pierre Serre of May 2, 1953, cited by the manuscript via Ranicki's reproduction 'The birth of the Borel conjecture'.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there are closed connected aspherical topological four-manifolds $M$ and $N$, with the same word-hyperbolic fundamental group, that are homotopy equivalent but not homeomorphic. Theorem 1.2: some such $M$ has a self-homotopy equivalence not homotopic to any homeomorphism, so the prescribed-class form also fails. The examples come from Davis reflection applied to a Poincaré chamber whose odd cyclic covers have no manifold model. This disproves the Borel conjecture as an all-dimension statement and in dimension four specifically. Not shown: anything in dimensions five or higher, or smooth-category statements; it also shows that Khan's rigidity up to s-cobordism cannot be upgraded to homeomorphism for such groups (curator's reading of the introduction).

problems.name: The Kannan-Lovász-Simonovits conjecture
problems.statement: Let $K \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a convex body in isotropic position (barycenter at the origin, identity covariance). Kannan, Lovász and Simonovits conjectured that the isoperimetric inequality on $K$ is saturated, up to a universal constant, by half-spaces: $\mathrm{Vol}_{n-1}(\partial A \cap K) \ge c \min\{\mathrm{Vol}_n(A \cap K), \mathrm{Vol}_n(K \setminus A)\}$ with $c > 0$ independent of $n$ and $K$. Equivalent forms: exponential concentration of 1-Lipschitz functions with a dimension-free rate, or a Poincaré inequality with a universal constant, for every isotropic log-concave measure. Is the KLS constant bounded independently of the dimension?
problems.posedBy: Ravi Kannan, László Lovász and Miklós Simonovits (Discrete & Computational Geometry, 1995)
problems.resultNote: Claims the conjecture in full, for all isotropic log-concave measures: $C_P(\mu) \le C$ with $C$ universal. The route bounds the third cumulant, propagates the estimate to cumulants of every order by Eldan's stochastic localization, realizes derivatives of tilt averages as mixed cumulants through a suspension construction, and closes with the Song-Zhang criterion. The previous best bounds were Klartag's $C\sqrt{\log n}$ and Song and Zhang's $C \cdot 16^{\log^* n}$ (1 October 2026). Priority: Song and Zhang revised their preprint on 4 October 2026, the day this paper was posted, to claim the same $O(1)$ bound by their own route; the two are parallel claims of the same result. Consequences include the thin-shell and variance conjectures, already known to follow from KLS.
problems.aiRole: From the paper's acknowledgements: "Most proofs and mathematical ideas in this paper were found by ChatGPT; a notable exception is the idea to use suspension which was suggested by the authors. The role of the authors has been mostly to understand these proofs and improve their exposition." The suspension construction is the step that turns tilt-average derivatives into cumulants of a larger isotropic log-concave measure, so a named human idea carries part of the argument. The model version is not stated.

problems.name: Deterministic polynomial-time factorization of polynomials over prime fields
problems.statement: Berlekamp's algorithms (1967, 1970) reduce factoring $f\in\mathbb F_p[x]$ to finding separating elements of a quotient algebra, and randomized algorithms such as Cantor-Zassenhaus factor in expected time polynomial in $\deg f$ and $\log p$. Deterministically, Shoup's bound depends on $p^{1/2+o(1)}$; under GRH, Ronyai handled a bounded number of factors and Evdokimov obtained $(n^{\log n}\log p)^{O(1)}$, still quasipolynomial. Altman (2025) surveys the remaining obstacles. Is there a deterministic algorithm that completely factors every polynomial of degree $n$ over $\mathbb F_p$, with $p$ given in binary, in time polynomial in $n$ and $\log p$, without GRH?

Theorem 1.2 (proved here, unconditional) does this given small auxiliary primes $\ell\equiv1\pmod{12q}$ with $p$ not a $q$th power mod $\ell$; the odd-degree splitter uses Jacobians of cyclic curves $Y^q=F(X)$ and norm equations in cyclic algebras. Small auxiliary primes are deduced from a uniform zero-free strip $\mathrm{Re}\,s>1-10^{-6}$ for all finite-order Hecke L-functions over cyclotomic fields containing $\mu_{12}$, imported from the companion on primitive roots and not proved here. problems.name: Modularity of elliptic curves over imaginary quadratic fields
problems.field: Langlands program: modularity of elliptic curves
problems.statement: Let $K$ be an imaginary quadratic field and $E/K$ an elliptic curve. The Langlands program predicts that $E$ is modular: there is an automorphic representation $\pi_E$ of $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb A_K)$ (a Bianchi modular form when $E$ has no complex multiplication) whose Galois representations are $H^1_{et}(E_{\bar K},\bar{\mathbb Q}_l)$, so that $L(E/K,s)=L(\pi_E,s-1/2)$. Over $\mathbb Q$ this is the theorem of Wiles, Taylor-Wiles and Breuil-Conrad-Diamond-Taylor. Over imaginary quadratic fields, potential modularity was known (Allen et al., 2023), Allen-Khare-Thorne proved modularity for a positive proportion of curves, and Caraiani-Newton for all curves over fields where $X_0(15)(K)$ has rank zero. Is every elliptic curve over every imaginary quadratic field modular?
problems.posedBy: Robert P. Langlands, Problems in the theory of automorphic forms, LNM 170 (1970), Section 7, as the manuscript cites; studied computationally by Grunewald-Helling-Mennicke and Cremona
problems.ageNote: The manuscript places the conjecture in the Langlands program and cites Langlands (1970, Section 7) for the automorphy of representations attached to elliptic curves over number fields. It does not name a first statement specific to imaginary quadratic fields; Grunewald-Helling-Mennicke (1978) and Cremona developed the computational side.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every imaginary quadratic $K$ and every $E/K$ there is an isobaric automorphic representation $\pi_E$ of $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb A_K)$ with trivial central character and weight zero such that $r_\iota(\pi_E)\simeq H^1_{et}(E_{\bar K},\bar{\mathbb Q}_l)$ for every $l$ and $\iota$, with local-global compatibility at every finite place $v\nmid l$ and the expected parameter at the complex place; hence $L(E/K,s)=L(\pi_E,s-1/2)$. $\pi_E$ is cuspidal when $E$ has no CM. The method is a geometric prime switch: cyclic covers of a quadratic twist of $E$ give a chain of mod $p$, mod 3, mod $p$ congruences that carries automorphy from an auxiliary curve to $E$ through the Caraiani-Newton lifting theorem. It does not treat other CM fields or totally real fields.

problems.name: Construction of the two-dimensional O(3) nonlinear sigma model as an interacting continuum quantum field theory with a mass gap
problems.shortName: O(3) sigma model continuum limit with mass gap
problems.field: Constructive quantum field theory; asymptotically free sigma models
problems.statement: The two-dimensional $O(3)$ nonlinear sigma model is the lattice measure $\propto\exp(\beta\sum_{x\sim y}q_x\cdot q_y)\prod_x d\sigma(q_x)$ with $q_x\in S^2$. Perturbative renormalization (Polyakov 1975; Brezin-Zinn-Justin 1976) predicts asymptotic freedom: as $\beta\to\infty$ and the lattice spacing shrinks, a finite physical mass survives, and integrability (Zamolodchikov-Zamolodchikov; Hasenfratz-Maggiore-Niedermayer) describes the expected massive continuum theory. Rigorous constructions existed only for large $N$ (Kupiainen, Kopper), for a hierarchical model (Gawedzki-Kupiainen), or in perturbation theory (Mitter-Ramadas), with Balaban's program partial. Does the nearest-neighbour lattice $O(3)$ model have a continuum limit that satisfies the Osterwalder-Schrader axioms, is interacting (non-Gaussian), and has a positive mass gap?
problems.posedBy: Long-standing goal of constructive field theory; the manuscript frames it via Polyakov (1975), Brezin-Zinn-Justin (1976) and work of Kupiainen, Gawedzki-Kupiainen and Balaban, naming no single poser
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites no single source posing the construction as a problem. The perturbative prediction it would confirm dates from Polyakov (1975), so the question is at least that old; left null rather than guessed.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.2: along bare couplings $\beta_N=H+\frac{\log L}{2\pi}N+O(\log N)$ with spacing $L^{-N}$, suitably normalized smeared lattice spins converge in law and in all moments; the limiting Schwinger distributions are Euclidean and $O(3)$ invariant, reflection positive and clustering with factorial bounds, reconstruct a local relativistic theory in $1+1$ dimensions with a unique vacuum and a Hamiltonian gap $m>0$ on the whole vacuum complement, and have a nonzero connected four-point function, so the theory is not Gaussian. Theorem 1.1: normalized by susceptibility and second-moment length, the limit exists along every real $\beta\to\infty$ without subsequences. The companion proves an isolated one-particle mass atom in the spin two-point spectral measure. Not shown: the value of the mass, the S-matrix of the constructed theory, or a continuum construction for other $O(N)$.

problems.name: Artin's Primitive Root Conjecture: Infinitude for Every Admissible Base
problems.shortName: Artin's conjecture: infinitude for every base
problems.statement: Artin conjectured in 1927 that every integer $a\ne-1$ that is not a perfect square is a primitive root modulo infinitely many primes $p$, and more precisely that the number of such $p\le x$ is asymptotic to $A(a)\,x/\log x$ for an explicit constant $A(a)>0$. Hooley (1967) proved this under the generalized Riemann hypothesis for Kummer fields. Unconditionally, Gupta-Murty and Heath-Brown (1986) showed that at most two prime bases fail the infinitude assertion, so one of $2,3,5$ works, but no single prescribed base such as $a=2$ was known to be a primitive root for infinitely many primes. Is every admissible integer $a$ a primitive root modulo infinitely many primes, with the predicted density?
problems.posedBy: Emil Artin (1927), recorded in the Artin-Hasse correspondence and Hasse's diaries
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every integer $a$ that is neither $-1$ nor a square there are $c_a>0$ and $x_a$ such that for $x\ge x_a$ at least $c_a\,x/(\log x)^2$ primes $p\in(x,2x)$ have $a$ as a primitive root. This gives the infinitude part of Artin's conjecture for every admissible base, including $a=2$. It does not give the predicted asymptotic $A(a)\,x/\log x$: the count is short by a factor $\log x$ and constants depend on $a$. The analytic input is Theorem 1.2: for every cyclotomic field $F\supseteq\mu_{12}$ and every finite-order Hecke character $\eta$ of $F$, $L_F(s,\eta)$ has no zeros with $\mathrm{Re}\,s>1-10^{-6}$. The companion on simultaneous primitive roots gives the same lower bound for any finite set of prime bases, assuming four inputs from this paper.

problems.name: Thue–Morse: all three Joshi–Rust first-occurrence formulas
problems.field: Combinatorics on words; automatic sequences and arithmetic progressions
problems.statement: Let $t(j)$ be the parity of the binary digit sum of $j$, with indexing from zero. Let $A(d)$ be the greatest length of a monochromatic arithmetic progression of positive difference $d$ in $t$, and let $i(d)$ be the least starting index attaining $A(d)$. Joshi–Rust Conjecture 3.8 asks for the three first-occurrence identities: $i(2^n+1)=3\cdot 2^{2n}-2^n-1$ for $n\ge2$; $i(2^{2n}-1)=3\cdot 2^{4n}-2^{2n}+1$ for $n\ge1$; and $i(2^{2n+1}-1)=2^{2n+1}-1$ for $n\ge0$. The ranges are explicit: the first formula excludes $n=1$, where the previously recorded value is $i(3)=45$.
problems.posedBy: Gandhar Joshi and Dan Rust, Monochromatic arithmetic progressions in the Fibonacci, Thue–Morse, and Rudin–Shapiro words (2025), Conjecture 3.8; arXiv:2501.05830v2, DOI 10.1016/j.tcs.2025.115391.
problems.resultNote: All three displayed first-occurrence families are proved in the stated ranges. The proof also gives exact all-start classifications for the plus and even-minus families, and rederives their established maximal-length values without assuming those values as hypotheses. For $q=2^m, m≥2$, every length-$(q+2)$ progression at difference $q+1$ starts at $lq²−q−1$ with $l≥1$ and $t(l−1)=t(l+1)=1−t(l)$. For even $m≥2$, every length-$(q+4)$ progression at difference $q−1$ starts at $lq²−q+1$ with the same condition. Its least $l$ is $3$. For odd $m$, the earliest length-$q$ progression at difference $q−1$ starts at $q−1$. Global maximality and exclusion of every earlier start are included. The prior length results and block-recognition methods of Parshina and Aedo–Grimm–Nagai–Staynova are explicitly credited. This is the first-occurrence conjecture, distinct from the existing avoiding-population matching-height entry. Broader all-difference classifications are not claimed.

problems.name: Period-doubling prefix palindromic length is not 2-regular
problems.field: Combinatorics on words; automatic sequences and palindromic factorization
problems.statement: Let $u$ be the fixed point beginning with 0 of the substitution $0\to01$, $1\to00$ (the period-doubling word). Let $P(n)$ be the least number of nonempty palindromes whose concatenation is the length-$n$ prefix of $u$, with $P(0)=0$, and put $d(n)=P(n+1)-P(n)$. Frid, Laborde and Peltomäki conjectured that $d$ is not 2-automatic, and so $P$ is not 2-regular. Is that true?
problems.posedBy: Anna E. Frid, Enzo Laborde and Jarkko Peltomäki, On prefix palindromic length of automatic words (2020 preprint; TCS 2021), Conjecture 17 in arXiv v2 / published Conjecture 2.
problems.resultNote: The exact period-doubling conjecture is proved: d(n)=P(n+1)−P(n) is not 2-automatic and P is not 2-regular. The proof uses a marker C(n) recording a singleton 1 in some globally optimal factorization. A Gray-code independent-set bound gives nonnegative palindrome-edge slack. Uniform constructions and an all-path diagonal obstruction distinguish infinitely many binary prefixes for C. The sole computer-assisted lemma is an all-length local inclusion proved by complete reachable-state closure, independently implemented twice; finite value tests are not its proof. This does not provide a full closed formula for P or settle the separate Fibonacci conjecture. Classical palindrome structure, automatic-sequence closure and state distinguishability, and the source regularity/difference equivalence are credited. Worldwide priority remains unassessed.

problems.name: Pro-modularity at p = 2: odd absolutely irreducible 2-adic representations occur in the completed Hecke algebra (auxiliary tame level allowed)
problems.field: Completed Hecke algebras; p-adic Langlands for GL2 over Q
problems.statement: Let $\mathbb T_p(N)$ be the full varying-weight $p$-adic Hecke algebra of tame level $N$. Emerton (2011, Conjecture 2.12) records the expectation that every continuous odd two-dimensional $p$-adic representation of $G_{\mathbb Q}$ unramified outside finitely many primes occurs in such an algebra, with no Hodge-theoretic condition at $p$ and with tame level prescribed by the ramification. Earlier pro-modularity theorems (Skinner-Wiles, Emerton, Pan) need $p>2$ or residual restrictions. For $p=2$, does every continuous, odd, absolutely irreducible $r:G_{\mathbb Q}\to\mathrm{GL}_2(E)$ unramified outside finitely many primes occur in $\mathbb T_2(N)$ for some odd $N$?
problems.posedBy: Matthew Emerton, p-adic families of modular forms, Seminaire Bourbaki 2009/2010, Asterisque 339 (2011), Conjecture 2.12, as the manuscript cites

Scalar and reducible residual representations are allowed; no de Rham hypothesis. It is an occurrence result and does not assert classical modularity; the tame level may contain auxiliary primes, unlike Emerton's formulation.

problems.name: The 8/3-plus stability conjecture for power-free binary morphism lengths
problems.statement: Shallit, Shur and Zorcic ask for the phase transitions in admissible lengths of uniform binary morphisms preserving repetition avoidance. In Section 4 of Power-free complementary binary morphisms, they conjecture that the set of admissible lengths stays constant whenever $(8/3)^+\leq\alpha<3$, with another transition at the strict threshold $8/3$. Here a morphism is $\alpha$-free if it sends every $\alpha$-free binary input word to an $\alpha$-free output; the plus convention permits exponent exactly $8/3$. Does this length-set stability hold, and is the strict endpoint different?
problems.posedBy: Jeffrey Shallit, Arseny Shur and Stefan Zorcic, Power-free complementary binary morphisms, arXiv:2310.15064v3 (8 December 2023), Section 4; JCTA 207 (2024), 105910.
problems.resultNote: For every extended-real threshold $(8/3)^+\leq\alpha<3$, the admissible positive lengths of $\alpha$-free uniform binary morphisms are exactly all integers except $3$ and $6$. Every admitted length has a complementary witness, $h(1)=\overline{h(0)}$; the broader binary class has the same length set by the credited prior impossibility theorem. At the strict threshold $8/3$, length $5$ is impossible, whereas it is possible at $(8/3)^+$. The decisive bound for the prior endpoint family is $\operatorname{ce}(h(w))\leq\max(8/3,\operatorname{ce}(w))$ for every cubefree input. A length-12 seed covers the remaining doubling family through the established finite sufficient criterion. The proof includes finite and infinite admissible inputs with the stated critical-exponent convention. It does not classify every preserving morphism or settle all transitions in the lower interval $[(7/3)^+,8/3]$. Equal zero/one counts in one image are not assumed.
problems.aiRole: OpenAI Codex produced the central strengthening of the existing boundary-marker argument, the complete length coverage using a new fixed length-12 seed, and the strict length-five endpoint obstruction. It also wrote exact finite certificate programs. A separate AI review checked the uniform proof and independently implemented the seed/endpoint controls. The prior clipped Thue-Morse constructions, cubefreeness theorem, exceptional-length impossibility result and Kobayashi sufficient criterion are explicitly credited. No human expert endorsement is claimed.

problems.name: The global quantum geometric Langlands conjecture at irrational level
problems.statement: For a connected simple complex group $G$ with Langlands dual $G^\vee$, lacing number $r$ and a smooth projective curve $X$, let $D_c(\mathrm{Bun}_G(X))$ be the DG category of D-modules on the moduli stack of $G$-bundles twisted by the power of the determinant line corresponding to shifted level $c$. The quantum geometric Langlands conjecture, in Stoyanovsky's inverse-parameter form attributed to Drinfeld and developed in Gaitsgory's quantum Langlands program, predicts an equivalence $D_c(\mathrm{Bun}_G(X))\simeq D_{-1/(rc)}(\mathrm{Bun}_{G^\vee}(X))$ compatible with localization and Whittaker coefficients, deforming ordinary geometric Langlands. Does this equivalence hold for every level $c$, in particular for irrational $c$?

problems.name: Pointwise convergence of multiple ergodic averages for mixing transformations
problems.statement: Let $T$ be an invertible measure-preserving transformation of a probability space and $f_1,\dots,f_n$ bounded measurable functions. Since Furstenberg's ergodic proof of Szemeredi's theorem, the multiple ergodic averages $\frac1N\sum_{k=1}^N\prod_{j=1}^n f_j(T^{jk}x)$ have been central. Host-Kra and Ziegler proved convergence in $L^2$ for every $n$, but almost-everywhere convergence was known only for $n=2$ (Bourgain) and under extra structure for larger $n$: K-systems, weakly mixing systems with spectral or joining restrictions, and distal systems (Huang-Shao-Ye). The general pointwise question asks whether these averages converge almost everywhere for every $n$ and every system; it was open even for mixing $T$. Do the multiple ergodic averages converge almost everywhere for every finite length?
problems.posedBy: The pointwise convergence question for multiple ergodic averages, arising from Furstenberg's ergodic Szemeredi theorem; surveyed by Kuca (2026)
problems.ageNote: The manuscripts state the general pointwise question and cite Furstenberg (1977) for the averages and Kuca's survey for the questions, but name no original poser or date.
problems.resultNote: Claims Theorem 1.1: for every invertible mixing probability-preserving $T$ (no standardness, no mixing rate), every $n\ge2$ and bounded $f_1,\dots,f_n$, $\frac1N\sum_{k\le N}\prod_j f_j(T^{jk}x)\to\prod_j\int f_j$ almost everywhere along all $N$. Companions treat $n=3,4$ and three distinct nonzero slopes of either sign for mixing $T$. Lemma 2.5 of the principal manuscript also states almost-everywhere convergence of averages of at most three functions at distinct positive slopes on every standard system, derived from the companion's oscillation estimate. It does NOT settle the general question for $n\ge4$ on non-mixing systems, nor polynomial iterates.

problems.name: Recovery balance is preserved by duality
problems.field: Coding theory; random access in DNA storage
problems.statement: Conjecture 1 of Gruica, Bar-Lev, Ravagnani and Yaakobi asks whether a linear code is recovery balanced if and only if its orthogonal dual is recovery balanced. Here, encoded coordinates are read independently and uniformly with replacement; recovery balance means that the expected number of reads needed to recover a coordinate is the same for every coordinate.
problems.posedBy: Gruica, Bar-Lev, Ravagnani and Yaakobi, A Combinatorial Perspective on Random Access Efficiency for DNA Storage: arXiv v1 §VII (Jan 2024), Conj. 1 in v2; IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory (2025).
problems.resultNote: More strongly, for every encoded coordinate $i$ of a linear code $C$ of length $n\geq1$, $$a_i(C)+a_i(C^\perp)=n,$$ where $a_i$ is the expected number of independent uniform reads with replacement needed to recover that coordinate. Consequently, the recovery profile is constant for $C$ exactly when it is constant for $C^\perp$, proving the conjecture. The argument pairs complementary observation sets, writes expectations as weighted sums over sets, and uses equal complementary weights. A coordinate known to be zero has recovery time zero. The written note also handles the convention requiring one read for such a coordinate: balance equivalence remains valid, but the coordinatewise sum requires a correction. Nonuniform sampling is outside this identity.
problems.aiRole: OpenAI Codex (GPT-6 Astra) selected and investigated the conjecture, developed the complementary-recovery and sampling argument, wrote the mathematical proof, implemented the Lean formalization and evidence checker, and prepared the exposition. The human collaborator directed the research, questioned scope and interpretation, and reviewed the presentation. The Lean build and axiom checks ran in bounded Azure jobs. This disclosure does not claim an independent human proof audit.
problems.verificationNote:
Read by this site on 6 October 2026, not rebuilt. Fifteen Lean files with mathlib, Lean 4.34.0; no sorry, admit, axiom declarations, native_decide, opaque, unsafe or implemented_by. The headline theorem codeRecoveryBalanced_dual_iff holds over any field; codeDual is the actual orthogonal complement, recovery is proved equivalent to the paper's column-in-span condition, and the expected number of reads is the correct tail sum. The repository's axiom log lists only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. At that review, only author-provided build logs were available. A separate exact-arithmetic check written here on 68 random codes over GF(2), GF(3) and GF(5) of length up to 7 confirmed a_i(C) + a_i(C^perp) = n in every case. No independent expert has audited the formal statement.

Author update: the linked public GitHub Actions run rebuilt all 13 positive modules from commit 80e4dbf, rejected 2 false controls, and printed the final theorem's axioms: propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Permanent compiler records and source hashes are in the repository. This does not replace an independent expert audit.

problems.name: Worst-case Subset Sum in time 2^((1/2 - c)n)
problems.statement: Given positive integers $a_1,\dots,a_n$ and a target $t$, Subset Sum asks whether some subset of the $a_i$ sums to $t$. The meet-in-the-middle algorithm of Horowitz and Sahni (1974) solves it in time $2^{n/2}\cdot\mathrm{poly}$, and Schroeppel and Shamir (1981) kept that time with space $2^{n/4}$. Later work saved only polynomial factors in the worst case (Chen, Jin, Randolph and Servedio, 2023, time $2^{n/2}/n^{\delta}$), while representation methods beat $2^{n/2}$ only on random instances. Is there an algorithm for worst-case $n$-input Subset Sum running in time $2^{(1/2-c)n}$ for some constant $c>0$?
problems.posedBy: Standing open question of exact exponential algorithms since Horowitz and Sahni (1974); stated as 'a major goal' by Chen, Jin, Randolph and Servedio (2023)
problems.ageNote: The 2^(n/2) barrier dates from Horowitz and Sahni (J. ACM 1974), cited by the manuscript. The manuscript cites no paper that first poses the question; Chen, Jin, Randolph and Servedio (APPROX/RANDOM 2023, cited) call it a major goal of the area in their abstract. Year left blank rather than guessed.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: a uniform randomized word-RAM algorithm decides Subset Sum with error at most 1/3 on every input and runs in worst-case time $O(2^{0.49n})$ for every fixed polynomial bound on input bit length, the time bound holding on every random execution. The method combines isolation, a random prime modulus, a filtered Fourier checksum and alias extraction. It is not deterministic, it does not treat super-polynomial bit lengths, and it does not improve the space bound. The companion manuscript separately gives one-sided error, time $\mathrm{poly}(n)2^{n/2}$ and space $O(2^{n/5})$.

The principal manuscript is dated October 4, 2026; the low-space companion (September 26, 2026) is an earlier, separate result at the 2^(n/2) time scale.

problems.name: Singular Bernoulli convolutions at non-Pisot parameters
problems.field: Fractal geometry and harmonic analysis: Bernoulli convolutions
problems.statement: For $0<\lambda<1$ the Bernoulli convolution $\nu_\lambda$ is the law of $\sum_{n\ge0}\pm\lambda^n$ with independent fair signs; it is either singular or absolutely continuous (Jessen-Wintner). It is singular for $\lambda<1/2$, and Erdos (1939) proved it singular whenever $1/\lambda$ is a Pisot number. Salem (1943) showed the Fourier transform tends to zero for every other $\lambda$, so Fourier nondecay cannot detect singularity there. Solomyak proved absolute continuity for almost every $\lambda\in(1/2,1)$ and Shmerkin showed the exceptional set has Hausdorff dimension zero, but no singular example was known with $1/\lambda$ not Pisot, for instance a Salem number. Is there $\lambda\in(1/2,1)$ with $1/\lambda$ not a Pisot number for which $\nu_\lambda$ is singular?
problems.posedBy: Recorded as open by Baker, Koivusalo, Troscheit and Zhang (J. London Math. Soc. 2026) and Kern and Sterk (arXiv:2608.14155, 2026), as cited; background Erdos (1939) and Salem (1943)
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites two 2026 papers as recording the existence question open and traces the background to Erdos (1939), Salem (1943), Garsia (1962) and the Peres-Schlag-Solomyak survey (2000), but does not say who first asked it or when, so no year is given.
problems.resultNote:
Two non-Pisot singularity theorems. If $ eta\in(1,2)$ is a Salem number of degree four then $
u_{1/ eta}$ is singular; explicit cases are the real roots of $x^4-x^3-x^2-x+1$ and $x^4-2x^3+x^2-2x+1$. An explicit degree-31 polynomial has a unique real root $ eta\in(1.8392,1.8393)$, not Pisot, with $
u_{1/ eta}$ singular. The manuscript also proves a criterion: $
u_\lambda$ is singular iff $\lambda$ lies in an explicit limsup set of one-sided approximations by finite sets of algebraic units; the paper says this is an infinite approximation condition, not a finite membership test, so it is not an effective classification. It does not decide Salem numbers of degree six or more, nor which non-Pisot parameters are singular in general.

This result is not among the README's stated exceptions (the Riemann zeta zero-free region work and the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties). The manuscript is credited to OpenAI alone and names no human author. The README also cautions that unformalized results could have issues.

problems.name: The effective Iitaka fibration conjecture
problems.statement: For a smooth projective variety $X$ with Kodaira dimension $\kappa(X)\ge0$, the pluricanonical systems $|mK_X|$ define the Iitaka fibration for all sufficiently large divisible $m$. For varieties of general type, Hacon-McKernan, Takayama and Tsuji found one $m$ depending only on $\dim X$; Birkar and Zhang proved an effective bound that also depends on invariants of the general fibre. Is there, for each $d$, an integer $m(d)$ such that $|m(d)K_X|$ defines the Iitaka fibration of every smooth projective $d$-fold with $\kappa(X)\ge0$?
problems.posedBy: Stated as Conjecture 1.1 by C. Birkar and D.-Q. Zhang, Effectivity of Iitaka fibrations and pluricanonical systems of polarized pairs (Publ. Math. IHES, 2016)
problems.ageNote: The question predates the 2016 statement: Fujino-Mori (2000) and Viehweg-Zhang (2009) proved cases, as the manuscript recounts.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for each $d\ge1$ there is $m(d)>0$ such that, over every algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, $|m(d)K_X|$ is nonempty and its section ratios generate the Iitaka function field for every smooth integral projective $d$-fold with $\kappa(X)\ge0$; every multiple of $m(d)$ works too. Theorem 1.2 gives a uniform $a(d,\Phi)$ with $a(K_X+B)\sim0$ for projective lc pairs with $K_X+B\sim_{\mathbb Q}0$ and coefficients in a DCC set $\Phi$. The bound $m(d)$ is existential; no explicit value is given.

problems.name: The sharp exponential singularity rate of symmetric random sign matrices: P(det A_n = 0) = (1/2 + o(1))^n
problems.shortName: Sharp singularity rate of symmetric sign matrices
problems.field: Random matrix theory; discrete random matrices
problems.statement: Let $A_n$ be a symmetric $n\times n$ matrix whose entries on and above the diagonal are independent uniform signs. Two rows agree with probability about $2^{-n}$, so $\Pr(\det A_n=0)\ge2^{-n+o(n)}$, and it is generally believed that $\Pr(\det A_n=0)=\Theta(n^22^{-n})$, mirroring the non-symmetric case where Tikhomirov proved the rate $(1/2+o(1))^n$. Symmetry destroys row independence: Costello, Tao and Vu proved $\Pr(\det A_n=0)\to0$, followed by polynomial and stretched-exponential bounds and the exponential bound $e^{-cn}$ of Campos, Jenssen, Michelen and Sahasrabudhe. Is the singularity probability of a symmetric random sign matrix $(1/2+o(1))^n$, i.e. governed by two equal rows at exponential scale?
problems.posedBy: Kevin Costello, Terence Tao and Van Vu, and Van Vu in later surveys (as the belief that the probability is of order n^2 2^{-n})
problems.ageNote: The OpenAI manuscripts cite no posing source. Campos-Jenssen-Michelen-Sahasrabudhe (arXiv 2105.11384, 2021) write that it is 'generally believed' that the probability is $\Theta(n^22^{-n})$, citing Costello-Tao-Vu (Duke 2006) and two Vu surveys; 2006 is that earliest cited source.
problems.resultNote: Principal theorem: for symmetric $A_n$ with independent uniform signs on and above the diagonal, $\Pr(\det A_n=0)=(1/2+o(1))^n=2^{-n+o(n)}$, via a Schur-complement reduction to symmetric 0/1 matrices, a corank-one reduction and a counting argument for admissible appended columns. Companion: for fixed bias $p\in(0,1)\setminus\{1/2\}$, the rate is $p^2+(1-p)^2$, attained by two agreeing rows. Not shown: the believed $\Theta(n^22^{-n})$ asymptotic, uniformity in $p$, or general entry distributions.

problems.name: The Lazić-Peternell Generalised Abundance Conjecture for projective klt pairs
problems.statement: Let $(X,B)$ be a projective klt pair with $K_X+B$ pseudo-effective, and let $L$ be a nef Cartier divisor such that $K_X+B+L$ is nef. Lazic and Peternell conjectured that $K_X+B+L$ is numerically equivalent to a semiample $\mathbb Q$-divisor (numerical equivalence is needed: a nontorsion degree-zero line bundle on an elliptic curve is nef with no sections). They proved it for surfaces and for threefolds where $K_X+B$ has positive numerical dimension, and reduced it in general to the minimal model program, abundance and a semiampleness conjecture on Calabi-Yau pairs. Is $K_X+B+L$ always numerically equivalent to a semiample divisor?
problems.posedBy: Vladimir Lazić and Thomas Peternell (On Generalised Abundance, I)
problems.ageNote: arXiv 1808.00438 (2018), published Publ. RIMS 56 (2020); the manuscript cites the arXiv v2 numbering.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for a projective klt $\mathbb Q$-pair $(X,B)$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero with $K_X+B$ pseudo-effective and $M$ nef $\mathbb Q$-Cartier on $X$, if $K_X+B+M$ is nef then it is numerically equivalent to a semiample $\mathbb Q$-Cartier divisor. Corollary: on a klt pair with $K_X+B\equiv0$ every nef $\mathbb Q$-Cartier divisor is numerically semiample. New ingredient: a nef divisor of full nef dimension on a klt Calabi-Yau pair is big. Kahler companion: for smooth compact Kahler $X$, snc $B$ with coefficients below one and nef $M$, $c_1(K_X+B+M)$ is represented in Bott-Chern cohomology by a semiample line bundle. Not shown: semiampleness of $K_X+B+M$ itself, lc pairs, or nef data living only on a higher model.

problems.name: The matrix multiplication exponent: is omega at most 9/4?
problems.field: Algebraic complexity, bilinear and tensor methods
problems.statement: The exponent $\omega$ of matrix multiplication over $\mathbb C$ is the infimum of the $\tau$ such that, for every $\varepsilon>0$, two $n\times n$ matrices can be multiplied with $O_\varepsilon(n^{\tau+\varepsilon})$ arithmetic operations. Strassen's 1969 algorithm gave $\omega\le\log_2 7<2.81$, and the laser method of Strassen, Coppersmith-Winograd and their successors (Stothers, Vassilevska Williams, Le Gall, Alman-Vassilevska Williams, Duan-Wu-Zhou and others) brought the bound down to $\omega<2.371177$ (Dupont et al., 2026). The trivial lower bound is $\omega\ge2$, and whether $\omega=2$ is a central open question of algebraic complexity. The related dual exponent $\alpha$, the largest $k$ for which $n\times n^k$ by $n^k\times n$ products take $n^{2+o(1)}$ operations, was known to satisfy $\alpha\ge0.321334$. How small can the upper bound on $\omega$ be made?
problems.posedBy: Volker Strassen, Gaussian elimination is not optimal (Numerische Mathematik, 1969), which introduced subcubic matrix multiplication and the exponent question
problems.ageNote: The exponent is a tracked open constant rather than a single stated conjecture; the manuscripts give the chain of records from Strassen (1969) to Dupont et al. (2026, omega < 2.371177) as the prior state.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every $\varepsilon>0$ two complex $n\times n$ matrices can be multiplied with $O_\varepsilon(n^{9/4+\varepsilon})$ arithmetic operations, so $\omega\le9/4$ over $\mathbb C$. The companions prove $\alpha>0.465$ over every field of characteristic zero, $\omega(1,0.709,1)<2.092$, $\omega<2.258$ over all fields outside one uncomputed finite set of positive characteristics, and $\omega<2.371054886006746$ over every field. Not shown: anything about $\omega=2$, bit complexity, or a practical crossover size; the 9/4 proof gives no competitive finite matrix size and its transfer to positive characteristic is not claimed.
problems.aiRole: Produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model as part of an OpenAI evaluation on open research problems. The release README says the vast majority of results used one fixed procedure, averaging about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result; this family is not among the README's stated exceptions (the Riemann zeta zero-free region work and the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties). The manuscripts are authored as OpenAI with no human author named. The README also cautions that unformalized results could have issues. The 9/4 bound is the October 2 manuscript; two September 24 companions in the same family give the weaker square bound omega < 2.258 with alpha > 0.465 and a rectangular bound (with Python certificate checks), and omega < 2.371054886006746 over every field including positive characteristic. All three main bounds have Lean formalizations in the release.
problems.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: the abstract, introduction and Theorem 1.1 of 'An Upper Bound of 9/4 for the Matrix Multiplication Exponent', read against the exponent as usually defined (arithmetic operations over C, epsilon slack). The proof (a separation inequality for tensors sharing one leg, polynomial-multiplication inequalities and Strassen's asymptotic spectrum) was not refereed. problems.name: Two-size Gasoline: the tight approximation guarantee for iterative rounding
problems.field: Approximation algorithms; inventory and buffer scheduling
problems.statement: For a Gasoline instance with deliveries $x_i\in\{1,K\}$, fixed positive integer demands $y_i$, equal list lengths and equal total supply and demand, does the position-first Iterative Rounding algorithm always return a schedule using at most twice the minimum storage capacity? At each position it tries each remaining delivery, solves the fractional assignment LP with the chosen prefix fixed, and takes a minimum-score candidate. Capacity includes every delivery peak and consumption trough, with a freely chosen initial stock. This is Conjecture 3.1.1 of Lorieau (2024), the $\{1,K\}$ case of Rajkovic's conjecture for the one-dimensional problem.
problems.posedBy: Lucas Lorieau, Iterative Rounding algorithms for the Extended Gasoline Problem (2024), Conjecture 3.1.1, p. 21; algorithm due to Rajkovic (2022).
problems.resultNote: For every integer $K\ge2$, deliveries in $\{1,K\}$ and positive integer demands, we prove $C_{\mathrm{IR}}\le L_{\mathrm{init}}+K-2\le\mathrm{OPT}+K-2$, where $L_{\mathrm{init}}$ is the initial fractional assignment-LP optimum. The upper bound permits every exact tie choice. For every $K\ge3$, an explicit family with $2K-3$ days has $L_{\mathrm{init}}=\mathrm{OPT}=K$ and $C_{\mathrm{IR}}=2K-2$ under original-index tie breaking. Hence the exact worst-case ratio for that rule is $2-2/K$, with uniform supremum $2$; the algorithm is optimal when $K=2$. The proof also yields an implementation using O(n) arithmetic operations instead of repeated LP solves. This settles the stated two-size positive-integer case, not the unrestricted one-dimensional or multidimensional conjectures. An additional exact finite example shows that preferring the smaller delivery on ties need not be optimal (capacity 7 versus 5); no improved universal guarantee for that alternative rule is claimed.

problems.name: Harmonic norms on quiver representations without spherical completeness (Haiden-Katzarkov-Kontsevich-Pandit Question 6.24)
problems.statement: Haiden, Katzarkov, Kontsevich and Pandit (Towards Categorical Kähler Geometry, arXiv:2609.00978, Theorem 6.23) prove that over a spherically complete non-archimedean field $K$, a polystable finite-dimensional representation of a finite quiver admits a harmonic norm, and a representation admitting one is semistable. Their Question 6.24 asks: can the spherical completeness assumption on $K$ be omitted in Theorem 6.23?
problems.posedBy: Fabian Haiden, Ludmil Katzarkov, Maxim Kontsevich and Pranav Pandit, Towards Categorical Kähler Geometry (arXiv:2609.00978, September 2026), Question 6.24
problems.resultNote: Yes, for finite quivers: over any complete non-archimedean field, every polystable finite-dimensional representation admits a split harmonic norm, and a representation admitting a harmonic norm is semistable, so both implications of Theorem 6.23 hold without spherical completeness. The norm produced is split (diagonalisable), which is the natural form here, since without spherical completeness norms need not diagonalise.

problems.name: Zhi-Hong Sun's Conjecture 3.7: two Apéry-like sums at discriminant -20
problems.field: Supercongruences, modular forms and elliptic curves
problems.statement:
Let $f_n=\sum_{j=0}^n\binom{n}{j}^3$, $a_n=\sum_{j=0}^n\binom{n}{j}^2\binom{2j}{j}$, $Q_n=\sum_{j=0}^n\binom{n}{j}(-8)^{n-j}f_j$ and $\varepsilon_p=(-1)^{(p-1)/2}$. For every prime $p\ne2,5$, is it true that
$$\varepsilon_p\sum_{n=0}^{p-1}\frac{\binom{2n}{n}a_n}{20^n}\equiv\varepsilon_p\sum_{n=0}^{p-1}\frac{\binom{2n}{n}Q_n}{(-16)^n}\equiv\begin{cases}4x^2-2p,&p=x^2+5y^2,\ p\equiv1,9\pmod{20},\\2x^2-2p,&2p=x^2+5y^2,\ p\equiv3,7\pmod{20},\\0,&p\equiv11,13,17,19\pmod{20}\end{cases}\pmod{p^2}?$$
Here $x,y$ are integers in the representation cases. This is Conjecture 3.7 of Zhi-Hong Sun, AIMS Mathematics 7(2) (2022), p. 2742, published online on 18 November 2021.
problems.posedBy: Zhi-Hong Sun, Conjecture 3.7, AIMS Mathematics 7(2) (2022), p. 2742; DOI 10.3934/math.2022153. Published online 18 November 2021.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1 claims the complete conjecture: both signed sums, every prime except 2 and 5, all representation classes, and modulus p squared. Split primes use two modular periods, an integral Hecke polynomial and separate finite specializations, including the degree-p endpoint and nonprincipal CM sign. For inert primes, a degree-five endomorphism with square [-5] forces Hasse vanishing, then a differential invariant lifts each original sum. The prime 3 is checked directly. The paper credits Sun's mod-p and Legendre antecedents, Straub's coefficient congruence and Beukers's framework. The stronger Sun-Ye quartic congruence concerns an auxiliary sum; the available finite transports alone have only mod-p precision. No uniform mod-p-cubed equality is claimed: at p=7 the unsigned target sums are 192 and 290 modulo 343.

problems.name: Mean and variance of finite 2-adic complexity (Question 3.1)
problems.field: Finite 2-adic complexity, rational approximation and probability
problems.statement: For a uniformly random binary string of length $N\ge1$, identified with $r\in\{0,\ldots,2^N-1\}$, let $R_N(r)=\min\{\max(|a|,b):a,b\in\mathbb Z,\ a\equiv rb\pmod{2^N},\ b>0\text{ odd}\}$ and let $L_N=\log_2 R_N(r)$, without rounding. Prove $\mathbb E[L_N]\le N/2$ and compute $\operatorname{Var}(L_N)$. This is Question 3.1 of Lin, Xiao and Chen (2026). The probability space includes all length-N binary strings, including zero.
problems.posedBy: Hezheng Lin, Lingmei Xiao and Zhixiong Chen, Question 3.1, AIMS Mathematics 11(7) (2026), p.20282, DOI 10.3934/math.2026823.
problems.resultNote: The manuscript claims both requested results: the exact mean upper bound for every N>=1 and an explicit finite arithmetic-logarithmic variance formula obtained from the complete distribution. It also evaluates the limiting variance as 0.892302571204274625294755... . The all-length mean proof combines a written lattice argument with exact finite certificates. The variance and asymptotic arguments use finite counting, marked-lattice equidistribution and uniform integrability. The limiting geometric law is explicitly credited to Boca-Gologan. The finite answer is a sum, not a short elementary expression in N; no convergence rate or raw-height variance theorem is claimed.

problems.field: Supercongruences, Apéry-like sequences and modular forms
problems.statement:
Let $f_n=\sum_{j=0}^n\binom{n}{j}^3$ and $Q_n=\sum_{k=0}^n\binom{n}{k}(-8)^{n-k}f_k$. Is it true that, for every odd prime $p$,

problems.name: Vinogradov's least quadratic nonresidue conjecture
problems.statement: For an odd prime $p$, let $n(p)$ be the least positive integer that is a quadratic nonresidue modulo $p$. Unconditionally, the best bounds (Burgess with Vinogradov's trick) give $n(p)\ll_\varepsilon p^{1/(4\sqrt e)+\varepsilon}$, while the generalized Riemann hypothesis gives $n(p)\ll(\log p)^2$. Vinogradov conjectured that $n(p)\ll_\delta p^\delta$ for every $\delta>0$. Is it true that for every $\delta>0$ the least quadratic nonresidue satisfies $n(p)\ll_\delta p^\delta$?
problems.posedBy: I. M. Vinogradov, as stated in Tao, The Elliott-Halberstam conjecture implies the Vinogradov least quadratic nonresidue conjecture (2015), Conjecture 1.1
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites the conjecture only through Tao (2015, Conjecture 1.1) and gives no date for Vinogradov's original formulation, which is usually placed around 1918-1919. yearPosed is left blank.
problems.resultNote: Claims absolute constants $A,C>0$ with $n(p)\le C(\log p)^A$ for every odd prime $p$, hence $n(p)\ll_\delta p^\delta$ for every $\delta>0$. This is a polylogarithmic bound, much stronger than the conjecture asks, though weaker than the $(\log p)^2$ that GRH gives. The same corollary gives a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm for square roots modulo a prime. The proof is conditional on nothing beyond the family's own zero-free half-plane $\Re s>7/8$ and the published theorem of Bhargava, Ivanyos, Mittal and Saxena; it is not an independent argument.

The manuscripts are credited to OpenAI with no human author named. The nonresidue bound is a corollary in the 7/8 manuscript, derived from the zero-free half-plane through a published theorem of Bhargava, Ivanyos, Mittal and Saxena.

problems.name: The Landau-Siegel zero problem: a uniform logarithmic gap for real zeros of real Dirichlet L-functions
problems.statement: For a primitive Dirichlet character $\chi$ of conductor $q$, the classical zero-free region $\Re s\ge1-c_1/\log(q(|\Im s|+2))$ holds with one possible exception: a single simple real zero $\beta$ attached to a real character, which could lie very close to $1$. Siegel's theorem (1935) gives $L(1,\chi)\gg_\varepsilon q^{-\varepsilon}$ only ineffectively, and Page's theorem limits such zeros to at most one per range of conductors, so a sequence of real zeros with $(1-\beta)\log q\to0$ is not ruled out. In its logarithmic formulation the Landau-Siegel zero problem asks: is there an absolute constant $c>0$ such that every real zero $\beta\in(0,1)$ of every primitive nonprincipal real Dirichlet $L$-function of conductor $q\ge3$ satisfies $(1-\beta)\log q\ge c$?
problems.posedBy: Classical exceptional-zero problem going back to Landau, Page and Siegel; logarithmic zero-gap conjecture as discussed by Friedlander and Iwaniec (2018)
problems.ageNote: The manuscript names no single poser. The problem is at least as old as 1935; yearPosed is left blank.
problems.resultNote: Claims an absolute constant $c>0$ such that every real zero $\beta\in(0,1)$ of every primitive nonprincipal real Dirichlet $L$-function of conductor $q\ge3$ satisfies $(1-\beta)\log q\ge c$. The proof combines a prime-bias estimate forced by a zero close to $1$ with an interpolation determinant on a biquadratic field $\mathbb Q(\sqrt d,\sqrt2)$. The constant is not made explicit, so the result does not by itself give effective class-number bounds with numbers attached. It excludes real zeros in $1-c/\log q<\beta<1$ only; zeros elsewhere in $(0,1)$ are not addressed by this manuscript (the family's 7/8 manuscript excludes those above $7/8$).

problems.name: The Pinwheel Kernel Conjecture: a six-task counterexample
problems.statement: A pinwheel instance is a sorted tuple of positive integers $A=(a_1,\ldots,a_k)$. A feasible schedule performs one task per integer time slot, with task $i$ appearing in every block of $a_i$ consecutive slots. The Kernel Conjecture asks whether every feasible $A$ dominates a feasible sorted instance $B=(b_1,\ldots,b_k)$ with $b_i\le a_i$ for every $i$ and $b_k\le 2^{k-1}$ (Conjecture 2.3 of Gąsieniec, Smith and Wild).
problems.posedBy: Leszek Gąsieniec, Benjamin Smith and Sebastian Wild, Towards the 5/6-Density Conjecture of Pinwheel Scheduling, Conjecture 2.3 (2021 preprint; ALENEX 2022).
problems.resultNote:
The instance $(3,4,5,20,22,36)$ is feasible, but $(3,4,5,20,22,32)$ is not. More strongly, $(3,4,5,20,22,b)$ is feasible exactly when $b\ge36$.

A 36-slot periodic witness proves feasibility. A forward-closed certificate for period 35 has 56,284 states and 107,847 legal transitions, with a natural-number rank decreasing at every step. This excludes all infinite schedules, including nonperiodic ones. Monotonicity rules out every dominated six-task instance with all periods at most $2^{6-1}=32$, refuting the original Kernel Conjecture. A separate certificate checks period 32.

The result shows that any universal six-task cap must be at least 36, not that 36 suffices universally. In practice, truncating deadlines to 32 can turn a schedulable input into an infeasible one: this preprocessing rule is unsound. The example also supplies a certified regression test for scheduling solvers.
problems.aiRole: Under human direction, Codex selected and investigated the conjecture, implemented finite-state searches, found the counterexample, sharpened the sixth-period threshold to 36, generated finite certificates, wrote a separate Python checker, and developed the Lean formalization from the infinite-schedule definition to the final theorem. The human set the research objective, supervised the workflow, requested prior-work searches and formal verification, and required review before publication. No independent human mathematical verification is claimed.
problems.verificationNote: Re-checked by this site on 4 October 2026 with an independent checker written from scratch (reachable age-state search with dead-state pruning, not the repository's code): (3,4,5,20,22,b) is infeasible for b = 30 to 35 and feasible for b >= 36, with state counts equal to the repository's (50,881 at b = 32, 56,284 at b = 35). The repository's check_counterexample.py also passed. The Lean development (260 modules, core Lean only, Lean 4.34.1) was searched and has no sorry, admit, axiom declarations, native_decide, opaque or unsafe; its log records only propext and Quot.sound. The site did not rebuild it, and the repository has no CI; the Azure and Nanoda logs are the author's. Statement fidelity to Conjecture 2.3 was checked by hand: ScheduleOK quantifies over all infinite schedules, and the formal claim drops sortedness, which makes it slightly stronger.

problems.name: Maximum number of pairwise equidistant lines in $\mathbb{R}^3$
problems.statement: Is seven the maximum cardinality of a family of affine lines in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with a common positive pairwise distance? Equivalently, can eight congruent infinite circular cylinders with pairwise disjoint interiors touch pairwise?
problems.posedBy: J. E. Littlewood, Some Problems in Real and Complex Analysis (1968), Problem 7, p. 20; the maximum was framed by Bezdek (2005)
problems.ageNote: Littlewood asked in 1968 whether seven unit cylinders can touch pairwise; Bozoki, Lee and Ronyai built seven in 2015. The maximum was open from at least Bezdek's 2005 upper bound of 24, later 18, 10 and 9 (Hofer, June 2026).
problems.resultNote: It is proved that no eight affine lines in $\mathbb{R}^3$ have a common positive pairwise distance. Together with the known construction of seven such lines by Bozóki, Lee and Rónyai, this establishes the exact maximum of seven. The upper bound combines a five-line obstruction from hyperbola secants with exact verification over 135 uniform rank-three oriented-matroid types. It settles the full stated maximum-cardinality question; it does not classify all seven-line configurations or address cylinders of unequal radii.
problems.aiRole: This work was developed through continuous collaboration between the author and AI models. OpenAI and Anthropic models contributed to proof development, exact computation, literature research, manuscript preparation and review.
problems.verificationNote: Rebuilt by this site on 6 October 2026. The Lean development added on 4 October (commit 065e5e2; Lean 4.32.1 with mathlib, about 6,760 lines) was built from a clean clone with no warnings, passed a fresh leanchecker kernel replay, and #print axioms gives only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound for thm_1_1 and cor_1_2_upper. No sorry, axiom declarations, native_decide or implemented_by; finite steps use decide +kernel. The statement was read: no eight affine lines in R^3 have pairwise distance 1, with lines as affine subspaces of one-dimensional direction and distance the infimum of explicit Euclidean point distances; the corollary covers any n >= 8 and any d > 0. No general-position, non-parallel or catalogue hypothesis. The proof formalises the parallel and coplanar direction lemma, the four-line circuit condition and the five-line obstruction, and replaces Finschi's catalogue with a self-contained kernel-checked enumeration. Separately, on 4 October the Python verifier at 9c37327 was re-run here and passed (135 classes, 1,027 metric certificates). Not formalised: the seven-line construction of Bozoki, Lee and Ronyai, which is published. The statement audit is this site's alone.

Above Kuperberg's six-cylinder conjecture at 20, a younger and narrower cylinder question, and below conjectures famous across a whole community at about 30. Scored as the maximum question, not the 1968 existence question, which was settled in 2015.

problems.name: Bras-Amorós genus-monotonicity conjecture
problems.statement: Let $n_g$ be the number of numerical semigroups of genus $g$, where a numerical semigroup is an additive submonoid of $\mathbb{N}_0$ with finite complement and its genus is the size of that complement. Is $n_{g+1}\ge n_g$ for every integer $g\ge0$?
problems.posedBy: Maria Bras-Amoros (Semigroup Forum 76, 2008) as a weak form of her Fibonacci-like conjecture; stated as Conjecture 2 in Nathan Kaplan, Counting numerical semigroups, Amer. Math. Monthly 124 (2017)
problems.resultNote: It is proved that $n_{g+1}\ge n_g$ for every $g\ge0$, without restrictions on multiplicity or conductor. A partial injection leaves a specified family of source semigroups; unused targets are then shown to be numerous enough to cover it. Exact transfer computations bound relaxed source counts for $1\le g\le836$, and generating-function estimates handle $g\ge837$. This is not an enumeration of all numerical semigroups through genus 836. The stronger Fibonacci inequality $n_{g+1}\ge n_g+n_{g-1}$ and fixed-multiplicity monotonicity are not proved.
problems.aiRole: This work was developed through continuous collaboration between the author and AI models. GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI) and Fable 5.1 (Anthropic) contributed to proof development and checking, exact computation, literature research, and preparation and review of the manuscript. The author takes full responsibility for all mathematical results and the contents of this manuscript.
problems.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked by this site on 7 October 2026: the statement matches Conjecture 2 of Kaplan's survey (arXiv 1707.02551), which also says the weak form was open and that Zhai's asymptotics leave only finitely many genera to settle. From a fresh clone at commit b1b6fb8, all five shipped checkers passed: capacity recurrences through degree 1500, the omitted-pivot multiplier below 0.221715, the guarded mass assembly, the analytic join (comparison fails at genus 836, holds from 837), and all 836 finite rows with nonnegative slack (smallest 1, at genera 1 and 2). A separate enumeration written here of all numerical semigroups through genus 23 reproduced the known counts and confirmed that each certified slack is at most the true difference $n_{g+1}-n_g$ for $g\le 22$. These are arithmetic checks only. The coefficient arrays were not regenerated from the C++ sources, and the combinatorial and analytic arguments that connect them to the theorem (about 2,000 lines of the manuscript) were not read. No Lean formalisation.
