problems.name: The quasi-Riemann hypothesis: a fixed zero-free half-plane for zeta and all Dirichlet L-functions
problems.statement: The quasi-Riemann hypothesis asks for one gap that works at every height: is there a fixed $\sigma_0<1$ such that the Riemann zeta function has no zeros in the half-plane $\Re s>\sigma_0$? Since Hadamard and de la Vallee Poussin (1896) it has been known that $\zeta(s)\ne0$ on $\Re s=1$, but every known zero-free region shrinks toward that line as the height grows. The uniform version over all Dirichlet characters asks for a single $\sigma_0<1$, independent of the modulus $q$, the character $\chi$ and the height, such that no $L(s,\chi)$ vanishes in $\Re s>\sigma_0$ (the pole of the principal character at $s=1$ aside). Does such a $\sigma_0$ exist?
problems.posedBy: Classical; the name is used by Billington, Cheng, Schettler and Suriajaya (2025), and the uniform Dirichlet form appears in Friedlander and Goldston (1997)
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites no original poser. The question is implicit since the 1896 proofs of the prime number theorem, which gave nonvanishing only on the line Re s = 1; it cites Billington et al. (2025) for the name and Friedlander and Goldston (1997, eq. 1.4) for the uniform Dirichlet formulation. yearPosed is left blank for that reason.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1 claims that every finite-order Hecke $L$-function over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$ and every Dirichlet $L$-function, including $\zeta(s)$, has no zero in $\Re s>7/8$, the principal pole at $s=1$ excepted. So the nontrivial zeros of $\zeta$ have real part at most $7/8$, and any exceptional real zero in $(7/8,1)$ is excluded. The proof runs through cubic theta series and sextic large sieves, first reaching $11/12$ and then refining to $7/8$; the Dirichlet case is transferred from the Hecke family. It does not prove the Riemann hypothesis or GRH, and says so; the boundary line $\Re s=7/8$ is not covered. A separate manuscript gives a different proof of the weaker half-plane $\Re s>11/12$.
problems.aiRole: The release README says every manuscript in the collection was produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model, and that the vast majority were obtained by one fixed procedure averaging about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result. It names the zero-free region for the Riemann zeta function as an exception to that fixed procedure, without saying what was done instead, and says the write-up of the companion Re(s) > 11/12 proof was human edited for readability. The manuscripts are credited to OpenAI with no human author named.
problems.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. The statement of Theorem 1 was read against the posed question: it asserts exactly a fixed half-plane Re s > 7/8, uniform over all Dirichlet characters and over finite-order Hecke characters of Q(sqrt(-3)). The release's formalization.yaml lists three main results for this manuscript: OAI.riemannZeta_ne_zero_of_seven_eighths_lt_re, OAI.DirichletCharacter.LFunction_ne_zero_of_seven_eighths_lt_re and the Hecke analogue. The zeta and Dirichlet comparator statements are short and use Mathlib's own riemannZeta and DirichletCharacter.LFunction, so they state the headline claim with the principal pole excluded; the Hecke statement builds its own character and L-function definitions in a 245-line statement file, which were not audited here. Permitted axioms are propext, Quot.sound and Classical.choice. Not rebuilt here. The README marks this result as an exception to the release's fixed procedure. The corollaries (least nonresidues, square roots mod p) are not in the Lean statements.
problems.significanceNote: A fixed zero-free half-plane is the best-known weakening of the Riemann hypothesis and was considered almost as far out of reach; it would be the largest advance on zeta zeros since 1896. Scored below the Riemann hypothesis at 100 because the line is seven eighths, not one half, above the Proportion of Zeta Zeros on the Critical Line at 68, and above Finite-time blowup for the 3D incompressible Euler equations from smooth data at 80.

problems.name: No countable universal family of avoiding populations, even with exact parent counts
problems.statement: Alexander (2013), Section 6, asks to what extent populations avoiding a sequence can be universal among all such populations, by analogy with universal-graph theory. Interpret embedding as an injective adjacency-preserving map. In the source population class (infinite, finitely many roots, finite children, real chronological birthdates with finite earlier sublevels, and an incoming parent of each label at every nonroot), can one host, or a countable host family, contain every population avoiding a fixed avoidable word? The result also asks whether the obstruction survives exactly one incoming parent of each label. The source does not prescribe a unique embedding category; this is the explicit ordinary-embedding interpretation.
problems.posedBy: Samuel A. Alexander, Biologically Unavoidable Sequences (2013), Section 6, published p.12; ordinary injective-embedding interpretation.
problems.resultNote: No. From any population avoiding s and any countable family of source-population hosts, construct an avoider with the same roots and exactly one incoming parent per label, admitting no injective map to any host with any finite global edge-stretch bound. Thus even adjacency embeddings fail. Parent selection preserves avoidance; terminal cloning preserves the selected infinite-word language exactly. The proof makes fibre sizes exceed enumerated finite host balls while preserving the actual population axioms. This strengthens the earlier complete-fibre obstruction by retaining exact parent counts. Separately, complete blow-ups preserve every corresponding least matching height, linking the obstruction to the rank question. Classical locally finite graph diagonalization is credited. Terminal vertices are permitted; fixed child caps, noninjective maps and arbitrarily unbounded stretch are outside the theorem. It answers the stated embedding interpretation, not every possible category.

problems.name: All-level NANUQ circularity and exact displayed-split support
problems.statement: Holtgrefe et al. proved the original NANUQ distance of a binary, semi-directed LSA, outer-labeled planar, galled level-two bloblet is circular decomposable, with support exactly the splits of its displayed trees. Their Section 6 asks whether this extends to multiple blobs at level two, conjectures circularity for level-three bloblets, and asks about a parametric distance-family extension. Does the circularity and exact-support statement persist at every finite level in the same structural class?
problems.posedBy: Holtgrefe et al., Distinguishing Phylogenetic Level-2 Networks with Quartets and Inter-Taxon Quartet Distances (2025), Theorem 4.7 and Section 6; DOI 10.1007/s11538-025-01549-4.
problems.resultNote: Original NANUQ is circular decomposable at every finite level and with any number of blobs in the binary semi-directed LSA, galled, outer-labeled planar class (at least four taxa). Its positive split support equals the union of displayed-tree splits. This answers the source's level-two multi-blob and level-three circularity questions. A six-label reduction, exact finite certificate and composition identity remove the level bound. The local four-score family has exact universal anchor-positivity domain $s=o=1$, $1/2<=a<=1$, $0<=c<=a$; five labels are the sharp testing cutoff. Contiguous multicopy trees admit an extreme-copy reduction. Raw-matrix error $<1/2$ is optimally correctable by rounding; exact support uses a supplied correct order. Planarity cannot be dropped for exact support. Full all-level Lean verification, network uniqueness, statistical inference and unrestricted ARGs are not claimed.

problems.name: Ordinal certificates and exact pruning characterize sequence realization
problems.statement: Alexander (2013), Section 6, asks whether the infinite gendered populations realizing a possibly avoidable sequence can be characterized, particularly using ordinal numbers. For a target s, use reachable vertex/phase states (v,k), witnessed by a path spelling the first k letters, with successors consuming s(k). Can avoidance be characterized by a decreasing ordinal certificate, and can finite-branching realization be characterized exactly by iterative removal of states without continuing children? This addresses ordinal membership and exact matching continuation, not a requirement that different avoiders receive different transfinite ranks.
problems.posedBy: Samuel A. Alexander, Biologically Unavoidable Sequences (2013), Section 6, published p.12; exact ordinal-membership and reachable-state interpretation.
problems.resultNote: Avoidance is equivalent to a strictly decreasing ordinal certificate on the reachable states; arbitrary vertex/label types are allowed. Under finite per-label branching, natural certificates suffice. It also proves that states surviving every finite pruning round form the greatest successor fixed point and are exactly those with infinite continuations. A start realizes the full target iff its phase-zero state survives. Every other state has an attained finite maximum h, is removed at round h+1, and has a pointwise least natural certificate, even in populations realizing the target elsewhere. Complete finite-fibre blow-ups preserve corresponding least heights. Reachability prevents confusing an unrelated suffix with the original word. These are classical well-founded and finite-branching methods made exact in the source setting. This is not a deciding algorithm for arbitrary infinite inputs or a rank hierarchy separating avoiders; the artificial-root history tree is a different object.

problems.name: Zhu, Fang and Shi's question on invariant projections of weighted irrational rotations
problems.statement: For irrational $\theta$, let $R_\theta$ be the hyperfinite II$_1$ factor generated by unitaries $U,V$ with $VU=e^{2\pi i\theta}UV$, and for $f$ on the circle let $T_f=Uf(V)$. Haagerup-Schultz give nontrivial invariant projections in the factor whenever the Brown measure is not a point mass; for these operators that happens exactly when the Fuglede-Kadison determinant $\exp\int\log|f|\,dm$ is positive. Zhu, Fang and Shi (2017, p. 264) asked: if $f$ is nonzero almost everywhere, $|f|$ is nonconstant and the determinant is zero, must $T_f$ have a nontrivial invariant projection $p\in R_\theta$, that is, $0<\tau(p)<1$ and $(1-p)T_fp=0$?
problems.posedBy: Z. Zhu, J. Fang and R. Shi, On a class of operators in the hyperfinite II1 factor, Math. Scand. (2017), p. 264, question after Proposition 5.7
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every irrational $\theta\in(0,1)$ there is a continuous $f:\mathbb T\to[0,1]$ vanishing only at $1$, with $\int\log f\,dm=-\infty$, such that every projection $p\in R_\theta$ with $(1-p)Uf(V)p=0$ is $0$ or $1$; the operator is nonzero and norm-quasinilpotent. The angle is prescribed in advance with no Diophantine condition. Invariant subspaces of the Hilbert-space representation whose projections lie outside the factor are not excluded. An appendix gives a second realization on an infinite product of circles.
problems.aiRole: Produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model as part of an OpenAI evaluation on open research problems. The release README says the vast majority of results used one fixed procedure, averaging about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result; this result is not among the README's stated exceptions (the Riemann zeta zero-free region work and the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties). The manuscript is authored as OpenAI with no human author named. The README also cautions that unformalized results could have issues.

problems.name: The least distortion of embedding edit distance into l1
problems.statement: Let $E_\Sigma(d)$ be the least distortion of an embedding into $\ell_1$ of the strings of length at most $d$ over an alphabet $\Sigma$, with unit-cost edit distance (insertions, deletions, substitutions). Ostrovsky and Rabani (2007) embedded binary strings with distortion $\exp(O(\sqrt{\log d\log\log d}))$. Lower bounds rose from $3/2$ (Andoni-Deza-Gupta-Indyk-Raskhodnikova 2003) to $(\log d)^{1/2-o(1)}$ (Khot-Naor 2006) and $\Omega(\log d)$ (Krauthgamer-Rabani 2009), leaving an exponential gap. What is the order of growth of $E_\Sigma(d)$; in particular, is the Ostrovsky-Rabani bound $\exp(O(\sqrt{\log d\log\log d}))$ optimal?
problems.posedBy: Open since the Ostrovsky-Rabani upper bound (J. ACM 2007) and the Krauthgamer-Rabani lower bound (2009); the manuscripts cite no explicit statement of the question
problems.ageNote: The manuscripts present the question through the gap between Ostrovsky-Rabani (2007) and Krauthgamer-Rabani (2009) and do not cite a paper that poses it, so no year is given.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there are absolute $c,C>0$ and $d_0$ with $\exp(c\sqrt{\log d\log\log d})\le E_\Sigma(d)\le\exp(C\sqrt{\log d\log\log d})$ for all $d\ge d_0$ and all finite $|\Sigma|\ge2$, so the Ostrovsky-Rabani scale is sharp up to constants in the exponent. The upper bound is Ostrovsky-Rabani's method made uniform over alphabets and lengths; the new content is the matching lower bound, given by three constructions across the family. The constants $c,C$ are not determined, and nothing is said about computational efficiency.

problems.name: The PPT-squared conjecture: is the composition of two PPT channels always entanglement breaking?
problems.field: Quantum channels: PPT maps and entanglement breaking
problems.statement: A linear map $F:M_a(\mathbb C)\to M_b(\mathbb C)$ is PPT if both $F$ and $T\circ F$ are completely positive, $T$ the transpose, and entanglement breaking if $(\mathrm{id}\otimes F)(X)$ is separable for every positive $X$, equivalently its Choi matrix is separable. Christandl conjectured that composing two PPT channels always yields an entanglement-breaking channel; the question was recorded as Problem G of the 2012 BIRS workshop 'Operator structures in quantum information theory', and stated for pairs of PPT maps as Conjecture IV.1 of Christandl, Muller-Hermes and Wolf (2019). Is $\Phi_2\circ\Phi_1$ entanglement breaking for all PPT channels $\Phi_1,\Phi_2$, in particular is $\Phi\circ\Phi$ entanglement breaking for every PPT channel $\Phi$?
problems.posedBy: M. Christandl, recorded as Problem G of the BIRS workshop report 12w5084 (2012); stated as Conjecture IV.1 by M. Christandl, A. Muller-Hermes and M. M. Wolf, Ann. Henri Poincare 20 (2019)
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites the 2012 BIRS report for the channel form and CMHW 2019 (arXiv 1807.01266) for the two-map form.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.3: there is an explicit trace-preserving PPT channel $\Theta$ on $M_{21}(\mathbb C)$ with $\Theta\circ\Theta$ not entanglement breaking, answering the 2012 channel question negatively with the same channel in both slots. Theorem 1.2: explicit PPT maps $\Phi_1,\Phi_2$ on $M_{10}(\mathbb C)$ (not trace preserving) whose composition has nonzero Choi matrix with no product vector in its range, refuting the unrestricted two-map Conjecture IV.1. The same pair yields the zero-key entangled state of the companion entry. Not shown: minimal dimensions, or whether every PPT channel becomes entanglement breaking after three compositions (the PPT-cubed question).

problems.name: The spacetime Penrose inequality: invariant ADM mass bounds the minimal area enclosing a trapped boundary, for general asymptotically flat initial data
problems.statement: Penrose (1973), as a test of weak cosmic censorship, argued that a black hole of horizon area $A$ requires total mass at least $\sqrt{A/16\pi}$. The time-symmetric (Riemannian) case was proved in dimension three by Huisken-Ilmanen and Bray, and in higher dimensions by Bray-Lee and Bi-Zhu. For initial data $(M^n,g,K)$ with nonzero second fundamental form the bound with the apparent horizon's own area fails (Ben-Dov; Carrasco-Mars), and the accepted formulation, following Bray and Khuri, uses the least area $A_{\min}$ of surfaces enclosing the trapped boundary. It was known in spherical symmetry, for some cohomogeneity-one data, and with a non-sharp constant (Allen-Bryden-Kazaras-Khuri, 2025). Does every asymptotically flat initial-data set obeying the dominant energy condition, with weakly trapped boundary, satisfy $m\ge\frac12(A_{\min}/\omega_{n-1})^{(n-2)/(n-1)}$ for the invariant ADM mass $m$, with equality only for Schwarzschild?
problems.posedBy: Roger Penrose (heuristic inequality); enclosing-area initial-data formulation following Hubert Bray and Marcus Khuri
problems.ageNote: Penrose, Naked singularities, Ann. N.Y. Acad. Sci. 224 (1973). The enclosing-area form for non-time-symmetric data follows Bray-Khuri (2010, 2011) and the Ben-Dov (2004) and Carrasco-Mars (2010) counterexamples to apparent-horizon formulations.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.3: for smooth one-ended initial-data exteriors in every dimension $n\ge3$ with integrable constraint densities, dominant energy condition, weakly future trapped boundary ($\theta^+\le0$, nothing on $\theta^-$), the stated decay, $E>|P|$ and $A_{\min}>0$: $m=(E^2-|P|^2)^{1/2}\ge\frac12(A_{\min}/\omega_{n-1})^{(n-2)/(n-1)}$, sharp; outermostness and outer area minimization are not assumed. Corollary 1.4 derives $E>|P|$; Theorem 1.5 ($n=3,4$) needs only two metric derivatives of decay. Companions: rigidity (equality only for Schwarzschild-Tangherlini slices, under horizon hypotheses), a conformal-flow Riemannian inequality in all dimensions, the boundary deformations, and a Bondi-mass version for CKS hyperboloidal data. Not shown: evolution or cosmic censorship. Priority: Allen-Bryden-Kazaras-Khuri (2025) proved the bound with a non-sharp constant.

problems.name: Hopkins' chromatic splitting conjecture (weak and odd-prime strong forms)
problems.statement: Fix a prime $p$, let $L_{n-1}$ be localization at $E(n-1)$ and $L_{K(n)}$ localization at Morava $K$-theory. Hopkins' chromatic splitting conjecture, recorded by Hovey (1995, Conjecture 4.2), describes the chromatic overlap $L_{n-1}L_{K(n)}S_p^\wedge$. Its weak form asserts that for the $p$-completion $X$ of a finite spectrum the canonical map $L_{n-1}X\to L_{n-1}L_{K(n)}X$ has a homotopy retraction (finite-input form: Beaudry-Goerss-Henn, Conjecture 1.1.11). Its strong form prescribes an explicit splitting of $L_{n-1}L_{K(n)}S_p^\wedge$ into suspended localized spheres indexed by an exterior algebra; Beaudry disproved this at $n=p=2$, and Barthel-Beaudry (2019, Conjecture 6.3) retain it at odd primes. Both forms were known through height two at odd primes. Does the canonical map split for all $n$ and $p$, and does the overlap decompose as predicted at odd primes?
problems.posedBy: M. J. Hopkins, recorded by M. Hovey, Bousfield localization functors and Hopkins' chromatic splitting conjecture (1995), Conjecture 4.2; refined by Barthel-Beaudry (2019) and Beaudry-Goerss-Henn
problems.ageNote: The conjecture is Hopkins' and circulated before Hovey's 1995 write-up, which the manuscripts cite as the record. The weak finite-input form is stated as Conjecture 1.1.11 of Beaudry-Goerss-Henn.
problems.resultNote: Weak form: for the derived $p$-completion $X=S_p^\wedge$, the canonical map $L_{n-1}X\to L_{n-1}L_{K(n)}X$ has no homotopy retraction at height $n=p$ for every $p\ge5$ and at $n=p+1$ for every $p\ge7$; the class $\beta_1^{(p-1)^2}$ is a nonzero kernel element (at $p=5$, $\beta_1^{16}$ in degree 608). Strong form: for $p\ge5$ the map $L_0L_{K(3)}S\to L_0L_{K(2)}L_{K(3)}S$ is nonzero on $\pi_{-3}$, so the height-three splitting fails even as an equivalence of $E(2)$-local spectra. Companions: at $n=p=3$ the overlap is not in the thick subcategory generated by $L_0S,L_1S,L_2S$; positively, for $p>n+1$ the overlap has a $2^n$-stage filtration with the predicted cofibers (nonsplit), with explicit attachments at height three. Heights below $p-1$ remain open.

problems.name: Secret key from all entangled states: does every entangled state have positive distillable secret key? (Kruger-Werner Problem 24)
problems.shortName: Secret key from all entangled states
problems.field: Quantum cryptography: distillable secret key and bound entanglement
problems.statement: For a bipartite state $\rho_{AB}$, the distillable secret key $K_D(\rho)$ is the best rate at which Alice and Bob, using local operations and authenticated public communication on many copies, can extract bits that agree and are independent of an eavesdropper holding a purification and the public record. Separable states have $K_D=0$, and Horodecki et al. showed that some bound entangled (PPT) states nevertheless have $K_D>0$, so key and distillable entanglement differ. The converse was posed as Problem 24, 'Secret key from all entangled states', in Kruger and Werner's 2005 collection of open problems in quantum information theory (contact P. Horodecki). Is $K_D(\rho)>0$ for every entangled state $\rho$?
problems.posedBy: P. Horodecki (contact), Problem 24 'Secret key from all entangled states' in O. Kruger and R. F. Werner (eds.), Some open problems in quantum information theory (2005)
problems.ageNote: The open-problem entry is dated 15 March 2005 (arXiv quant-ph/0504166). The manuscript notes the question is also discussed in the private-state literature.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there is an explicit entangled density operator $\rho$ on $\mathbb C^{10}\otimes\mathbb C^{10}$ whose range contains no nonzero product vector, such that for every $n$ and every admitted completed bit-output protocol on $\rho^{\otimes n}$ the output is at trace-norm distance at least $1/5$ from an ideal secret bit; hence $K_D(\rho)=0$. The state is the normalized Choi matrix of a composition of two PPT maps; a coherence inequality for such states bounds secrecy by disagreement probability. So the answer to Problem 24 is no. Not shown: minimality of dimension ten, or a zero-key example for protocol models beyond the paper's admitted class.

problems.name: Bang's half-area cylinder covering question (and the 1-codimensional cylinder covering conjecture)
problems.statement: A cylinder in $\mathbb R^3$ is $B+\mathbb Ru$ with $u$ a unit vector and $B\subset u^\perp$ of finite area. Bang's plank theorem says plank widths in a covering of a convex body sum to at least its minimal width; for cylinders, the two-cylinder cover of a regular tetrahedron has total base area exactly half the minimum projection area $A_{\min}(K)$. Bezdek and Litvak, attributing the example to Bang (1951), asked whether every finite cylinder covering of a convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^3$ satisfies $\sum_i|B_i|\ge\frac12A_{\min}(K)$; Bezdek and Khan conjectured the stronger directionwise bound $\sum_i|B_i|/|\pi_{u_i^\perp}K|\ge\frac12$. Do these half-area lower bounds hold?
problems.posedBy: Thoger Bang (example); Karoly Bezdek and Alexander Litvak; Karoly Bezdek and Muhammad Khan (directionwise form)
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites Bezdek (2009, Problem 3.1) and Bezdek-Litvak (2009), who attribute the tetrahedral example and the half-area question to Bang's 1951 plank paper; the directionwise form is Bezdek-Khan (arXiv 1602.06040, 2016), Conjecture 4.13. Bezdek-Litvak proved the directionwise bound 1/3 in general.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: a regular tetrahedron $K$ with $A_{\min}(K)=\sqrt2$ has, for each $0<\varepsilon\le1/2000$, a cover by $2\lceil2/\varepsilon^2\rceil$ cylinders with compact triangular perpendicular bases and $\frac1{\sqrt2}\sum|B_i|=\frac12-\frac{13}{6000}\varepsilon^2+O(\varepsilon^4)$, strictly below half. Corollary 1.2: every nondegenerate tetrahedron has a finite cover with directionwise relative cost below 1/2, refuting the Bezdek-Khan conjecture. Not shown: the optimal constant (Bezdek-Litvak's lower bound 1/3 stands) or counterexamples among centrally symmetric bodies.

problems.name: The hyperinvariant subspace problem on Hilbert space
problems.statement: A closed subspace is hyperinvariant for a bounded operator $T$ on a Hilbert space $H$ if it is invariant under every operator commuting with $T$; equivalently, $T$ has no nontrivial hyperinvariant subspace exactly when its commutant $\{T\}'$ is a transitive algebra. Douglas and Pearcy (1972) studied the problem and its link to transitive algebras; it sits beside the invariant subspace problem and is known to be distinct from it (a claimed equivalence by Kerchy-Pearcy was withdrawn). Does every bounded nonscalar operator on an infinite-dimensional separable complex Hilbert space have a nonzero proper closed hyperinvariant subspace?
problems.posedBy: Classical operator-theory problem; the manuscript cites R. G. Douglas and C. Pearcy, Hyperinvariant subspaces and transitive algebras, Michigan Math. J. 19 (1972), and names no original poser
problems.ageNote: The earliest source the manuscripts cite for the problem is Douglas-Pearcy (1972), described as studying it rather than posing it; no posing date is given.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2: on $L^2(\mathbb Z_2;\ell^2(\mathbb Z))$ a fibered bilateral weighted shift $S$ with quadratically decaying weights over the 2-adic odometer is nonzero with $\|S^n\|\le\exp(-10\lfloor(n+1)^2/4\rfloor)$, hence norm-quasinilpotent, and its commutant (containing a backward intertwiner $V$ and all scalar multipliers) is transitive. So every infinite-dimensional separable Hilbert space carries a nonzero quasinilpotent operator with no nonzero proper closed hyperinvariant subspace. The operator has many ordinary invariant subspaces (the fiberwise tails), so the invariant subspace problem itself is untouched. The companion reaches the same existence statement by a different construction.

problems.name: The transitive algebra problem
problems.statement: An algebra of bounded operators on a Hilbert space $H$ is transitive if its only common closed invariant subspaces are $\{0\}$ and $H$. Arveson (1967) proved that a transitive algebra containing a maximal abelian self-adjoint algebra is strongly dense in $B(H)$, and Douglas and Pearcy (1972) related the general question to hyperinvariant subspaces. Is every unital transitive operator algebra on an infinite-dimensional separable complex Hilbert space strongly (equivalently weakly) dense in $B(H)$?
problems.posedBy: Question in the setting of W. B. Arveson, A density theorem for operator algebras, Duke Math. J. 34 (1967); the manuscript states it without attribution
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites Arveson (1967) for the main positive result and Douglas-Pearcy (1972) for the link to hyperinvariant subspaces, but does not say who posed the question or when; the conventional attribution to Arveson 1967 is not made in the source.
problems.resultNote: Corollary 1.2 of the principal manuscript: the commutant of the constructed nonzero quasinilpotent operator $S$ is a proper, strongly closed, unital, transitive complex algebra, so it is not strongly dense in $B(H)$. This answers the question negatively on every infinite-dimensional separable Hilbert space. It is an immediate consequence of the hyperinvariant counterexample, since the commutant of an operator without hyperinvariant subspaces is transitive. The algebra is a commutant, so nothing is said about singly generated transitive algebras, which is the invariant subspace problem.

problems.name: Must a reflexive Banach space with no AUC renorming contain the countably branching diamonds uniformly? (Baudier-Lancien Problem 39)
problems.field: Banach space theory: asymptotic geometry and metric embeddings
problems.statement: A norm is asymptotically uniformly convex (AUC) if $\overline\delta(t)=\inf_{\|x\|=1}\sup_{F}\inf_{y\in F,\|y\|=1}(\|x+ty\|-1)>0$ for all $t>0$, $F$ ranging over finite-codimensional subspaces, and asymptotically midpoint uniformly convex (AMUC) if the same holds for the average of $\|x+ty\|$ and $\|x-ty\|$. The countably branching diamonds $D_k$ replace each edge by countably many two-edge paths, $k$ times. Baudier, Causey, Dilworth, Kutzarova, Randrianarivony, Schlumprecht and Zhang (2017) proved that an equivalent AMUC norm prevents uniform bi-Lipschitz embeddings of the $D_k$, and that for reflexive spaces with unconditional asymptotic structure, failure of AUC renormability forces uniform diamond embeddings; Swift and Perreau extended the latter under similar structure. Baudier and Lancien record the general question as Problem 39: if $X$ is reflexive and admits no equivalent AUC norm, must the countably branching diamonds embed into $X$ with uniformly bounded distortion?
problems.posedBy: F. P. Baudier and G. Lancien, Asymptotic and nonlinear geometries of Banach spaces and their interactions (arXiv 2512.00817, 2025; Cours Specialises 33, SMF 2026), Problem 39
problems.ageNote: The year is the arXiv posting of the monograph that numbers the problem; the question grows out of Baudier et al. (2017), who proved the implication under unconditional asymptotic structure. Whether that 2017 paper already stated it as open was not checked here.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: the dual $X=J^*$ of a countably branching segment-forest space with finite, unbounded component heights is infinite-dimensional, separable and reflexive, admits no equivalent AUC norm, and its given norm has averaged midpoint modulus $\widehat\delta_X(t)\ge\sqrt{1+t^2/12}-1$; every embedding of $D_k$ into $X$ has distortion at least $\sqrt{1+k/12}$. So Problem 39 has a negative answer, and AMUC does not imply AUC renormability even for reflexive spaces (Baudier had shown the non-reflexive separation in 2026). Companions add midpoint-lens estimates, a sharper $D^2\ge1+k/4$ bound, exact moduli in a Daugavet subspace of $L_1$, and further tree-potential and $L_1$ examples. Not shown: sharp distortion growth rates.

problems.name: The Sharan-Sidford-Valiant precision question: do learners with $o(d^2)$ memory need $\Omega(d\log(1/\epsilon))$ samples for linear regression?
problems.statement: A streaming learner sees pairs $(x_t,y_t)$ with independent rows $x_t\sim N(0,I_d)$ and labels $y_t=\langle x_t,s\rangle$ for an unknown unit vector $s$, reads each pair once and keeps at most $M$ bits between samples. With enough memory to store the equations, about $d$ samples determine $s$; with real registers, Kaczmarz projection reaches accuracy $\epsilon$ after about $d\log(1/\epsilon)$ samples. Building on Raz's memory-sample lower bounds for parity, Sharan, Sidford and Valiant (STOC 2019) showed that $d^2/4$ bits force $\Omega(d\log\log(1/\epsilon))$ samples in a noisy version of this experiment, and asked (Section 1.1) whether the first-order dependence of the sample count on the precision is optimal under bounded memory. Must every learner with $o(d^2)$ (or at most $Ad^2$) bits of memory use $\Omega(d\log(1/\epsilon))$ samples to estimate $s$ to accuracy $\epsilon$?
problems.posedBy: Vatsal Sharan, Aaron Sidford and Gregory Valiant (Memory-sample tradeoffs for linear regression with small error, STOC 2019, Section 1.1)
problems.resultNote: Main theorem: for fixed $A>0$ there are $c_A,d_A$ such that any learner with $M\le Ad^2$ bits, $d\ge d_A$, $0<\epsilon\le1/10$ and uniform-prior success at least $2/3$ in reaching angular error $\epsilon$ needs horizon $T\ge c_A d\log(1/\epsilon)$; for $M=o(d^2)$ the constant is absolute, and the bound also holds under an every-signal guarantee. Transitions may use unbounded computation and randomness; the output uses only the terminal state, stopping index and fresh randomness, with a deterministic horizon. It implies an $\Omega_A(dr\log d)$ bound in the noisy experiment of Sharan-Sidford-Valiant at Euclidean accuracy $d^{-r}$ in their range. No matching finite-memory upper bound is proved, and memory well above $d^2$ is not treated.

problems.name: De Giorgi's conjecture on monotone solutions of the Allen-Cahn equation
problems.field: Elliptic PDE; Allen-Cahn equation and phase transitions
problems.statement: De Giorgi conjectured in 1978 that if $u\in C^2(\mathbb R^n)$ solves the Allen-Cahn equation $\Delta u=u^3-u$ with $|u|\le1$ and $\partial_{x_n}u>0$ everywhere, then for $n\le8$ the level sets of $u$ are hyperplanes, i.e. $u(x)=\tanh((e\cdot x-c)/\sqrt2)$ for a unit vector $e$ and $c\in\mathbb R$. It is the phase-transition analogue of the Bernstein problem for minimal graphs. Ghoussoub-Gui proved it for $n=2$, Ambrosio-Cabre for $n=3$, Savin for $4\le n\le8$ under the extra assumption that $u(x',t)\to\pm1$ as $t\to\pm\infty$, and del Pino-Kowalczyk-Wei gave counterexamples for $n\ge9$. Is every such monotone solution one-dimensional in every dimension $n\le8$, without the limit assumption?
problems.posedBy: Ennio De Giorgi
problems.ageNote: Stated at the International Meeting on Recent Methods in Nonlinear Analysis, Rome 1978; proceedings published by Pitagora, Bologna, 1979, as cited by the manuscript.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: every $u\in C^2(\mathbb R^8,(-1,1))$ with $\Delta u=u^3-u$ and $\partial_8u>0$ equals $\tanh((e\cdot x-c)/\sqrt2)$ with $e_8>0$. Theorem 1.2: every stable solution $v:\mathbb R^7\to[-1,1]$ is $\pm1$ or planar, without an energy-growth assumption; this is sharp by Pacard-Wei's nonplanar stable solutions in $\mathbb R^8$. A final section explains why the argument fails in dimension nine, consistent with del Pino-Kowalczyk-Wei. The paper does not treat other potentials, the stable De Giorgi problem in dimension eight, or the Gibbons and Savin variants beyond what the monotone theorem implies.

problems.name: Kalton's question: does the Lipschitz-free space of every uniformly discrete metric space have the bounded approximation property?
problems.shortName: Kalton's BAP question for uniformly discrete free spaces
problems.statement: For a pointed metric space $(M,d,o)$, the Lipschitz-free space $\mathcal F(M)$ is the closed span of the evaluations $\delta_x$ in $\mathrm{Lip}_0(M)^*$. Kalton showed that if $M$ is uniformly discrete ($d(x,y)\ge\theta>0$ for $x\ne y$) then $\mathcal F(M)$ has the approximation property, and Dalet proved the metric approximation property for countable proper spaces. Kalton asked, and Godefroy-Ozawa (Question 1) and Godefroy's survey (Problem 6.2) restated: if $M$ is uniformly discrete, must $\mathcal F(M)$ have the bounded approximation property, that is, can the finite-rank approximants of the identity be chosen with a uniform norm bound?
problems.posedBy: Nigel Kalton (Collectanea Mathematica 2004, remarks after Proposition 4.4); restated by Godefroy and Ozawa (2014, Question 1) and Godefroy (2015 survey, Problem 6.2)
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there is a countable, unbounded, nonproper pointed metric space with $d(x,y)\ge1$ for distinct points whose real Lipschitz-free space has AP but fails $\lambda$-BAP for every finite $\lambda$. It is built as a wedge of bounded blocks (Theorem 1.2) in which a finite anchor set defeats every finite-rank operator of norm at most $p$. Consequences stated in the paper: for each $p$, real $\ell_1$ has an equivalent norm with $2B_p$-BAP failing $p$-BAP (for $p=1$ failing MAP), and $\mathcal F(M)$ is a separable Banach space that is not approximable in Kalton's nonlinear sense (Kalton 2012, Problem 1). Real scalars only; the proper countable case is excluded by Dalet's theorem.

problems.name: Nienhuis's 3/4 exponent for self-avoiding walk on the honeycomb lattice, in diameter form
problems.statement: Let $\mathbb P_n$ be the uniform law on $n$-step self-avoiding walks from a fixed vertex of a planar lattice. Nienhuis's Coulomb-gas analysis of the dilute $O(n)$ model at $n=0$ (1982) predicts the size exponent $\nu=3/4$: a typical $n$-step walk has spatial extent $n^{3/4}$, equivalently its trace has mass dimension $4/3$; Lawler, Schramm and Werner's conjectured $SLE_{8/3}$ scaling limit gives the same value. On the honeycomb lattice Duminil-Copin and Smirnov proved that the connective constant is $\sqrt{2+\sqrt2}$, but no polynomial size exponent was known; the best fixed-length bound was sub-ballistic (Krachun-Panagiotis: within $Cn/\log n$). Does a uniform $n$-step self-avoiding walk on the honeycomb lattice have spatial extent $n^{3/4+o(1)}$?
problems.posedBy: Bernard Nienhuis (prediction from the dilute O(n) model)
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites Nienhuis, Phys. Rev. Lett. 49 (1982), for the exponent 3/4 at n=0. The prediction concerns end-to-end distance and other size statistics; this paper treats diameter, local mass and covering numbers.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every $\delta>0$ and $k>0$ there are $C_{\delta,k}$ and $n_0$ such that for every integer $n\ge n_0$, with $\mathbb P_n$-probability at least $1-C_{\delta,k}n^{-k}$, the diameter satisfies $n^{3/4-\delta}\le D(\gamma)\le n^{3/4+\delta}$, and simultaneously for all visited $z$ and $s\in[1,n]$ the ball mass is within $n^{\pm\delta}$ of $\min\{n,s^{4/3}\}$ and the covering number by $s$-balls within $n^{\pm\delta}$ of $1+ns^{-4/3}$. Corollaries: span at least $n^{3/4-\delta}$ in each lattice normal, covering dimension $4/3$, radius of gyration $n^{3/4+o(1)}$ and $\mathbb E_n[D^p]=n^{3p/4+o(1)}$. Not shown: a fixed-length lower bound for the end-to-end distance (a companion has it only on a density-one set of lengths), an exponent without $n^{o(1)}$ slack, other lattices, or convergence to $SLE_{8/3}$.

problems.name: The Hajlasz-Onninen endpoint question for the centered maximal function, planar disk case: is $\|\nabla Mf\|_1\le C\|\nabla f\|_1$ on $W^{1,1}(\mathbb R^2)$?
problems.field: Harmonic analysis: regularity of maximal functions
problems.statement:
For $f\in L^1_{loc}(\mathbb R^n)$ let $Mf(x)=\sup_{r>0}|B(x,r)|^{-1}\int_{B(x,r)}|f|$ be the centered Hardy-Littlewood maximal function. Kinnunen proved that $M$ is bounded on $W^{1,p}$ for $1<p<\infty$, using $|
abla Mf|\le M|
abla f|$, but this argument fails at $p=1$ because $M$ is not bounded on $L^1$. Hajlasz and Onninen (2004, Question 1) asked whether the endpoint gradient bound nevertheless holds: is $f\mapsto|
abla Mf|$ bounded from $W^{1,1}(\mathbb R^n)$ to $L^1(\mathbb R^n)$? Known before this work: one dimension (Tanaka and Aldaz-Perez Lazaro for the uncentered operator, Kurka for the centered one), radial or block-decreasing inputs and the uncentered operator in higher dimensions (Luiro, Aldaz-Perez Lazaro), dyadic and uncentered-cube variants (Weigt), and fractional centered operators (Weigt). The centered operator in dimension at least two was open in general. In the plane, with disks: is there an absolute $C$ such that $\|
abla Mf\|_{L^1(\mathbb R^2)}\le C\|
abla f\|_{L^1(\mathbb R^2)}$ for every $f\in W^{1,1}(\mathbb R^2)$, with $Mf$ weakly differentiable?
problems.posedBy: P. Hajlasz and J. Onninen, On boundedness of maximal functions in Sobolev spaces, Ann. Acad. Sci. Fenn. Math. 29 (2004), Question 1
problems.ageNote: The question is posed in every dimension; this entry records only its planar centered-disk case, which the manuscript answers.
problems.resultNote:
Theorem 1.1: there is an absolute $C<\infty$ such that for every real $f\in W^{1,1}(\mathbb R^2)$ the centered disk maximal function $Mf$ is locally integrable, lies in $W^{1,1}_{loc}(\mathbb R^2)$ and satisfies $\int|
abla Mf|\le C\int|
abla f|$. The key step is a signed finite-band estimate for $\sup_{a\le t\le b}A_tg$ uniform in the number of dyadic scales, combined with Lahti-Weigt's conditional regularity theorem. Not shown: dimensions $n\ge3$, balls in other norms, the BV (variation) version, the optimal constant, or continuity of $f\mapsto
abla Mf$.

problems.name: The Gopalan-Servedio conjecture: is $\sum_i\widehat f(\{i\})=O(\sqrt{\deg f})$ for Boolean functions?
problems.statement: For $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ write $\widehat f(S)=\mathbb E[f(X)\prod_{i\in S}X_i]$ with $X$ uniform, and let $\deg f$ be the degree of its real multilinear representation. Cauchy-Schwarz gives $\sum_i\widehat f(\{i\})=\mathbb E[f(X)\sum_iX_i]\le\sqrt n$, attained up to constants by majority, while total influence gives $\sum_i|\widehat f(\{i\})|\le\deg f$. Gopalan and Servedio conjectured, around 2009, that $\sqrt n$ can be replaced by $\sqrt{\deg f}$; the conjecture is recorded in O'Donnell's list of open problems in analysis of Boolean functions and as Conjecture 3.17 of Filmus, Hatami, Keller and Lifshitz. A sharper majority-benchmark version was refuted at degree 4 by Kudin and Pasalic, which does not decide the square-root form. Is there an absolute constant $C$ with $\sum_i\widehat f(\{i\})\le C\sqrt{\deg f}$ for every Boolean function $f$?
problems.posedBy: Parikshit Gopalan and Rocco Servedio (c. 2009), recorded in O'Donnell's Open Problems in Analysis of Boolean Functions (2012, p. 9)
problems.ageNote: The manuscript attributes the conjecture to Gopalan and Servedio circa 2009 via O'Donnell's 2012 problem list; no dated original source is cited.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1: for every $C>0$ there is a nonconstant $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ with $\sum_i\widehat f(\{i\})>C\sqrt{\deg f}$; equivalently $\sum_i|\widehat f(\{i\})|/\sqrt{\deg f}$ is unbounded over Boolean functions of positive degree, so no constant multiple of the conjectured bound holds. The dimension and copy counts in the construction are finite but not usefully bounded, so no growth rate of the violation in terms of degree is given. The true order between $\sqrt{\deg f}$ and the linear bound $\deg f$ is left open.

problems.name: Kalton's Problem 2: does a bi-Lipschitz copy of $c_0$ force a linear copy of $c_0$?
problems.statement: Godefroy, Kalton and Lancien (2000) proved that a Banach space bi-Lipschitz equivalent to $c_0$, or to a linear subspace of $c_0$, is linearly isomorphic to such a space. Those theorems concern an equivalence of whole spaces and say nothing about a space that merely contains a bi-Lipschitz image of $c_0$. Kalton recorded that question as Problem 2 in his 2008 survey of the nonlinear geometry of Banach spaces, and Hajek, Johanis and Schlumprecht described it as apparently open in 2024. If a Banach space contains a bi-Lipschitz image of $c_0$, must it contain a closed linear subspace isomorphic to $c_0$?
problems.posedBy: Nigel J. Kalton, The nonlinear geometry of Banach spaces, Rev. Mat. Complut. 21 (2008), Problem 2
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there is a separable real Banach space $Z$ with no closed subspace isomorphic to $c_0$ and an onto bi-Lipschitz map $F:Z\oplus_\infty c_0\to Z$. Restricting $F$ to the $c_0$ summand embeds $c_0$ bi-Lipschitzly in $Z$, so Problem 2 has a negative answer. With Aharoni's theorem, $Z$ is bi-Lipschitz universal for separable metric spaces, and $Z$, $Z\oplus_\infty c_0$ form a second separable Lipschitz-isomorphic, linearly non-isomorphic pair. Real scalars only; it does not address analogous questions for other classical spaces.

problems.name: Iitaka's subadditivity conjecture C(n,m), with its logarithmic form and Campana's orbifold form
problems.statement: For a surjective morphism $f:X\to Y$ with connected fibres between smooth projective complex varieties, with general fibre $F$, Iitaka's conjecture $C_{n,m}$ asks whether $\kappa(X)\ge\kappa(F)+\kappa(Y)$. Iitaka also stated a logarithmic version for open varieties, $\bar\kappa(U)\ge\bar\kappa(F)+\bar\kappa(V)$, and Campana conjectured an orbifold form in which rational boundaries and multiple fibres enter through an orbifold base: $\kappa(X,K_X+\Delta)\ge\kappa(F,K_F+\Delta_F)+\kappa(f\mid\Delta)$ for compact manifolds in Fujiki class $\mathcal C$. Known cases included curve bases and fibres with good minimal models (Kawamata), general-type bases (Viehweg) and fibres (Kollar), total dimension at most six (Birkar), and abelian or maximal-Albanese bases. Does subadditivity hold for every such fibration?
problems.posedBy: Shigeru Iitaka (J. Math. Soc. Japan 1971; Classification of Algebraic Varieties, Proc. Japan Acad. 1977); orbifold form by F. Campana (J. Inst. Math. Jussieu 2011, Conj. 6.1)
problems.ageNote: The manuscript traces the problem to Iitaka's 1971 D-dimension paper and cites the explicit logarithmic conjecture to his 1977 note; the ordinary C(n,m) form is from the same period. Campana's orbifold conjecture is in the 2011 journal version of his arXiv 0705.0737.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for a smooth compact connected manifold $X$ in Fujiki class $\mathcal C$ with rational SNC boundary $\Delta$ (coefficient one allowed) and a fibration $f:X\to Y$ onto a normal compact complex space, $\kappa(X,K_X+\Delta)\ge\kappa(F,K_F+\Delta_F)+\kappa(f\mid\Delta)$ for a very general fibre. Corollaries: logarithmic subadditivity for compatible reduced-SNC pairs, and ordinary $\kappa(X)\ge\kappa(F)+\kappa(Y)$ for projective fibre spaces over any algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. Not covered: positive characteristic, real or non-SNC boundaries, and the variation refinement, which is a separate entry.

problems.name: Schramm's Hausdorff-measure problem for SLE: an exact gauge function for the chordal SLE trace, 0 < kappa < 8
problems.field: Schramm-Loewner evolution; fractal geometry of random curves
problems.statement: For $0<\kappa<8$ the chordal $\mathrm{SLE}_\kappa$ trace has Hausdorff dimension $d=1+\kappa/8$ (Beffara 2008), and Rezaei (2018) proved its $d$-dimensional Hausdorff measure is zero. For a gauge $h$ (continuous, nondecreasing, $h(0)=0$) let $\mathcal H^h$ be the corresponding Hausdorff measure. Schramm, in his 2006 ICM collection of problems (Problem 7.1), asked whether the SLE trace has a sigma-finite Hausdorff measure and suggested $r^d\log\log(1/r)$ as a possible gauge. Is there a deterministic gauge $h$ such that almost surely $0<\mathcal H^h(\gamma([s,t]))<\infty$ for nontrivial trace segments, and if so, which?
problems.posedBy: Oded Schramm, Conformally invariant scaling limits: an overview and a collection of problems (ICM 2006), Problem 7.1
problems.ageNote: Posed in Schramm's ICM 2006 address (arXiv February 2006); the proceedings appeared in 2007.
problems.resultNote: For fixed $0<\kappa<8$, $d=1+\kappa/8$, the gauge $h(r)=r^d(\log\log(1/r))^{(2-d)/2}$ satisfies almost surely $0<\mathcal H^h(\gamma([s,t]))<\infty$ for all $0<s<t<\infty$, and $\mathbb E\mathcal H^h(\Gamma\cap\overline B(0,R))<\infty$. Corollary 1.2: Schramm's suggested gauge $r^d\log\log(1/r)$ is not sigma-finite on any such segment, so the exponent he proposed is wrong. The September 25 companion first proved existence of an exact (non-closed-form) gauge. Not addressed: $\kappa\ge8$, whether the two gauges are equivalent, and the relation of $\mathcal H^h$ to natural parametrization or Minkowski content.

problems.name: The Gaussian moat problem
problems.statement: A Gaussian prime is an irreducible element of $\mathbb Z[i]$, viewed as a point of the plane. For a step bound $D$, join two Gaussian primes when their distance is at most $D$. Large prime-free disks exist with centers on any line (Gethner, Wagon, Wick), but a walk in the plane can go around them, and computations bound only the component of a particular starting region (Tsuchimura, steps up to 6 from the origin). Gethner and Stark (1997) formulated a version uniform in the starting point and proved it for step bounds $\sqrt2$ and $2$ by periodic sieving. Is it impossible, for every finite $D$, to walk to infinity through distinct Gaussian primes with steps of length at most $D$?
problems.posedBy: Basil Gordon, at the 1962 International Congress of Mathematicians in Stockholm (per Gethner and Stark, Periodic Gaussian moats, Experimental Math. 6, 1997); Erdos credited Gordon and Motzkin
problems.ageNote: Gethner and Stark trace the question to Gordon at the 1962 ICM; Erdos (1977) recalled hearing it from Motzkin in November 1963 and credited Gordon and Motzkin.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every real $D$ there is a finite $B_D$ such that every connected component of the graph on Gaussian primes with edges of length at most $D$ has at most $B_D$ vertices, independent of the starting prime and including primes on the axes; so every walk through distinct Gaussian primes with steps at most $D$ has at most $B_D$ terms. The proof finds, for each $D$, a finite set of split primes whose joint sieve leaves a periodic set with no infinite bounded-step walk, using geometric sampling and entropy estimates. $B_D$ is nonexplicit, so no numerical moat width is given for any particular $D$.

problems.name: The Hahn-Wilson conjecture: fp-type at most n spectra are exactly the thick subcategory generated by BP<n>
problems.field: Chromatic homotopy theory; stable homotopy theory
problems.statement: Fix a prime $p$. A bounded-below $p$-complete spectrum $X$ is fp if $H^*(X;\mathbb F_p)$ is finitely presented over the Steenrod algebra; it has fp-type at most $n$ if $\pi_*(V\wedge X)$ is finite in total for a finite spectrum $V$ of type $n+1$ (Mahowald-Rezk). Hahn-Wilson redshift shows $K(\mathrm{BP}\langle n\rangle)$ has fp-type $n+1$, and Lee-Pstragowski proved the statement below at height one. The Hahn-Wilson conjecture asks whether finite presentation plus a height bound characterizes finite constructions from truncated Brown-Peterson spectra: is $\{X:\ X\text{ has fp-type at most }n\}=\mathrm{Thick}(\mathrm{BP}\langle n\rangle_p^\wedge)$, the closure under finite sums, shifts, cofiber sequences and retracts, for every $n$ and $p$?
problems.posedBy: Jeremy Hahn and Dylan Wilson (reported from 2021); written as Conjecture 1.1 in David Jongwon Lee and Piotr Pstragowski, The monochromatic Hahn-Wilson conjecture, Inventiones Mathematicae (2026)
problems.ageNote: The manuscript says Lee and Pstragowski give the written formulation (Conjecture 1.1 and Note 1) and report learning it from Dylan Wilson in 2021; yearPosed uses 2021. The first written statement is 2026.
problems.resultNote: Claims that for every sufficiently large prime $p$ there is a connective $p$-complete spectrum $X$ of exact fp-type two with $X\notin\mathrm{Thick}(\mathrm{BP}\langle2\rangle_p^\wedge)$ for a standard form of $\mathrm{BP}\langle2\rangle$, refuting the universally quantified conjecture at height two. The same $X$ satisfies $L_2^fX\simeq L_2X$ and $L_{T(2)}X\simeq L_{K(2)}X$, so the obstruction lies in how the chromatic pieces are glued, not in a telescope-type failure; the monochromatic form proved by Lee-Pstragowski is untouched. It does NOT treat small primes, heights above two, or the height-one case, which Lee-Pstragowski proved.

problems.name: The $N^{-1/4}$ law for the critical strip-crossing mass of honeycomb self-avoiding walk
problems.statement: On the honeycomb lattice at the critical weight $x_c=1/\sqrt{2+\sqrt2}$, let $B_N$ be the total weight of self-avoiding paths from a fixed boundary point of a strip of height $N$ to its opposite side. Duminil-Copin and Smirnov's parafermionic identity, which proved the value of the connective constant, gives $c/N\le B_N\le 1$. Lawler, Schramm and Werner's boundary exponent $5/8$ predicts a boundary-to-boundary mass of power $-5/4$, and summing over the far side predicts $B_N\approx N^{-1/4}$; Duminil-Copin and Smirnov state this prediction explicitly (Annals 2012, Section 4). Beaton, Bousquet-Melou, de Gier, Duminil-Copin and Guttmann proved $B_N\to0$, and Krachun and Panagiotis a polynomial upper bound with exponent $10^{-10}$. Is the critical strip-crossing mass of order $N^{-1/4}$?
problems.posedBy: Hugo Duminil-Copin and Stanislav Smirnov (explicit prediction, from the Lawler-Schramm-Werner boundary exponent)
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites Duminil-Copin and Smirnov, Ann. of Math. 175 (2012), Section 4, for the explicit prediction; the exponent goes back to Nienhuis (1982) and Lawler-Schramm-Werner (2004).
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every $N\ge1$ the strip sums are finite, $c\mathcal A_N+\mathcal B_N=1$ with $c=\cos(3\pi/8)$, $m_{N+1}-m_N\asymp\mathcal B_N$, the first rightward displacement moment of arches satisfies $m_N\asymp N^{3/4}$, and the bridge mass satisfies $\mathcal B_N\asymp N^{-1/4}$, nonincreasing in $N$, with constants independent of $N$. The route computes $m_N$ through rhombic transfer matrices and a positive integral, then recovers $\mathcal B_N$ from its increments. Not shown: a limiting constant for $N^{1/4}\mathcal B_N$, statements about walks of fixed length (treated in companions), or other lattices.

problems.name: Optimal-order mixing of the Thorp shuffle on $2^d$ cards: is the mixing time $O(\log n)$?
problems.field: Markov chain mixing times; card shuffling
problems.statement: The Thorp shuffle on $n=2^d$ cards cuts the deck into two halves, pairs the cards in corresponding positions, orders each pair by an independent fair coin, and interleaves the pairs. Each card is uniform after $d$ shuffles and a counting argument gives a lower bound of order $d$ for the whole permutation, while the known upper bounds were $O(d^{44})$ (Morris 2008), $O(d^{29})$ (Montenegro-Tetali) and $O(d^3)$ (Morris 2013). Is the total-variation mixing time of the full permutation $O(d)=O(\log n)$?
problems.posedBy: Line of work begun by Ben Morris (2008); the logarithmic order is discussed as the target in Johan Jonasson's notes (2009). The model is due to Edward O. Thorp (1973)
problems.ageNote: The manuscript does not attribute the O(log n) question to a named poser. It cites Morris's first polynomial bound (SIAM J. Comput. 2008), later improvements, and Jonasson, 'The Mathematics of Card Shuffling' (course notes, 2009, Section 5), for the logarithmic order. yearPosed is left empty because no single posing date is given.
problems.resultNote: Principal Theorem 1.1: for $n=2^d$, $\|q_d^{*1600d}-U_n\|_{TV}\to0$ as $d\to\infty$, uniformly over initial decks, and $\|q_d^{*t}-U_n\|_{TV}\ge1-2^{tn/2}/n!$, so $t_{mix}(d)\ge2d-O(1)$ and $t_{mix}(d)=\Theta(d)$. Companions give alternative proofs with other constants and the supporting Fourier and coordinate-sweep estimates. The constant 1600 is not claimed sharp; no cutoff or leading constant is determined, and the optimal-order question for general even deck sizes is explicitly not addressed.
problems.aiRole: The release README says all results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model using one fixed procedure, about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result on average. This result is not among the README's exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties, and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region whose write-up was human-edited). All eleven manuscripts are authored 'OpenAI' and name no human author. They give several routes to O(d) mixing with different constants (1600d in the principal paper; 512d, 2048d and unspecified absolute multiples in companions), plus supporting representation-theoretic estimates.

Checked here: the introduction and Theorem 1.1 of the principal manuscript were read against the question. lean/docs/238.md lists thirteen challenges. The solution file exists at the pinned commit. ThorpRemaining is not in the formalization catalogue; the catalogued BinarySweep, CoordinateSweeps, ThorpRouting and ThorpWeightedCompatibility state supporting sweep estimates, not the physical-shuffle mixing time. The statement was read here. Not rebuilt. Only deck sizes 2^d are covered.

problems.name: The Nam-Sly-Zhang conjecture: the free Ising state on the d-regular tree is a factor of IID up to the reconstruction threshold
problems.shortName: Free Ising on trees as a factor of IID
problems.field: Ergodic theory on trees; Ising model, factors of IID
problems.statement: Let $T_d$ be the infinite $d$-regular tree, $d\ge3$, and $\mu_{d,\beta}$ the free zero-field ferromagnetic Ising measure with $\theta=\tanh\beta$. A spin law is a factor of IID if it is the law of $\Phi(U)$ for IID uniform vertex labels $U$ and a measurable $\Phi$ commuting with tree automorphisms. Lyons (2017) studied which such Gibbs measures are factors of IID: the free state is one when $\theta\le1/(d-1)$, and Sly's argument shows it is not when $\theta>(d-1)^{-1/2}$, beyond the reconstruction threshold. Nam, Sly and Zhang (arXiv 2020, CMP 2022) proved it is a factor for $\theta\le c/\sqrt{d-1}$ and $d\ge d_0$ and conjectured the sharp threshold. Is $\mu_{d,\beta}$ a factor of IID for every $d\ge3$ whenever $\tanh\beta\le(d-1)^{-1/2}$, including equality?
problems.posedBy: D. Nam, A. Sly and L. Zhang, Ising model on trees and factors of IID (arXiv 2012.09484, 2020; Comm. Math. Phys. 2022), following R. Lyons, Factors of IID on trees (2017)
problems.ageNote: The Nam-Sly-Zhang preprint appeared in December 2020 and was published in 2022; Lyons's broader question on factor-of-IID Gibbs measures on trees dates from arXiv 2014, published 2017.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every $d\ge3$ and $\beta\ge0$, $\mu_{d,\beta}$ is a factor of IID if and only if $\tanh\beta\le(d-1)^{-1/2}$; the new part is the positive implication including equality, and the factor can be chosen to commute with every automorphism on every input. The converse is Sly's, as given by Lyons, with the Backhausz-Szegedy-Virag bound. The construction inverts the innovations of the Nam-Sly-Zhang stochastic-localization observation process. It does not treat antiferromagnetic or nonzero-field states, other Gibbs measures, or finitary factors.

The manuscript is authored 'OpenAI' and names no human author.

problems.name: Scale invariance implies local conformal invariance for a class of four-dimensional unitary QFTs
problems.field: Axiomatic quantum field theory: scale and conformal symmetry
problems.statement:
In a scale-invariant QFT with symmetric conserved stress tensor $T_{\mu
u}$, the dilatation current is $D_\mu=x^
u T_{\mu
u}-V_\mu$ with $T^\mu{}_\mu=\partial^\mu V_\mu$; the theory is conformal if $T$ can be improved to a traceless tensor, for instance when $\partial^\mu V_\mu=\Box L$ for a local scalar $L$. Zamolodchikov and Polchinski (1988) proved that scale implies conformal invariance in two-dimensional unitary theories under mild assumptions, and Polchinski raised the four-dimensional case. Perturbative results (Fortin-Grinstein-Stergiou, Jack-Osborn) and dilaton-based arguments (Luty-Polchinski-Rattazzi; Dymarsky-Komargodski-Schwimmer-Theisen) support it but leave gaps. In a four-dimensional unitary, positive-energy QFT with a Poincare- and scale-invariant vacuum, does scale invariance imply conformal invariance?
problems.posedBy: J. Polchinski, Scale and conformal invariance in quantum field theory, Nucl. Phys. B 303 (1988)
problems.ageNote: Polchinski's 1988 paper proved the two-dimensional case and discussed the four-dimensional question; the manuscript cites it with Zamolodchikov (1986) for the history. The question is also linked to earlier improvement work of Callan, Coleman and Jackiw (1970).
problems.resultNote:
Theorem 1.1: under the paper's framework (unitary, positive energy, Poincare- and scale-invariant vacuum, discrete bounded-below dimension spectrum with finite multiplicities, finite scaling support, bounded local net, physical stress tensor and virial current), there is a Hermitian dimension-two physical scalar $L$ with $\partial^\mu V^{(3)}_\mu=\Box L$, so $T^{(4)}_{\mu
u}+	frac13(\partial_\mu\partial_
u-\eta_{\mu
u}\Box)L$ is symmetric, conserved and traceless with unchanged translation and Lorentz charges, and conformal currents have unbroken local Ward identities. It does not treat theories outside these hypotheses (continuous spectra, no bounded net, no local virial current), and integration to a global conformal action on the net is left open.
problems.aiRole: The OpenAI math release (github.com/openai/math, commit adc7f12) states that its results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model under one fixed procedure, averaging about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result. This result is not among the README's stated exceptions (the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region write-up and the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties). The manuscript is credited to OpenAI alone and names no human author.
problems.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: the abstract, introduction and Theorem 1.1 of the TeX source, read against the scale-versus-conformal question as described in the manuscript's history section; the proof was not refereed. The theorem is conditional on the paper's standing framework assumption: a discrete, bounded-below spectrum of scaling dimensions with finite multiplicities, finite scaling support of every field, a causally commuting bounded local net with compatible affiliated field realizations, and a physical local dilatation current with local Ward identities. These hypotheses delimit the class and exclude the known free-field subtleties (e.g. shift-invariant scalar, noncompact two-form) by requiring the virial current to be a physical field. The conclusion is local; a global conformal action is not claimed. No Lean formalization is supplied for this family.
problems.significanceNote: The four-dimensional scale-versus-conformal question is a well-known open problem of quantum field theory, but this answers it only inside an axiomatic class whose hypotheses carry much of the weight, so it is scored as a conditional special case well below the parent. Placed with the lonely runner conjecture for nine and ten runners (30), below Cardy's formula for square-lattice bond percolation (48) and the partial Rohde-Schramm result (52).

problems.name: The dimension exponent of first-order query complexity for well-conditioned log-concave sampling
problems.statement:
Let $V\in C^2(\mathbb R^d)$ with $V(0)=0$, $
abla V(0)=0$ and $I_d\preceq
abla^2V\preceq2I_d$, and let $\pi_V\propto e^{-V}$. An algorithm queries $(V(x),
abla V(x))$ adaptively and must output a sample within total variation $\varepsilon$ of $\pi_V$. Chewi's book Log-Concave Sampling calls it a fundamental open question to determine, up to a universal constant, the minimum number of first-order queries needed uniformly over this class. Known upper bounds grew polynomially in $d$ (about $d^{1/2}$ for Langevin-type methods, $\widetilde O(d^{1/3})$, then $\widetilde O(d^{1/6})$ expected queries), and the lower bounds of Chewi et al. were logarithmic. What is the query complexity, and in particular, is a positive power of $d$ necessary at fixed accuracy?
problems.posedBy: Sinho Chewi, Log-Concave Sampling (book draft), preface: 'a fundamental open question about the complexity of log-concave sampling'
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites no posing source. The statement was read in the preface of the current draft of Chewi's book (version dated August 20, 2026); the year the question first appeared in the draft was not established here, so yearPosed is left null. Chewi, de Dios Pont, Li, Lu and Narayanan (2023) proved the first dimension-dependent lower bounds for this class.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: in the exact first-order oracle model with unrestricted computation between queries, for every $\varepsilon>0$ the worst-case query budget $Q(d)$ for TV error $1/10$ satisfies $Q(d)\le C_\varepsilon d^{\varepsilon}$ for all $d\ge2$, on every execution; and $Q(d)\ge c\log d$ for arbitrary randomized adaptive algorithms. Hence the optimal dimension exponent is $\gamma_*=0$. Not shown: the growth rate of $Q(d)$ beyond the exponent (no polylogarithmic bound is claimed), dependence on the accuracy or condition number, or any running-time bound; the constants and approximation orders depend on $\varepsilon$.
problems.aiRole: The release README says every result was produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model with a fixed procedure of roughly three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result. This family is not among the README's exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties, and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region, whose write-up was human-edited). The manuscripts are authored 'OpenAI' and name no human author. The family is a single manuscript dated September 26, 2026.
problems.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: the abstract, introduction and Theorem 1.1 were read against the question as stated in Chewi's book. The book asks for the complexity up to a universal constant at accuracy $\varepsilon$; the paper fixes TV accuracy 1/10 and determines only the dimension exponent, so this entry is partial. Lean: formalization.yaml lists ComparatorChallenges/LogConcaveQuery.json with declaration OAI.LogConcaveSampling.exact_source_main in OAI/Probability/LogConcave/Main.lean. The challenge statement was read: for admissible potentials (C2, V(0)=0, gradient zero at 0, Hessian between I and 2I), measurable randomized adaptive algorithms with a deterministic query budget, TV at most 1/10, it asserts queryComplexity(d) <= C d^eps for every eps>0, >= c log d eventually, and gammaStar = 0. That is the headline claim. Not rebuilt here. The paper states that computation between queries is unrestricted and no arithmetic or bit cost is bounded.

Placed below the KLS conjecture for quadratic forms (45) and the randomized versus quantum query conjecture (38), above the oracle-complexity gap in derivative-free convex optimization (15).

problems.name: Anticanonical nonvanishing for smooth projective varieties with smoothly semipositive anticanonical bundle
problems.statement: Let $X$ be a smooth connected complex projective variety whose anticanonical bundle $-K_X$ carries a smooth Hermitian metric of semipositive curvature (equivalently, by Yau's theorem, a Kahler metric of nonnegative Ricci curvature in that class). Such $-K_X$ is nef. Demailly-Peternell-Schneider and Campana-Demailly-Peternell described the universal cover of such $X$, but the existence of anticanonical sections was open in general; for nef log-anticanonical divisors it was known only in dimension three and under fiber semiampleness. The manuscript attaches the question to Yau's Problem 75. Does $H^0(X,-mK_X)\ne0$ for some integer $m>0$?
problems.posedBy: Shing-Tung Yau, Open problems in geometry (Lectures on Differential Geometry, 1994), Problem 75, as the manuscript cites it
problems.ageNote: The manuscript calls its theorem 'the positive-multiple formulation associated with' Yau's Problem 75; Yau's own wording was not available here and was not read.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: if $X$ is smooth connected complex projective and $-K_X$ admits a smooth Hermitian metric of semipositive curvature, then $H^0(X,-mK_X)\ne0$ for some $m>0$. The key intermediate result (Theorem 1.2) gives sections of $aL+bD$ on varieties without holomorphic forms from a finite-volume adjoint metric. Not shown: an effective bound on $m$, the case $m=1$ (false in general, e.g. Enriques surface times $\mathbb P^1$), or nonvanishing when $-K_X$ is only nef or carries a singular semipositive metric.
problems.aiRole: The release README says every result was produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model with a fixed procedure of roughly three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result. This family is not among the README's exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties, and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region, whose write-up was human-edited). The manuscripts are authored 'OpenAI' and name no human author. The family has seven manuscripts, all dated September 26, 2026. The principal one proves the headline from a finite-volume theorem by induction on dimension and a torus-invariant section on the rationally connected factor; companions give invariant indices, klt and torus-quotient versions, metric descent and effectivity with controlled boundary. One cited 2026 paper by other authors (Chen-Filip-Sun-Tosatti-Zhang) records that ChatGPT suggested a preliminary lemma; that is outside this release.

problems.name: Viehweg's conjecture C(n,m)+ and Popa's logarithmic Iitaka-Viehweg inequality
problems.field: Birational geometry, Kodaira dimension and variation
problems.statement: Viehweg's conjecture $C^+_{n,m}$ strengthens Iitaka's subadditivity by the birational variation of the family: for a fibre space $f:X\to Y$ of smooth projective varieties with $\kappa(Y)\ge0$, $\kappa(X)\ge\kappa(F)+\max\{\kappa(Y),\mathrm{Var}(f)\}$. Kollar proved it for fibres of general type and Kawamata for fibres with good minimal models. Popa (Conjecture 3.8 of his note Conjectures on the Kodaira dimension) asked for the logarithmic version: for a projective fibre space $f:U\to V$ of smooth quasi-projective varieties with $\bar\kappa(V)\ge0$ and generic fibre $F$, is $\bar\kappa(U)\ge\kappa(F)+\max\{\bar\kappa(V),\mathrm{Var}(f)\}$?
problems.posedBy: Mihnea Popa, Conjectures on the Kodaira dimension, Conjecture 3.8 (author version 2023; LMS LNS 489, 2025), generalising E. Viehweg's C(n,m)+ conjecture (1983)
problems.ageNote: The logarithmic form answered here is Popa's, cited to his 2023 author version (published 2025; his note mentions an earlier first version). The ordinary C(n,m)+ conjecture it contains goes back to Viehweg's work of the early 1980s, which the manuscript cites.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for a projective surjective morphism $f:U\to V$ with connected fibres between smooth connected complex quasi-projective varieties with $\bar\kappa(V)\ge0$ and geometric generic fibre $F$, $\bar\kappa(U)\ge\kappa(F)+\max\{\bar\kappa(V),\mathrm{Var}(f)\}$, with no good-minimal-model or abundance hypothesis on $F$. Corollary 1.2 gives Viehweg's ordinary $C^+_{n,m}$ for projective complex fibre spaces with $\kappa(Y)\ge0$. Not covered: bases with $\bar\kappa(V)=-\infty$, positive characteristic, and the additivity equalities for smooth families (a separate entry).

This manuscript uses the reduced-SNC subadditivity theorem and full-period adjoint comparison of the family's orbifold subadditivity paper as stated inputs, so it stands or falls with that entry as well.

problems.name: The effective log Iitaka conjecture for log canonical pairs with finite rational coefficient sets
problems.statement: Chen, Han and Liu conjectured a logarithmic version of effective Iitaka fibrations: for fixed dimension $d$ and a DCC set $\Phi\subset[0,1]$, one integer $m$ should make the rounded system $|\lfloor m(K_X+B)\rfloor|$ nonempty with section ratios generating the Iitaka field, for every projective lc pair $(X,B)$ of dimension $d$ with coefficients in $\Phi$ and nonnegative Kodaira dimension. They proved it in dimension at most three. Does it hold in every dimension when $\Phi$ is a finite set of rationals?
problems.posedBy: G. Chen, J. Han and J. Liu, On effective log Iitaka fibrations and existence of complements (IMRN 2024; arXiv 2301.04813), Conjecture 1.2
problems.ageNote: Posed in the January 2023 arXiv version; published in IMRN in 2024.
problems.resultNote: 'Uniform effective log Iitaka fibrations for fourfolds' (September 26): for normal projective lc complex fourfolds with coefficients in a fixed finite rational set and pseudo-effective rational Cartier adjoint, one degree makes the rounded system nonempty with section ratios generating the Iitaka field; it also bounds the canonical index of klt Calabi-Yau fourfolds. 'Uniform log Iitaka fibrations and bounded moduli denominators' (October 4): the same conclusion for $d\ge5$ over any algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, with bounded Cartier denominators for moduli divisors. Not shown: the DCC case of the conjecture in dimension four or more.

problems.name: Popa's logarithmic additivity conjecture for log-smooth families
problems.field: Birational geometry, Kodaira dimension of smooth families
problems.statement: For smooth families, subadditivity of Kodaira dimension is expected to become equality. Popa (Conjecture 3.9 of Conjectures on the Kodaira dimension) asked: let $f:X\to Y$ be an algebraic fibre space between smooth projective varieties, $E$ an SNC divisor on $X$ and $D$ an SNC divisor on $Y$ with $\mathrm{Supp}(f^*D)\subseteq E$, and assume $f$ is log-smooth over $V=Y\setminus D$ (each stratum of $(X,E)$, including $X$, is smooth over $V$). For a general fibre $F$ over $V$, is $\kappa(X,K_X+E)=\kappa(Y,K_Y+D)+\kappa(F,K_F+E_F)$? It generalises his Conjecture 3.1 for smooth projective fibre spaces $U\to V$ of quasi-projective varieties, known when the base is of log general type, a curve, or compactifies to an abelian variety, or when $F$ has semiample canonical bundle.
problems.posedBy: Mihnea Popa, Conjectures on the Kodaira dimension, Conjecture 3.9 and footnote 5 (author version 13 June 2023; LMS Lecture Note Series 489, 2025)
problems.ageNote: Dated to the 13 June 2023 author version the manuscript cites; the note was published in 2025 and mentions an earlier first version whose date the manuscripts do not give.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: under Popa's hypotheses (reduced SNC $E$, $D$, support inclusion, stratum smoothness over $V$), $\kappa(X,K_X+E)\le\kappa(Y,K_Y+D)+\kappa(F,K_F+E_F)$, and if either term on the right is $-\infty$ every $H^0(X,m(K_X+E))$ vanishes; no abundance or good-model hypothesis. With the family's logarithmic subadditivity this gives equality, Corollary 1.2. Either divisor may be zero, which covers additivity for smooth projective morphisms; the paper itself claims only Conjecture 3.9. Not covered: families that are not log-smooth over the open base.

problems.name: The Ara-Maltsiniotis conjecture: Thomason model structures on strict n-categories for every n
problems.field: Homotopy theory; strict higher categories and model structures
problems.statement: Thomason (1980) put a model structure on small categories, transferred from simplicial sets along $c_1\mathrm{Sd}^2\dashv\mathrm{Ex}^2N_1$, that is Quillen equivalent to simplicial sets. For strict globular $n$-categories, $1\le n\le\infty$, with the Street nerve $N_n$ built from orientals, Ara and Maltsiniotis (2014) proved the case $n=2$, reduced the general case to two conditions, and conjectured the general statement; Ara (2023) and Guetta-Maltsiniotis (2024) restate it. Is there, for every $n$ including $\omega$, a model structure on small strict $n$-categories whose weak equivalences and fibrations are those maps sent by $\mathrm{Ex}^2N_n$ to weak equivalences and Kan fibrations, and is $c_n\mathrm{Sd}^2\dashv\mathrm{Ex}^2N_n$ a Quillen equivalence with simplicial sets?

problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every $n\in\{1,2,\dots\}\cup\{\infty\}$, the classes $W_n=N_n^{-1}(W_{KQ})$, $F_n=(\mathrm{Ex}^2N_n)^{-1}(\mathrm{Fib}_{KQ})$ and $C_n={}^{\perp}(F_n\cap W_n)$ form a proper combinatorial model structure on small strict $n$-categories, cofibrantly generated by the images of boundary and horn inclusions under $c_n\mathrm{Sd}^2$, and $c_n\mathrm{Sd}^2\dashv\mathrm{Ex}^2N_n$ is a Quillen equivalence with Kan-Quillen simplicial sets. The key step proves the Ara-Maltsiniotis pushout condition (Scholie 5.14 (d')). It concerns strict globular categories only, not weak higher categories or n-fold categories.

problems.name: Is block sensitivity at most quadratic in sensitivity? (Nisan-Szegedy)
problems.statement: For a total Boolean function $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$, the sensitivity $s(f)$ is the largest number of single bits whose flip changes $f$ at some input, and the block sensitivity $\mathrm{bs}(f)$ the largest number of disjoint blocks of bits each of whose flip changes $f$ at some input. Nisan and Szegedy (1994) explicitly suggested $\mathrm{bs}(f)\le s(f)^2$. Rubinstein's functions give $\mathrm{bs}=s^2/2$, improved to $\frac23s^2-\frac13s$ by Ambainis and Sun (2011); Huang's 2019 proof of the Sensitivity Conjecture gives $\mathrm{bs}(f)\le s(f)^4$. Is there a universal constant $C$ with $\mathrm{bs}(f)\le C\,s(f)^2$ for every total Boolean function?
problems.posedBy: Noam Nisan and Mario Szegedy (Section 4, Computational Complexity 1994)
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every integer $d\ge1$ an explicit recursive construction gives a nonconstant total Boolean function with $\mathrm{bs}(f)/s(f)^2\ge2^d/(4(d+2)^2)$, so no bound $\mathrm{bs}\le C s^2$ holds; the abstract also claims a fixed $\alpha>2$ with $\mathrm{bs}(f)\ge s(f)^\alpha$ along an unbounded family. This does not close the gap to Huang's upper bound $\mathrm{bs}\le s^4$; the true exponent remains open. Because $\lambda(f)\le s(f)$, it also implies a negative answer to the spectral-sensitivity question $\mathrm{bs}=O(\lambda^2)$, which Meiburg had already disproved (see block-sensitivity-spectral-sensitivity-squared).

problems.name: Homogeneous depth-five lower bounds for iterated matrix multiplication with unrestricted bottom fan-in (Bera-Chakrabarti question, balanced regime)
problems.field: Algebraic complexity; arithmetic circuit lower bounds
problems.statement: Let $\mathrm{IMM}_{w,d}$ be the $(1,1)$ entry of a product of $d$ generic $w\times w$ matrices. Nisan and Wigderson (1995) asked for superpolynomial lower bounds for homogeneous $\Sigma\Pi\Sigma\Pi\Sigma$ circuits, and Kayal and Saha asked for depth-five bounds for IMM. Bera and Chakrabarti (CCC 2015) proved that homogeneous $\Sigma\Pi\Sigma\Pi\Sigma$ circuits computing $\mathrm{IMM}_{n^q,n}$ in $N$ variables need $N^{\Omega(\sqrt n)}$ gates, but only when every bottom linear form has fan-in at most $N^{\mu}$ with $\mu<1/2$. They called it the most immediate and natural open question whether the bound survives bottom fan-in up to $N^{1-\Theta(1)}$ or $N$, the general case. Does the $\sqrt n$-exponent lower bound for homogeneous depth-five circuits computing IMM hold with unrestricted bottom fan-in?
problems.posedBy: Suman K. Bera and Amit Chakrabarti, A Depth-Five Lower Bound for Iterated Matrix Multiplication (CCC 2015), closing open question; background question of Nisan and Wigderson (1995)
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites Nisan-Wigderson (1995) and Bera-Chakrabarti (2015) but quotes no posing sentence; the closing sentence of Bera-Chakrabarti was read here. Superpolynomial depth-five lower bounds over characteristic zero already follow from Limaye-Srinivasan-Tavenas (2021), so what remained open was the sharp $\sqrt n$ exponent with unrestricted bottom forms.
problems.resultNote: Claims that over every field of characteristic zero every syntactically homogeneous $\Sigma\Pi\Sigma\Pi\Sigma$ circuit computing $\mathrm{IMM}_{n,n}$ has at least $n^{\sqrt n/400}$ gates for large $n$, with gate sharing, arbitrary fan-in and bottom linear forms of arbitrary support allowed, and a block construction gives $n^{\sqrt n+4}$ over every field, so the gate complexity is $n^{\Theta(\sqrt n)}$. The measure is the rank of a partial-derivative-times-multiplication operator. It does NOT treat the Bera-Chakrabarti regime $\mathrm{IMM}_{n^q,n}$ directly, positive characteristic, non-homogeneous circuits, or depths beyond five.
