problems.name: The PCP-for-PPAD conjecture of Babichenko, Papadimitriou and Rubinstein (quasilinear form)
problems.field: Computational complexity; PPAD and equilibrium computation
problems.statement: End-of-Line is the canonical PPAD-complete problem: given successor and predecessor circuits on $\{0,1\}^n$ with a known source, find another endpoint. A generalized circuit asks for an assignment of values in $[0,1]$ to wires that $\varepsilon$-satisfies local arithmetic, comparison and Boolean gates. Rubinstein proved PPAD-hardness for constant $\varepsilon$ when every gate must be satisfied. Babichenko, Papadimitriou and Rubinstein (2016) conjectured a PCP analogue: are there constants $\varepsilon,\delta>0$ and a quasilinear-size reduction from End-of-Line to generalized circuits such that any assignment $\varepsilon$-satisfying all but a $\delta$ fraction of gates, wherever the failures lie, yields an End-of-Line solution in polynomial time?
problems.posedBy: Yakov Babichenko, Christos Papadimitriou and Aviad Rubinstein, Conjecture 2 of 'Can almost everybody be almost happy?' (ITCS 2016)
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there are fixed rational $0<\varepsilon<1/10$ and $0<\delta<1$, and deterministic polynomial-time algorithms $R,D$, such that $R$ maps an End-of-Line instance of length $N$ to a generalized circuit of total binary length at most $AN\lceil\log_2(N+2)\rceil^b$, every generalized circuit has an acceptable rational assignment of polynomially bounded length, and from any such assignment $\varepsilon$-satisfying all but a $\delta$ fraction of gates $D$ recovers an End-of-Line solution. This also implies the weaker polynomial-size PCP-for-PPAD statement. It does not by itself give new Nash lower bounds; those (Rubinstein, Golowich) still need an exponential-time hypothesis for PPAD.

problems.name: Does the exact discrete Fourier transform require order n log n operations in unrestricted linear circuits?
problems.shortName: The n log n lower bound for the DFT
problems.field: Algebraic complexity; arithmetic circuits for the Fourier transform
problems.statement: The fast Fourier transform computes $F_n=(\zeta_n^{jk})$ with $O(n\log n)$ arithmetic operations, and no asymptotically faster method was known. Matching lower bounds were proved only in restricted models: Morgenstern for linear circuits with bounded coefficients, Ailon for unitary two-coordinate gates or bounded intermediate conditioning. In the unrestricted model, a linear circuit uses gates $u+v$, $u-v$ and $\lambda u$ with arbitrary fixed complex $\lambda$, each costing one, and must output $F_nx$ exactly for every $x$. Is the minimum size $L(n)$ of such a circuit at least $cn\log n$ for some $c>0$ and all large $n$, or can the Fourier transform be computed exactly with $o(n\log n)$ operations?
problems.posedBy: Long-standing open question in algebraic complexity; discussed by Ailon (2013) and Alman and Rao (2023)
problems.ageNote: The manuscripts give no posing date. They cite Ailon (2013, abstract) and Alman-Rao (2023, Section 1) for the question; the restricted lower bound it contrasts with is Morgenstern (1973).
problems.resultNote: Principal (Theorem 1.1): in exact complex linear circuits with arbitrary prechosen coefficients, $\liminf_n L(n)/(n\log_2 n)=0$, along lengths that are products of distinct primes, so the unrestricted $\Omega(n\log n)$ lower bound is false. Companion (Theorem 1.1): one deterministic algorithm computes $F_nx$ at every length in $O(n(\log n)^{\theta}(\log\log n)^{4-\theta})$ operations with $\theta<1-10^{-13}$, counting scalar preparation and indexing, given one specified root of unity. Neither result concerns bounded coefficients (where Morgenstern's bound stands), numerical stability, bit complexity or finite fields, and the constants are astronomically large.

problems.name: Polynomial complementation of two-way nondeterministic finite automata
problems.statement: A two-way nondeterministic finite automaton (2NFA) has one read-only head moving in both directions between endmarkers. Deterministic two-way automata can be complemented with linearly many states (Geffert, Mereghetti and Pighizzini 2007), and Vardi (1989) complemented 2NFAs into exponential one-way automata. Kapoutsis (ICALP 2006) proved that small sweeping 2NFAs are not closed under complement, leaving unrestricted 2NFAs open. Is there a polynomial $p$, independent of the alphabet, such that for every $n$-state 2NFA over a finite alphabet the complementary language is recognized by a 2NFA with at most $p(n)$ states?
problems.posedBy: Open question in two-way automata state complexity; the manuscript cites it as open in Guillon, Prigioniero and Taheri (STACS 2026), after Kapoutsis's sweeping case (2006)

problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every $n\ge4$ there is an $n$-state 2NFA $A_n$ for relation-product liveness on $n-2$ points such that every 2NFA for its complement has at least $\tfrac12 2^{\lfloor(n-4)/127\rfloor}-1$ states. Corollary: every 2DFA for the same language needs $\tfrac12 2^{\lfloor(n-4)/127\rfloor}$ states when $n\ge131$. The alphabet has $2^{(n-2)^2}$ letters, so the result says nothing about complementation over a fixed alphabet, about transition-table size, or about uniform logarithmic-space classes.

problems.name: Gersten's conjecture: are Baumslag-Solitar-free one-relator groups hyperbolic?
problems.statement: The Baumslag-Solitar groups $\mathrm{BS}(m,n)=\langle a,t\mid ta^mt^{-1}=a^n\rangle$, $m,n\ne0$, are the basic obstructions to word-hyperbolicity among one-relator groups: a hyperbolic group contains none of them. Gersten asked whether they are the only subgroup obstructions. Known cases included proper-power relators (Newman's spelling theorem), relators of primitivity rank other than two (Louder-Wilton, Linton) and ascending HNN extensions of free groups (Mutanguha). Let $G=\langle X\mid r\rangle$ with $X$ finite. If $G$ contains no subgroup isomorphic to $\mathrm{BS}(m,n)$ for any nonzero $m,n$, must $G$ be word-hyperbolic?
problems.posedBy: S. M. Gersten, 'Problems on automatic groups' (MSRI Publications 23, p. 228)
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: if a one-relator group $\langle X\mid r\rangle$, $X$ finite, contains no $\mathrm{BS}(m,n)$ with $m,n\ne0$, it is word-hyperbolic. The technical core is a combination theorem for a class of HNN extensions of torsion-free hyperbolic groups with free, possibly proper edge groups, applied along the Magnus-Moldavanskii hierarchy. Combined with the companion and with Kielak-Linton, Corollary: every Baumslag-Solitar-free one-relator group is virtually free-by-cyclic, with a finite-index embedding in a free-by-$\mathbb Z$ group with finitely generated kernel. The paper does not treat infinitely generated or multi-relator groups. Unrelated to the K-theoretic Gersten conjecture addressed in family 209 of the same release.

problems.statement: In complex dimension one, a complete simply connected surface with curvature bounded above by a negative constant is biholomorphic to the disc. H. Wu (1967) asked whether a complete simply connected Kahler manifold with nonpositive sectional curvature and holomorphic sectional curvature bounded above by a negative constant must be biholomorphic to a bounded domain. Wu and Yau (2019, Conjecture 4.3) state the two-sided version: if a simply connected complete Kahler manifold $M$ of complex dimension $n$ has every real sectional curvature between two negative constants, $-B\le K\le -A<0$, must $M$ be biholomorphic to a bounded (pseudoconvex) domain in $\mathbb C^n$?
problems.posedBy: H. Wu (1967, normal families paper, p. 195, question (1)); two-sided pinched form by Damin Wu and S.-T. Yau (2019 survey, Conjecture 4.3)
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites Wu's 1967 question as the early formulation and the Wu-Yau 2019 survey for the two-sided pinched conjecture it disproves; 1967 is the earliest date it gives.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there is a contractible domain $M\subset\mathbb C^3$ (a Hartogs-type disc bundle over the unit ball of $\mathbb C^2$) with a smooth complete Kahler metric whose real sectional curvatures satisfy $-B\le K\le -A<0$, such that no bounded holomorphic map $M\to\mathbb C^3$ has nowhere-vanishing Jacobian; hence $M$ is not biholomorphic to any bounded domain. This disproves Wu-Yau Conjecture 4.3 and gives a negative answer under the hypotheses of Wu's 1967 question. It does not show absence of bounded holomorphic functions (two base coordinates are bounded), and the example is Stein. Only complex dimension three is constructed.

The challenge statement was read here: there exist an open, nonempty, contractible set $M\subset\mathbb C^2\times\mathbb C$ and a smooth Kahler metric on it that is geodesically complete with all real sectional curvatures in $[-B,-A]$, $0<A\le B$, such that no bounded holomorphic map to $\mathbb C^3$ has nowhere-vanishing Jacobian and $M$ is not biholomorphic to a bounded domain. problems.name: The satisfiability threshold conjecture: a limiting random k-SAT threshold for every k >= 3
problems.field: Random constraint satisfaction; random k-SAT phase transition
problems.statement: Fix $k\ge3$ and let $F_{n,m}$ be a conjunction of $m$ independent uniformly random $k$-clauses on $n$ Boolean variables (distinct variables in a clause, fair signs). Friedgut (with Bourgain) proved a sharp threshold: there is a sequence $c_k(n)$ around which the satisfiability probability drops from near one to near zero, but not that $c_k(n)$ converges. Ding, Sly and Sun proved convergence, with the predicted value, for all sufficiently large $k$; the case $k=2$ is classical. Chvatal and Reed conjectured that each fixed clause size has a limiting density. Is there, for every fixed $k\ge3$, a constant $\alpha_k$ such that $\Pr(F_{n,\lfloor cn\rfloor}\text{ satisfiable})\to1$ for $c<\alpha_k$ and $\to0$ for $c>\alpha_k$?
problems.posedBy: Vasek Chvatal and Bruce Reed (Mick gets some (the odds are on his side), FOCS 1992)
problems.resultNote: Claims Theorem 1.1: for every fixed $k\ge3$ there is $\alpha_k\in(0,\infty)$ with $\Pr(F_{n,\lfloor cn\rfloor}\in\mathrm{SAT})\to1$ for $c<\alpha_k$ and $\to0$ for $c>\alpha_k$; it says nothing at $c=\alpha_k$ and does not identify $\alpha_k$ for small $k$. Companions claim hitting-time variance $\Theta_k(n)$ for $k\ge4$ and $\Theta(n)$ for $k=3$, and that $\alpha_3$ is a computable real. Priority: the release credits Gaia Carenini's ECCC TR26-229 (made public 5 October 2026) with first resolving the existence conjecture; this is an independent second proof of the same result, not a contradiction. Carenini's paper states that none of its mathematical arguments was generated by a large language model; it proves the existence via a scaling window of width $O(n^{1/2+1/k})$ and the Abbe-Montanari criterion.

The release itself credits Gaia Carenini (ECCC TR26-229, public 5 October 2026) with priority for the threshold-existence result and presents this family as an alternative proof plus sharper variance and computability results.

problems.name: The Friedgut-Kalai sharp-threshold conjecture: threshold width O(1/log^2 n) for monotone graph properties
problems.field: Random graphs, analysis of Boolean functions
problems.statement: For a nontrivial increasing graph property $P$ on $n$ vertices and $0<\varepsilon<1/2$, let $p_a$ be the edge probability at which $G(n,p)$ has $P$ with probability $a$. Friedgut and Kalai (1996), combining the KKL and BKKKL influence theorems with Russo's formula, proved $p_{1-\varepsilon}-p_\varepsilon\le C\log(1/2\varepsilon)/\log n$, observed that containing a clique of size about $\log n$ has width of order $(\log n)^{-2}$, and conjectured that this is the truth (Conjecture 1.2). Bourgain and Kalai reached $(\log n)^{-2+\delta}$ for every $\delta>0$. Is $p_{1-\varepsilon}-p_\varepsilon\le C\log(1/2\varepsilon)/(\log n)^2$ for every such property, with $C$ universal?
problems.posedBy: Ehud Friedgut and Gil Kalai
problems.ageNote: Friedgut-Kalai, Proc. AMS 124 (1996), Conjecture 1.2.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every $n\ge2$, nontrivial increasing vertex-symmetric graph property and $0<\varepsilon<1/2$, $p_{1-\varepsilon}-p_\varepsilon\le2^{19}\log(1/(2\varepsilon))/(\log n)^2$. It follows from Theorem 1.2, $\mathrm{Var}_p(f)\le2^{17}I_p(f)/(\log n)^2$ for every vertex-symmetric Boolean $f$ and every $0<p<1$, without monotonicity, which removes the $(\log\log n)^2$ loss of Kelman-Kindler-Lifshitz-Minzer-Safra at $p=1/2$. The order is optimal for fixed $\varepsilon$ (clique example). Not shown: the best constant, or where thresholds lie (a different question).

problems.name: The Erdős-Faudree-Rousseau-Schelp cycle-clique conjecture: $R(C_m,K_n)=(m-1)(n-1)+1$ for $m\ge n\ge3$
problems.statement: Let $R(C_m,K_n)$ be the least $N$ such that every red-blue colouring of the edges of $K_N$ contains a red cycle of length exactly $m$ or a blue $K_n$. Taking $n-1$ disjoint red cliques of order $m-1$ with all edges between them blue gives $R(C_m,K_n)\ge(m-1)(n-1)+1$. Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau and Schelp (1978) conjectured equality for $m\ge n\ge3$, apart from $R(C_3,K_3)=6$. Bondy and Erdős proved it for $m\ge n^2-2$, Nikiforov for $m\ge4n+2$, it was settled for $n\le7$, and Keevash, Long and Skokan (2021) proved it for $m\ge C\log n/\log\log n$ with an unspecified absolute constant, leaving finitely many pairs that could not be listed. Is $R(C_m,K_n)=(m-1)(n-1)+1$ for all $m\ge n\ge3$ with $(m,n)\ne(3,3)$?
problems.posedBy: Paul Erdős, Ralph Faudree, Cecil Rousseau and Richard Schelp (J. Graph Theory 1978); Erdős Problem #551
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1: $R(C_m,K_n)=(m-1)(n-1)+1$ for every $m\ge n\ge3$ other than $(3,3)$, where $R(C_3,K_3)=6$. The proof takes a minimal counterexample (independent sets expand), finds a clique of order at least $\max\{3,\lfloor k/2\rfloor\}$, optimizes path systems between clique vertices, and reduces the rest to 3,099 finite instances excluded by two exact programs. Keevash-Long-Skokan had already left only finitely many pairs open, without an explicit list; this result closes all of them. It does not address the side questions recorded with Problem #551 for fixed $n$ (the least cycle length at which the identity holds when $m<n$ is allowed, and the minimum of $R(C_k,K_n)$ over $k$).

problems.name: The Kirchberg-Rordam character question: does absence of characters on the central sequence algebra characterize Jiang-Su stability?
problems.field: Operator algebras; Jiang-Su stability and central sequences
problems.statement: For a nonzero unital separable C*-algebra $A$ and a free ultrafilter $\omega$, let $F_\omega(A)=A_\omega\cap A'$ be the norm central-sequence algebra. Kirchberg and Rordam proved $A\cong A\otimes\mathcal Z$ exactly when $F_\omega(A)$ contains, with the same unit, a separable subhomogeneous algebra without characters; absence of characters on $F_\omega(A)$ is then necessary. They asked (Question 3.1) whether it is sufficient, and related it to tensor powers (Question 3.7); the question reappears as Problem LXXX of Schafhauser, Tikuisis and White. Is $A$ Jiang-Su stable whenever $F_\omega(A)$ has no characters?
problems.posedBy: Eberhard Kirchberg and Mikael Rordam (When central sequence C*-algebras have characters, Internat. J. Math. 26 (2015), Questions 3.1 and 3.7); listed as Problem LXXX by Schafhauser, Tikuisis and White
problems.ageNote: The Kirchberg-Rordam paper appeared on arXiv in 2014 (1409.1395) and in print in 2015.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every nonzero unital separable complex C*-algebra $A$ and every free ultrafilter $\omega$, $F_\omega(A)$ has no characters iff $A\cong A\otimes_{\min}\mathcal Z$; no nuclearity, simplicity, trace or comparison hypothesis. Theorem 1.2: every nonzero unital characterless $D$ admits a unital map $I(2,3)\to D^{\otimes_{\max}m}$ for some $m$. Corollary: the infinite minimal tensor power of a nonzero unital separable characterless algebra is $\mathcal Z$-stable (bearing on Kirchberg-Rordam Question 3.7, via Dadarlat-Toms). Not shown: any finite tensor power is $\mathcal Z$-stable, or nonseparable cases.

problems.name: Villani's conjecture: weak Ma-Trudinger-Wang curvature implies convex tangent injectivity domains on compact manifolds
problems.field: Riemannian geometry and optimal transport regularity
problems.statement: Let $(M,g)$ be a compact connected Riemannian manifold without boundary, $c=d^2/2$, and $I(x)\subset T_xM$ the open tangent injectivity domain. The Ma-Trudinger-Wang tensor $\mathfrak S_{(x,v)}(\xi,\eta)$ is a fourth derivative of $c$; weak MTW (A3w) requires $\mathfrak S_{(x,v)}(\xi,\eta)\ge0$ whenever $\langle\xi,\eta\rangle=0$. Weak MTW is necessary for continuity of optimal transport maps (Loeper), and regularity theory (Figalli-Rifford-Villani) needed convex injectivity domains as an extra hypothesis. Villani proposed that weak MTW should by itself force convexity of every $I(x)$; Loeper-Villani proved convexity under strong MTW with nonfocality, and Figalli-Gallouet-Rifford proved the implication for nonfocal manifolds, where cut points come strictly before conjugate points. Does weak MTW imply that $I(x)$ is convex for every $x\in M$, with no nonfocality assumption?
problems.posedBy: C. Villani, Regularity of optimal transport and cut locus: from nonsmooth analysis to geometry to smooth analysis, Discrete Contin. Dyn. Syst. 30 (2011), Section 4.2
problems.ageNote: The manuscript says the result resolves Villani's conjecture 'in this setting', that is compact boundaryless manifolds of dimension at least two, which is the setting of the cited conjecture.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: if $(M,g)$ is smooth, connected, compact, boundaryless, of dimension $n\ge2$, and satisfies weak MTW on orthogonal pairs, then every tangent injectivity domain $I(x)$ is convex, and so is the closed minimizing domain; conjugate cut points are allowed. Theorem 1.2 adds global supporting mountains at every subgradient of a $c$-convex potential and $C^{1,1}$ intermediate-time geometry, with no density hypothesis. Companion: uniform bi-Holder estimates for optimal maps and their inverses over all densities pinched between fixed positive bounds. Not shown: strict convexity or boundary regularity of $I(x)$, noncompact manifolds, or constants uniform over varying metrics.

problems.name: The sharp constant for the terminal leave of random triangle removal (triangle case of the Joos-Kühn conjecture)
problems.field: Random graph processes; random greedy packing
problems.statement: Start from $K_n$ and repeatedly delete the three edges of a uniformly random remaining triangle until none is left; let $F_n$ be the number of edges remaining. Bollobas and Erdos conjectured (1990) that $F_n$ has order $n^{3/2}$; after work of Spencer, Rodl-Thoma and Grable, Bohman, Frieze and Lubetzky proved $F_n=n^{3/2+o(1)}$ with high probability (2015). Joos and Kuhn (2024) studied removal of a general strictly balanced hypergraph and conjectured (Conjecture 16.2) an asymptotic constant for the terminal leave, whose triangle case predicts $F_n/n^{3/2}\to 1/(2\sqrt2)$ in probability. Is that so?
problems.posedBy: Felix Joos and Marcus Kühn (Conjecture 16.2 of The hypergraph removal process); order of magnitude conjectured by Bollobás and Erdős (1990)
problems.ageNote: arXiv 2412.15039, first version 19 December 2024; the manuscript cites the conjecture's numbering from version 2. The Bollobas-Erdos order-of-magnitude conjecture is cited through Bohman-Frieze-Lubetzky (2015).
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for uniform triangle removal from $K_n$, $\mathbb E[(F_n/n^{3/2}-1/(2\sqrt2))^2]\to0$; hence $F_n/n^{3/2}\to1/(2\sqrt2)$ in probability and $\mathbb E F_n/n^{3/2}\to1/(2\sqrt2)$. The paper says it does not give the sharp constant for other starting graphs, for general hypergraph removal (the rest of Joos-Kuhn Conjecture 16.2), or a fluctuation law.

problems.name: Is every word-hyperbolic group CAT(0)?
problems.field: Geometric group theory; CAT(0) and CAT(-1) groups
problems.statement: A group is CAT(0) (respectively CAT(-1)) if it acts geometrically, that is properly, cocompactly and by isometries, on a proper complete CAT(0) (respectively CAT(-1)) space. Word-hyperbolic groups are characterised by a linear isoperimetric inequality, a coarse form of negative curvature, and Gromov sought geometric realisations of them by negatively curved spaces. Free groups, closed hyperbolic manifold groups and many cubulated groups are CAT(0); Brady and Crisp found hyperbolic groups with no such action in dimension two. Does every hyperbolic group act geometrically on a proper CAT(0) space, or even a proper CAT(-1) space?
problems.posedBy: M. Gromov (realisation question); CAT(-1) form as Problem H11 in Baumslag-Myasnikov-Shpilrain, Open problems in combinatorial group theory (1999); both forms in E. Stark (2025)
problems.ageNote: 1999 is the earliest printed record the manuscript cites (Baumslag-Myasnikov-Shpilrain, CAT(-1) form); the CAT(0) form is cited from Stark's 2025 survey and Duchesne-Simon (2026), and the question goes back to Gromov's work on hyperbolic groups in the 1980s by his own account.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there is a finite connected two-dimensional aspherical simplicial complex $K$ with linear combinatorial disk filling, so $\pi_1K$ is word-hyperbolic with a finite classifying space, such that $\pi_1K$ has no geometric action on any proper complete CAT(0) space in any dimension. Hence it is neither CAT(0) nor CAT(-1), and no finite complex homotopy equivalent to $K$ carries a locally CAT(0) metric inducing its topology. problems.name: Are hyperbolic one-relator groups virtually compact special?
problems.field: Geometric group theory; special cube complexes
problems.statement: A group is virtually compact special if a finite-index subgroup is the fundamental group of a compact nonpositively curved cube complex admitting a local isometry to the Salvetti complex of a right-angled Artin group; for hyperbolic groups this gives residual finiteness, linearity and separability of quasiconvex subgroups. Wise proved it for one-relator groups with torsion (answering Baumslag's 1967 residual-finiteness question for that class) and asked, in his question on cocompact cubulation of hyperbolic groups with hierarchies, about hyperbolic one-relator groups in general. Linton settled the case where all two-generator subgroups are free. Is every word-hyperbolic one-relator group $F(X)/\langle\langle r\rangle\rangle$ virtually compact special?
problems.posedBy: Daniel T. Wise, 'The cubical route to understanding groups', ICM 2014 (Problem 13.15)
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites Wise's ICM 2014 Problem 13.15, a broader cubulation question in which Wise singled out hyperbolic one-relator groups, and Wise's Conjecture 17.8 (virtually free-by-cyclic) as recalled by Kielak-Linton. Baumslag's 1967 Conjecture A is the older residual-finiteness question for the torsion case only.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: every word-hyperbolic one-relator group is virtually compact special. Theorem 1.2: every hyperbolic ascending mapping torus of an injective endomorphism of a finitely generated free group is virtually compact special. With Kielak-Linton, every hyperbolic one-relator group is virtually free-by-cyclic (kernel possibly of infinite rank in the subgroup-closed sense, with a finite-index embedding in a free-by-$\mathbb Z$ group with finitely generated kernel), which is Wise's Conjecture 17.8 for this class, and every hyperbolic one-relator group is residually finite and linear over $\mathbb Z$. It says nothing about non-hyperbolic one-relator groups. Consistent with the release's non-residually-finite hyperbolic group (catalog entry on residual finiteness), which is not one-relator.

problems.name: The Basso-Farhi-Marwaha-Villalonga-Zhou conjecture: QAOA attains the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick ground-state energy as depth grows
problems.shortName: QAOA eventual Parisi optimality on SK
problems.statement: For the zero-field Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model the expected QAOA energy per spin at fixed depth $p$ and fixed angles has an infinite-size limit $v_p(\gamma,\beta)$ (Farhi-Goldstone-Gutmann-Zhou), and $Q_p=\sup v_p$ cannot exceed the Parisi ground-state value $P_*$. Fixed-instance optimality as depth grows (Farhi-Goldstone-Gutmann) gives no depth uniform in system size. Basso, Farhi, Marwaha, Villalonga and Zhou, relating the limit to QAOA on large-girth regular graphs, conjectured that increasing depth eventually reaches the Parisi optimum; numerics (Boulebnane et al., Sels-Morone) supported it. Is $\lim_{p\to\infty}Q_p=P_*$?
problems.posedBy: J. Basso, E. Farhi, K. Marwaha, B. Villalonga and L. Zhou (The QAOA at high depth for MaxCut on large-girth regular graphs and the SK model, TQC 2022, Section 7, Eq. (7.2))
problems.ageNote: The conjecture is in the arXiv version 2110.14206 (October 2021), published at TQC 2022.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: $\lim_{p\to\infty}Q_p=P_*$ for the zero-field SK model; for every $\varepsilon>0$ some finite depth and deterministic angles, independent of $n$ and the disorder, reach expected energy per spin $\ge P_*-\varepsilon$ in the limit $n\to\infty$ taken first, with the standard cost Hamiltonian and transverse-field mixer. It also gives leading-order optimal expected MaxCut on large-degree random regular graphs (size before degree). Not given: any depth bound, finite-size estimate, efficient angle selection, or concentration beyond expectation. The companion proves full support on $[0,1)$ of zero-temperature Parisi minimizers, a result H.-B. Chen had already posted (arXiv 2607.18032), as the companion acknowledges.

problems.name: Kirchberg-Rordam comparison question: pure infiniteness implies strong pure infiniteness, and weak equals strong for exact C*-algebras
problems.statement: Kirchberg and Rordam introduced three notions for (possibly nonsimple) C*-algebras: $C$ is purely infinite if every positive element $h$ is properly infinite ($h\oplus h\precsim h$ in Cuntz comparison), weakly purely infinite if $h^{\oplus n}$ is properly infinite for every positive $h$ and one fixed $n$, and strongly purely infinite if for all positive $x,y$ and $\varepsilon>0$ there are $s,t$ with $\|s^*x^2s-x^2\|<\varepsilon$, $\|t^*y^2t-y^2\|<\varepsilon$, $\|s^*xyt\|<\varepsilon$. Strong implies ordinary implies weak, and for separable nuclear algebras strong pure infiniteness is tied to $\mathcal O_\infty$-absorption. Do the three notions coincide, in general and for nuclear algebras?
problems.posedBy: Eberhard Kirchberg and Mikael Rordam (Adv. Math. 2002, Question 9.5); recorded as Problem LXXII by Schafhauser, Tikuisis and White
problems.ageNote: The notions were introduced in Kirchberg-Rordam, 'Infinite non-simple C*-algebras: absorbing the Cuntz algebra O-infinity' (Adv. Math. 167, 2002). The question is restated in Schafhauser-Tikuisis-White, 'Nuclear C*-algebras: 99 problems' (arXiv 2506.10902, Section 21, Problem LXXII).
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: every complex C*-algebra in which every positive element is properly infinite is strongly purely infinite, with an arbitrary cross term in the diagonalization. Theorem 1.2: for exact algebras, proper infiniteness of $h^{\oplus n}$ for one fixed $n$ and all positive $h$ implies proper infiniteness of every positive element, hence strong pure infiniteness. Corollary: a separable nuclear algebra with this fixed-amplification property absorbs $\mathcal O_\infty$, with no unitality or simplicity assumption (via Kirchberg's central-sequence results). Not settled: whether weak pure infiniteness implies pure infiniteness for non-exact algebras, which the paper states remains outside its conclusions.

problems.name: The Kannan-Tetali-Vempala conjecture for simple undirected graphs
problems.field: Markov chain mixing time; sampling graphs with given degrees
problems.statement: For a graphical degree vector $d=(d_1,\dots,d_n)$, let $\Omega_d$ be the simple undirected graphs on $\{1,\dots,n\}$ with degrees $d$. The switch chain removes two disjoint edges and inserts a different perfect matching on their four endpoints when both new edges are absent. Kannan, Tetali and Vempala began this program for bipartite graphs and suggested broad applicability; rapid mixing was then proved for regular sequences (Cooper-Dyer-Greenhill) and for P-stable families, and the bipartite case was settled in 2026. The modern form of the conjecture (Erdos, Greenhill, Mezei, Miklos, Soltesz and Soukup, Conjecture 1.1) asks for rapid mixing for every realizable degree sequence in the bipartite, directed and simple undirected models. Does the switch chain on $\Omega_d$ mix in time polynomial in $n$ for every graphical $d$?
problems.posedBy: Ravi Kannan, Prasad Tetali and Santosh Vempala (SODA 1997, RSA 1999); undirected form as Conjecture 1.1 of Erdos, Greenhill, Mezei, Miklos, Soltesz and Soukup (2022)
problems.ageNote: Kannan, Tetali and Vempala treated bipartite sequences and raised broad applicability (SODA 1997, journal 1999); the manuscript cites the explicit three-model formulation from Erdos et al., Eur. J. Combin. 2022. 1997 matches the catalog's bipartite entry.
problems.resultNote: Claims Theorem 1.1: for every $n\ge4$ and every graphical labeled degree vector $d$, the lazy switch chain has total-variation mixing time at most $2n^8$ and, if $|\Omega_d|>1$, spectral gap at least $[24n^2\binom n4]^{-1}$. Corollary: an exactly uniform sampler for any graphical $d$ with expected polynomial bit running time, terminating almost surely. This settles the simple undirected formulation; the bipartite formulation was proved earlier by Fu, Qin and Wang (listed separately), and the directed formulation is not addressed. The exponent 8 is not claimed to be sharp.

problems.name: The asymptotic Gotsman-Linial conjecture on average sensitivity of polynomial threshold functions
problems.field: Analysis of Boolean functions; polynomial threshold functions
problems.statement: A degree-$d$ polynomial threshold function on $\{-1,1\}^n$ is $f(x)=\mathrm{sgn}(p(x))$ for a real polynomial $p$ of degree at most $d$. Its average sensitivity (total influence) is $I(f)=\sum_{i=1}^n\Pr[f(X)\ne f(X^{\oplus i})]$ for uniform $X$. Gotsman and Linial proposed that the maximum of $I(f)$ over degree-$d$ PTFs is attained by a symmetric function of $x_1+\dots+x_n$, which would give $I(f)=O(d\sqrt n)$; Chapman disproved the exact extremal form and separated it from the asymptotic bound. The best bounds were sublinear for fixed $d$ (Harsha-Klivans-Meka, Diakonikolas-Raghavendra-Servedio-Tan) and $\sqrt n(\log n)^{O(d\log d)}2^{O(d^2\log d)}$ (Kane). Is $I(f)=O(d\sqrt n)$ for every degree-$d$ polynomial threshold function, with an absolute constant?
problems.posedBy: Craig Gotsman and Nathan Linial (exact extremal form); asymptotic form stated by Chapman
problems.ageNote: Gotsman and Linial, Spectral properties of threshold functions (Combinatorica 1994, Section 5, p. 47), as cited by the manuscript. The asymptotic O(d sqrt n) form is stated as a separate conjecture by Chapman (2018, Conjectures 1.1-1.2) after the exact form was refuted.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for $n\ge1$, $1\le d\le n$ and a real multilinear polynomial $p$ of degree at most $d$, $f=\mathrm{sgn}(p)$ with $\mathrm{sgn}(0)=1$ has $I(f)\le8d\sqrt n$; the constant is absolute and $d$ may grow with $n$. Symmetric examples show the order $d\sqrt n$ is sharp for $d\le\sqrt n$. It removes the polylogarithmic loss in Kane's bound. It makes no claim about the exact extremizers of the original Gotsman-Linial proposal (already refuted by Chapman and by Kim-Maldonado-Wellens) and does not address non-uniform distributions.

problems.name: Sharpness of the Kesten-Stigum reconstruction threshold for three-state symmetric and ferromagnetic four-state Potts channels on trees
problems.field: Broadcasting on trees; reconstruction and community detection
problems.statement: A root spin, uniform on $q$ states, is broadcast down a tree through a symmetric channel with second eigenvalue $\lambda$; reconstruction means the spins at depth $\ell$ keep non-vanishing information about the root. Kesten-Stigum gives reconstruction when $d\lambda^2>1$ ($d$ the branching number); Sly showed this is not sharp for $q\ge5$, and proved sharpness for $q=3$ on regular trees of large degree. Mezard and Montanari conjectured sharpness for three states (either sign of $\lambda$) and small alphabets, and discussed all branching parameters. For $q=3$ and for the ferromagnetic $q=4$ channel, on every regular tree and every Poisson Galton-Watson tree, is there non-reconstruction whenever $d\lambda^2\le1$?
problems.posedBy: Marc Mezard and Andrea Montanari (Reconstruction on trees and spin glass transition, J. Stat. Phys. 2006, Conjecture 2 and Section 8); all-degree regular-tree form in Allan Sly (2011, Conjecture 1)
problems.resultNote: Three-state theorem: for the symmetric channel with $-1/2\le\lambda\le1$, on every $b$-ary tree ($b\ge2$) and every observed Poisson($d$) tree with $d>1$, reconstruction holds iff $d\lambda^2>1$, with non-reconstruction at equality for both signs (so the 3-coloring channel is non-reconstructible at branching four). Corollary: weak recovery in the symmetric three-community sparse block model is possible iff $(a-b)^2>3(a+2b)$. Four-state theorem: for the ferromagnetic channel ($0\le\lambda\le1$), non-reconstruction whenever $d\lambda^2\le1$ on $d$-ary and Poisson trees. Companion: an $L^3$-capacity criterion for four-state reconstruction on bounded-degree trees. Not shown: the antiferromagnetic four-state channel.

problems.name: Robert's trace-cone question: does the cone of extended traces classify W-stabilized separable nuclear C*-algebras?
problems.field: Operator algebras; classification of nuclear C*-algebras
problems.statement: The Razak-Jacelon algebra $\mathcal W$ is simple, monotracial, stably projectionless and nuclear; tensoring with it removes K-theory and leaves trace data. For a C*-algebra $A$ let $T(A)$ be the cone of all lower-semicontinuous extended traces $A_+\to[0,\infty]$, including the zero/infinity weights of ideals, with its canonical topology (Elliott-Robert-Santiago). Known classification results cover simple algebras and the traceless (purely infinite) case. Leonel Robert asked, as recorded by Santiago (2012) and listed as Problem LXVIII by Schafhauser, Tikuisis and White, whether this cone is a complete invariant: if $A,B$ are separable nuclear C*-algebras with $T(A)\cong T(B)$ as topological cones, is $A\otimes\mathcal W\otimes\mathcal K\cong B\otimes\mathcal W\otimes\mathcal K$?
problems.posedBy: Leonel Robert, recorded in L. Santiago, W-stable C*-algebras (West Coast Operator Algebra Seminar abstract, 2012); Problem LXVIII in Schafhauser-Tikuisis-White, Nuclear C*-algebras: 99 problems
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: if $A,B$ are separable nuclear complex C*-algebras and $T(A)\cong T(B)$ as topological cones, then $A\otimes\mathcal W\otimes\mathcal K\cong B\otimes\mathcal W\otimes\mathcal K$, and the isomorphism can be chosen to induce the given cone map. No density condition on finite domains of the weights and no UCT is assumed. It does not classify algebras without the $\mathcal W\otimes\mathcal K$ stabilization, and does not determine the range of the invariant.

problems.name: Kohn-Sham ensemble v-representability of Coulomb ground-state densities by potentials in L^{3/2}+L^infinity
problems.statement: Kohn-Sham density functional theory replaces an interacting electronic ground state by noninteracting electrons in a common local potential that reproduces its density. Levy and Lieb separated the existence of states with a prescribed density from the existence of a potential for which such states are ground states; ensembles of degenerate noninteracting ground states enlarge the class (Ullrich-Kohn). Explicit non-representable model densities and numerical violations are known, but not for an actual Coulomb system. Is the ground-state density of every finite Coulomb molecule the density of a ground-state ensemble of noninteracting electrons in some real local potential $v\in L^{3/2}(\mathbb R^3)+L^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$?

problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there is a finite positive integer $Z$ such that the three-electron Coulomb Hamiltonian with two nuclei of charge $Z$ at $\pm(D/Z)e_z$, $D=10^{200}$, has a normalizable absolute ground state $\Psi$ (sector $S_z=1/2$) whose spin-summed density is not the density of any ground-state ensemble of $H_s(v)$ for any real $v\in L^{3/2}+L^\infty$. The mechanism is the Gori-Giorgi-Gal-Baerends nodal-plane asymptotics, made rigorous, plus a kinetic certificate against all ensembles. A corollary rules out a local-potential first variation of the ensemble Hartree-exchange-correlation functional at that density. problems.name: Voiculescu's question: do microstates and nonmicrostates free entropy agree when finite?
problems.statement: For a bounded self-adjoint tuple $X$ in a tracial von Neumann algebra, Voiculescu defined the microstates free entropy $\chi(X)$ from volumes of matrix approximations and the nonmicrostates entropy $\chi^*(X)$ from free Fisher information along free semicircular noise. They agree for one variable, and Biane-Capitaine-Guionnet proved $\chi\le\chi^*$ in general; equality is known under convexity hypotheses. Agreement was one of the questions of Voiculescu's unification problem, and Guionnet stated the finite-entropy form as a conjecture. Does $\chi(X)>-\infty$ imply $\chi(X)=\chi^*(X)$?

problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites Voiculescu's 2002 survey for the unification problem; the question appears in Voiculescu's free entropy papers of the 1990s, which the manuscript does not quote for it.
problems.resultNote: Claims a negative answer: a bounded self-adjoint tuple with $-\infty<\chi(X)\le\chi^*(X)-\tfrac12<\infty$, built as a small semicircular perturbation of free semicirculars tensored with a commuting discrete variable. It does NOT settle equality for every smaller number of variables (the example uses a large fixed $n$), and uses the limsup version of $\chi$; equality under the known convexity conditions is unaffected.

problems.name: Williams's one-tape question: simulating one-tape time $T$ in $O(T^{1/2-\delta})$ space
problems.statement: A classical simulation (attributed to Hopcroft and Ullman) computes the outcome of a deterministic one-tape Turing machine running for $T$ steps in $O(\sqrt T)$ space, with unrestricted simulation time. Williams (2025) proved that multitape time $t$ can be simulated in $O(\sqrt{t\log t})$ space using the Cook-Mertz tree-evaluation algorithm, and asked in Section 5 of his full version whether, for one-tape machines, the square-root exponent can be lowered by a fixed positive constant. Is there $\delta>0$ such that a one-tape machine running for $T$ steps can be simulated in $O(T^{1/2-\delta})$ space?
problems.posedBy: R. Ryan Williams (Simulating Time with Square-Root Space, STOC 2025; question in Section 5 of the full version)
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for a fixed deterministic machine with one writable tape and head (and finitely many read-only input heads), the finite-control and halting outcome by time $T$ can be computed in $O(T^{2/5}\log^C(T+2))$ work-space bits given the cap $T$; without a supplied cap, a machine halting at time $t$ is simulated in $O((t+2)^{2/5}\,\mathrm{polylog})$ space. Hence $O(T^{1/2-\delta})$ for every $\delta<1/10$. Simulation time is unrestricted, the final tape is not materialized, no lower bound or optimality is claimed, and for several writable tapes only $O(\sqrt T\,\mathrm{polylog})$ is given.

problems.name: Is the free uniform spanning forest a factor of IID?
problems.shortName: FUSF as a factor of IID
problems.field: Probability on graphs, uniform spanning forests
problems.statement: The free uniform spanning forest (FUSF) of an infinite connected locally finite graph is the weak limit of uniform spanning trees on finite exhaustions, without wiring the boundary. The wired forest is a factor of IID on transient graphs via Wilson's algorithm rooted at infinity, and Timar proved the free forest is a factor of IID on recurrent and invariantly amenable unimodular random graphs. Lyons (2013) asked, for Cayley graphs, whether the FUSF is a factor of IID. Can the FUSF be generated as an equivariant measurable factor of independent vertex labels, in general and in particular on nonamenable Cayley graphs?
problems.posedBy: Russell Lyons
problems.ageNote: Lyons, l2-Betti numbers, cost, and the free uniform spanning forest, Oberwolfach Reports 10 (2013), p. 2392, as cited by the manuscript; Timar (arXiv, December 2025 version) states the unrestricted question as open.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there is one Borel, root-independent, equivariant rule $\Phi(G,U,e)$ such that for every infinite connected locally finite simple unweighted graph $G$ with IID uniform vertex labels $U$, the edge set selected by $\Phi$ has the FUSF law. Further results: every translation-invariant strongly Rayleigh binary process on a countable group, including invariant determinantal processes with Hermitian positive-contraction kernels, is a factor of IID, with no amenability needed. Not shown: finitary factors or weighted graphs beyond the strongly Rayleigh results.

problems.name: Patterson's conjecture on the first moment of cubic Gauss sums over primes
problems.field: Analytic number theory; cubic Gauss sums and metaplectic forms
problems.statement: For a rational prime $p\equiv1\pmod 3$, Kummer studied the cubic sum $S_p=\sum_{x\bmod p}e(x^3/p)$ and observed a bias toward positive values. Heath-Brown and Patterson (1979) proved that the normalized sums are equidistributed on the circle, so any bias lives below the prime-counting scale. Patterson (1978) predicted a bias of exact order $X^{5/6}/\log X$; Heath-Brown's cubic large sieve gave $O(X^{5/6+\epsilon})$ and Dunn-Radziwill (2024) proved a smoothed asymptotic under GRH. With $G(\pi)$ the normalized cubic Gauss sum at a primary Eisenstein prime and $c_*=(2\pi)^{2/3}/(3\Gamma(2/3))$, is $\sum_{N\pi\le X}G(\pi)\sim\frac65c_*X^{5/6}/\log X$ unconditionally?
problems.posedBy: S. J. Patterson (1978); first-moment normalization as stated by Dunn and Radziwill (2024, display after Equation (1.8)) and Wan (2021, Conjecture 4.13)
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: unconditionally, $\sum_{N\pi\le X,\ \pi\equiv1(3)\text{ prime}}G(\pi)=\frac65c_*X^{5/6}/\log X+o(X^{5/6}/\log X)$, over all primary Eisenstein primes; equivalently $\sum_{p\le X}S_p/(2\sqrt p)\sim\frac35c_*X^{5/6}/\log X$, matching Wan's Conjecture 4.13. Also cancellation in every fixed nonzero angular mode and for fixed powers $G(\pi)^k$ with $3\nmid k$, $|k|>1$. The error term is only little-oh, with no rate; powers $k$ divisible by 3 (part of Patterson's complementary conjecture) remain open. Uses the unconditional Dunn-Radziwill Voronoi formula, not their GRH estimates.

problems.name: Berkholz's question: is Weisfeiler-Leman equivalence with the dimension as part of the input EXPTIME-complete?
problems.field: Computational complexity; graph isomorphism and finite model theory
problems.statement: The $k$-dimensional Weisfeiler-Leman algorithm repeatedly refines colours of $k$-tuples of vertices; two graphs are $k$-WL equivalent if their stable colour histograms agree. For fixed $k$ this takes time $n^{O(k)}$, so with $k$ given in binary the equivalence problem lies in EXPTIME. Seppelt (MFCS 2024), and independently Lichter, Rassmann and Schweitzer, proved it coNP-hard when $k$ is part of the input, and Seppelt recorded Christoph Berkholz's question whether it is in fact EXPTIME-complete. Given two graphs by adjacency matrices and a dimension $k\ge2$ in binary, is deciding $k$-WL equivalence EXPTIME-complete?
problems.posedBy: Christoph Berkholz, as recorded by Tim Seppelt (MFCS 2024, the question preceding Theorem 5)
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites the question only through Seppelt (2024); when Berkholz first raised it is not stated.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1 (principal manuscript): deciding joint-update $k$-WL equivalence with $k\ge2$ in binary and explicit adjacency matrices is EXPTIME-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions, also for connected simple uncoloured graphs of equal order and maximum degree three. Companions claim: deciding whether a given dimension identifies a graph (WL dimension at most $k$) is EXPTIME-complete, also with $k$ in unary; for every large fixed $k$, deciding $k$-WL equivalence needs $n^{\Omega(k)}$ deterministic sequential time unconditionally (multitape Turing machines and log-word RAMs, diameter-two graphs); and parity lifts give $n^{\Omega(k)}$ exclusions under ETH. No randomized or nonuniform lower bounds are claimed, and the separate-update convention is treated only in the fixed-dimension companions.

problems.name: Curtis's conjecture: the mod-2 stable Hurewicz image of the sphere is spanned by the Hopf- and Kervaire-invariant-one classes
problems.statement: For $d>0$ let $h_d:\pi_d^S\to H_d(Q_0S^0;\mathbb F_2)$ be the mod-2 Hurewicz homomorphism into the homology of the basepoint component of $QS^0=\mathrm{colim}_r\Omega^rS^r$. The obvious elements with nonzero image are the Hopf-invariant-one classes $\eta,\nu,\sigma$ in degrees 1, 3, 7 and the Kervaire-invariant-one classes $\theta_j$ in degrees $2^{j+1}-2$, when they exist. Curtis (1975), in his study of the Dyer-Lashof and lambda algebras, conjectured that nothing else is detected; May (1977) recorded a gap, found by Wellington, in the proposed proof. The conjecture implies Eccles's conjecture for spheres. Is the image of $\bigoplus_{d>0}h_d$ spanned over $\mathbb F_2$ by the Hurewicz images of $\eta,\nu,\sigma$ and of the Kervaire-invariant-one classes that exist?
problems.posedBy: Edward B. Curtis
problems.ageNote: Curtis, The Dyer-Lashof algebra and the Lambda-algebra, Illinois J. Math. 19 (1975); May, Infinite loop space theory, Bull. AMS 83 (1977), p. 484, footnote 3, records the gap found by Wellington.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: the image of $\bigoplus_{d>0}h_d$ is spanned over $\mathbb F_2$ by the Hurewicz images of $\eta,\nu,\sigma$ and of the Kervaire-invariant-one classes $\theta_j$ (degree $2^{j+1}-2$) whenever they exist; no existence is posited. Corollary 1.2: Eccles's conjecture holds for every sphere $S^n$, $n>0$: each nonzero spherical class in $H_*(QS^n;\mathbb F_2)$ is the bottom class or a suspended Hopf-invariant-one image. Corollary 1.3 (with Hill-Hopkins-Ravenel): $h_d=0$ for $d>0$ outside $\{1,2,3,6,7,14,30,62,126\}$, so the positive image vanishes above degree 126. Not shown: an exact dimension of the image or nonvanishing in each listed degree, odd primes, or Eccles's conjecture for $QX$ with $X$ other than a sphere.

problems.name: The smooth realization problem: does finite entropy suffice for a smooth volume-preserving model?
problems.field: Ergodic theory; smooth realization of measure-preserving systems
problems.statement: A smooth positive-volume model of an invertible ergodic transformation $(X,\mu,T)$ of a standard nonatomic probability space is a $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism $S$ of a compact finite-dimensional manifold $M$ preserving a probability $\nu$ with strictly positive smooth density, together with a measurable isomorphism $F$ between invariant conull sets with $F\circ T=S\circ F$. Finite Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy is necessary (Ruelle's inequality), and Lind and Thouvenot realized every finite-entropy ergodic system by a homeomorphism of the two-torus, but a realization with a singular invariant measure does not give a smooth volume. The smooth realization problem, as discussed by Katok and Thouvenot, asks whether this entropy restriction is the only one. Does every ergodic invertible transformation with finite entropy admit a smooth positive-volume model?
problems.posedBy: The classical smooth realization problem, in the formulation discussed by Anatole Katok and Jean-Paul Thouvenot (Ann. IHP Probab. Stat. 1997, pp. 324-326)
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites Katok and Thouvenot (1997) for the classical formulation and Foreman and Weiss (2022) for a variant; it does not name an earlier originator, though the problem is commonly traced to Anosov and Katok (1970). Year taken from the cited source.
problems.resultNote: Claims Theorem 1.1: there is an ergodic invertible transformation of a standard nonatomic probability space with $h_\mu(T)=0$ that is not measurably conjugate on invariant conull sets to any $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism of a compact finite-dimensional manifold (boundary allowed, orientation not required) preserving a strictly positive smooth probability density. A single symbolic example excludes every dimension. So finite entropy, even zero entropy, does not suffice. It does not exclude models whose invariant measure is only equivalent to volume, and it does not characterize which systems are smoothly realizable.

problems.name: Erdős and Prachar's question: do the increases of $p_n/n$ have positive lower density?
problems.statement: Let $p_n$ be the $n$th prime and $u_n=p_n/n$. Erdős and Prachar (1962) proved $\sum_{p_n<x}|u_{n+1}-u_n|\asymp(\log x)^2$ and that the set of $n$ with $u_n>u_{n+1}$ has positive density, and asked about the reverse inequality. Since $u_n<u_{n+1}$ is equivalent to $p_{n+1}-p_n>p_n/n\sim\log p_n$, the question asks whether a positive proportion of prime gaps exceed the average gap, which needs control of how often gaps are large rather than of the largest gaps. Positive proportions were known only for gaps above a fixed fraction (about $0.579$) of $\log p_n$. Does the set of $n$ with $p_n/n<p_{n+1}/(n+1)$ have positive lower density?
problems.posedBy: Paul Erdős and Karl Prachar (Abh. Math. Sem. Univ. Hamburg 1962, p. 256); Erdős Problem #968
problems.ageNote: erdosproblems.com cites Erdős (1965) for the question and Erdős-Prachar for the background results; the manuscript cites the Erdős-Prachar paper, dated 1962.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every fixed $C>0$ there are $c(C)>0$ and $N_0(C)$ with $\#\{n\le N:p_{n+1}-p_n>C\log p_n\}\ge c(C)N$ for all $N\ge N_0$, with ordinary lower density and equal weight on prime indices. Corollary 1.2 (take $C=2$) answers Erdős-Prachar: the increases of $p_n/n$ have positive lower density. The main theorem is stronger than the posed question. The constant $c(C)$ is not made explicit or compared with the Poisson prediction $e^{-C}$, and the further questions recorded with Problem #968 on $u_n<u_{n+1}<u_{n+2}$ and $u_n>u_{n+1}>u_{n+2}$ are not addressed.

problems.name: Schramm's Problem 2.3: Gaussian free field and SLE$_4$ limits of uniform real Lipschitz heights on the triangular lattice
problems.field: Statistical mechanics; random surfaces and SLE
problems.statement: Let $D$ be a smooth simply connected planar domain with two marked boundary points splitting its boundary into arcs $A_+$ and $A_-$, approximated by triangular-lattice polygons of mesh $\delta$. Sample real heights on the vertices uniformly (Lebesgue measure) subject to $|h(x)-h(y)|\le1$ across every edge, with boundary values $+\lambda$ on $A_+$ and $-\lambda$ on $A_-$. This hard-constraint gradient model lies outside the uniformly convex potentials covered by Schramm-Sheffield and Miller. In his ICM 2006 problem collection Schramm asked (Problem 2.3) for its scaling limits: a Gaussian free field for the height and SLE$_4$ for the zero-height interface at a suitable boundary amplitude; Problem 2.2 asks the analogous questions for uniform odd integer heights with increments $0,\pm2$. As $\delta\to0$, does the height converge to a multiple of the Dirichlet Gaussian free field, and does the zero interface converge to chordal SLE$_4$ for a tuned $\lambda$?
problems.posedBy: Oded Schramm (Conformally invariant scaling limits: an overview and a collection of problems, ICM 2006, Problems 2.2 and 2.3)
problems.ageNote: Posed in Schramm's ICM 2006 (Madrid) lecture, published in the Proceedings in 2007.
problems.resultNote: Principal manuscript: on approximations of smooth simply connected domains, the centered uniform real Lipschitz height converges as a random distribution to a multiple of the Dirichlet GFF, and at one tuned amplitude $\lambda$ the zero-height interface converges in uniform curve distance to chordal SLE$_4$; the variance-boundary relation is given through an implicit coefficient, so constants are not explicit. Companion: the field part of Problem 2.2 (uniform odd integer heights, boundary $\pm1$) with an absolutely convergent normalization formula; the Problem 2.2 interface is not proved. Companion: GFF limits for zero-boundary integer Lipschitz heights weighted by $x\in[1/\sqrt2,1]$ (loop $O(2)$), part of a conjecture discussed by Glazman and Lammers; larger $x$ is not covered.

problems.name: The Barendregt-Geuvers-Klop conjecture for beta reduction: weak normalization implies strong normalization in every pure type system
problems.field: Type theory; lambda calculus; pure type systems
problems.statement: A pure type system is given by a set of sorts $\mathcal S$, axioms $\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal S^2$ and product rules $\mathcal R\subseteq\mathcal S^3$, with full $\beta$-reduction allowed everywhere, including inside type annotations. The system is weakly normalizing if every legal expression in every valid context has a $\beta$-normal form, and strongly normalizing if no such expression admits an infinite $\beta$-reduction sequence. Strong normalization was known to follow from weak normalization only for restricted classes (Sorensen; Barthe, Hatcliff and Sorensen for nondependent systems). Is every weakly $\beta$-normalizing pure type system strongly $\beta$-normalizing?
problems.posedBy: Barendregt, Geuvers and Klop; stated by Herman Geuvers as Conjecture 8.1.2 of his thesis (Nijmegen, 1993)
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites Geuvers's 1993 thesis (Conjecture 8.1.2) for the system-wide conjecture, which he states for both beta and beta-eta reduction. The name credits Barendregt, Geuvers and Klop; the thesis is the earliest written statement the manuscript gives.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every pure type system $(\mathcal S,\mathcal A,\mathcal R)$, with no functionality assumption on $\mathcal A$ or $\mathcal R$, if every legal expression in every valid context is weakly $\beta$-normalizing then every such expression is strongly $\beta$-normalizing; reduction acts inside annotations and contexts may be open. Both properties are system-wide: the theorem does not say that an individual term with a normal form is strongly normalizing. It makes no claim about $\beta\eta$-reduction, the other half of Geuvers's formulation. The proof uses Tait-Girard style candidates indexed by sort profiles and a realization of Hurkens's paradox to exclude a graph configuration.

problems.name: Litt's potential integral density question for $\mathrm{SL}_r$ character varieties of curves
problems.shortName: Litt's integral density question for curves
problems.field: Arithmetic geometry; character varieties, integral points
problems.statement: For a smooth complex variety $X$, the $\mathrm{SL}_r$-character variety of $\pi_1(X)$ has a natural model $M_r(X)$ over $\mathbb Z$. Litt asked whether integral points on such character varieties become Zariski dense after a finite extension of the ground field, including a variant with prescribed boundary monodromy, and whether one number field $L$ suffices so that the points over the full ring of integers $\mathcal O_L$ are dense in every component. Coccia and Litt proved this for $\mathrm{SL}_2$ and $\mathrm{PGL}_2$ and conjectured it for Chevalley groups with fixed boundary data. For a smooth connected curve $X$, every rank $r$ and prescribed quasi-unipotent boundary classes, is there one number field over whose full ring of integers the integral points are Zariski dense?
problems.posedBy: Daniel Litt (Problems I Like, Problem 7; survey 2024, Question 5.4.3(2)); Simone Coccia and Daniel Litt (2025, Conjecture 1.1.1)
problems.ageNote: The survey 'Motives, mapping class groups, and monodromy' (arXiv 2409.02234, 2024) asks explicitly whether one number field suffices. The manuscript cites the Problems I Like page without a posting date.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every smooth connected complex curve $X$, rank $r$ and quasi-unipotent conjugacy classes at the punctures (nonsemisimple allowed), there is a finite extension $L$ of the field of eigenvalues with $M_r(X)(\mathcal O_L)\cap Y(\mathbb C)$ Zariski dense in every component of the relative locus $Y$; an explicit $L$ is given. The same holds when only characteristic polynomials are fixed, and for the whole character variety with base field $\mathbb Q$. This settles the determinant-one curve case of Litt's question and the $\mathrm{SL}_r$ curve case of the Coccia-Litt conjecture for quasi-unipotent data; higher-dimensional varieties are not treated.

problems.name: The weak inhomogeneous Duffin-Schaeffer conjecture
problems.statement: Koukoulopoulos and Maynard (2020) proved the Duffin-Schaeffer conjecture: for $\psi:\mathbb{N}\to[0,\infty)$ with $\sum_q\phi(q)\psi(q)/q=\infty$, almost every $x$ has infinitely many reduced fractions $a/q$ with $|x-a/q|<\psi(q)/q$. For a fixed shift $\gamma$, unweighted divergence does not suffice without monotonicity (Ramirez; Chow-Hauke-Pollington-Ramirez), and the coprime-numerator inhomogeneous version is false. The weak inhomogeneous conjecture (Yu 2021, Question 1.2; Chow-Technau 2024, Conjecture 1.22; Beresnevich-Hauke-Velani 2024, Conjecture 2), proved for rational shifts by Beresnevich-Hauke-Velani, asks: for every fixed $\gamma\in\mathbb{R}$ and every $\psi$ with $\sum_q\phi(q)\psi(q)/q=\infty$, does $\|qx-\gamma\|<\psi(q)$ hold for infinitely many $q$, for almost every $x$?
problems.posedBy: H. Yu, J. Number Theory (2021), Question 1.2; named by Chow and Technau (2024, Conjecture 1.22); also Beresnevich, Hauke and Velani (2024), Conjecture 2
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every fixed $\gamma\in\mathbb{R}$ and finite-valued $\psi:\mathbb{N}\to[0,\infty)$ with $\sum_q\phi(q)\psi(q)/q=\infty$, almost every $x$ satisfies $\|qx-\gamma\|<\psi(q)$ for infinitely many $q$; the null set may depend on $\gamma$ and $\psi$. Corollary 1.2 gives the Hausdorff-measure analogue via mass transference. The arithmetic core adapts the Koukoulopoulos-Maynard common-pivot method (as simplified by Green-Walker). It proves no convergence converse, no quantitative asymptotic, no coprime-numerator statement, and no result uniform in the shift.

problems.name: Quasipolynomial-time solution of mean-payoff games with binary weights
problems.field: Algorithmic game theory; games on graphs; complexity of NP and coNP problems
problems.statement: In a finite two-player mean-payoff game on a directed graph with integer edge weights $w$ given in binary, Max wins from a vertex if she can force $\liminf_{T\to\infty}\frac1T\sum_{t<T}w(e_t)\ge0$. Ehrenfeucht and Mycielski proved positional determinacy, which puts the threshold problem in $\mathrm{NP}\cap\mathrm{coNP}$, and Zwick and Paterson (1996) gave pseudopolynomial algorithms, polynomial in the largest weight but exponential in its bit length; the best general bounds were randomized subexponential. The quasipolynomial algorithm for parity games (Calude, Jain, Khoussainov, Li and Stephan) does not transfer, since the reduction runs from parity to mean payoff. Can the winning regions of mean-payoff games be computed in polynomial time, or at least in quasipolynomial time, in the binary input length?
problems.posedBy: Uri Zwick and Mike Paterson, The complexity of mean payoff games on graphs (1996), as cited by the manuscript; the question is the polynomial-time status of a problem in NP and coNP
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites Zwick and Paterson (1996) and Ehrenfeucht and Mycielski (1979) for the setting and does not quote a single posing sentence. The quasipolynomial form of the question became pointed after the 2017 parity-games breakthrough; this entry answers that intermediate question, not the polynomial-time one.
problems.resultNote: Claims a deterministic algorithm computing the exact set of vertices from which Max can force nonnegative liminf mean payoff, for arbitrary signed binary weights, self-loops and parallel edges, in $2^{O((\log(L+2))^2)}$ bit operations; a reduction gives exact rational values and optimal positional strategies for both players, energy-game minimum credits, and tropical feasibility tests within the same bound. A randomized companion of the same date gives a Las Vegas algorithm with a polynomial-time certificate check. It does NOT give a polynomial-time algorithm, which the paper names as a further improvement. Conflicting claim: Truffet (arXiv:2603.26423, and a 2025 HAL note) claims a strongly polynomial algorithm via tropical optimization; the randomized companion gives a small example on which the printed rule of version 4 loses the optimum, and makes no claim about the 2025 note.

problems.name: Erdős Problem 416: does $V(2x)/V(x)\to2$ for the number $V(x)$ of totient values up to $x$, and is there an asymptotic formula?
problems.field: Multiplicative number theory; values of arithmetic functions
problems.statement: Let $V(x)$ count the integers $v\le x$ for which $\varphi(m)=v$ is solvable. Pillai showed these values have density zero; after Erdős, Erdős-Hall, Pomerance and Maier-Pomerance, Ford (1998) determined $V(x)$ up to a bounded factor and showed $V(cx)-V(x)\asymp_c V(x)$, but this falls short of an asymptotic formula. Erdős and Hall asked whether $V(cx)/V(x)\to c$ for fixed $c>1$. Does $V(2x)/V(x)\to2$, and is there an asymptotic formula for $V(x)$?

problems.name: Landsberg's Problem 7.19: a polynomial stabilization bound for the canonical Foulkes-Howe map
problems.field: Representation theory; Chow varieties and geometric complexity theory
problems.statement: For $a,b\ge1$ and a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$, the canonical Foulkes-Howe (Hadamard-Howe) map $\mu_{a,b,V}:\mathrm{Sym}^b(\mathrm{Sym}^aV)\to\mathrm{Sym}^a(\mathrm{Sym}^bV)$ is induced by multiplication in $(\mathrm{Sym}V)^{\otimes a}$; its image is the degree-$b$ part of the coordinate ring of the Chow variety of products of $a$ linear forms, whose normalization is the whole target. Surjectivity in degree $b$ gives an equivariant embedding as in Foulkes' conjecture. Brion proved eventual surjectivity and later an effective bound depending on both $a$ and $\dim V$. Landsberg's survey of geometric complexity theory (Problem 7.19) asks for a polynomial bound. Is there a degree bound, polynomial in $a$ and valid in every dimension, beyond which $\mu_{a,b,V}$ is surjective?
problems.posedBy: J. M. Landsberg (Geometric complexity theory: an introduction for geometers, Ann. Univ. Ferrara 2015, Problem 7.19)
problems.ageNote: Cited from the published 2015 version (arXiv:1305.7387, 2013). The underlying stabilization question goes back to Brion (1993, 1997).
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1: for every $a\ge2$, $b\ge a(a-1)$ and finite-dimensional complex $V$, $\mu_{a,b,V}$ is surjective; equivalently the Chow-variety coordinate ring agrees with its normalization in degree $b$. In Landsberg's notation the bound is $d\ge n(n-1)$, in every dimension. By complete reducibility this yields Foulkes' embedding $\mathrm{Sym}^a(\mathrm{Sym}^bV)\hookrightarrow\mathrm{Sym}^b(\mathrm{Sym}^aV)$ for $b\ge a(a-1)$. The least stabilization degree is not determined, the bound is not claimed sharp, and nothing is said about injectivity of the map in the other direction (which fails at $(5,5)$ and $(6,6)$).

problems.name: Jacobsthal's quadratic-bound question: is h(k) = O(k^2)?
problems.statement: Let $h(k)$ be the least $m$ such that every interval of $m$ consecutive integers contains an integer coprime to any prescribed positive integer with at most $k$ distinct prime factors. Brun's sieve gives $h(k)\ll k^{C}$; Iwaniec's linear-sieve work gave $h(k)\ll k^2\log^2k$ (1978), improving Vaughan's $k^2\log^4k$; the best lower bound, from Ford, Green, Konyagin, Maynard and Tao, is about $k(\log k)^2\log\log\log k/\log\log k$. Jacobsthal asked, and Erdos recorded (1962; Erdos Problem #970), whether the upper bound is quadratic. Is $h(k)\ll k^2$?
problems.posedBy: E. Jacobsthal (papers from 1960); recorded by P. Erdos (1962, p. 163) and as Erdos Problem #970
problems.ageNote: Jacobsthal studied the function in papers beginning in 1960; the manuscript cites Erdos (1962) as the record of Jacobsthal's question, and erdosproblems.com lists it as #970 citing Erdos (1965).
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: $h(k)\le Ck^2/(\log\log(3k))^2$ for an absolute constant $C$ and every $k\ge1$, uniformly over prime sets and interval positions; in particular $h(k)\ll k^2$, answering Jacobsthal's question and improving Iwaniec's $k^2\log^2k$. The proof pushes the linear sieve to its limiting parameter, keeping a boundary term, and controls the discrepancy with the actual residue classes through an inverse estimate and stopped counts. The constant is not explicit, and the true order of $h(k)$ (Erdos #970's broader ask) is not determined: the gap to the lower bound near $k(\log k)^2$ remains.

problems.name: Yau's question on bounded holomorphic functions: does a complete simply connected Kahler manifold with sectional curvature at most $-a^2<0$ carry a nonconstant bounded holomorphic function?
problems.shortName: Bounded holomorphic functions under negative curvature
problems.statement: Let $M$ be a complete simply connected Kahler manifold of complex dimension at least two whose real sectional curvature satisfies $\mathrm{Sec}_g\le -a^2<0$, with no lower curvature bound assumed. A biholomorphism to a bounded domain would give bounded coordinates; the weaker question asks only for one nonconstant bounded holomorphic function. Must $M$ admit a nonconstant bounded holomorphic function, that is, is $H^\infty(M)\ne\mathbb C$?
problems.posedBy: S.-T. Yau, Problem 38 of his 1982 problem list, as recorded by Damin Wu and S.-T. Yau (2020, p. 103; 2019 survey, Section 3)
problems.ageNote: The manuscript uses the formulation recorded by Wu and Yau (2020) and traces it, through their 2019 survey, to Yau's 1982 Problem 38.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for some finite $m\ge2$ there is a domain $\mathcal T\subset\mathbb C^m$, diffeomorphic to $\mathbb R^{2m}$, with a complete Kahler metric $g$ satisfying $\mathrm{Sec}_g\le -1$ and $H^\infty(\mathcal T)=\mathbb C$: every bounded holomorphic function is constant, so the Caratheodory pseudometric vanishes. This disproves the universal assertion in the one-sided question, and also answers Wu's 1967 bounded-domain question negatively under its hypotheses. The sectional curvatures are unbounded below, so the question under a two-sided bound $-b^2\le\mathrm{Sec}\le -a^2$ remains open; the dimension is large and not made explicit.

problems.name: The Monge (co-motion) ansatz for three-marginal Coulomb transport in $\mathbb R^3$: is the optimum always attained by maps?
problems.field: Multi-marginal optimal transport; density functional theory
problems.statement: For a probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb R^3$, minimize $\int c\,d\pi$ over couplings $\pi$ with three marginals equal to $\mu$, where $c(x_1,x_2,x_3)=\sum_{i<j}|x_i-x_j|^{-1}$. In the strictly correlated electron limit of density functional theory one expects optimizers of co-motion (Monge) form $(\mathrm{Id},T_2,T_3)_\#\mu$ with measure-preserving maps. This holds for two marginals (Cotar-Friesecke-Kluppelberg) and in one dimension (Colombo-De Pascale-Di Marino). If $\mu$ is absolutely continuous with finite Coulomb transport value, is the minimum always attained by a Monge plan?
problems.posedBy: Recorded by G. Friesecke, A. Gerolin and P. Gori-Giorgi (2022 preprint of their DFT chapter, Theorem 2.4 and discussion); still stated open by Friesecke (January 2026)
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites the 2022 preprint of Friesecke-Gerolin-Gori-Giorgi as recording the higher-dimensional question and Friesecke (January 2026) for the three-particle Coulomb case in R^3 being open. The co-motion ansatz itself goes back to Seidl, Gori-Giorgi and Savin (2007) and earlier SCE work.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there is $\rho\ge0$ with $\int\rho=1$ and $\rho,\sqrt\rho\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ such that for $\mu=\rho\,dx$ the three-marginal Coulomb minimum is finite and attained, but every pair of Borel maps $T_2,T_3$ pushing $\mu$ to itself has cost strictly above the minimum. The Monge and Kantorovich infima are nevertheless equal. The same holds for every Riesz cost $\sum_{i<j}|x_i-x_j|^{-s}$, $s>0$, in every dimension $d\ge2$, with a suitable density. It concerns one constructed density: it does not say Monge plans fail generically, and no external potential realizing the density is asserted.

problems.name: A power saving over Dey's bound for planar halving lines
problems.statement: For a set $P$ of $n$ points in the plane in general position ($n$ even), a halving line passes through two points of $P$ and leaves $(n-2)/2$ points on each side. Lovasz (1971) and Erdos, Lovasz, Simmons and Straus (1973) introduced the problem of determining the maximum number $h(n)$ of halving lines (and more generally of $k$-sets), proving $O(n^{3/2})$ and constructing $\Omega(n\log n)$. Dey (1998) proved $h(n)=O(n^{4/3})$; the best lower bound is $n e^{\Omega(\sqrt{\log n})}$ (Toth, Nivasch). What is the true order of $h(n)$; in particular, can Dey's exponent $4/3$ be improved?
problems.posedBy: L. Lovasz, On the number of halving lines (1971); P. Erdos, L. Lovasz, A. Simmons and E. G. Straus, Dissection graphs of planar point sets (1973)
problems.ageNote: The halving-line count goes back to Lovasz (1971) and the k-set problem to Erdos, Lovasz, Simmons and Straus (1973). The specific target of beating Dey's 1998 exponent 4/3 is the open part addressed here.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there are absolute $\varepsilon>0$, $C$, $n_0$ with $h(P)\le Cn^{4/3-\varepsilon}$ for every even $n\ge n_0$ and every $n$-point planar set with no three collinear. Theorem 1.2 bounds the switches at every rank uniformly by $CN^{4/3-\varepsilon}$, and Corollary 1.3 gives $O(n(k+1)^{1/3-\varepsilon_0})$ $k$-sets for $1\le k\le n/2$ (also for levels in line arrangements). The constants and exponent are ineffective; no numerical value of $\varepsilon$ is given. It does not determine the order of $h(n)$, which could still lie anywhere between $n e^{\Omega(\sqrt{\log n})}$ and $n^{4/3-\varepsilon}$.

problems.name: The Sakoda-Sipser problem: exponential cost of simulating nondeterministic automata by two-way deterministic ones
problems.statement: Sakoda and Sipser (STOC 1978) asked how many states a two-way deterministic finite automaton (2DFA) needs to simulate an $n$-state one-way or two-way nondeterministic automaton (1NFA, 2NFA). The best known simulations are exponential, and they showed that the family $B_h$ (one-way liveness: words of binary relations on an $h$-element set whose product is nonempty) is complete for the one-way case. Exponential lower bounds were known only for restricted deterministic targets (Sipser's sweeping automata, Kapoutsis's few-reversal machines), and against unrestricted 2DFAs only quadratic bounds were known. Is there a polynomial $p$ such that every $n$-state 1NFA, or 2NFA, over any finite alphabet has an equivalent 2DFA with at most $p(n)$ states?
problems.posedBy: William J. Sakoda and Michael Sipser
problems.ageNote: Sakoda and Sipser, Nondeterminism and the size of two way finite automata, STOC 1978, cited by both manuscripts.
problems.resultNote: For every $h\ge2$, one-way liveness $\mathrm{OWL}_h$ has a nondeterministic automaton with $h+3$ states and no left moves, while every equivalent 2DFA with $s$ states satisfies $4(s+2)^2\ge2^{\lfloor(h-2)/31\rfloor}$. Hence no polynomial $Cn^c$ bounds 1NFA-to-2DFA (and so 2NFA-to-2DFA) conversion uniformly over finite alphabets. The deterministic target is unrestricted (stay moves, partial rules, infinite rejecting runs). The companion gives the weaker-rate bound $\tfrac12 2^{\lfloor(n-4)/127\rfloor}$ for the same family. Not shown: any lower bound over a fixed alphabet (e.g. binary), any bound in transition-table size, or anything about L versus NL.

problems.name: The Alcalde Lopez-Heeney-Lis conjecture: joint scaling limit of critical Ashkin-Teller heights and current clusters
problems.field: Statistical mechanics; conformally invariant scaling limits
problems.statement: On the critical line of the Ashkin-Teller model ($J>0$, $U\le J$, $\sinh 2J=e^{-2U}$), Lis's representation gives a height function and primal and dual current-cluster collections. At the Ising point $U=0$ (double random currents) the height converges to a Gaussian free field and the clusters to two-valued local sets of that field. Alcalde Lopez, Heeney and Lis proved the joint limit of the height and both complete cluster collections in Jordan domains at that point and conjectured (Conjecture 1.2) the critical-line extension with $\sqrt2$ replaced by $\sqrt g$, $g=\frac8\pi\arcsin(\sqrt{1+e^{4U}}/2)$. Does this joint scaling limit hold at every point of the critical line, including the four-state Potts endpoint?
problems.posedBy: Tomas Alcalde Lopez, Lorca Heeney and Marcin Lis (arXiv 2602.05886, 2026, Conjecture 1.2)
problems.resultNote: For every fixed point of the critical Ashkin-Teller line, including the four-state Potts endpoint, every bounded Jordan domain and every admissible polygonal approximation, the height, the wired and free current-cluster collections and the distinguished boundary cluster converge jointly: the height to a GFF with the predicted coupling constant $\pi\sqrt g$, and the clusters to canonical recursive two-valued local sets of the same field, at all nesting depths, in positive-diameter Hausdorff matching topology. Not claimed: cluster area measures, magnetization fields, all spin-domain-wall curves, or metric exponents.

problems.name: The Ajtai-Erdos-Komlos-Szemeredi conjecture on independent sets in K_r-free graphs
problems.statement: Every graph with $n$ vertices and average degree $d$ has an independent set of size at least $n/(d+1)$, and disjoint cliques show this is sharp. Ajtai, Komlos and Szemeredi (1980) proved that triangle-free graphs have $\alpha(G)\gg n\log d/d$, and Shearer sharpened the constant to $1-o(1)$. In 1981 Ajtai, Erdos, Komlos and Szemeredi conjectured the same order for every fixed forbidden clique; they proved $\Omega_r(n\log\log d/d)$, and Shearer (1995) improved this to $\Omega_r(n\log d/(d\log\log d))$. For fixed $r\ge4$, does every $K_r$-free graph on $n$ vertices with average degree $d$ have an independent set of size $\Omega_r(n\log d/d)$?
problems.posedBy: M. Ajtai, P. Erdos, J. Komlos and E. Szemeredi, On Turan's theorem for sparse graphs, Combinatorica 1 (1981), p. 314; Erdos Problem #802
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every $r\ge4$ there is $c_r>0$ such that every finite $K_r$-free graph with $n$ vertices and average degree $d\ge2$ has $\alpha(G)\ge c_r n\log d/d$, removing the $\log\log d$ loss in Shearer's 1995 bound. The proof maximizes an entropy functional over vertex weights and shows that the weighted triangle mass is at most $O_r$ times the edge mass, via random multipliers, vertex splitting and a recursion on the clique size. The constant $c_r$ is not optimized and no leading coefficient (as in Shearer's triangle-free result) is claimed.

problems.name: Harary's Snaky problem: is the Snaky hexomino a winner in the planar Maker-Breaker achievement game?
problems.statement: In Harary's polyomino achievement games two players alternately claim cells of the infinite square grid; Maker wins on owning a translated, rotated or reflected copy of a fixed polyomino. The target is the hexomino Snaky, $\{(0,0),(1,0),(2,0),(3,0),(3,1),(4,1)\}$. Known: no pairing defense for Breaker, a win in 41 and in three dimensions, a loss on the $8\times8$ board, and a planar win with handicap one (Halupczok-Schlage-Puchta, Ito-Miyagawa, Sieben). Can Maker, moving first on the empty infinite plane with no handicap, force a copy of Snaky?
problems.posedBy: Frank Harary (polyomino achievement games, as attributed by Sieben 2004); the ordinary planar case recorded as undecided by Nandor Sieben (Integers 8, 2008)
problems.ageNote: The manuscript attributes the games to Harary via Sieben (2004) but gives no date for Harary's question; the latest cited statement that it is open is Sieben (Integers 8, 2008, G07).
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1: one globally legal Maker policy completes Snaky within 21 Maker claims (by the 41st turn) against every legal Breaker play on the empty infinite board, so Snaky is a winner in the planar weak game. It works on a $17\times17$ board, using a fixed 251-cell region; 25- and 35-move constructions are also given. problems.name: The Phillips-Toms conjecture for minimal homeomorphisms: radius of comparison equals half the mean dimension
problems.field: Operator algebras; C*-dynamics and mean dimension
problems.statement: For a minimal homeomorphism $h$ of an infinite compact metrizable space $X$, the crossed product $C(X)\rtimes_h\mathbb Z$ is a simple unital nuclear C*-algebra. Toms's radius of comparison $\mathrm{rc}(A)$ is the least $r$ such that $d_\tau(a)+r<d_\tau(b)$ for every trace $\tau$ forces Cuntz subequivalence $a\precsim b$; the Lindenstrauss-Weiss mean dimension $\mathrm{mdim}(X,h)$ measures dimension per orbit coordinate. Giol and Kerr built minimal systems of positive mean dimension with large radius of comparison; Phillips proved $\mathrm{rc}\le1+36\,\mathrm{mdim}$, Elliott and Niu settled zero mean dimension, and Niu proved $\mathrm{rc}\le\frac12\mathrm{mdim}$. The Phillips-Toms conjecture, recorded for integer actions by Elliott-Niu and as Problem XXXVI of Schafhauser-Tikuisis-White, predicts equality. Is $\mathrm{rc}(C(X)\rtimes_h\mathbb Z)=\frac12\mathrm{mdim}(X,h)$ for every such system, including the value $\infty$?
problems.posedBy: N. Christopher Phillips and Andrew Toms; integer-action form recorded by Elliott and Niu (Duke 2017) and as Problem XXXVI of Schafhauser-Tikuisis-White
problems.ageNote: The manuscript names Phillips and Toms but does not date the conjecture. The earliest record it cites is Elliott-Niu (Duke Math. J. 2017; preprint arXiv:1406.2382, 2014); Schafhauser-Tikuisis-White list it as Problem XXXVI (2025-2026). Niu states a broader form for free minimal actions of amenable groups.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every minimal homeomorphism $h$ of an infinite compact metrizable $X$, $\mathrm{rc}(C(X)\rtimes_h\mathbb Z)=\frac12\mathrm{mdim}(X,h)$ in $[0,\infty]$. The new part is $\mathrm{mdim}\le2\,\mathrm{rc}$, obtained by turning comparison witnesses into bundle data and compressing cube-valued maps via the companion's cobordism theorem, for every finite open cover and with no finite-dimensionality hypothesis on $X$. Corollary 1.2: zero mean dimension, the small boundary property, Jiang-Su stability, finite nuclear dimension and nuclear dimension at most one are equivalent for these crossed products. It does not treat $\mathbb Z^d$ or general amenable group actions (Niu's broader formulation).
