problems.name: The Lins-de Melo-Pugh conjecture for quintic Lienard systems: at most two limit cycles
problems.statement: Lins, de Melo and Pugh conjectured that the classical Lienard system $\dot x=y-F(x)$, $\dot y=-x$, with $F$ a real polynomial of degree $n\ge1$, has at most $\lfloor (n-1)/2\rfloor$ limit cycles. The conjecture fails for every $n\ge6$ (Dumortier-Panazzolo-Roussarie in degree seven, De Maesschalck-Dumortier in degree six, De Maesschalck-Huzak in all degrees $n\ge6$) and holds for $n\le4$ (Li and Llibre for the quartic case); Rychkov proved it for odd quintic $F$. That left degree five. Does every classical Lienard system with $\deg F\le5$ have at most two limit cycles?
problems.posedBy: A. Lins, W. de Melo and C. C. Pugh, On Lienard's equation (Lecture Notes in Mathematics 597, Springer, 1977)
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites an August 2026 preprint by Chen, Li, Zhang and Zhang whose introduction reports the unrestricted degree-five case as open.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: if $\deg F\le5$, with no parity or coefficient-sign assumption, the system $\dot x=y-F(x)$, $\dot y=-x$ has at most two limit cycles in $\mathbb R^2$, counted as geometric images regardless of multiplicity, stability or hyperbolicity, and some member of the class has exactly two. This confirms the conjectured value $\lfloor (5-1)/2\rfloor=2$. It concerns only the classical form with restoring force exactly $x$; generalized Lienard systems and other degrees are not treated. The paper also shows that a proposed degree-five four-cycle example of Hernandez Rosales has only two cycles.

problems.name: Three-machine unit-job scheduling with precedence constraints (Garey-Johnson OPEN8): is P3|prec,p_j=1|Cmax in P?
problems.statement: Given a directed acyclic graph on $n$ unit-length jobs and a deadline $T$, can the jobs be scheduled on $m$ identical machines, at most $m$ per time slot, so that every precedence $u\to v$ has $u$ strictly before $v$ and all jobs finish by $T$? For $m=2$ this is polynomial (Fujii-Kasami-Ninomiya 1969, Coffman-Graham 1972); with $m$ part of the input it is NP-complete (Ullman 1975). The fixed case $m=3$, $P3\mid\mathrm{prec},p_j=1\mid C_{\max}$, is listed as open problem OPEN8 in Garey and Johnson's book; the best exact algorithm known ran in time $2^{O(\sqrt n\log n)}$ (Nederlof-Swennenhuis-Wegrzycki). Is three-machine unit-job scheduling with precedence constraints solvable in polynomial time, or is it NP-complete?
problems.posedBy: Michael R. Garey and David S. Johnson, Computers and Intractability (1979), Appendix A13, OPEN8
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: a uniform deterministic algorithm constructs a minimum-makespan schedule for unit-length jobs with arbitrary precedence constraints on three identical machines, and decides feasibility for a deadline $1\le T\le n$ exactly, in $O((L+2)^{150020})$ Turing machine steps. The method decomposes schedules into gaps whose job sets have bounded-size global Boolean descriptions and searches them by dynamic programming. The exponent is astronomically large and no practical claim is made. It does not settle $m\ge4$ fixed machines, which remains open.

problems.name: Ostmann's inverse Goldbach conjecture
problems.field: Additive number theory; sumsets and the primes
problems.statement: Two subsets of $\mathbb N_0$ are asymptotically equal if their symmetric difference is finite. Ostmann conjectured that the set $\mathcal P$ of primes is asymptotically additively indecomposable. Is it true that there are no sets $A,B\subseteq\mathbb N_0$, each with at least two elements, such that $A+B$ differs from $\mathcal P$ in only finitely many elements?
problems.posedBy: Hans-Heinrich Ostmann (Additive Zahlentheorie, 1956, p. 13); restated by Elsholtz and Harper (2015, Conjecture 1.2)
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: if $A,B\subseteq\mathbb N_0$ have $|A|,|B|\ge2$, then $(A+B)\triangle\mathcal P$ is infinite. After the Laffer-Mann reduction to two infinite summands, the proof combines residue restrictions at every prime, decorrelation from translated multiplicative characters, prime coverage and a positive statistic averaged over arrangements; it does not use Green and Harper's conditional inverse-sieve route. In particular, if $A+B$ contains every large prime it contains infinitely many composites. No quantitative version is claimed.

problems.name: The existential Hilbert sixteenth problem: a uniform bound on the number of limit cycles of planar polynomial vector fields
problems.field: Planar polynomial vector fields; limit cycles
problems.statement: Hilbert's sixteenth problem asks, in its second part, for the maximum number and the relative position of the limit cycles of a real planar polynomial vector field $\dot x=P(x,y)$, $\dot y=Q(x,y)$ of degree $d$. Its existential form, which Ilyashenko's centennial survey separates from finiteness for each individual field, asks whether that maximum is finite at all. Even the quadratic case $d=2$ was open. Is there, for every $d\ge1$, a finite number $H(d)$ such that every real planar polynomial vector field of degree at most $d$ has at most $H(d)$ limit cycles?
problems.posedBy: David Hilbert (1900), Problem 16, second part; the uniform-boundedness form as distinguished by Yu. Ilyashenko, Centennial history of Hilbert's 16th problem (Bull. AMS, 2002)
problems.ageNote: Posed at the 1900 Paris congress; the manuscript cites the 1902 Bulletin AMS translation. Finiteness for each single field (Dulac's problem) is a different, weaker statement, proved by Ecalle and Ilyashenko around 1991-1992. The uniform bound was open in every degree d >= 2.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for each $d\ge1$ there is a finite integer $B(d)$ such that every real planar polynomial vector field of degree at most $d$ has at most $B(d)$ limit cycles in the whole plane, with no restriction on coefficients, location, stability or hyperbolicity. The proof works with matching systems of local passages and shows that each fixed auxiliary system has finitely many isolated solutions, uniformly as coefficients vary. It does NOT give an explicit or effective $B(d)$, so it says nothing about the value of $H(2)$, about Smale's question whether $H(d)\le Kd^q$, or about the relative positions of cycles asked for in Hilbert's full second part. The exact quintic Lienard bound in the same family is a separate entry.
problems.aiRole: The release README states that the vast majority of its results were produced by one fixed procedure with an unreleased internal OpenAI model, using on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result; roughly 4,000 problems were posed and the output was aggregated into result families and manuscripts, keeping those judged significant enough. This family consists of two manuscripts dated September 24, 2026; the uniform-bound manuscript is the principal one. The manuscript is credited to 'OpenAI' alone, names no human author and has no acknowledgements. The README's two exceptions to the fixed procedure (the zeta zero-free region work, whose Re(s) > 11/12 write-up was also human-edited, and the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties) do not concern this family, so the result is presented as found and written up by the model. The release does not say how problems were chosen or how much human review happened before publication.

Checked here: the abstract, introduction and Theorem 1.1 of the principal manuscript were read against the problem as the manuscript's own historical section describes it. The theorem states the uniform bound in full generality: every degree, the whole plane, no genericity, cycles counted as geometric images regardless of stability or hyperbolicity. problems.name: Kuznetsov's rationality conjecture for cubic fourfolds
problems.field: Algebraic geometry: rationality, derived categories, cubic fourfolds
problems.statement: For a smooth complex cubic fourfold $X\subset\mathbf P^5$, the Kuznetsov component $\mathrm{Ku}(X)$ is the right orthogonal of $\mathcal O_X,\mathcal O_X(1),\mathcal O_X(2)$ in $D^b(X)$, a K3 category. All known rational cubics (Pfaffian, containing a plane with a section, divisors $\mathcal C_{26},\mathcal C_{38},\mathcal C_{42}$) have $\mathrm{Ku}(X)$ equivalent to the derived category of a K3 surface, and by Addington-Thomas this matches Hassett's lattice condition for associated K3 surfaces. Kuznetsov conjectured that $X$ is rational if and only if $\mathrm{Ku}(X)\simeq D^b(S)$ for a projective K3 surface $S$. Is that true?
problems.posedBy: Alexander Kuznetsov (Derived categories of cubic fourfolds, 2010, Conjecture 1.1)
problems.ageNote: Kuznetsov's paper appeared in the 2010 Progress in Mathematics volume (arXiv 2008). The Hodge-theoretic associated-K3 form goes back to Hassett (2000) and Harris-Hassett folklore; the manuscript cites Huybrechts' 2025 survey for its explicit form.
problems.resultNote: Claims that for every sufficiently large admissible Hassett discriminant $d$ a very general cubic fourfold of discriminant $d$ is irrational although its Kuznetsov component is the derived category of a K3 surface and it has an associated polarized K3 in Hassett's Hodge-theoretic sense. This disproves Kuznetsov's conjecture and the sufficiency of the associated-K3 criterion (and of Fano variety birational to a K3 Hilbert square). The threshold is ineffective; no specific discriminant is shown irrational, the necessity direction is untouched, and stable rationality is not decided. These are not the first irrational cubic fourfolds: the paper cites Katzarkov-Kontsevich-Pantev-Yu (very general cubic) and Fay (some special divisors).
problems.aiRole: The OpenAI math release (github.com/openai/math) states that its results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model, with on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result, under one fixed procedure applied to roughly 4,000 posed problems; outputs were then grouped into families and filtered for significance. The manuscript is credited to OpenAI alone and names no human author.
problems.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 and Corollaries 1.2 and 1.3 of the TeX source read against the posed problem. For every admissible $d$ above an ineffective $d_0$, a very general cubic in $\mathcal C_d$ is irrational yet has $\mathrm{Ku}(X)\simeq D^b(S)$; this refutes the categorical-implies-rational direction, which is enough to disprove the conjecture. The categorical equivalence comes from published work (Addington-Thomas; Bayer, Lahoz, Macri, Nuer, Perry, Stellari); the new part is irrationality, via an additive invariant of birational maps computed by weak factorization with Gromov-Witten operators and by Sarkisov links. Not refereed. No Lean formalization is listed.

problems.name: The David-Semmes problem in higher codimension: bounded Riesz transforms force uniform rectifiability for 1 < n < d-1
problems.field: Harmonic analysis; geometric measure theory, uniform rectifiability
problems.statement: Let $\mu$ be an $n$-Ahlfors-David regular measure on $\mathbb R^d$ and $R_\mu$ the $n$-dimensional Riesz transform with kernel $x/|x|^{n+1}$. David and Semmes asked whether boundedness of $R_\mu$ on $L^2(\mu)$ implies that $\mu$ is uniformly $n$-rectifiable. The answer is yes for $n=1$ (Mattila-Melnikov-Verdera in the plane, curvature methods in general) and for $n=d-1$ (Nazarov-Tolsa-Volberg, 2014), whose maximum-principle argument has no known higher-codimension analogue; Mas and Tolsa characterized uniform rectifiability through $\rho$-variation, a stronger hypothesis. Is every $n$-AD-regular measure on $\mathbb R^d$ with $L^2$-bounded Riesz transform uniformly $n$-rectifiable when $1<n<d-1$?
problems.posedBy: Guy David and Stephen Semmes
problems.ageNote: David and Semmes, Singular integrals and rectifiable sets in R^n (Asterisque 193, 1991) and Analysis of and on uniformly rectifiable sets (AMS, 1993); the remaining range is Question 4.4 of Tolsa's ICM survey, all as cited by the manuscript.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.3: for integers $d\ge4$ and $2\le n\le d-2$, an $n$-AD-regular Radon measure on $\mathbb R^d$ whose hard-truncated Riesz transforms are uniformly bounded $L^2(\mu)\to L^2(\mu;\mathbb R^d)$ is uniformly $n$-rectifiable, with constants depending only on $d,n,C_{AD},C_R$; the conclusion is given as uniform big pieces of Lipschitz images of balls. With the known cases $n=1$ and $n=d-1$ this answers the David-Semmes question in every dimension and codimension. The converse direction and non-integer dimensions are not addressed here.

The single manuscript (September 24, 2026) is the whole family.

The proof was not refereed. lean/formalization.yaml lists RieszQuantitative (OAI.RieszRectifiability.quantitative_higher_codimension_riesz_rectifiability). problems.name: Irrationality of Catalan's constant
problems.statement: Catalan's constant is $G=\beta(2)=\sum_{j\ge0}(-1)^j/(2j+1)^2=L(2,\chi_{-4})$, the simplest even value of the Dirichlet beta function. Odd beta values are rational multiples of powers of $\pi$, but nothing was known about the arithmetic of $G$ itself. Rivoal and Zudilin (2003) proved that infinitely many even beta values are irrational and that at least one of $\beta(2),\beta(4),\ldots,\beta(14)$ is, a list later cut to $\beta(2),\ldots,\beta(10)$; such family results never single out $G$. Apery-like recurrences and continued fractions for $G$ (Zudilin 2003) converge fast, but the integer linear forms they give do not tend to zero once denominators are cleared. Is Catalan's constant irrational?
problems.posedBy: Long-standing open problem with no single poser; the manuscript frames it through Rivoal and Zudilin (Math. Ann. 2003) and Zudilin (2003)
problems.ageNote: The manuscript names no poser and no date for the question. Zhi-Wei Sun's preprint on the same question (arXiv:2609.04176) calls it a long-standing open problem about a constant introduced by Catalan in the nineteenth century. Year left blank rather than guessed.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: $G$ is irrational. Under the hypothesis $G\in\mathbb Q$ the paper builds mixed determinants $\Delta_N$ of size $48N$ from moments of two kernels, whose $\zeta(2)$ terms cancel by Taylor contact of Chebyshev rows, so all $\Delta_N$ are rational; a finite certificate gives $\Delta_p\ne0$ for large primes $p$, prime-by-prime denominator bounds give $\liminf\mathcal L_p>-2.29084$, and a real-place integral estimate gives $\limsup\mathcal L_N<-2.2909$, a contradiction. Corollaries: $4G$, the minimal volume of a two-cusped orientable hyperbolic 3-manifold, and every arithmetic hyperbolic 3-orbifold volume over $\mathbb Q(i)$ are irrational. Not shown: an irrationality measure, transcendence, or anything about $\beta(4),\beta(6),\ldots$. An earlier preprint by Zhi-Wei Sun (arXiv:2609.04176, 3 September 2026) also claims irrationality; the manuscript says it uses nothing from it, so the first claimed proof may not be this one.

The manuscript is credited to OpenAI alone, names no human author and has no acknowledgements. A Lean formalization of the irrationality statement is in the release's lean/ library (lean/docs/005.md). The release does not say how much human review happened before publication.

problems.name: The Virasoro conjecture for smooth complete intersections in projective space (and its transfer to projective bundles)
problems.statement: For a smooth projective variety $X$, let $Z_X=\exp(\sum_g\hbar^{g-1}F_g^X)$ be the total descendant Gromov-Witten potential. Eguchi, Hori and Xiong (1997) proposed target-dependent differential operators $L_k^X$, $k\ge-1$, built from the Poincare pairing, a Hodge grading and cup product with $c_1(TX)$, generalising the Witten-Kontsevich KdV constraints for a point; Eguchi, Jinzenji and Xiong extended them to odd and off-diagonal classes. The Virasoro conjecture asserts $L_k^XZ_X=0$ for all $k\ge-1$. Genus zero, Calabi-Yau targets with $H^1=0$, curves, toric bundles and semisimple theories (Givental-Teleman) were known, but non-semisimple higher-genus targets largely were not. Does the Virasoro conjecture hold, in every genus and curve class with arbitrary insertions, for every smooth complete intersection in projective space?
problems.posedBy: Tohru Eguchi, Kentaro Hori and Chuan-Sheng Xiong (extended by Eguchi, Jinzenji and Xiong)
problems.ageNote: Eguchi, Hori and Xiong, Quantum cohomology and Virasoro algebra, Phys. Lett. B 402 (1997), cited by the manuscript; odd-class extension Eguchi-Jinzenji-Xiong, Nucl. Phys. B 510 (1998).
problems.resultNote: Principal theorem: for a smooth complete intersection $X\subset\mathbb P^N_{\mathbb C}$, $L_k^XZ_X=0$ for all $k\ge-1$ in Getzler's first-Hodge-degree superspace convention, coefficientwise in every genus and curve class, with arbitrary insertions from $H^*(X;\mathbb C)$. Companion: if the full constraints hold for a smooth connected projective base $B$, they hold for $\mathbb P_B(E)$ for any algebraic vector bundle $E$ of rank at least 2 (no splitting or positivity), hence for projective-bundle towers. The conjecture for general smooth projective varieties (for example general hypersurfaces in other ambients, or varieties with no degeneration to known pieces) remains open.

problems.name: Rigidity of the Turing degrees: is every automorphism of the Turing degrees the identity?
problems.statement: The Turing degrees $\mathcal D_T$ are the classes of subsets of $\mathbb N$ under mutual Turing reducibility, partially ordered by $\le_T$. Jockusch and Solovay showed jump-preserving automorphisms fix every degree above $\mathbf 0^{(4)}$; Shore and Slaman showed the jump is definable, so every automorphism preserves it; Nerode and Shore showed each automorphism fixes a cone; and Slaman and Woodin showed every automorphism fixes all degrees above $\mathbf 0''$, that the automorphism group is countable, and that rigidity is equivalent to their biinterpretability conjecture. The rigidity problem asks: is every order automorphism $\pi$ of $(\mathcal D_T,\le_T)$ the identity?
problems.posedBy: Classical problem of degree theory; equivalent (Slaman-Woodin) to the Slaman-Woodin biinterpretability conjecture
problems.ageNote: The manuscript calls it the rigidity conjecture for the Turing degrees without naming who first posed it. It cites Slaman-Woodin's 2005 manuscript for the equivalent biinterpretability conjecture; the automorphism question is older (Nerode-Shore 1980 and Jockusch-Solovay 1977 already work on it). Year left blank.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: every order automorphism of $(\mathcal D_T,\le_T)$ is the identity. The proof represents an arbitrary automorphism by an arithmetic, hence Borel, map on reals (Slaman-Woodin), recovers any irrational from four values of such a map at rational affine combinations of it and two auxiliary reals, for a comeager set of auxiliary pairs, and removes the auxiliaries by Sacks-type category cone avoidance. As a corollary it settles the Slaman-Woodin biinterpretability conjecture positively. It does not address rigidity of other degree structures such as the computably enumerable degrees or the degrees below $\mathbf 0'$.
problems.aiRole: The release README says every result in openai/math was produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model with a fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result. This result is not one of the README's two exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region). The manuscript is authored 'OpenAI' and names no human author. The manuscript is short (five sections). Its external input is the Slaman-Woodin representation theorem from their 2005 unpublished manuscript; the proof adds a four-value recovery argument for Borel maps and a category cone-avoidance step.

problems.name: Zilber-Pink for Hodge-generic curves in the Siegel modular threefold A_2
problems.statement: Let $\mathcal A_2$ be the moduli space of principally polarized abelian surfaces. Pink's Zilber-Pink conjecture for mixed Shimura varieties (2005, Conjecture 1.3) predicts that a Hodge-generic curve meets the union of special subvarieties of codimension at least two only finitely often; in $\mathcal A_2$ these are the special points and the special curves (products with a CM elliptic factor, squares of non-CM elliptic curves, quaternionic multiplication). Pila and Tsimerman proved Andre-Oort for $\mathcal A_2$, and Daw and Orr proved the curve loci under boundary or multiplicative-reduction hypotheses. For a Hodge-generic algebraic curve $C\subset\mathcal A_2$ over $\bar{\mathbb Q}$, is $C\cap\bigcup_{\dim Z\le1}Z$ finite?
problems.posedBy: Richard Pink (2005, Conjecture 1.3, for mixed Shimura varieties); the A_2 curve case studied by Christopher Daw and Martin Orr (2021-2025)
problems.resultNote: Claims the full curve case of Zilber-Pink in $\mathcal A_2$ over $\bar{\mathbb Q}$: a Hodge-generic algebraic curve contains only finitely many points whose abelian surface is isogenous to a product with a CM factor, to the square of a non-CM elliptic curve, or has quaternionic-division endomorphism algebra, besides finitely many special points. Previous unconditional results needed the curve to meet the Baily-Borel boundary or to have multiplicative degeneration. It does NOT treat higher-dimensional subvarieties of $\mathcal A_2$, $\mathcal A_g$ for $g\ge3$, or curves not defined over $\bar{\mathbb Q}$.

Its named exceptions to that procedure (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties and the zeta zero-free region work) do not concern this family. All three manuscripts are credited to OpenAI with no human author named.

It assembles three branch theorems: elliptic squares (proved here, by establishing the Galois-orbit lower bound Daw and Orr state as their Conjecture 6.2 and applying their Theorem 1.3), and the E x CM and quaternionic-division branches from the two companions, plus Pila-Tsimerman for special points. The companions were read at the level of their main theorems only. No Lean formalization. Curves over $\mathbb C$ not defined over $\bar{\mathbb Q}$ are not covered.

problems.name: The Kapovich-Millson saturation conjecture for simply laced groups, type D: tensor saturation for $\mathrm{Spin}(2n)$
problems.field: Representation theory: tensor product multiplicities and saturation
problems.statement:
Let $G$ be a simply connected complex semisimple group with root lattice $Q$, and $V(\lambda)$ the irreducible representation of highest weight $\lambda$. For dominant $\lambda,\mu,
u$ with $\lambda+\mu+
u\in Q$, saturation asks whether $(V(N\lambda)\otimes V(N\mu)\otimes V(N
u))^G
e0$ for some positive integer $N$ forces $(V(\lambda)\otimes V(\mu)\otimes V(
u))^G
e0$. Knutson and Tao proved this for type A. Kapovich and Millson conjectured it for all simply laced groups. Known before this work: $\mathrm{Spin}(8)$ (Kapovich-Kumar-Millson), $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$ and $\mathrm{Spin}(12)$ (Kiers), and saturation factors two or four for classical groups (Kapovich-Millson, Belkale-Kumar, Sam, Hong-Shen), which do not give the factor-one statement. Does saturation with factor one hold for $\mathrm{Spin}(2n)$ for every $n$?

problems.resultNote:
Theorem 1.1: for $G=\mathrm{Spin}(2n)$, $n\ge2$, and dominant integral $\lambda,\mu,
u$ with $\lambda+\mu+
u\in Q(D_n)$, and every positive integer $N$, $(V(\lambda)\otimes V(\mu)\otimes V(
u))^G
e0$ if and only if $(V(N\lambda)\otimes V(N\mu)\otimes V(N
u))^G
e0$. This settles the type-D part of the simply laced saturation conjecture, extending the known cases $\mathrm{Spin}(8),\mathrm{Spin}(10),\mathrm{Spin}(12)$. Not shown: the exceptional types $E_6,E_7,E_8$, non-simply-laced groups, or any statement about multiplicities beyond nonvanishing.

problems.name: The ionization conjecture: bounded excess charge, ionization energy and radius for Coulomb atoms and molecules (Simon's Problem 9)
problems.statement: For the nonrelativistic Coulomb Hamiltonian of $n$ electrons (two spin states, Fermi statistics) around fixed nuclei of total charge $Z$, let $N_c$ be the largest number of electrons that is strictly bound. Lieb proved $N_c<2Z+M$, Lieb-Sigal-Simon-Thirring proved $N_c/Z\to1$ for atoms, and later work gave sublinear and explicit bounds such as $1.22Z+3Z^{1/3}$, but no uniform bound on the excess. Simon's Problem 9 (2000) asks whether $N_c(Z)-Z$ stays bounded for atoms; the molecular form asks for $N_c\le Z+CM$ with $M$ nuclei (Lewin 2025). The ionization conjecture as surveyed by Solovej also asks that the first ionization energy and the outer radius of neutral atoms stay bounded independently of $Z$. Is the excess charge bounded by a universal constant per nucleus, and are the neutral-atom ionization energy and radius bounded uniformly in $Z$?
problems.posedBy: Barry Simon (Problem 9 of his 2000 list); molecular form in Mathieu Lewin's 2025 open-problem survey
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites Simon, Schrodinger operators in the twenty-first century (2000), Problem 9, and Lewin (C. R. Physique 2025, Section 2.1.2) for the molecular form, and Solovej (2016, Section 2) for the boundedness of the ionization energy. The conjecture circulated earlier, in the Lieb-Sigal-Simon-Thirring era of the 1980s, but the manuscript gives no earlier statement.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there is a universal $C$ such that for every $M\ge1$, all distinct nuclear positions and all real charges $z_j\ge1$ with $Z=\sum z_j$, strict binding $E_n<E_{n-1}$ implies $n\le Z+CM$, and $E_n=E_{n-1}$ for $n>Z+CM$. For atoms this is Simon's bounded excess charge. Theorem 1.2: for every integer $Z\ge1$ and every neutral ground state, the radius outside which half an electron remains lies between universal constants. Corollary 1.3: the neutral first ionization energy satisfies $c\le I_1(Z)\le C$. Not shown: the value of the constants, relativistic or magnetic models, or the asymptotic (generalized) form, which is the separate generalized ionization entry.

problems.name: The Zilber-Pink conjecture for abelian varieties over number fields
problems.statement: Let $A$ be an abelian variety over a number field and $X\subseteq A_{\bar{\mathbb Q}}$ an irreducible subvariety, and let $S$ be the smallest torsion coset containing $X$. A component $Y$ of $X\cap T$, for a torsion coset $T\subseteq S$, is atypical if $\dim Y>\dim X+\dim T-\dim S$. Zilber (2002, for semiabelian varieties) and Pink (2005) conjectured that such unlikely intersections are controlled, generalizing Manin-Mumford and Mordell-Lang. The curve case was proved by Habegger and Pila (2016); higher dimensions were known only under extra quotient-dimension or height conditions or in codimension one or two. Does every such $X$ have only finitely many maximal atypical subvarieties?
problems.posedBy: Boris Zilber (J. London Math. Soc., 2002) and Richard Pink (ETH preprint, 2005, Conjecture 5.1 for semiabelian varieties)
problems.ageNote: Zilber's 2002 paper formulated the principle for semiabelian varieties; Pink's 2005 preprint gave the semiabelian and mixed Shimura formulations. The manuscript proves the abelian case over number fields.
problems.resultNote: Claims that for any abelian variety over a number field, every irreducible subvariety has only finitely many maximal atypical subvarieties inside its smallest containing torsion coset, via a non-density theorem for $X\cap A^{[\dim X+1]}$ for $X$ in no proper torsion coset. A corollary gives the abelian algebraic-point case of Pink's Conjecture 5.2 for finite-rank translates. It does NOT treat semiabelian varieties, abelian varieties over $\mathbb C$ not defined over $\bar{\mathbb Q}$, or Shimura varieties, and gives no effective or uniform bound.
problems.aiRole: The release README says the manuscripts were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model, the vast majority by one fixed procedure using on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result, and that some outputs build on earlier results produced by the models. The manuscript is credited to OpenAI with no human author named.

It is the abelian case over $\bar{\mathbb Q}$ of Zilber-Pink, not the semiabelian, complex-field or Shimura cases. The reduction to a non-density theorem uses Barroero and Dill's optimal-subvariety argument as a cited input; the height part builds on Vojta, Faltings, Remond and Dill. No Lean formalization. The finiteness is not effective.

problems.name: The Bass trace conjecture for complex group rings of all discrete groups
problems.field: K-theory of group rings; Hattori-Stallings traces
problems.statement: For a discrete group $G$ and an idempotent matrix $e$ over the group ring $\mathbb CG$, the Hattori-Stallings trace assigns to each conjugacy class $C$ the coefficient $\sum_{g\in C}\sum_i e_{ii}(g)$, giving a map $K_0(\mathbb CG)\to\bigoplus_{C}\mathbb C\,C$. Bass (1976) conjectured that for the integral group ring the trace is supported at the identity; the complex form asks that it vanish on every conjugacy class of infinite-order elements. Berrick, Chatterji and Mislin (2004) also stated an $\ell^1$ form (finite support on finite-order classes for idempotents over $\ell^1(G)$), proved when the Bost assembly map is rationally surjective. Known for many classes of groups but open in general. Does the Hattori-Stallings trace of every finitely generated projective $\mathbb CG$-module vanish on infinite-order conjugacy classes, for every group $G$?
problems.posedBy: H. Bass, Euler characteristics and characters of discrete groups (Inventiones 1976); complex and l1 forms: Berrick, Chatterji and Mislin, Math. Annalen (2004), Conjectures 2.1 and 2.2
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1 (24 September): for every discrete group $G$, every $x\in K_0(\mathbb CG)$ and every infinite-order $g$, $\mathrm{HS}_G(x)([g])=0$; the integral (identity-support) form for $\mathbb ZG$ is deduced in Section 9. The 5 October companion proves the $\ell^1$-Bass conjecture (BCM 2004, Conjecture 2.2): the trace of every idempotent over $\ell^1(G)$ is supported on finitely many finite-order classes, with no assembly hypothesis, which implies the complex form. Neither manuscript addresses the reduced $C^*$-algebra (the Kadison-Kaplansky question), where this release separately claims a counterexample.

problems.name: Barnette's conjecture
problems.field: Graph theory: Hamiltonian cycles in planar graphs
problems.statement: A graph is cubic if every vertex has degree three, and polyhedral if it is planar and 3-vertex-connected, that is, the graph of a convex polyhedron. Tait conjectured that every cubic polyhedral graph is Hamiltonian; Tutte disproved this in 1946. Barnette's conjecture restricts to bipartite graphs. Known before this work: all faces of size 4 or 6 (Goodey), arbitrary faces in one face color class with only quadrilaterals and hexagons in the other two (Feder-Subi), and all faces of size at most 8 (Schnieders, 2025). Does every finite simple cubic bipartite planar 3-vertex-connected graph have a Hamiltonian cycle?
problems.posedBy: David Barnette; recorded by Branko Grunbaum as Unsolved Problem 5 in Recent Progress in Combinatorics (Proceedings of the Third Waterloo Conference, May 1968), Academic Press, 1969
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites Grunbaum's record in the 1969 proceedings of the May 1968 Waterloo conference; it gives no separate date for Barnette's own formulation.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: every finite simple cubic bipartite planar 3-vertex-connected graph has a Hamiltonian cycle. In the dual triangulation (Stein; Alt-Payne-Schmidt-Wood) the paper splits the vertices into two induced trees with a prescribed facial pattern, using Tutte states, a signed exponential sum over pairs of states, and gluing along separating triangles. Corollaries: the Hamiltonian cycle can avoid any prescribed edge (a known equivalent strengthening, via Kelmans, Hertel and Gorsky-Steiner-Wiederrecht), and every three-edge path in a cubic 3-connected Pfaffian bipartite graph lies in a Hamiltonian cycle. The result is confined to the bipartite polyhedral class.

problems.name: Polynomial-size black-box identity testing for noncommutative rational formulas
problems.shortName: Polynomial hitting sets for NC rational formulas
problems.field: Algebraic complexity; derandomization of polynomial identity testing
problems.statement: A noncommutative rational formula is a formula with $+$, $\times$ and inverse gates over noncommuting variables, evaluated on tuples of square matrices where every inverse is defined. Hrubes and Wigderson reduced its identity testing to noncommutative singularity, solved deterministically in the white-box model by operator scaling. In the black-box model, Forbes-Shpilka gave quasipolynomial matrix hitting sets for division-free formulas, and Arvind, Chatterjee and Mukhopadhyay gave deterministic quasipolynomial-size rational matrix hitting sets for rational formulas of any inversion height, asking in their conclusion for polynomial matrix dimension. Is there a deterministic polynomial-time construction of a polynomial-size list of matrix tuples hitting every nonzero rational formula of size $s$ in $n$ variables?
problems.posedBy: V. Arvind, Abhranil Chatterjee and Partha Mukhopadhyay, Black-box identity testing of noncommutative rational formulas in deterministic quasipolynomial time, arXiv:2309.15647 (2023), conclusion
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites the 2025 revision of the arXiv preprint (first posted September 2023) for the request for polynomial matrix dimension.
problems.resultNote: Claims deterministic polynomial-time construction of polynomial-size rational matrix hitting lists for noncommutative rational formulas over $\mathbb Q$, with no bound on inverse nesting or constant heights, each nonzero formula receiving an invertible value. Companions: one rational tuple of dimension at most $2ns^2$ hits every nonzero division-free formula over every characteristic-zero field, and an analogous tuple over $\mathbb F_p$ works in each positive characteristic. It does NOT cover general noncommutative circuits, and the rational result is over $\mathbb Q$ only.

The manuscripts are credited to OpenAI with no human author named. The family has three manuscripts: the rational-formula hitting lists (principal), a single rational hitting point for division-free formulas over every characteristic-zero field (same date), and a positive-characteristic version (4 October). The release formalizes the principal theorem and the single-point theorem in Lean.

problems.name: The Fourier restriction conjecture in three dimensions for positively curved surfaces: bounded-data and diagonal forms
problems.statement: For a compact smooth positively curved surface $\Sigma\subset\mathbb R^3$, such as the sphere, let $E_\Sigma f(x)=\int_\Sigma f(\xi)e^{2\pi i x\cdot\xi}\,d\sigma(\xi)$. Stein's restriction conjecture in $\mathbb R^3$ asks that $E_\Sigma$ map $L^q(\Sigma)$ to $L^p(\mathbb R^3)$ whenever $p>3$ and $p\ge 2q'$. Its bounded-data form asks for $L^\infty(\Sigma)\to L^p(\mathbb R^3)$ for all $p>3$ (Guth reached $p>13/4$), and its diagonal form for $L^p(\Sigma)\to L^p(\mathbb R^3)$ for all $p>3$ (Wang and Wu reached $p>22/7$). The constant function on the sphere shows $p=3$ fails. Do the bounded-data and diagonal estimates hold for every $p>3$?
problems.posedBy: Elias M. Stein; the manuscripts date the problem to Stein's work and cite his Some problems in harmonic analysis (1979) and the Tomas-Stein theory
problems.ageNote: 1979 is the date of the Stein problem survey the manuscripts cite. The restriction phenomenon is usually traced to Stein's unpublished work of the late 1960s; the manuscripts do not give that date.
problems.resultNote: Principal manuscript, Theorem 1.1: for every compact smooth positively curved $\Sigma\subset\mathbb R^3$, possibly with smooth boundary, and every $3<p<\infty$, $\|E_\Sigma f\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^3)}\le C_{\Sigma,p}\|f\|_{L^p(\Sigma)}$; the proof in fact bounds $L^3$ data into $L^p$. A corollary is free Schrodinger local smoothing in two space dimensions for $p>3$, $s>2-6/p$. Companion: for the sphere, $L^\infty(S^2)\to L^p(\mathbb R^3)$ for every $p>3$, and through Bourgain factorization the strict mixed-norm range $L^a\to L^b$ with $b>3$, $b>2a'$. Not shown: the scaling-line endpoint $p=2q'$ that the full conjecture includes, surfaces with vanishing or mixed-sign curvature, and higher dimensions.

This family consists of two manuscripts dated September 24, 2026; the diagonal-extension manuscript is taken as principal, since its theorem contains the sphere bounded-data case. The manuscript is credited to 'OpenAI' alone, names no human author and has no acknowledgements. problems.name: Existence of bounded-degree F2 coboundary expanders in every dimension
problems.statement: A finite pure $d$-dimensional simplicial complex $X$ is an $\varepsilon$-coboundary expander over $\mathbb{F}_2$ if, with the standard weighted norms, $\|\delta f\|\ge\varepsilon\,\mathrm{dist}(f,B^i(X))$ for every $i$-cochain $f$ and all $i<d$; this forces vanishing cohomology below $d$. Linial-Meshulam random complexes, Latin-square complexes (Lubotzky-Meshulam) and Steiner-system complexes (Lubotzky-Luria-Rosenthal) are coboundary expanders, but their vertex degrees grow. Bounded-degree cosystolic expanders exist in every dimension (Kaufman-Kazhdan-Lubotzky; Evra-Kaufman), and Chapman-Lubotzky (2025) built bounded-degree two-dimensional coboundary expanders. Gromov (2010) asked for large complexes with bounded degree and uniform filling, and Chapman-Lubotzky posed the problem in general: for every $d\ge3$, are there arbitrarily large bounded-degree $d$-dimensional $\mathbb{F}_2$ coboundary expanders with uniform constant?
problems.posedBy: M. Gromov, Singularities, expanders and topology of maps, Part 2 (GAFA 2010), Sections 2.3-2.5 and 2.14; M. Chapman and A. Lubotzky, Adv. Math. 463 (2025), Problem 1.3
problems.ageNote: Gromov's 2010 paper asks for bounded-degree complexes with uniform cohomological filling inequalities; the full coboundary-expansion problem, including vanishing cohomology, is formulated as Problem 1.3 of Chapman-Lubotzky (2025).
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every $d\ge3$ there are $D$, $\varepsilon>0$ and finite connected pure $d$-dimensional complexes $X_m$ with $|X_m(0)|\to\infty$, every vertex in at most $D$ top faces, and $\|\delta_if\|\ge\varepsilon\,\mathrm{dist}(f,B^i)$ for all $i<d$. The complexes are $d$-skeleta of congruence quotients modulo $t^m$ of a coset complex for the Iwahori-type subgroup of $\mathrm{SL}_{2d+1}(k[t])$ over a large odd prime field; cohomology vanishing comes from an affine twin building, and quantitative expansion from Oppenheim-Valentiner-Branth. Constants depend on $d$ and are not explicit; only $\mathbb{F}_2$ coefficients are treated.

problems.name: A (1+epsilon)-approximation of edit distance in almost-linear time
problems.statement: Edit distance between strings of total length $N$ is computable in quadratic time, and Backurs and Indyk showed that a strongly subquadratic exact algorithm would refute SETH. Approximation algorithms reached polylogarithmic factors in time $N^{1+\delta}$ (Andoni-Krauthgamer-Onak), a constant factor in subquadratic time (Chakraborty-Das-Goldenberg-Koucky-Saks), and constant factors depending on $\delta$ in time $N^{1+\delta}$ (Andoni-Nosatzki 2020). For accuracy $1+\varepsilon$ the best known time saved only a quasi-polynomial factor, $N^2/2^{\log^{\Omega(1)}N}$ (Mao-Rubinstein 2026). For every fixed $\varepsilon>0$, is there a randomized $(1+\varepsilon)$-approximation of edit distance running in time $N^{1+o(1)}$?
problems.posedBy: Open question of the edit-distance approximation line (Andoni, Krauthgamer and Onak; Andoni and Nosatzki; Mao and Rubinstein); no single poser cited
problems.ageNote: The manuscript recounts the history of approximation algorithms but cites no paper that poses the question, and none was located here, so no year is set; it has been an open target at least since near-linear constant-factor algorithms appeared (2020).
problems.resultNote: Main theorem: one randomized algorithm, uniform in a rational accuracy input $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, returns for explicitly stored strings with polynomially bounded integer symbols an estimate within factor $1+\varepsilon$ of unit-cost edit distance with probability at least 2/3, in worst-case expected time $N^{1+o(1)}$ on a logarithmic-word RAM; equal strings give 0 deterministically. The bound is pointwise in fixed $\varepsilon$: no polynomial dependence on $1/\varepsilon$ is claimed, and exact computation is used below very large accuracy-dependent thresholds, so it is an asymptotic scheme. Not shown: an alignment or edit script, weighted costs, a deterministic algorithm, or bounds when $\varepsilon$ shrinks with $N$.

problems.name: The second Kahn-Kalai conjecture
problems.field: Random graphs; thresholds and expectation thresholds
problems.statement: For a graph $H$ with at least one edge and at most $n$ vertices, let $p_c(n,H)$ be the density at which $G(n,p)$ contains a copy of $H$ with probability $1/2$, and $p_E(n,H)$ the least density at which every subgraph $F\subseteq H$ has expected copy count at least one (or one half). Always $p_E\le p_c$, and perfect matchings and Hamilton cycles show a logarithmic gap can occur. Kahn and Kalai conjectured in 2007 that this elementary first-moment obstruction determines the threshold up to a logarithm, uniformly in $H$. The abstract (first) Kahn-Kalai conjecture was proved by Park and Pham; it does not give the graph statement, and the best prior general bound was $O(\log^2)$ loss. Is $p_c(n,H)=O(p_E(n,H)\log n)$ for every such $H$, with a universal constant?
problems.posedBy: Jeff Kahn and Gil Kalai (Thresholds and expectation thresholds, Combin. Probab. Comput. 16, 2007)
problems.resultNote: Claims Theorem 1.1: for every $n\ge2$ and every finite simple graph $H$ with $h\ge1$ edges and at most $n$ vertices, $p_c(n,H)\le\min\{1,2048e^{50}p_E(n,H)(1+\log_2 h)\}$, hence $p_c(n,H)\le6144e^{50}p_E(n,H)\log_2 n$. The logarithm depends only on the number of edges of $H$, which is stronger than the conjectured $\log n$. The proof builds on Tran's spread-link cores and the Mossel-Niles-Weed-Sun-Zadik resampling, with a tree reduction replacing Tran's proposed coupling conjecture. Constants are explicit but huge; it says nothing about optimal constants or about hypergraph targets.

The release README says the vast majority of results used one fixed procedure, averaging about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result; this result is not among the README's stated exceptions (the Riemann zeta zero-free region work and the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties). The manuscript is authored as OpenAI with no human author named.

problems.name: The Kervaire conjecture: adjoining one generator and one relator never kills a nontrivial group
problems.field: Combinatorial group theory; equations over groups
problems.statement: Let $A$ be a nontrivial group, let $t$ generate an infinite cyclic group, and let $w$ be any element of the free product $A*\langle t\rangle$. Kervaire's characterization of high-dimensional knot groups (1965) led to the group-theoretic question whether the quotient $(A*\langle t\rangle)/\langle\langle w\rangle\rangle$ can ever be trivial, that is, whether $A*\mathbb Z$ can be normally generated by one element. Known cases included torsion-free $A$ (Klyachko, unimodular case), residually finite and hyperlinear $A$ (via Gerstenhaber-Rothaus and Pestov), and $w$ of special forms. Is $(A*\langle t\rangle)/\langle\langle w\rangle\rangle$ nontrivial for every nontrivial group $A$ and every $w$?
problems.posedBy: Michel Kervaire, Les noeuds de dimensions superieures (1965); the group-theoretic form is traced to this setting by Chen (2026)
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites Kervaire (1965) for the knot-group origin and Chen's survey for the group-theoretic formulation. The stronger Kervaire-Laudenbach injectivity form is covered by the separate entry for Howie's conjecture.
problems.resultNote: Claims Theorem 1.1: for every group $A$ (no torsion, cardinality or presentation hypothesis) and every $w\in A*\langle t\rangle$ with exponent sum $\pm1$ in $t$, the canonical map $A\to(A*\langle t\rangle)/\langle\langle w\rangle\rangle$ is injective, so the equation $w(t)=1$ is solvable in an overgroup. Corollary 1.2: the quotient is nontrivial for every $w$ when $A\ne1$, which is the Kervaire conjecture. It does NOT prove injectivity for other nonzero exponent sums (the Kervaire-Laudenbach form); that is the companion's nonsingular-systems theorem. It does not assert a solution inside $A$ itself.
problems.aiRole: The release README says the manuscripts were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model, the vast majority by one fixed procedure using on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result, and that some outputs build on earlier results produced by the models. Its named exceptions to that procedure (the zeta zero-free region work, whose Re(s) > 11/12 write-up was human edited, and the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties) do not concern this family. Both manuscripts of the family are credited to OpenAI with no human author named. The Kervaire manuscript proves the result directly through a spectral-phase inequality in the group von Neumann algebra and a fixed-space theorem for unitary matrices; the later nonsingular-systems manuscript (5 October 2026) names it as its direct antecedent.
problems.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2 of the principal manuscript were read against the conjecture as posed: Corollary 1.2 is the nontriviality statement for every nontrivial $A$ and every word $w$. The Lean challenge ComparatorChallenges/Kervaire.json (theorem OAI.Kervaire.coefficient_injective, solution module OAI.GroupTheory.Kervaire.Main, present at the pinned commit) is not in the formalization catalogue formalization.yaml; it was found through lean/docs/256.md. Its statement was read here: for every group $A$ and every $w$ in the coproduct of $A$ with multiplicative $\mathbb Z$ whose exponent sum is $\pm1$, the map from $A$ to the quotient by the normal closure of $w$ is injective. That is Theorem 1.1, which is stronger than the headline for unimodular words; the remaining exponent sums follow by the one-line surjection onto $\mathbb Z/d$ given in the paper, which is not itself formalised. Permitted axioms are propext, Quot.sound and Classical.choice. Not rebuilt here. The manuscript records that Kawauchi (2024) published a proposed resolution through ribbon sphere-link groups, which it does not use.

Below Kaplansky's zero-divisor conjecture (62), whose reach is wider, tied with Dixmier's unitarizability problem (55), above the word problem for finite-rank Artin groups (45).

problems.name: Fast mixing of Glauber dynamics for the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model throughout the high-temperature phase, zero external field
problems.shortName: SK Glauber dynamics spectral gap for all beta < 1
problems.statement: For the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model with couplings $J_{ij}\sim N(0,\beta^2/n)$, single-site Glauber (heat-bath) dynamics resamples one spin from its conditional Gibbs law. Physics predicts fast relaxation in the whole replica-symmetric phase $\beta<1$; rigorous fast-mixing results reached $\beta<1/4$ (Eldan-Koehler-Zeitouni; Anari et al.), about $0.295$ (Anari-Koehler-Vuong), $\beta<1/2$ (Wang 2026) and $1/2+\varepsilon_0$ (Boban-Li-Oveis Gharan 2026). Open Problem 15 of the ETH randomstrasse101 list asks: considering the SK model with an arbitrary external field, does Glauber dynamics fast mix (in polynomial time) up to the replica symmetry breaking threshold $\beta^*=1$?
problems.posedBy: Almut Roedder (ETH randomstrasse101 open problems, Problem 15)
problems.ageNote: Open Problem 15 posted 20 December 2024 on the ETH Zurich randomstrasse101 blog, which credits no single original proposer; the expectation of fast mixing for all beta < 1 is older physics folklore. The release's manuscripts do not cite this or any posing source.
problems.resultNote: Spectral-gap paper, Theorem 1.1: for fixed $0<\beta<1$, with probability tending to one over the disorder, $\mathrm{Var}_{\mu_0}(f)\le C_\beta\mathcal D_0(f)$ for all $f$ (zero field), so the uniform-site heat-bath chain has gap at least $1/(C_\beta n)$. Companions: worst-start total-variation cutoff at $\log n/(2\lambda(\beta))$ for $0\le\beta<1$; at $\beta=1$ mixing time $n^{2/3+o(1)}$ and slow mixing from typical starts before $n^{2/3}$; for $\beta>1$ stretched-exponential barriers from typical starts and an $\exp(n^{1-c})$ typical-start upper bound; at $\beta=1$ universal random limits of rescaled autocorrelations for Gaussian and Rademacher disorder. Not shown: nonzero external fields, or an $O(n\log n)$ bound from the gap paper alone.

problems.name: The Kervaire invariant problem at the prime three: which standard classes $b_j$ survive the mod-3 Adams spectral sequence
problems.field: Stable homotopy theory; odd-primary Kervaire invariant
problems.statement: In the mod-$p$ Adams spectral sequence $\mathrm{Ext}_{\mathcal A_p}^{s,t}(\mathbb F_p,\mathbb F_p)\Rightarrow \pi_*^S$, the odd-primary analogues of the Kervaire classes are $b_j\in E_2^{2,2(p-1)p^{j+1}}$. Toda showed that $b_1$ supports a differential at every odd prime, and Ravenel (1978) proved that no $b_j$ with $j\ge1$ survives for $p\ge5$. At $p=3$ the argument fails: $b_0$ (stem 10) and $b_2$ (stem 106) survive, and the fate of the higher classes was open; Hill, Hopkins and Ravenel proposed attacking it through the action of $C_9$ on height-six Morava $E$-theory. The strong form also asks for representatives of order $p$. At $p=3$, for which $j$ does $b_j$ survive to $E_\infty$, and when it does, is it detected by an element of order three?
problems.posedBy: Douglas Ravenel (1978), whose odd-primary nonexistence theorem left p = 3 open; program of Hill, Hopkins and Ravenel (2011)
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites Ravenel, Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. (1978) for the p >= 5 theorem and the special behaviour at three, Hill-Hopkins-Ravenel's 2011 manuscript on the 3-primary problem, and Belmont-Ray's 'Towards the p=3 Kervaire invariant problem'. The order-p refinement is Selick's (1983) reformulation.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: at $p=3$, $K=K_3=\{0,2,3\}$, i.e. $b_j$ survives to $E_\infty$ exactly for $j=0,2,3$ (stems 10, 106 and 322), and each surviving class is detected by an element of additive order three; $b_1$ and all $b_j$ with $j\ge4$ die. The new content is the order-three element in stem 322 and the exclusion of every $j\ge4$. Corollaries via Amelotte and Selick: $\Omega S^{2n+1}\{3\}$ splits nontrivially exactly for $n\in\{3,27,81\}$, and the Anick space $T^{2n+1}(3)$ is homotopy associative exactly for those $n$. Side result: an infinite-order class in $\pi_{2n}(E_6^{hC_9})$ for every $n$, refuting the full-gap clause of Belmont-Ray's Conjecture 0.1. Not covered: other odd primes (already settled for $p\ge5$) or the prime-two problem.

problems.name: Convergence of the Flint Hills series
problems.statement: The Flint Hills series is $\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{1}{n^3\sin^2 n}$, with $n$ in radians. Its terms are large exactly when $n$ is very close to a multiple of $\pi$, so convergence depends on how well $\pi$ is approximated by rationals. Alekseyev (2011) showed convergence would force $\mu(\pi)\le5/2$, and Meiburg (2022) showed $\mu(\pi)<5/2$ suffices, while the best known bound was about $7.1$. Does the Flint Hills series converge?
problems.posedBy: Popularized by Clifford Pickover (per the manuscript); studied by Max Alekseyev, On convergence of the Flint Hills series, arXiv:1104.5100 (2011)
problems.ageNote: The manuscript says only that the problem was popularized by Pickover and gives no date or reference for him. The earliest dated reference it cites on the series is Alekseyev's 2011 preprint, which calls convergence unknown.
problems.resultNote: Corollary 1.2: $\sum_{n\ge1}1/(n^3\sin^2 n)$ converges, deduced from $\mu(\pi)=2$ via a dyadic spacing estimate valid for any exponent below $5/2$. More generally $\sum n^{-a}|\sin n|^{-b}$ converges iff $a>\max\{1,b\}$ (Corollary 5.2). No value or numerical estimate of the sum is given.

problems.name: Can an infinite self-dual uniform matroid be constructed in ZFC?
problems.statement: An infinite matroid is uniform if exchanging any element of a basis for any element outside it again gives a basis. Bowler and Geschke developed a basis criterion for infinite uniform matroids and constructed countable self-dual uniform examples under Martin's axiom for countable posets, hence under the continuum hypothesis, and left open whether such a matroid exists in ZFC alone. Gollin and Joo recorded even the ZFC existence of a uniform matroid of infinite rank and infinite corank as open. Is there, provably in ZFC, an infinite self-dual uniform matroid?

problems.resultNote: The manuscript constructs, in ZFC, a self-dual uniform matroid $Q$ on a countable set with every basis and its complement infinite, answering the Bowler-Geschke question and the Gollin-Joo existence question affirmatively. Its bases satisfy an extra ordinal inequality used to build the packing/covering counterexample. It does not address uncountable ground sets or classify such matroids.

problems.shortName: Rationality of the canonical Arthur filtration
problems.field: Automorphic functions over function fields; geometric Langlands
problems.statement: For a split connected semisimple group $G$ over $\mathbb F_q$ and a curve $X$, Gaitsgory, Lafforgue and Raskin define a canonical filtration, indexed by nilpotent orbits of the dual Lie algebra, on the space of finitely supported unramified automorphic functions with $\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell$ coefficients, using singular support of $\ell$-adic sheaves and the trace of Frobenius. The space of functions has a natural rational form. Their Conjecture 2.7.3, formulated jointly with Kazhdan, asserts that the canonical filtration is defined over $\mathbb Q$. Is the canonical Arthur filtration rational?
problems.posedBy: Dennis Gaitsgory, Vincent Lafforgue and Sam Raskin, jointly with David Kazhdan
problems.ageNote: GLR, arXiv:2603.26925 (2026), Section 2.7, Conjecture 2.7.3, as cited by the manuscript.
problems.resultNote: Under the stated characteristic assumptions, the canonical Arthur filtration on finitely supported unramified automorphic functions is defined over $\mathbb Q$, for split connected semisimple $G$, including the noncuspidal part and every closed invariant nilpotent support. Using the companion decomposition at trivial level, each cuspidal filtration step is identified with the scalar extension of the corresponding rational summands (the common-scope form of GLR Conjectures 3.4.9 and 3.4.11). It does not treat small characteristic or nonsplit groups.

The manuscript is authored 'OpenAI' and names no human author.

It is proved for split connected semisimple groups under four explicit characteristic hypotheses (the restricted-theory assumptions), for the whole space including the noncuspidal part; outside those hypotheses the conjecture is not addressed, hence Partial. It uses the restricted geometric Langlands results and trace-of-Frobenius theorems as inputs. The proof was not refereed. No Lean formalization exists for this family.

Placed below the Ramanujan-Arthur decomposition entry of this family (38) and The index conjecture for slc log Calabi-Yau pairs (25), and above The Huang-Jiang-Oblomkov Conjecture at a = 3 (12).

problems.name: Can worst-case trace reconstruction be done with polynomially many traces?
problems.statement: An unknown binary string $x\in\{0,1\}^n$ is passed repeatedly through a deletion channel that removes each bit independently with known probability $q\in(0,1)$ and concatenates the survivors; each output is a trace. Worst-case trace reconstruction asks how many independent traces $T_q(n)$ suffice to recover every $x$ with probability at least $2/3$. The problem was formulated by Batu, Kannan, Khanna and McGregor (2004). For fixed $q$ the best upper bounds fell from $\exp(\widetilde O(\sqrt n))$ (Holenstein et al. 2008) to $\exp(O(n^{1/3}))$ (De-O'Donnell-Servedio; Nazarov-Peres 2017), $\exp(O(n^{1/5}\log^5 n))$ (Chase 2021) and a quasipolynomial bound (Burudgunte-Valiant-Wang 2026), while the best lower bound was $\Omega(n^{3/2}/\log^7 n)$ (Chase 2021). For a fixed deletion probability, is $T_q(n)$ bounded by a polynomial in $n$?
problems.posedBy: Open since Batu, Kannan, Khanna and McGregor formulated worst-case trace reconstruction (SODA 2004); the manuscript calls it the polynomial-sample question without naming who first asked it
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites Batu, Kannan, Khanna and McGregor (2004) for the problem and Holenstein et al. (2008) for the first subexponential bound; it gives no explicit first statement of the polynomial question, so 2004 dates the problem rather than that sentence.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for fixed $s\in(0,1]$ and $0<c<1/(4\log 2)$, $T_{q,s}(n)\ge n^{c\log(q^3\log n)}$ eventually whenever $q^3\log n\to\infty$; so $T_q(n)=n^{\Omega(\log\log n)}$ at every fixed $q$, a negative answer to the polynomial question. Theorem 1.2: the minimum total variation between one-trace laws of distinct length-$n$ words is $o(n^{-A})$ for all $A$. The companions give a matching-type upper side: quasipolynomial samples and bit complexity with a uniform decoder for known rational retention, and polynomial bounds when $q\le n^{-\varepsilon}$. A gap remains between $\log T$ of order $\log n\log\log n$ (lower) and a power of $\log n$ (upper); the exact complexity is not determined.

They give $T_{q,s}(n)\ge n^{c\log(q^3\log n)}$ along any sequence with $q^3\log n\to\infty$, and $T_{q,s}(n)/n^A\to\infty$ for every fixed $q,s,A$, with unrestricted computation and randomized estimators. problems.name: The local p-adic section conjecture for curves of genus at least two
problems.field: Anabelian geometry; etale fundamental groups of p-adic curves
problems.statement: Let $k$ be a finite extension of $\mathbb Q_p$ and $X/k$ a smooth proper geometrically connected curve of genus at least two, with arithmetic etale fundamental group sequence $1\to\pi_1(X_{\bar k})\to\pi_1(X)\to G_k\to1$. Each rational point gives a section of $\pi_1(X)\to G_k$, well defined up to conjugation. The local p-adic section conjecture, the local analogue of the section conjecture in Grothendieck's 1983 letter to Faltings, asserts that this map from $X(k)$ to conjugacy classes of sections is a bijection. Koenigsmann proved the birational analogue, Pop-Stix localized every section at a valuation, and Bresciani handled toric sections. Is every section of $\pi_1(X)\to G_k$ induced by a unique rational point of $X$?
problems.posedBy: Local analogue of Grothendieck's section conjecture (letter to Faltings, 27 June 1983); studied as the p-adic section conjecture by Koenigsmann (2005), Pop (2010) and Pop-Stix (2017)
problems.ageNote: The manuscript presents the local conjecture as an analogue of Grothendieck's 1983 global conjecture and does not name who first stated the local form; Koenigsmann (2005) and Pop-Stix (2017) are the earliest cited works on it.
problems.resultNote: Claims Theorem 1.1: for every finite extension $k/\mathbb Q_p$ and every smooth proper geometrically connected curve $X/k$ of genus at least two, $X(k)\to\{\text{sections of }\pi_1(X)\to G_k\}/\pi_1(X_{\bar k})$ is bijective. Through Theorem 1.2 every section localized at a rank-one valuation lifts to a birational section. It does NOT prove the global section conjecture over number fields in general (see the separate entry for the cases it does reach), and says nothing about affine hyperbolic curves or curves over other local fields.
problems.aiRole: The release README says the manuscripts were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model, the vast majority by one fixed procedure using on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result, and that some outputs build on earlier results produced by the models. Its named exceptions to that procedure (the zeta zero-free region work, whose Re(s) > 11/12 write-up was human edited, and the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties) do not concern this family. Both manuscripts of the family are credited to OpenAI with no human author named. The proof patches finite etale covers over annuli, using lifting theorems of Amini-Baker-Brugalle-Rabinoff and the resolution of nonsingularities of Mochizuki-Tsujimura as cited inputs.
problems.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Theorem 1.1 was read against the conjecture as posed: for every prime $p$, every finite $k/\mathbb Q_p$ and every smooth proper geometrically connected curve of genus at least two, the point-to-section map is bijective, with conjugation by the full geometric fundamental group. The key new input is Theorem 1.2 (the universal etale field is dense in the separable closure at every rank-one valuation extending the p-adic norm), combined with Koenigsmann's birational theorem and the Pop-Stix localization. No Lean formalisation exists for this family. The release README warns that some unformalised results could have issues.
problems.significanceNote: The p-adic section conjecture is a central open problem of anabelian geometry, the local form of Grothendieck's conjecture, worked on by Koenigsmann, Pop, Stix and others for two decades. Level with the Hodge standard conjecture for abelian varieties (50), below the Zilber-Pink conjecture for abelian varieties over number fields (58), above Grothendieck's Finite Flat Group Scheme Order Question (30).

problems.name: The Gaussian propeller conjecture
problems.statement: For a measurable partition $A_1,\dots,A_k$ of $\mathbb R^d$ and the standard Gaussian measure $\gamma_d$, let $z(A_i)=\int_{A_i}x\,d\gamma_d$ and $F=\sum_i\|z(A_i)\|^2$. Khot and Naor, studying approximate kernel clustering and its Unique Games hardness, conjectured that for $k\ge3$ the maximum of $F$ is attained by the propeller: three planar sectors of angle $2\pi/3$ times an orthogonal factor, giving $9/(8\pi)$. Heilman, Jagannath and Naor proved it in $\mathbb R^3$. Is $\sum_i\|\int_{A_i}x\,d\gamma_d\|^2\le 9/(8\pi)$ for every finite partition in every dimension?
problems.posedBy: S. Khot and A. Naor, Approximate kernel clustering, Mathematika 55 (2009)
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for all $d,k$, every measurable partition of $\mathbb R^d$ satisfies $\sum_i\|\int_{A_i}x\,d\gamma_d\|^2\le9/(8\pi)$, with equality for the propeller when $d\ge2$, $k\ge3$. The new step shows extremizers with five or more active cells cannot beat $9/(8\pi)$, using Ehrhard's inequality and residual-score estimates; four-cell configurations come from Heilman-Jagannath-Naor. Consequence stated: combined with the release's Unique Games theorem, NP-hardness of beating the factor $(8\pi/9)(1-1/k)$ for identity-target kernel clustering, $k\ge3$. Uniqueness of extremizers is not claimed.

problems.name: The two-point Chowla conjecture (ordinary averages)
problems.field: Analytic number theory; correlations of multiplicative functions
problems.statement: Let $\lambda(n)=(-1)^{\Omega(n)}$ be the Liouville function. Chowla's conjecture predicts that $\sum_{n\le X}\lambda(n+h_1)\cdots\lambda(n+h_k)=o(X)$ for every fixed set of distinct shifts. Its two-point case asks whether the parities of $\Omega(n)$ and $\Omega(n+h)$ become uncorrelated. Matomaki and Radziwill obtained a bound $(1-\delta(h))X$, Matomaki-Radziwill-Tao proved cancellation on average over shifts, and Tao proved the logarithmically averaged version, with quantitative log-averaged savings by Helfgott-Radziwill and Pilatte. Does $\sum_{n\le X}\lambda(n)\lambda(n+h)=o(X)$ hold for every fixed $h\ge1$?
problems.posedBy: Sarvadaman Chowla, The Riemann Hypothesis and Hilbert's Tenth Problem (Gordon and Breach, 1965)
problems.resultNote: There is an absolute $c>0$ such that for all fixed integers $a_1,a_2\ge1$, $b_1,b_2\ge0$ with $a_1b_2\ne a_2b_1$, $\left|\sum_{n\le X}\lambda(a_1n+b_1)\lambda(a_2n+b_2)\right|\le C_{a,b}X/(\log X)^c$ for every real $X\ge3$. With $a_1=a_2=1$, $b_1=0$, $b_2=h$ this is the ordinary two-point Chowla conjecture with a power-of-log saving. Constants are ineffective, and coefficients may not grow with $X$. Nothing is proved for three or more points.

problems.name: The Goemans-Linial integrality gap for uniform sparsest cut is nearly square-root logarithmic
problems.shortName: Uniform sparsest cut SDP integrality gap
problems.field: Approximation algorithms; semidefinite relaxations and metric embeddings
problems.statement: The Goemans-Linial relaxation of uniform sparsest cut minimizes $\sum_{i<j}c_{ij}d(i,j)$ over negative-type semimetrics $d$ with $\sum_{i<j}d(i,j)=1$. Arora, Rao and Vazirani showed its integrality gap with uniform demands is $O(\sqrt{\log n})$. Devanur, Khot, Saket and Vishnoi refuted the conjecture that the uniform gap is bounded, with an $\Omega(\log\log n)$ lower bound, and Kane and Meka raised it to $\exp(\Omega(\sqrt{\log\log n}))$. For general demands the gap is $\Theta(\sqrt{\log n})$ up to lower-order factors (Naor-Young, Chang-Naor-Ren), but those constructions have constant average distortion and give nothing for uniform demands. What is the order of growth of the Goemans-Linial integrality gap for uniform sparsest cut, and does it reach $\sqrt{\log n}$?
problems.posedBy: Open after Arora, Rao and Vazirani (2004) and Devanur, Khot, Saket and Vishnoi (2006); see also Kane and Meka (2013)
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites no explicit statement of the question. The uniform constant-gap conjecture was refuted by Devanur-Khot-Saket-Vishnoi (STOC 2006); the remaining question of the true order sits between their and Kane-Meka's lower bounds and the ARV $O(\sqrt{\log n})$ upper bound (first presented 2004).
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there are an absolute $c>0$ and uniform-demand instances on $n_j\to\infty$ vertices with Goemans-Linial integrality gap at least $c\sqrt{\log n_j}/(\log\log n_j)^3$. This improves the Kane-Meka bound $\exp(\Omega(\sqrt{\log\log n}))$ to within $(\log\log n)^3$ of the ARV upper bound. It is an existential sequence of sizes, not a bound at every $n$; it does not determine whether the gap is exactly $\Theta(\sqrt{\log n})$, and it concerns the basic SDP, not Sherali-Adams or Lasserre strengthenings.

This result is not among the README's exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region). The manuscript is authored 'OpenAI' and names no human author. The family has two manuscripts dated September 24, 2026: this integrality-gap construction and a separate NP-hardness reduction (its own entry). This manuscript is the formalised one.

problems.name: Solovej's generalized ionization conjecture for neutral Coulomb atoms (energies and radii)
problems.statement: For the full nonrelativistic Coulomb atom with nuclear charge $Z$ and two spin states, let $I_m(Z)=E_Z(Z-m)-E_Z(Z)$ be the energy needed to remove $m$ electrons from the neutral atom, and let $R_m(Z)$ be the radius outside which an expected $m$ electrons of a neutral ground state lie. Thomas-Fermi theory predicts $I_m^{TF}\sim a_{TF}m^{7/3}$ and radii $\sim(81\pi^2/2)^{1/3}m^{-1/3}$ as $Z\to\infty$ and then $m\to\infty$. Solovej (2016) conjectured that the same asymptotics hold for the true many-body atom: $\lim_{m\to\infty}m^{-7/3}\limsup_{Z\to\infty}I_m(Z)=\lim_{m\to\infty}m^{-7/3}\liminf_{Z\to\infty}I_m(Z)=a_{TF}$, and likewise $m^{1/3}R_m(Z)\to(81\pi^2/2)^{1/3}$ for the upper and lower large-$Z$ limits. He had proved the analogues in Hartree-Fock theory. Do these iterated limits hold for the full Schrodinger atom?
problems.posedBy: Jan Philip Solovej
problems.ageNote: Solovej, A new look at Thomas-Fermi theory, Molecular Physics 114 (2016), Section 3, Equation (1), cited by both companion manuscripts.
problems.resultNote: Energy (principal, Theorem 1.1): $I_m(Z)/m^{7/3}\to a_{TF}>0$ whenever $m\to\infty$ and $Z/m\to\infty$, with $a_{TF}$ the Thomas-Fermi constant; this is stronger than and implies Solovej's iterated limits, which are stated as (1.4)-(1.5). Radius (companion, Theorem 1.1): for every choice of neutral ground states, $m^{1/3}\limsup_Z R_m(Z)$ and $m^{1/3}\liminf_Z R_m(Z)$ both tend to $(81\pi^2/2)^{1/3}$, with $Z\to\infty$ first. Not shown: convergence of $I_m(Z)$ or $R_m(Z)$ at fixed $m$, a joint limit for radii, or relativistic and molecular versions.

problems.name: Zariski's multiplicity conjecture: does embedded topology determine the multiplicity of a hypersurface singularity?
problems.field: Singularity theory; topology of hypersurface singularities
problems.statement: For a reduced convergent power series $f\in\mathbb{C}\{z_1,\ldots,z_N\}$ with $f(0)=0$, the multiplicity of the hypersurface germ $V(f)$ is $\mathrm{ord}_0 f$, the least degree of a monomial in $f$. Two germs are ambiently homeomorphic if a homeomorphism of neighbourhoods of $0$ in $\mathbb{C}^N$ fixing $0$ carries one zero set onto the other. For plane curves the embedded topology determines multiplicity, and by A'Campo and Le a germ ambiently homeomorphic to a smooth one is smooth. Zariski asked in 1971 whether this holds in general: if $(\mathbb{C}^N,V(f),0)$ and $(\mathbb{C}^N,V(g),0)$ are homeomorphic, must $V(f)$ and $V(g)$ have the same multiplicity?
problems.posedBy: Oscar Zariski, 'Some open questions in the theory of singularities', Bull. AMS 77 (1971)
problems.resultNote: Two independent counterexample constructions. September 24: for some finite $N>3$ divisible by eight, reduced weighted homogeneous real polynomials $f_1,f_2$ on $\mathbb{C}^N$ with isolated critical points, $\mathrm{ord}_0f_1=2$, $\mathrm{ord}_0f_2=3$, and $(\mathbb{C}^N,V(f_1),0)\cong(\mathbb{C}^N,V(f_2),0)$; the germs are also topologically right equivalent, so the right-equivalence version and its mod-2 version (Sampaio 2025, Conjectures 2 and Z mod 2) fail too. September 27: reduced convergent germs $f_4,f_5$ on $\mathbb{C}^4$ with isolated critical points, orders $4$ and $5$, ambiently homeomorphic zero sets. problems.name: Quillen's conjecture on the poset of elementary abelian p-subgroups
problems.field: Finite group theory; subgroup complexes and homotopy
problems.statement: Let $G$ be a finite group, $p$ a prime, and $\mathcal A_p(G)$ the poset of nontrivial elementary abelian $p$-subgroups of $G$. Quillen showed that a nontrivial normal $p$-subgroup ($O_p(G)\ne1$) makes $\mathcal A_p(G)$ contractible, and proved the converse for solvable groups, $p$-rank at most two and groups of Lie type in defining characteristic. Aschbacher and Smith reduced the problem for $p>5$ to unitary-group cases and later work (Piterman, Smith, Diaz Ramos) narrowed it further, settling the rational form for odd primes, but the prime $2$ remained open. Conjecture: if $\mathcal A_p(G)$ is contractible, must $O_p(G)\ne1$?
problems.posedBy: Daniel Quillen, Homotopy properties of the poset of nontrivial p-subgroups of a group, Advances in Mathematics 28 (1978), Conjecture 2.9
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every finite group $G$ and prime $p$, if $O_p(G)=1$ then $\widetilde H_*(\mathcal A_p(G);\mathbb Q)\ne0$ (augmented, so the empty poset counts). This gives Quillen's conjecture and its stronger rational-homology form, and acyclicity over any field characterizes $O_p(G)\ne1$. Priority: the manuscript credits Diaz Ramos (arXiv:2303.15613v6, July 2026) with the rational form at all odd primes, so the new content is chiefly the prime $2$ (via Piterman's component eliminations) plus a direct proof of the unitary dimension property. It does not prove the Quillen dimension property (homology in top degree) in general.

problems.name: The Laughlin spectral gap conjecture for the V1 pseudopotential on the sphere
problems.field: Fractional quantum Hall effect; spectral gaps
problems.statement: On the sphere with $Q$ flux quanta, $N$ fermions in the lowest Landau level interact through Haldane's $V_1$ pseudopotential $H_{N,Q}=\sum_{i<j}P^{(1)}_{ij}$, which penalizes each pair in relative angular momentum one. At $Q=3(N-1)$ the Laughlin state $\prod_{i<j}(u_iv_j-u_jv_i)^3$ is its unique zero mode. Numerics since Haldane and Rezayi (1985) indicate a gap above it, and the folklore spectral-gap conjecture is recorded in Rougerie's survey (Conjecture A.1); uniform gaps were proved only for truncated pseudopotentials on thin cylinders and tori (Nachtergaele-Warzel-Young, Warzel-Young). Is there $\gamma>0$ with $H_{N,3(N-1)}\ge\gamma(1-P_{\mathrm L})$ for all sufficiently large $N$?
problems.posedBy: Folklore since Haldane (1983) and Haldane-Rezayi (1985); recorded as Conjecture A.1 in N. Rougerie's survey, as cited by the manuscript
problems.ageNote: The manuscript dates the gap question to Haldane and Rezayi's 1985 finite-size study, which distinguished the expected gap from a proof; the written conjecture it cites is in Rougerie's survey, whose year the manuscript's text does not give.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every $0<\gamma<\gamma_*=4616733319001/10^{14}>1/25$ there is $Q_\gamma$ with $H_Q^2\ge\gamma H_Q$ on the full lowest-Landau-level fermionic Fock space for $Q\ge Q_\gamma$, independently of particle number. Corollary 1.2: $H_{N,3(N-1)}\ge\frac1{25}(1-P_{\mathrm L,N})$ for $N\ge N_0$. Section 7 proves the planar analogue at $\gamma_*$, the fermionic cubic case of Rougerie's Conjecture A.1. The companion adds stability under bounded projected scalar potentials. Thresholds are existential; bosonic and other fillings are not treated.

problems.name: The elastic Calderon problem in three dimensions: do boundary measurements determine smooth isotropic Lame moduli?
problems.statement: Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded connected smooth domain and $\lambda,\mu\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega)$ Lame moduli with $\mu>0$, $3\lambda+2\mu>0$. The static displacement-to-traction map $\Lambda_{\lambda,\mu}$ sends boundary displacements $f$ to the tractions $\sigma_{\lambda,\mu}(u_f)n$ of the solution of $\operatorname{div}(\lambda(\operatorname{div}u)I+2\mu e(u))=0$ with trace $f$. Nakamura and Uhlmann claimed global uniqueness in 1994; their 2003 erratum proved it only when $\|\nabla\mu_j\|_{C^m}$ is small. Does $\Lambda_{\lambda_1,\mu_1}=\Lambda_{\lambda_2,\mu_2}$ imply $\lambda_1=\lambda_2$ and $\mu_1=\mu_2$ for all such smooth moduli?
problems.posedBy: Elastic analogue of Calderon's problem; global uniqueness claimed by G. Nakamura and G. Uhlmann (1994), reduced to a small-gradient result in their 2003 erratum
problems.ageNote: The manuscript does not call the problem open in so many words; it cites the 1994 Nakamura-Uhlmann claim and the 2003 erratum restricting it to small gradients, and later partial results (Eskin-Ralston, Lin-Nakamura 2017, Tan-Liu 2023, Imanuvilov-Yamamoto in 2D). 2003 is when the general three-dimensional case became open again; the question itself dates to 1994.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: on any bounded connected domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ with $C^\infty$ boundary, if $\lambda_j,\mu_j\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega)$ satisfy $\mu_j>0$, $3\lambda_j+2\mu_j>0$ and $\Lambda_{\lambda_1,\mu_1}=\Lambda_{\lambda_2,\mu_2}$, then $\lambda_1=\lambda_2$ and $\mu_1=\mu_2$. No analyticity, smallness or prior boundary agreement is assumed. It is a uniqueness theorem for smooth coefficients and full static data only: no reconstruction algorithm, no stability estimate, no partial-data or low-regularity version, and nothing about anisotropic elasticity.

problems.name: Grothendieck's homotopy hypothesis for weak globular infinity-groupoids (Ara-Henry coherators)
problems.statement: In Pursuing Stacks (1983) Grothendieck defined weak globular $\infty$-groupoids as models of a coherator, a globular theory obtained by freely adjoining coherence operations, and conjectured that they model homotopy types: their homotopy theory, with weak equivalences detected by components and homotopy groups, is equivalent to that of spaces. Maltsiniotis made the formulation precise; strict $\infty$-groupoids are known to fail. Henry (2016) reduced the hypothesis to a pushout conjecture: attaching an $(n+1)$-cell along the source face of an $n$-cell of a cellular model is a weak equivalence. The case of 3-groupoids was settled by Henry and Lanari. Do Grothendieck $\infty$-groupoids, for every coherator, recover the homotopy theory of spaces?
problems.posedBy: Alexander Grothendieck (Pursuing Stacks); precise formulation by Georges Maltsiniotis
problems.ageNote: Grothendieck, Pursuing Stacks (manuscript of 1983), with Maltsiniotis's formulation (2007 onward) and Henry's pushout conjecture (arXiv:1609.04622, 2016), all as cited by the manuscript.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1 (Henry's pushout conjecture): for every Grothendieck coherator in the Ara-Henry convention, elementary expansions of cellular models are weak equivalences. Section 5 derives the canonical left semi-model structure and, through Henry's comparison, a Quillen equivalence with spaces, so the homotopy theory is independent of the coherator within that convention. It does not cover coherators outside the Ara-Henry convention, Grothendieck's weak $\infty$-categories (the non-invertible case), or Taylor's generalized pushout conjecture for algebraic coherators.

problems.name: Spontaneous magnetization of the three-dimensional quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet at low temperature (Lieb's Problem A)
problems.statement: The nearest-neighbour quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet on $\mathbb Z^d$ has Hamiltonian $H=-\sum_{|x-y|=1}\mathbf S_x\cdot\mathbf S_y$ with spin-$S$ matrices at each site. Mermin and Wagner excluded order at positive temperature for $d\le2$; Frohlich-Simon-Spencer proved ordering for the classical model in $d\ge3$ and Dyson-Lieb-Simon for quantum antiferromagnets, but the reflection-positivity method gives no infrared bound for the quantum ferromagnet. Lieb listed the problem in 1999 (Problem A), and it was still described as open in 2025. Does the quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet in dimension $d\ge3$, for every spin $S$, order at sufficiently low positive temperature, i.e. have an equilibrium state with nonzero spontaneous magnetization at zero field?
problems.posedBy: Elliott H. Lieb (1999, Problem A of his list of statistical-mechanics problems); obstruction noted by Dyson, Lieb and Simon (1978)
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites Lieb (1999) Problem A as the explicit posing and Seiringer's 2025 account, which states it with a volume-averaged finite-volume two-point order parameter. Dyson-Lieb-Simon (1978, pp. 339-340) already explained why their method did not reach the ferromagnet.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every $d\ge3$ and $S\in\{1/2,1,3/2,\dots\}$ there is $\beta_0(d,S)$ such that for every $\beta\ge\beta_0$ the zero-field nearest-neighbour dynamics has a translation-invariant $\beta$-KMS state with $\omega(S_0^z)\ge S/4$. The proof uses an exchange-cycle (random interchange) representation with boundary pins, stable-polynomial negative dependence and a determinant identity for conditioned walks. Not shown: long-range order in the finite-volume two-point formulation, the critical temperature, or anything in $d\le2$. The companion manuscripts in the family prove Bloch's law and the spherical magnetization law in $d=3$.
