problems.name: A cubic lower bound for the border determinantal complexity of the permanent (beyond the quadratic Mignon-Ressayre barrier)
problems.shortName: Cubic border determinantal lower bound for the permanent
problems.field: Algebraic complexity; permanent versus determinant, geometric complexity theory
problems.statement: The determinantal complexity $\mathrm{dc}(f)$ of a polynomial $f$ is the least $n$ with $f=\det(A_0+\sum_j x_jA_j)$ for $n\times n$ complex matrices, and the border determinantal complexity $\mathrm{bdc}(f)$ is the least $n$ such that $f$ is a coefficientwise limit of such determinants. Valiant's algebraic completeness theory (1979) makes the growth of $\mathrm{dc}(\mathrm{per}_m)$ the algebraic analogue of P versus NP: it is conjectured to be superpolynomial, and the Mulmuley-Sohoni geometric complexity program targets $\mathrm{bdc}$. The best lower bounds were quadratic: $\mathrm{dc}(\mathrm{per}_m)\ge m^2/2$ (Mignon-Ressayre 2004) and $\mathrm{bdc}(\mathrm{per}_m)\ge m^2/2$ (Landsberg-Manivel-Ressayre 2010). How fast must $\mathrm{bdc}(\mathrm{per}_m)$ grow; in particular, can the quadratic lower bound be improved?
problems.posedBy: Leslie Valiant (permanent versus determinant, algebraic completeness); border version from the Mulmuley-Sohoni geometric complexity program
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites Valiant (1979) for the completeness framework, Mulmuley-Sohoni (2001, 2008) for the orbit-closure formulation, and Landsberg-Manivel-Ressayre (2010) for the previous border bound $m^2/2$. Superpolynomial growth remains the open target; this is a new polynomial bound on a tracked quantity.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: $\mathrm{bdc}(\mathrm{per}_m)\ge cm^3$ for $m\ge m_0$, with $c=1/(5529600e)$ and $m_0=1408$, over $\mathbb C$ with arbitrary affine-linear entries and coefficientwise limits at fixed size; the same bound holds for $\mathrm{dc}$, and affine-linear algebraic branching programs for $\mathrm{per}_m$ need $\Omega(m^3)$ vertices and edges (also in the border sense at fixed budget). The route is a smooth-hypersurface bound $(r-1)(d-1)/(4e)$ for forms of degree $r$ in $d$ variables, applied to a coefficient polynomial extracted from a permanent. It remains a fixed polynomial bound: superpolynomial $\mathrm{dc}$ or $\mathrm{bdc}$ for the permanent, and VP versus VNP, stay open.

problems.name: Kraetzer's conjecture on the universal integral means spectrum
problems.field: Geometric function theory, integral means spectrum
problems.statement: For a bounded univalent map $f$ of the unit disk, $\beta_f(p)$ is the growth exponent of $\int|f'(re^{i\theta})|^p d\theta$ as $r\to1$, and the universal bounded spectrum is $B_b(p)=\sup_f\beta_f(p)$. From numerical experiments Kraetzer (1996) conjectured $B_b(p)=p^2/4$ for $|p|\le2$ and $B_b(p)=|p|-1$ for $|p|\ge2$. The conjecture contains Brennan's conjecture ($B(-2)=1$) and the value $B_b(1)=1/4$ related to the Carleson-Jones coefficient problem. Hedenmalm-Shimorin and Sola gave upper bounds above $1/4$ at $p=-1$. Is Kraetzer's formula for $B_b$ correct?
problems.posedBy: Philipp Kraetzer, Experimental bounds for the universal integral means spectrum of conformal maps (Complex Variables, 1996)
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there are constants $0<\varepsilon<1/4$ and $C$ with $M_{-1}[f'](r)\le C(1-r)^{-1/4+\varepsilon}$ for every $f\in\mathcal S$ and $1/2\le r<1$, so $B_b(-1)<1/4=p^2/4$ at $p=-1$ and Kraetzer's formula is false. The bound needs no bounded image or boundary regularity. Not shown: the true value of $B_b(-1)$ or any explicit gap, and nothing about $p=1$ or the Carleson-Jones question; Brennan's value $B(-2)=1$, also predicted by Kraetzer, is proved in the companion (separate entry).

problems.name: Grothendieck's section conjecture for the modular curves X0(N) and X1(N) over Q
problems.field: Anabelian geometry; rational points on curves
problems.statement: Let $C$ be a smooth proper geometrically connected curve of genus at least two over a number field $K$. Grothendieck's section conjecture (letter to Faltings, 1983) asserts that the map from $C(K)$ to conjugacy classes of sections of $\pi_1(C)\to G_K$ is a bijection. Before this work it was known only in restricted or conditional forms (for instance via the finite-descent framework of Harari-Stix and Stix, or for curves with no adelic points), and no standard family such as the modular curves was covered. Does the section conjecture hold for every smooth proper curve of genus at least two over a number field, in particular for the modular curves $X_0(N)$ and $X_1(N)$ over $\mathbb Q$?
problems.posedBy: Alexander Grothendieck, letter to G. Faltings (27 June 1983)
problems.resultNote: Claims Theorem 8.2: the global section conjecture holds for every smooth proper geometrically connected curve of genus at least two over a number field whose finite-cover descent locus equals its rational points; by Stoll's criteria this includes curves mapping nonconstantly to an abelian variety with finitely many rational points and trivial divisible Sha, and the modular curves $X_0(N)$, $X_1(N)$ of genus at least two over $\mathbb Q$. It does NOT prove the section conjecture for arbitrary curves over number fields; the descent-locus equality remains a separate hypothesis in general.
problems.aiRole: The release README says the manuscripts were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model, the vast majority by one fixed procedure using on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result, and that some outputs build on earlier results produced by the models. Its named exceptions to that procedure (the zeta zero-free region work, whose Re(s) > 11/12 write-up was human edited, and the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties) do not concern this family. The manuscript is credited to OpenAI with no human author named. The global statements are deduced in its Section 8 from the local theorem together with established descent results (Harari-Stix, Stix, Stoll), which are credited to their authors.

problems.name: Bin packing within an additive constant: is there a polynomial-time algorithm using at most OPT + C bins?
problems.field: Approximation algorithms; hardness of bin packing
problems.statement: Bin packing is NP-hard and admits no multiplicative ratio below $3/2$ unless P = NP, but its asymptotic behaviour is much better: Fernandez de la Vega and Lueker gave an asymptotic scheme, Karmarkar and Karp (1982) an algorithm using $OPT+O(\log^2OPT)$ bins, Rothvoss $OPT+O(\log OPT\log\log OPT)$ and Hoberg and Rothvoss $OPT+O(\log OPT)$. No hardness of any additive form was known, so even an $OPT+1$ algorithm was not excluded. Williamson and Shmoys list the question among the open problems of their 2011 book (Chapter 17, Problem 3). Is there a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that, for some absolute constant $C$, packs every instance into at most $OPT(I)+C$ bins?
problems.posedBy: David P. Williamson and David B. Shmoys (listed open problem), in the line of Karmarkar and Karp's additive algorithm
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites Williamson-Shmoys, The Design of Approximation Algorithms (2011), Chapter 17, Problem 3. The question is older, following Karmarkar-Karp (1982), but the manuscript gives no earlier posing reference.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.2: for every fixed integer $c\ge0$ it is NP-hard to distinguish pairs $(I,B)$ where $I$ packs into $B$ bins from pairs where $I$ needs more than $B+c$ bins, with rational sizes all greater than $1/6$. Corollary 1.3: a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm using at most $OPT(I)+C$ bins for an absolute constant $C$ exists if and only if P = NP. The reduction goes from vertex cover with Håstad's gap through a competing two-tree interval construction encoded in five-item bins. Not shown: a lower bound of order $\log OPT$ matching Hoberg-Rothvoss, or hardness for a fixed number of item sizes (polynomial by Goemans-Rothvoss).

This result is not among the README's exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties, and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region whose write-up was human-edited). The manuscripts are authored 'OpenAI' and name no human author. The family is a single manuscript, 'Additive hardness and unbounded configuration gaps in bin packing' (September 24, 2026); the same reduction also disproves the Modified Integer Round-Up Conjecture, entered separately.

problems.name: The Kakeya set conjecture in four dimensions (Hausdorff dimension)
problems.statement: A Kakeya set in $\mathbb R^n$ contains a unit line segment in every direction. Besicovitch showed such a set can have measure zero; the Hausdorff-dimension Kakeya conjecture asserts it must still have Hausdorff dimension $n$. It was known for $n=2$ (Davies, 1971) and $n=3$ (Wang and Zahl, 2025). In $\mathbb R^4$, Wolff's hairbrush gave dimension at least $3$, and the best Hausdorff bound before this work was about $3.059$ (Katz and Zahl). Does every subset of $\mathbb R^4$ containing a unit line segment in every direction have Hausdorff dimension $4$?
problems.posedBy: Hausdorff-dimension form of the Kakeya conjecture (classical, after Besicovitch and Davies); the manuscript cites the Katz-Tao (2002) formulation
problems.ageNote: The manuscript names no poser or year. The dimension question has been open since Davies proved the planar case in 1971, and the four-dimensional case has a long record of partial bounds (Wolff 1995, Laba-Tao, Guth-Zahl, Katz-Zahl).
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: if $K\subset\mathbb R^4$ contains, for every $e\in S^3$, a segment $\{a_e+te:0\le t\le1\}$, then $\dim_H K=4$. No measurability, compactness, stickiness or packing-dimension hypothesis is imposed. The paper also derives packing and Minkowski-dimension consequences, a projection lower bound in higher dimensions, and Nikodym and curved-Kakeya applications via cited transfers. It does NOT prove the four-dimensional Kakeya maximal conjecture, and does not settle the conjecture in dimension five or higher.

This family consists of two manuscripts dated September 23 and 24, 2026; this entry draws on the September 24 one. The manuscript is credited to 'OpenAI' alone, names no human author and has no acknowledgements. The release does not say how problems were chosen or how much human review happened before publication.

problems.name: The fixed point property for nonexpansive maps in reflexive Banach spaces
problems.shortName: Nonexpansive fixed points in reflexive spaces
problems.field: Functional analysis: metric fixed point theory
problems.statement: A Banach space has the fixed point property for nonexpansive maps if every $T:C\to C$ with $\|Tx-Ty\|\le\|x-y\|$, on every nonempty closed bounded convex set $C$, has a fixed point, nonexpansiveness being measured in the given norm. Browder and Gohde (1965) proved it for uniformly convex spaces and Kirk (1965) for reflexive spaces when the domain has normal structure; Karlovitz showed normal structure is not necessary, Maurey proved it for reflexive subspaces of $L^1$, and Alspach (1981) gave a fixed-point-free nonexpansive map on a weakly compact convex subset of $L^1$, so weak compactness alone does not suffice. Dominguez Benavides showed that every reflexive space has an equivalent norm with the property. Does every real reflexive Banach space have the fixed point property for nonexpansive maps in its original norm?
problems.posedBy: Classical question of metric fixed point theory arising from Kirk's 1965 theorem; the manuscript calls it the reflexive-space fixed point problem and names no poser
problems.ageNote: The manuscript does not say who first asked the question or when. It frames it through Kirk's 1965 theorem and cites Nourouzi (2026) as recording it as unresolved. It also notes earlier claimed proofs of the same statement by Hanebaly (a 2019 journal article and a 2021 preprint).
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: if $X$ is a real reflexive Banach space and $C\subseteq X$ is nonempty, closed, bounded and convex, every nonexpansive $F:C\to C$ has a fixed point, with no uniform convexity, normal structure or separability assumed and the norm unchanged. Corollary: for any commuting family of nonexpansive self-maps of such $C$, the common fixed set is nonempty and a nonexpansive retract (via Bruck 1974). The proof argues by contradiction from a minimal invariant set, using the Goebel-Karlovitz lemma, an adaptive anchor, a tree of approximate fixed point images and a weighted switching estimate. It says nothing about nonreflexive spaces with the weak fixed point property, and gives no constructive iteration.
problems.aiRole: The OpenAI math release (github.com/openai/math, commit adc7f12) states that its results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model under one fixed procedure, averaging about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result, across roughly 4,000 posed problems; outputs were then grouped into families and filtered for significance. This result is not among the README's stated exceptions (the Riemann zeta zero-free region work and the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties). The manuscript is credited to OpenAI alone and names no human author.
problems.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: the introduction and Theorem 1.1 of the TeX source; the proof was not refereed. problems.name: Hilbert's tenth problem over the rational numbers
problems.field: Diophantine decidability and definability, arithmetic of elliptic curves
problems.statement: Hilbert's tenth problem (1900) asked for a procedure deciding whether a polynomial equation with integer coefficients has an integer solution; Davis, Putnam, Robinson and Matiyasevich showed by 1970 that none exists. Over $\mathbb Q$ the question remained open: enumeration finds any rational zero, but no method certifies that none exists, and the natural transfer route, an existential definition of $\mathbb Z$ in $\mathbb Q$, would contradict Mazur's conjecture on the topology of rational points. Is there an algorithm which, given $f\in\mathbb Z[X_1,\ldots,X_n]$ with $n$ part of the input, decides whether $f$ has a zero in $\mathbb Q^n$?
problems.posedBy: David Hilbert (1900) for the integer problem; the rational version has been the central open case since the Davis-Putnam-Robinson-Matiyasevich theorem (1970)
problems.ageNote: The manuscript dates Hilbert's integer problem to 1900 and the integer answer to 1970, but cites no single paper posing the rational version. It has been open at least since 1970 and was discussed by Robinson (1949), Mazur (1992, 1995), Poonen and Koenigsmann among those cited.
problems.resultNote: Claims a negative answer: rational solvability of integer polynomial equations (variables unbounded) is undecidable, of Turing degree $0'$, and stays so for total degree at most four. The method reduces integer solvability to finitely many rational-solvability tests per input, using rank-one elliptic curves, a five-point height estimate and a parity condition from 2-descent. It does not define $\mathbb Z$ existentially in $\mathbb Q$ (consistent with Mazur's conjecture), does not bound the number of variables, and does not address other number fields beyond what is known.
problems.aiRole: The OpenAI math release (github.com/openai/math) states that its results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model, with on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result, under one fixed procedure applied to roughly 4,000 posed problems; outputs were then grouped into families and filtered for significance. The manuscript is credited to OpenAI alone and names no human author. The proof relies on two other manuscripts from the same release as theorem inputs: a pointwise 2-converse (the family companion) and Fontaine-Mazur modularity at the prime 2 (a separate family).
problems.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 of the TeX source read against the posed problem; it states there is no algorithm deciding rational solvability of integer polynomials with the number of variables part of the input, which is the problem as posed. A corollary gives Turing degree $0'$, also for quartics and sums of squares of quadrics. The paper does not give an existential definition of $\mathbb Z$ in $\mathbb Q$; it uses a finite-test reduction with compactness. Its inputs include two unrefereed manuscripts of the same release (pointwise 2-converse; Fontaine-Mazur modularity at 2), so the result is only as solid as they are. No Lean formalization is listed.
problems.significanceNote: The rational case has been the most famous open question in Diophantine decidability since 1970, attacked by Robinson, Mazur, Poonen and Koenigsmann. Scored above the Jacobian conjecture at 65 and the Kothe conjecture at 60, tied with the forced Euler blowup at 70, and below the Navier-Stokes candidate at 87 since it lacks a Millennium-level reach.

problems.name: Almost-sure global well-posedness for high-regularity random data in energy-supercritical defocusing NLS (Deng-Nahmod-Yue Open Problem 3), refuted on the twelve-torus
problems.shortName: Stable blowup for supercritical defocusing NLS
problems.field: Dispersive PDE; nonlinear Schrodinger equation; random data; blowup
problems.statement: Consider the defocusing nonlinear Schrodinger equation $i\partial_t u+\Delta u=|u|^{p-1}u$ on the torus $\mathbb T^d$ with odd $p$, in the energy-supercritical range $s_{cr}=d/2-2/(p-1)>1$, where the conserved energy does not control the regularity needed for global classical solutions. Deng, Nahmod and Yue (2020) observed that if classical solutions with random initial data of high regularity, such as Gaussian Fourier series $\sum_n g_n\langle n\rangle^{-\alpha}e^{in\cdot x}$ with $\alpha$ large, were almost surely global, then blowup for these equations would be non-generic and unstable, as the known whole-space blowup examples are. Their Open Problem 3 asks: in the energy-supercritical case, does almost-sure global well-posedness hold for random initial data of high regularity?
problems.posedBy: Yu Deng, Andrea R. Nahmod and Haitian Yue, Random tensors, propagation of randomness, and nonlinear dispersive equations (arXiv:2006.09285v1, 2020), Section 9.2.3, Open Problem 3
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites Open Problem 3 of Deng-Nahmod-Yue and says its own eventual-alpha, $H^m$ quantified formulation is the one considered there, not a verbatim restatement. The posing text was read here in arXiv v1. The wider question of whether energy-supercritical defocusing NLS can blow up goes back to Bourgain's surveys.
problems.resultNote: Claims: there are an odd $p$ (which can be taken arbitrarily large), an integer $k>8$ and a nonempty open set $\mathcal U\subset H^k(\mathbb T^{12})$ such that every solution of the defocusing NLS with data in $\mathcal U$ blows up in finite time $T$ with $(T-t)^{1/(p-1)}|u(t,x_*)|\to c_0>0$, a type-I self-similar singularity with logarithmic phase. Since Gaussian measures charge open sets, for every $\alpha>k+6$ the Gaussian Fourier datum blows up with positive probability, so almost-sure global existence for high-regularity random data fails for this $(d,p)$. It does NOT give probability-one blowup, a bound uniform in $\alpha$, an explicit $p$, or anything for low dimensions such as $d\le 11$; the question for other pairs $(d,p)$ stays open.
problems.aiRole: The release README says all results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model, the vast majority by one fixed procedure using on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result. Its named exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties, and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region, whose write-up was human edited for readability) do not concern this family. The manuscript is credited to OpenAI with no human author named. The proof is computer assisted: the release ships an exact rational-arithmetic verifier (Python standard library only) for the finite comparisons behind the self-similar profile and its spectral stability; the README says these checks do not verify the analytic arguments linking them to the blowup theorem. The main theorem and its Gaussian corollary also have a Lean comparator challenge in the release.

This is the headline. The Sobolev product is a challenge definition whose summability proof the solution must supply. Not rebuilt here.

problems.name: Hovey-Strickland finite-generation question: are the homotopy groups of the $K(n)$-local sphere finitely generated over $\mathbb Z_p$?
problems.shortName: Finite generation of the K(n)-local sphere
problems.statement: Fix a prime $p$ and height $n\ge1$, and let $L_{K(n)}S$ be the Bousfield localization of the $p$-complete sphere at Morava $K$-theory $K(n)$. It is not connective, so finiteness must be controlled degree by degree. At height one the answer follows from the classical computation; at height two and $p\ge5$ Hovey and Strickland derived it from Shimomura's computations. Is $\pi_t L_{K(n)}S_p^\wedge$ a finitely generated $\mathbb Z_p$-module for every prime $p$, every height $n$ and every integer $t$?
problems.posedBy: Mark Hovey and Neil Strickland, Problem 16.2 of 'Morava K-theories and localisation' (Memoirs AMS, 1999); also Problem 1 of Hovey's Morava K- and E-theory problem list
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every prime $p$, height $n\ge1$ and integer $t$, $\pi_t L_{K(n)}S_p^\wedge$ is a finitely generated $\mathbb Z_p$-module; equivalently $\pi_t L_{K(n)}F$ is finitely generated for every finite $p$-local spectrum $F$. Combined with the rational computation of Barthel-Schlank-Stapleton-Weinstein this fixes the free ranks. The key step is finiteness of continuous cohomology of the stabilizer with mod $p$ Lubin-Tate coefficients. It gives no bound on the number of generators or the torsion as $p$, $n$, $t$ vary, computes no torsion, and does not extend to all invertible $K(n)$-local spectra (known to fail at height two).

problems.name: A power saving in the Furstenberg-Sarkozy theorem (square-difference-free sets)
problems.statement: Let $s(N)$ be the largest size of a set $A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with no two elements differing by a nonzero perfect square. Answering a question of Lovasz, Furstenberg and Sarkozy proved $s(N)=o(N)$. Quantitative bounds improved through Pintz-Steiger-Szemeredi and Bloom-Maynard to Green and Sawhney's $s(N)\ll N\exp(-c\sqrt{\log N})$, while Ruzsa-type constructions give $s(N)\gg N^{0.7334}$. Green and Sawhney asked whether a fixed power saving holds. Is there an absolute $c>0$ with $s(N)\ll N^{1-c}$?
problems.posedBy: B. Green and M. Sawhney, New bounds for the Furstenberg-Sarkozy theorem (arXiv:2411.17448), Section 1.1; the underlying problem originates with Lovasz
problems.ageNote: Green and Sawhney's arXiv preprint (2411.17448) dates from November 2024; the manuscript's bibliography lists it as 2025. The underlying density question goes back to Lovasz, answered qualitatively by Furstenberg (1977) and Sarkozy (1978).
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: absolute $c>0$, $C$ with $|A|\le CN^{1-c}$ for every square-difference-free $A\subseteq[N]$; consequently the square-difference graph on $[N]$ has chromatic number at least $C^{-1}N^c$. Companions: for an intersective $h$ of degree $k\ge2$, a power saving $O_h(N^{1-c_k})$ with exponent depending only on $k$; and for $h$ with a unit root modulo every modulus, a power saving $C_hN^{1-c_h}$ for differences $h(p)$ at primes. The exponent is tiny and not computed, far from Ruzsa's lower-bound exponent $0.733$; the true exponent is not addressed.

problems.name: Brennan's conjecture
problems.statement: Let $W\subset\mathbb C$ be a simply connected domain whose boundary in the Riemann sphere has at least two points, and $\varphi:W\to\mathbb D$ a conformal bijection onto the unit disk. Brennan (1978) conjectured that $\int_W|\varphi'|^s\,dA<\infty$ for every $4/3<s<4$; the Koebe function shows the range cannot be enlarged. Equivalently, for the inverse map $f$, $\int_{\mathbb D}|f'|^{t}\,dA<\infty$ for $-2<t<2/3$, and in integral-means language $B_{\mathcal S}(-2)=1$. Brennan proved the range up to a bit beyond $s=3$; Carleson-Makarov, Pommerenke, Bertilsson ($s<3.421$), Hedenmalm-Shimorin and Sola ($B(-2)\le1.206$) improved the bounds. Does the full range $4/3<s<4$ hold?
problems.posedBy: James E. Brennan, The integrability of the derivative in conformal mapping (J. London Math. Soc., 1978)
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $C_\varepsilon$ with $M_{-2}[f'](r)\le C_\varepsilon(1-r)^{-1-\varepsilon}$ for all $f\in\mathcal S$ and $1/2\le r<1$; $B_{\mathcal S}(-2)=1$; and every conformal bijection $\varphi:W\to\mathbb D$ has $|\varphi'|^s$ area-integrable for $4/3<s<4$. Also $B_{\mathcal S}(t)=|t|-1$ for all $t\le-2$, and the Koebe function shows both endpoints fail. Not shown: the integral-means spectrum at other interior exponents; the companion's $B_b(-1)<1/4$ is a separate entry.

problems.name: The duality conjecture for metric entropy (Pietsch)
problems.statement: For convex bodies $A,B$ let $N(A,B)$ be the least number of translates of $B$ covering $A$, and let $K^\circ$ be the polar of $K$. The duality conjecture for metric entropy, originating in Pietsch's 1972 work on entropy numbers of operators and formulated geometrically by Artstein, Milman, Szarek and Tomczak-Jaegermann (2004, Conjecture 1), asks whether covering complexity is preserved under polarity up to universal changes of scale and constant factors. It was proved when one body is an ellipsoid (Artstein-Milman-Szarek 2004) and with logarithmic losses in general (E. Milman). Are there absolute constants $a,b\ge1$ such that $\frac1b\log N(L^\circ,aK^\circ)\le\log N(K,L)\le b\log N(L^\circ,a^{-1}K^\circ)$ for all dimensions and all origin-symmetric convex bodies $K,L$?
problems.posedBy: Albrecht Pietsch (1972, operator form); geometric form as Conjecture 1 of Artstein, Milman, Szarek and Tomczak-Jaegermann (GAFA 2004)
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every $a,b\ge1$ there exist $n$ and an origin-symmetric convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^n$ such that, with $L$ the cube, $\log N(K,L)>b\log N(L^\circ,a^{-1}K^\circ)$. A further construction (per the Lean scope note) makes the dual-to-primal entropy ratio tend to zero. This disproves the two-sided dimension-free conjecture. It leaves intact the ellipsoid case, the convexified-packing duality, bounds with constants depending on the K-convexity constant, and Milman's logarithmic-loss comparison; no fixed-dimension claim is made.

problems.name: Franz-Parisi jamming exponents in the negative spherical perceptron, at margin -1
problems.field: Spin glasses; jamming; random constraint satisfaction
problems.statement: In the spherical perceptron with negative margin, $x\in\sqrt N S^{N-1}$ must satisfy $g^a\cdot x/\sqrt N\ge\sigma$ for $M=\alpha N$ Gaussian patterns, and the feasible set is nonconvex. Franz and Parisi (2016) identified this model with the jamming universality class of high-dimensional spheres and, from a full replica-symmetry-breaking solution, predicted isostaticity at the SAT-UNSAT threshold and power laws for small gaps $g(h)\sim h^{-\gamma}$ and weak forces $p(f)\sim f^{\theta}$ with $\gamma\approx0.41269$, $\theta\approx0.42311$ and $\gamma=1/(2+\theta)$, confirmed as universal across negative margins by Franz, Parisi, Sevelev, Urbani and Zamponi (2017). Rigorous work gave only density bounds. Does the negative perceptron have a sharp jamming threshold with these gap and force exponents?
problems.posedBy: Silvio Franz and Giorgio Parisi, The simplest model of jamming (J. Phys. A, 2016); Franz, Parisi, Sevelev, Urbani and Zamponi (SciPost Phys., 2017)
problems.ageNote: The exponent values originate in the full-RSB hard-sphere solution of Charbonneau, Kurchan, Parisi, Urbani and Zamponi (2014); the perceptron identification is Franz-Parisi 2016, as the manuscript cites.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for the spherical perceptron with margin $-1$ and quadratic penalty there is a sharp feasibility threshold $\alpha_c$; the ordered limits (size, then zero temperature, then $\alpha\downarrow\alpha_c$) of the contact-removed gap law and mean-one force law exist with $G_J(u)=u^{1-\gamma+o(1)}$, $F_J(s)=s^{1+\theta+o(1)}$, $\gamma=(2+\theta)^{-1}$, $0.4126930<\gamma<0.4126934$, $0.4231063<\theta<0.4231088$, and the critical limit is isostatic. The same holds for a small Gaussian scale mixture of coordinates. Not shown: other negative margins, the unpenalized hard-constraint model directly, other limit orders, or finite-size scaling.

problems.name: Pixton's conjecture: do Pixton's relations give all tautological relations on the moduli of stable curves?
problems.field: Algebraic geometry; moduli of curves; tautological rings
problems.statement: The tautological ring $R^*(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})$ is the image of the strata algebra of decorated stable graphs in the Chow ring. In 2012 Pixton proposed an explicit system of graph relations extending the Faber-Zagier relations; Pandharipande-Pixton-Zvonkine proved them valid in cohomology and Janda in Chow. Pixton conjectured completeness: that the span $P_{g,n}$ of his relations (with the operations it is closed under) is the whole kernel of the realization map, in Chow and in cohomology (recorded as Pixton's conjecture in Canning 2025). Is $\ker(\mathcal S_{g,n}\to CH^*(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n};\mathbb Q))=P_{g,n}$ for every stable pair $(g,n)$?

problems.name: Quasi-isometric rigidity of virtually polycyclic groups (the Eskin-Fisher-Whyte lattice-recognition conjecture)
problems.statement: Gromov's polynomial growth theorem implies that a finitely generated group quasi-isometric to a virtually nilpotent group is virtually nilpotent. For solvable groups of exponential growth, quasi-isometric rigidity was known only for special classes: Sol and lamplighters (Eskin-Fisher-Whyte), nondegenerate abelian-by-abelian groups (Peng), SOL-like groups (Dymarz; Dymarz-Fisher-Xie), and under stronger hypotheses such as commability (Le Boudec). Shalom showed such a group virtually has infinite abelianization. Eskin, Fisher and Whyte (2007) conjectured that a finitely generated group quasi-isometric to a lattice in a connected simply connected solvable Lie group is virtually a lattice in a possibly different such Lie group; equivalently: if a finitely generated group $H$ is quasi-isometric to a finitely generated virtually polycyclic group, must $H$ be virtually polycyclic?
problems.posedBy: A. Eskin, D. Fisher and K. Whyte, Quasi-isometries and rigidity of solvable groups, Pure Appl. Math. Q. 3 (2007), Conjecture 1.2 and Remark (3), p. 929
problems.ageNote: The question of quasi-isometric rigidity for polycyclic and solvable groups is older (Gromov's program; Farb-Mosher around 2000); the manuscript cites Eskin-Fisher-Whyte 2007 for the precise conjecture answered.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: every finitely generated group quasi-isometric to a finitely generated virtually polycyclic group is virtually polycyclic; Corollary 1.2: a finitely generated group quasi-isometric to a lattice in a connected simply connected solvable Lie group has a finite-index subgroup that is a uniform lattice in some (possibly different) such Lie group. The key input is a uniform bounded-height theorem: every $(K,C)$ self quasi-isometry of a unimodular real-triangulable solvable Lie group preserves the exponential height map up to bounded error and one of finitely many linear symmetries. Amenability then gives elementary amenability, and finiteness and duality give virtual polycyclicity. It does not classify solvable groups up to quasi-isometry or describe their quasi-isometry groups in general.

problems.name: The tensor square conjecture for symmetric groups: some irreducible representation of S_n has a tensor square containing every irreducible
problems.field: Representation theory of symmetric groups; Kronecker coefficients
problems.statement:
For partitions of $n$ let $g(\lambda,\mu,
u)$ be the Kronecker coefficients of $S_n$. Heide, Saxl, Tiep and Zalesski showed that for most finite simple groups of Lie type the Steinberg character has a tensor square containing every irreducible character. For symmetric groups, Pak, Panova and Vallejo formulated the tensor square conjecture (Conjecture 1.1): for every $n\ge3$ other than $4$ and $9$ there is $\lambda\vdash n$ with $g(\lambda,\lambda,
u)>0$ for all $
u\vdash n$; it fails for $n=2,4,9$. Saxl's conjecture would give it at triangular $n$; elsewhere only partial and asymptotic results were known (Luo and Sellke found irreducibles whose fourth tensor power contains everything). Does every $S_n$ with $n
otin\{2,4,9\}$ have an irreducible representation whose tensor square contains every irreducible representation?
problems.posedBy: Igor Pak, Greta Panova and Ernesto Vallejo
problems.ageNote: Pak, Panova and Vallejo, arXiv 1304.0738 (2013), published in Adv. Math. 288 (2016), Conjecture 1.1, as cited by the manuscript; it follows Heide-Saxl-Tiep-Zalesski's Steinberg-square theorem for groups of Lie type.
problems.resultNote:

otin\{2,4,9\}$ there is $\lambda\vdash n$, necessarily self-conjugate, with $g(\lambda,\lambda,
u)>0$ for every $

problems.name: The Lê-Ramanujam mu-constant problem for surface singularities: are mu-constant families in three variables topologically trivial?
problems.statement: Let $f_t:(\mathbb C^N,0)\to(\mathbb C,0)$ be a holomorphic one-parameter family with isolated critical points at the origin, and $\mu(f_t)=\dim_{\mathbb C}\mathcal O_{\mathbb C^N,0}/(\partial f_t/\partial x_i)$ its Milnor number. Lê and Ramanujam (1976) proved that constant $\mu$ implies constant embedded topological type whenever $N\ne3$, using the h-cobordism theorem, and Timourian and King obtained topological triviality of the family of functions there. The argument fails for complex surfaces, $N=3$, where Briançon-Speder examples show that $\mu$-constant families need not be Whitney equisingular. This remaining case is the surface case of the $\mu$-constant problem. Is every $\mu$-constant holomorphic family of isolated hypersurface singularities in $\mathbb C^3$ topologically trivial?
problems.posedBy: Lê Dũng Tráng and C. P. Ramanujam (the case left open by their theorem)
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites Lê and Ramanujam, Amer. J. Math. 98 (1976), whose theorem excludes hypersurface dimension two, and calls the remaining case 'the surface case of the mu-constant problem' without a separate posing reference.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: every holomorphic one-parameter family $f_t$ of isolated hypersurface singularities in $\mathbb C^3$ with constant $\mu(f_t,0)$ is topologically right-trivial: after shrinking there is a homeomorphism germ $\Phi(x,t)=(\phi_t(x),t)$, with $\Phi$ and $\Phi^{-1}$ jointly continuous, $\phi_t(0)=0$, $\phi_0=\mathrm{id}$ and $f_t(\phi_t(x))=f_0(x)$. With Lê-Ramanujam and Timourian-King this gives $\mu$-constant topological triviality in every dimension. The key step shows that constant $\mu$ forces constancy of Wahl's logarithmic invariant $-P^2$ for non-log-canonical germs. Not shown: Whitney equisingularity (false in general), families over higher-dimensional parameter spaces, or Zariski's multiplicity question.

problems.name: Chen's conjecture on smooth long-time existence of the Calabi flow
problems.shortName: Chen's Calabi flow long-time existence conjecture
problems.statement: Calabi introduced the Calabi flow $\partial_t\phi=S(\omega_\phi)-\bar S$, $\omega_\phi=\omega_0+i\partial\bar\partial\phi$, to search for extremal and constant-scalar-curvature Kahler metrics in a fixed Kahler class of a compact Kahler manifold. Short-time existence and stability near cscK metrics were proved by Chen and He, and global existence is known on Riemann surfaces. Chen conjectured that the flow exists smoothly for all positive time from arbitrary smooth Kahler initial data (He-Zeng 2021, Conjecture 1.1); Chen and Cheng emphasized the case of classes containing a cscK metric. Does the smooth Calabi flow starting from any smooth Kahler metric on a compact Kahler manifold exist for all time?
problems.posedBy: Xiuxiong Chen
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites the conjecture as stated in He and Zeng, The Calabi flow with rough initial data, IMRN 2021, Conjecture 1.1, and Chen-Cheng, JAMS 34 (2021); it does not give the year Chen first stated it, so yearPosed is left blank.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there is a smooth $U(10)$-invariant Kahler form $\omega_0$ on $\mathbb{CP}^{10}$ in the Fubini-Study class whose maximal smooth Calabi flow exists only on $[0,T_*)$ with $0<T_*<\infty$, and at a point $p$ the scalar curvature blows up like $a(T_*-t)^{-1/2}$. Since the class contains the cscK Fubini-Study metric, smooth global existence fails even there. Corollary 1.2 gives finite-time singularities in every complex dimension $n\ge10$ on $\mathbb{CP}^{10}\times\mathbb{CP}^{n-10}$. Not shown: anything in complex dimensions 2 to 9, or about weak (Streets, Berman-Darvas-Lu) flows, which continue to exist.

problems.name: The unrestricted infinite matroid intersection and packing/covering conjectures
problems.statement: Work with infinite matroids in the sense of Bruhn-Diestel-Kriesell-Pendavingh-Wollan. Two matroids $M,N$ on a common ground set $E$ satisfy intersection if some $J$ independent in both splits as $J=J_M\sqcup J_N$ with $\mathrm{cl}_M(J_M)\cup\mathrm{cl}_N(J_N)=E$. Nash-Williams conjectured this for finitary matroids, and Joo proved it for countable ground sets; Bowler and Carmesin formulated the unrestricted Matroid Intersection Conjecture and the packing/covering conjecture (every family has a partition $E=P\sqcup C$ with disjoint spanning sets in each $M_i\restriction P$ and independent sets in each contraction onto $C$ covering $C$) and showed them related. Joo asked whether intersection holds for two partitional matroids on a countable set. Do every two infinite matroids on a common ground set satisfy intersection, and does every family have a packing/covering partition?
problems.posedBy: Nathan Bowler and Johannes Carmesin (Combinatorica 2015), extending Nash-Williams' intersection conjecture; Joo (2021, Question 1.5) for partitional matroids
problems.ageNote: Nash-Williams' original finitary intersection conjecture is older and is not settled here; the year is that of Bowler-Carmesin's unrestricted formulation, which is what is disproved.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: in ZFC there are a countably infinite set $E$ and two self-dual infinite matroids $M_0,M_1$ on $E$ with $I_0\cup I_1\ne E$ for all independent $I_0,I_1$; the pair has no packing/covering partition, so the infinite matroid packing/covering conjecture is false. Corollary 1.2: the same partitional pair fails intersection, refuting the unrestricted infinite Matroid Intersection Conjecture and answering Joo's Question 1.5 negatively. The examples are neither finitary nor cofinitary, so Nash-Williams' original conjecture for finitary matroids and the cofinitary cases are untouched. The local building block also answers the Bowler-Geschke ZFC question on self-dual uniform matroids (separate entry).

problems.name: Local smooth isometric immersion of surfaces in three-space
problems.shortName: Local isometric immersion of smooth surfaces in R3
problems.statement: Given a smooth Riemannian metric $g$ on a surface, can a neighbourhood of each point be realised as a smooth surface in $\mathbb R^3$, i.e. is there a smooth $F$ with $\langle\partial_iF,\partial_jF\rangle=g_{ij}$ near the point? The analytic case is the Janet-Cartan theorem (1926 to 1927); smooth local existence holds where the Gaussian curvature is nonzero, and Lin, Nakamura-Maeda, Han-Khuri and others treated nonnegative curvature and various degenerate zero sets. Nash-Kuiper gives $C^1$ realisations, and Pogorelov and Nadirashvili-Yuan gave $C^{2,1}$ metrics with no $C^2$ realisation. Does every smooth surface metric admit a smooth local isometric immersion into $\mathbb R^3$?
problems.posedBy: Discussed by S.-T. Yau, Review of geometry and analysis (Asian J. Math., 2000, p. 236), and stated as Problem 1.9 in M. Ghomi, Open problems in geometry of curves and surfaces (2019)
problems.ageNote: Dated to Yau's 2000 discussion, the earliest statement the manuscript cites in the text; the question is older (the analytic case was settled by Janet and Cartan in 1926 to 1927, and the manuscript's bibliography also lists a Schoen-Yau 1994 problem list not cited in the text).
problems.resultNote: Theorem A: there is a $C^\infty$ positive definite metric $g$ on $(-1,1)^2$ such that no open neighbourhood of the origin admits a $C^\infty$ isometric immersion into $\mathbb R^3$; the metric can have the full Taylor jet of the Euclidean metric at the origin, so local realisability is not decided by the jet. The curvature takes both signs. Not settled: the smooth local problem under $K\ge0$ or $K\le0$, finite-regularity versions, and realisation in $\mathbb R^4$.

problems.name: The Euclidean Steinitz-Bergstrom conjecture: is the Euclidean Steinitz constant O(sqrt d)?
problems.field: Discrepancy theory; rearrangements of vector sums
problems.statement: Let $S_2(d)$ be the least number such that every finite family of vectors $v_1,\dots,v_N$ in the Euclidean unit ball of $\mathbb R^d$ with $\sum v_i=0$ has an ordering whose partial sums all have norm at most $S_2(d)$. Steinitz's lemma gives a bound depending only on $d$; Grinberg and Sevastyanov (1980) proved $S\le d$ for every norm, and the simplex example shows $S_2(d)\ge\tfrac12\sqrt d$. The expected square-root scale in Euclidean space was discussed by Behrend (1954), and the conjecture is attributed to Bergstrom. Is $S_2(d)=O(\sqrt d)$?
problems.posedBy: Attributed to Viktor Bergstrom (attribution recorded by Ambrus and Heck, Mathematika 2026, Conjecture 5); square-root growth discussed by F. A. Behrend (1954)
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites Behrend (1954, p. 108) for the expected square-root growth and Ambrus-Heck for the attribution to Bergstrom; Bergstrom's 1931 paper is in its bibliography but is not cited in the text, so 1954 is the earliest dated statement the paper itself relies on.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.2: there is an absolute constant $C$ such that every zero-sum family of vectors in the Euclidean unit ball of $\mathbb R^d$ (repetitions allowed) has an ordering with all partial sums of norm at most $C\sqrt d$; with the simplex lower bound, $\tfrac12\sqrt d\le S_2(d)\le C\sqrt d$. It follows from the prescribed-order signing theorem (separate entry). The constant is not made explicit, and the construction is existential: no online rule or efficient algorithm is given.

problems.name: The Bochner-Riesz conjecture in three dimensions (strict-order range)
problems.field: Harmonic analysis; Fourier multipliers and summability
problems.statement: For $\delta\ge0$ the Bochner-Riesz means on $\mathbb R^n$ are $\widehat{T_\delta f}(\xi)=(1-|\xi|^2)_+^\delta\widehat f(\xi)$. Fefferman (1971) showed the ball multiplier ($\delta=0$) is unbounded on $L^p$ for $p\ne2$ when $n\ge2$; Carleson and Sjolin (1972) proved the conjectured range in the plane. The Bochner-Riesz conjecture asserts that $T_\delta$ is bounded on $L^p(\mathbb R^n)$ whenever $\delta>\max\{n|1/p-1/2|-1/2,0\}$; Tao (1999) showed it implies the restriction conjecture. In $\mathbb R^3$ the strict range was known only for $\max\{p,p'\}\ge 22/7$ (Lee, Wu, Gao-Wu-Xi). Is $T_\delta$ bounded on $L^p(\mathbb R^3)$ for every $1\le p\le\infty$ and every $\delta>\max\{3|1/p-1/2|-1/2,0\}$?
problems.posedBy: Bochner-Riesz summability (Riesz 1923; Bochner 1935-36); the manuscript cites no single source for the conjectured range
problems.ageNote: The manuscript traces the problem to Riesz (1923) and Bochner (1935-36) and to Fefferman (1971) and Carleson-Sjolin (1972), but does not say who first stated the conjectured range or when; left null rather than guessed.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every $\delta>0$, $\|T_\delta f\|_{L^3(\mathbb R^3)}\le C_\delta\|f\|_{L^3(\mathbb R^3)}$. By complex interpolation and duality this gives boundedness on $L^p(\mathbb R^3)$ for all $1\le p\le\infty$ and $\delta>\max\{3|1/p-1/2|-1/2,0\}$, the full strict-order range in three dimensions, hence $L^p$ convergence of Bochner-Riesz means for $3/2\le p\le3$ at every positive order. Via Tao's implication it yields the spherical extension estimate $\|Eg\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^3)}\le C_p\|g\|_{L^\infty(S^2)}$ for $p>3$. Not shown: the endpoint order, the maximal Bochner-Riesz operator, or any dimension $n\ge4$; it is a partial result on the $n$-dimensional conjecture.

problems.name: Bloch's Conjecture for Surfaces with $p_g=0$
problems.statement: For a smooth connected projective complex surface $S$, the Albanese map $\mathrm{CH}_0(S)^0\to\mathrm{Alb}(S)(\mathbb{C})$ on degree-zero zero-cycles modulo rational equivalence is surjective. Mumford showed that $p_g(S)>0$ makes $\mathrm{CH}_0(S)$ infinite-dimensional, and Bloch conjectured the converse. Bloch-Kas-Lieberman proved it for Kodaira dimension below 2, leaving surfaces of general type with $p_g=q=0$, where it says any two points are rationally equivalent; only special families (Godeaux, Campedelli, Burniat, Inoue, Barlow, Catanese) were known. If $p_g(S)=0$, is the Albanese map an isomorphism?
problems.posedBy: Spencer Bloch
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites Bloch's Lectures on Algebraic Cycles (first edition 1980) for the conjecture and Bloch-Kas-Lieberman (1976) for its proof below general type, so it was stated by 1976. The exact first statement is not given.
problems.resultNote: For every smooth connected projective complex surface $S$ with $p_g=q=0$, $\deg:\mathrm{CH}_0(S)\to\mathbb{Z}$ is an isomorphism with integral coefficients, with no minimality, fundamental-group or construction hypothesis. With Bloch-Kas-Lieberman this gives $\mathrm{CH}_0(S)^0\cong\mathrm{Alb}(S)(\mathbb{C})$ for every such surface with $p_g=0$. Over $\mathbb{C}$ only; it does not address the generalized Bloch conjecture in higher dimension. An earlier proof of the same statement was proposed by Guletskii (arXiv:2512.12451, December 2025), which the manuscript cites; this entry claims no priority over it.

problems.name: The Benson-Etingof-Ostrik conjecture for finite symmetric tensor categories
problems.field: Tensor categories; positive characteristic, Verlinde categories
problems.statement: In characteristic zero, Deligne's theorem gives every symmetric tensor category of moderate growth a fiber functor to supervector spaces. In characteristic $p>0$, Benson, Etingof and Ostrik constructed the tower of higher Verlinde categories $\mathrm{Ver}_p\subset\mathrm{Ver}_{p^2}\subset\cdots$ and conjectured that every symmetric tensor category of moderate growth over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$ admits a fiber functor to the union of this tower. Ostrik proved it for fusion categories (to $\mathrm{Ver}_p$). Does every finite symmetric tensor category in characteristic $p$, including $p=2$, admit a fiber functor to some $\mathrm{Ver}_{p^n}(k)$?
problems.posedBy: D. Benson, P. Etingof and V. Ostrik, New incompressible symmetric tensor categories in positive characteristic, Duke Math. J. 172 (2023), Conjecture 1.4
problems.ageNote: Year of the Duke publication cited by the manuscript; the preprint circulated earlier, which the manuscript does not date.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: every finite symmetric tensor category over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$ has a fiber functor to a single finite level $\mathrm{Ver}_{p^n}(k)$, including $p=2$. Consequences stated: classification of finite incompressible categories (the finite case of Coulembier-Etingof-Ostrik's Conjecture B), uniqueness of the functor in characteristic two via their subterminality theorem, and a generalized Tannakian realization. The full conjecture for non-finite categories of moderate growth is not addressed.

problems.name: The near-boundary Birkhoff conjecture: billiards integrable near the boundary are ellipses
problems.field: Dynamical systems; convex billiards and integrability
problems.statement: In a planar billiard in a strictly convex domain $\Omega$, a caustic is a curve such that a trajectory tangent to it stays tangent after every reflection. Ellipses are integrable: confocal ellipses foliate a neighbourhood of the boundary by caustics. The Birkhoff conjecture, traditionally attributed to Birkhoff and first printed by Poritsky (1950), asserts that every integrable strictly convex billiard is an ellipse. Lazutkin found a Cantor family of caustics near the boundary for every smooth positively curved table; Bialy proved rigidity under integrability of the whole phase space; Avila-De Simoi-Kaloshin and Kaloshin-Sorrentino proved local versions near ellipses. Is a smooth, strictly convex, positively curved billiard table an ellipse whenever it is integrable near the boundary?
problems.posedBy: Traditionally attributed to G. D. Birkhoff (Dynamical Systems, 1927); first printed formulation by Hillel Poritsky, Ann. of Math. 51 (1950), as the manuscripts cite
problems.ageNote: The manuscripts attribute the conjecture to Birkhoff and cite his 1927 book for the setting, with Poritsky's 1950 paper as the early printed formulation; the near-boundary form is not attributed to a separate poser.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1 (phase foliations): if a $T$-invariant open annulus containing $(\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z)\times(0,\eta)$ in the billiard phase space is homeomorphically foliated by individually invariant essential curves, then $\Omega$ is an ellipse. The companion proves the same conclusion from a continuous collar of smooth closed convex caustics, via analytic regularity of the boundary and complex continuation. Only continuity across leaves is assumed. Not covered: integrability only on a Cantor set, rational integrability, or integrability away from the boundary; the full Birkhoff conjecture (global integrability as typically defined) is reduced to but not identical with this case.

problems.name: Deterministic black-box noncommutative singularity testing for rational linear matrices (Garg-Gurvits-Oliveira-Wigderson question)
problems.shortName: Black-box NC singularity over the rationals
problems.field: Algebraic complexity; noncommutative rank; operator scaling
problems.statement: A linear matrix $L=A_0+\sum_i A_ix_i$ with matrix coefficients is noncommutatively singular if it is not invertible over the free skew field, equivalently if $L(X)$ is singular for every tuple of matrices $X$ of every dimension. Garg, Gurvits, Oliveira and Wigderson gave a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm for this problem that reads the coefficients (white box). In Section 6 of their Operator Scaling paper they asked for a black-box construction: a deterministic, polynomial-size list of matrix tuples, depending only on the sizes, on which every noncommutatively nonsingular pencil becomes invertible. Can such a list be constructed in deterministic polynomial time?
problems.posedBy: Ankit Garg, Leonid Gurvits, Rafael Oliveira and Avi Wigderson, Operator scaling: theory and applications, Found. Comput. Math. 20 (2020), Section 6, p. 280
problems.ageNote: The Operator Scaling paper first appeared as a preprint in 2015; the manuscript cites the 2020 journal version for the question.
problems.resultNote: Claims a deterministic polynomial-time, polynomial-size list of rational matrix tuples on which every noncommutatively nonsingular rational affine pencil of bounded order becomes invertible, and a list recovering the noncommutative rank of rectangular rational pencils from ordinary ranks. It does NOT treat pencils with coefficients from other fields; the GGOW question for general fields remains.
problems.aiRole: The release README says all results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model, the vast majority by one fixed procedure using on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result. The manuscripts are credited to OpenAI with no human author named. The answer is a corollary in Section 5 (the pencil-hitting corollary) of the rational-formula hitting-list manuscript, which also gives a rank-detecting list for rectangular rational pencils.

problems.name: The entanglement area law for gapped ground states in two dimensions
problems.shortName: 2D area law for gapped ground states
problems.field: Quantum many-body systems; entanglement and spectral gaps
problems.statement: Let $H=\sum_X h_X$ be a Hamiltonian on finitely many spins $\mathbb C^q$ placed on a finite domain $\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z^2$, with interactions of bounded range $R$ and norm at most $J$, and a unique ground state $\Omega$ separated from the rest of the spectrum by a gap $\Delta>0$ independent of the system size. Hastings (2007) proved that in one dimension the entanglement entropy $S_\Omega(A)$ of any interval is bounded by a constant depending only on $q,R,J,\Delta$. The gap-to-area-law conjecture asks for the higher-dimensional analogue; in two dimensions only subvolume or near-linear bounds for frustration-free, locally gapped models were known. Is there a constant $C=C(q,R,J,\Delta)$ such that $S_\Omega(A)\le C|\partial A|$ for every region $A$ of every such two-dimensional system?
problems.posedBy: The gap-to-area-law conjecture, cited by the manuscript to M. B. Hastings (2007) and Arad, Landau and Vazirani (2012)
problems.ageNote: Area scaling of entanglement goes back to Bombelli-Koul-Lee-Sorkin (1986) and Srednicki (1993). The lattice conjecture for gapped ground states is cited by the manuscript to Hastings 2007, whose one-dimensional proof left higher dimensions open.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for fixed $q,R,J,\Delta$ there is $C$ such that for every finite induced domain $\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z^2$ and every Hamiltonian of range $R$ and term norm $J$ with a unique ground vector $\Omega$ and $H-E_0\ge\Delta(1-|\Omega\rangle\langle\Omega|)$, every $A\subseteq\Lambda$ has $S_\Omega(A)\le C|\partial_\Lambda A|$. Corollary 1.2 gives the vertex-boundary forms. The companion proves that on open $L\times L$ grids with nearest-neighbour interactions the ground state has a PEPS approximation of bond dimension $CL^c$ and global error $L^{-1}$. It does not treat dimensions three and higher, Renyi entropies, or degenerate ground states, and gives no explicit constant.

The release has no Lean formalization for this family. The result is two-dimensional only: the paper makes no claim for $\mathbb Z^d$ with $d\ge3$. The constant is existential.

problems.name: QMA-hardness of the electronic Coulomb ground energy in the full continuum, with unit nuclear charges
problems.statement: Given clamped nuclei at rational positions in $\mathbb R^3$ and $N$ electrons, the electronic Hamiltonian is $H=-\frac12\sum_i\Delta_{x_i}-\sum_{i,\alpha}Z_\alpha/|x_i-R_\alpha|+\sum_{i<j}1/|x_i-x_j|$ on antisymmetric spinful wave functions. O'Gorman, Irani, Whitfield and Fefferman showed that estimating the ground energy is QMA-complete when the many-electron states are restricted to a supplied finite orbital basis, and raised the question for the complete infinite-dimensional space, where an unrestricted continuum state can lie below every basis state. Is approximating the continuum ground-energy infimum $\inf\mathrm{spec}\,H$ to inverse-polynomial precision QMA-hard?
problems.posedBy: Bryan O'Gorman, Sandy Irani, James Whitfield and Bill Fefferman (PRX Quantum 3, 2022, Section V)
problems.resultNote: Unit-charge paper, Theorem 1.1: the promise problem for the electronic Coulomb infimum with distinct rational nuclear positions, all charges 1, unary electron number and thresholds separated by at least $L^{-1}$ is QMA-hard under deterministic polynomial-time many-one reductions; the reductions output polynomially many nuclei and electrons and threshold gap at least 1, with no basis, magnetic field or extra potential. Companion: the same with binary-encoded, possibly exponentially large charges. No membership in QMA, no spectral-gap or binding assumption, and no claim about chemically natural instances.

problems.name: The $n^{1/6}$ free-energy fluctuation scale of the low-temperature Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model, with a limiting law
problems.statement: In the zero-field Gaussian Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model $H_n(\sigma)=\frac{1}{\sqrt n}\sum_{i<j}g_{ij}\sigma_i\sigma_j$, let $F_n=\log\sum_\sigma e^{\beta H_n(\sigma)}$. At high temperature $\beta<1$ the fluctuations of $F_n$ are of order one (Aizenman-Lebowitz-Ruelle). For fixed $\beta>1$, Crisanti, Paladin, Sommers and Vulpiani predicted that the free energy per spin fluctuates on the scale $n^{-5/6}$, that is $\mathrm{sd}(F_n)\asymp n^{1/6}$, and Parisi and Rizzo developed the related large-deviation calculation. Is the standard deviation of $F_n$ of order $n^{1/6}$ at every fixed $\beta>1$, and does the centered, rescaled free energy converge to a limiting law?
problems.posedBy: A. Crisanti, G. Paladin, H.-J. Sommers and A. Vulpiani (J. Phys. I France 2, 1992); developed by Parisi and Rizzo (2008-2009)
problems.ageNote: The prediction is in Crisanti-Paladin-Sommers-Vulpiani, 'Replica trick and fluctuations in disordered systems' (1992), following Kondor's 1983 replica expansion. The best rigorous bounds before this work were Aronow-Lopatto (2026): n^(4/15) <= Var F_n <= n^(7/15).
problems.resultNote: Companion (fluctuation scale): for every fixed $\beta>1$, $\mathrm{sd}(F_n)=n^{1/6+o(1)}$ and $|F_n-\mathbb EF_n|$ is typically between $n^{1/6-\eta}$ and $n^{1/6+\eta}$. Principal (limiting law): $\mathrm{Var}(F_n)/n^{1/3}$ converges to a constant in $(0,\infty)$, every moment of the $n^{-1/6}$-rescaled completed free energy converges with a polynomial rate, exponential moments are uniformly bounded, and $(F_n-\mathbb EF_n)/\mathrm{sd}(F_n)$ converges along all $n$ to a nondegenerate law with mean 0 and variance 1, uniquely determined by its moments. The law is not identified with a named distribution and no formula for the variance constant is given.

problems.name: The isoperimetric conjecture for the cubic flat three-torus (balls, tubes, slabs)
problems.field: Geometric measure theory; periodic isoperimetric problem
problems.statement: In the unit cubic flat torus $\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3$, which regions of prescribed volume $V$ have least perimeter? The conjecture predicts that the minimizers are, in turn, round balls, solid circular tubes about shortest closed geodesics, and slabs between parallel coordinate tori, followed by their complements, so the profile is $\min\{(36\pi)^{1/3}v^{2/3},2\sqrt{\pi v},2\}$ with $v=\min(V,1-V)$. Small volumes (Morgan-Johnson) and volumes near one half (Acerbi-Fusco-Morini) were known, and Milman reduced the profile to the two transition volumes, but excluding higher-genus competitors in between remained open. Is the ball-tube-slab picture the true isoperimetric profile of the cubic three-torus?
problems.posedBy: Hauswirth, Perez, Romon and Ros, The periodic isoperimetric problem, Trans. AMS 356 (2004); also A. Ros, The isoperimetric problem (Clay Math. Proc. 2, 2005), Section 1.6
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites the 2004 HPRR paper and Ros's 2005 survey as where the prediction appears explicitly; it may be older in the folklore of the periodic problem, but no earlier written source is given.
problems.resultNote: Claims the full isoperimetric profile of $\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3$, $I(V)=\min\{(36\pi)^{1/3}v^{2/3},2\sqrt{\pi v},2\}$, and a classification of all finite-perimeter minimizers: balls for $V\le4\pi/81$, tubes about shortest geodesics for $4\pi/81\le V\le1/\pi$, coordinate slabs for $1/\pi\le V\le1/2$, complements above $1/2$, with exactly the two adjacent types at each transition volume. The new step excludes three- and four-vertex nonstandard configurations at the two transition volumes via nested planar sections. It does NOT treat non-cubic flat tori, the cube with relative perimeter beyond the reflection correspondence, or higher dimensions.

The manuscript is credited to OpenAI with no human author named. Some one-variable estimates are closed with explicit outward-rounded arithmetic bounds in an appendix. problems.name: The Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer formula in Selmer corank at most one
problems.shortName: BSD formula in Selmer corank at most one
problems.field: Arithmetic of elliptic curves; Iwasawa theory
problems.statement: For an elliptic curve $E/\mathbb{Q}$ of rank $r$, the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture predicts $\mathrm{ord}_{s=1}L(E,s)=r$, finiteness of the Tate-Shafarevich group, and the leading-term formula $L^{(r)}(E,1)/r! = \Omega_E\,\mathrm{Reg}_E\,\#Sha(E/\mathbb{Q})\prod_\ell c_\ell(E)/\#E(\mathbb{Q})_{tors}^2$. Gross-Zagier and Kolyvagin gave the rank equality and finiteness of Sha when the analytic rank is at most one, but the exact leading-term formula in that range was known only at particular primes and under reduction, residual or CM hypotheses (Skinner-Urban, Jetchev-Skinner-Wan, Rubin, Burungale-Flach). Does the full leading-term formula, at every prime, hold for every elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ whose $q^\infty$-Selmer group has corank $0$ or $1$ for some prime $q$?
problems.posedBy: Bryan Birch and Peter Swinnerton-Dyer (the conjecture); Tate's 1966 Bourbaki account fixed the leading-term formula
problems.ageNote: Year of Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer, Notes on elliptic curves II (1965), cited by the manuscript. The low-rank integral formula as a target is the program of Skinner-Urban (2014) and Jetchev-Skinner-Wan, also cited.
problems.resultNote: For every $E/\mathbb{Q}$ and prime $q$ with $s_q(E)=\mathrm{corank}\,\mathrm{Sel}_{q^\infty}(E/\mathbb{Q})\in\{0,1\}$: $\mathrm{rank}\,E(\mathbb{Q})=\mathrm{ord}_{s=1}L(E,s)=s_q(E)$, $Sha(E/\mathbb{Q})$ is finite, and the full BSD leading-term formula holds at every prime, with no hypotheses on reduction, torsion, isogenies, CM or residual representations. By Gross-Zagier-Kolyvagin this covers every curve of analytic rank at most one (curator's reading). The new step is the exact $p$-adic valuation at every odd $p$; $p=2$ comes from the two-primary companion. With family 006 it gives full BSD for a density-one set of quadratic twists of each curve. It says nothing about analytic rank $\geq 2$.

The principal manuscript (October 3, 2026) builds on two companion manuscripts in this family and on the release's Goldfeld-density manuscript (family 006).

problems.name: Erdos Problem #371: do the integers with P(n) < P(n+1) have density 1/2? (Erdos-Pomerance joint independence of largest prime factors)
problems.field: Analytic number theory; smooth numbers and largest prime factors
problems.statement: Let $P^+(n)$ be the largest prime factor of $n$ and $\rho$ the Dickman function, so that $P^+(n)\le n^a$ has density $\rho(1/a)$. Erdos and Pomerance (1978) conjectured that the largest prime factors of $n$ and $n+1$ behave independently, so that $P^+(n)\le n^a$ and $P^+(n+1)\le n^b$ hold simultaneously with density $\rho(1/a)\rho(1/b)$, and in particular that the set of $n$ with $P^+(n)<P^+(n+1)$ has natural density $1/2$ (Erdos Problem #371). They proved positive lower density for each ordering; later bounds reached about $0.28$. Teravainen (2018) proved the logarithmic-density version and Tao and Teravainen (2019) the natural-density version at almost all scales. Does $\{n:P^+(n)<P^+(n+1)\}$ have natural density $1/2$, and are $\log P^+(n)/\log n$ and $\log P^+(n+1)/\log n$ asymptotically independent?
problems.posedBy: P. Erdos and C. Pomerance, On the largest prime factors of n and n+1, Aequationes Math. (1978), p. 311; Erdos Problem #371
problems.ageNote: The manuscript notes that the comparison conjecture is usually attributed to Erdos and Turan; the joint-independence form is cited to Erdos and Pomerance (1978).
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for fixed $a,b\in(0,1)$, $\frac1X\#\{2\le n\le X:P^+(n)\le n^a,P^+(n+1)\le n^b\}\to\rho(1/a)\rho(1/b)$, unconditionally and at every large scale. Corollary 1.2: $P^+(n)<P^+(n+1)$ and the reverse ordering each have natural density $1/2$. Inclusion-exclusion also gives the Erdos-Pomerance upper-tail independence statement. It gives no rate and no uniformity in $a,b$ (unlike the almost-all-scales quantitative law of Tao-Teravainen 2026), and says nothing about three consecutive integers (Erdos #372 and Balog's density 1/6 conjecture).

problems.name: Donovan's conjecture on Morita finiteness of blocks with a given defect group
problems.field: Modular representation theory of finite groups; block theory
problems.statement: Let $p$ be a prime and $k$ an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$ (or, in the integral form, a complete discrete valuation ring $\mathcal O$ with residue field $k$). A block of $kG$ has a defect group, a $p$-subgroup determined up to conjugacy. Donovan's conjecture states that for a fixed finite $p$-group $P$, as $G$ ranges over all finite groups, the blocks with defect group isomorphic to $P$ fall into only finitely many Morita equivalence classes. Known cases include symmetric-group blocks (Scopes), abelian 2-groups (Eaton-Livesey), extraspecial groups of order $p^3$ for $p\ge5$ (An-Eaton) and quaternion defect groups (Eaton-Eisele-Kessar-Linckelmann-Schaeffer Fry, 2026). Does Donovan finiteness hold for every finite $p$-group, every prime, over $k$ and over $\mathcal O$?
problems.posedBy: P. Donovan; recorded as Conjecture M in J. L. Alperin, Local representation theory, Santa Cruz Conference on Finite Groups, Proc. Sympos. Pure Math. 37 (1980)
problems.ageNote: The manuscripts attribute the conjecture to Peter Donovan and cite Alperin's 1980 account (from the 1979 Santa Cruz conference) as where it appears; Donovan's own formulation is not dated there.
problems.resultNote: Field paper, Theorem 1.1: for each prime $p$, algebraically closed $K$ of characteristic $p$ and bound $M$, blocks of finite groups over $K$ with defect groups of order at most $M$ represent only finitely many $K$-linear Morita classes; defect groups may be nonabelian and $p=2$ is included. Integral companion, Theorem 1.1 and Corollary: the same over $W(\overline{\mathbb F}_p)$ and over each fixed complete DVR of characteristic zero with algebraically closed residue field, ramified included. Consequences: bounded Cartan entries and Loewy lengths. Not shown: explicit lists or bounds on the number of classes, or Morita finiteness over coefficient fields that are not algebraically closed.

problems.name: Prescribed-order Euclidean prefix discrepancy O(sqrt d), independent of length (Bansal-Jiang-Meka-Singla-Sinha Conjecture 6.3)
problems.statement: Given vectors $v_1,\dots,v_N$ in the Euclidean unit ball of $\mathbb R^d$ in a fixed order, choose signs $\varepsilon_i\in\{\pm1\}$ to keep every prefix sum $\sum_{i\le k}\varepsilon_iv_i$ small. Banaszczyk proved a bound $O(\sqrt d+\sqrt{\log N})$, which grows with the length when $N$ is large compared with $d$. Bansal, Jiang, Meka, Singla and Sinha (2021, Section 6, Conjecture 6.3), following Banaszczyk, conjectured the length-free square-root bound. Is there an absolute $C$ such that every such sequence has signs with all prefix sums of norm at most $C\sqrt d$?
problems.posedBy: Nikhil Bansal, Haotian Jiang, Raghu Meka, Sahil Singla and Makrand Sinha, Prefix Discrepancy, Smoothed Analysis, and Combinatorial Vector Balancing, arXiv 2111.07049 (2021), Conjecture 6.3
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: an absolute constant $C$ such that every finite sequence in the Euclidean unit ball of $\mathbb R^d$, in prescribed order, has one signing with every prefix of norm at most $C\sqrt d$, independent of $N$. This removes the $\sqrt{\log N}$ term from Banaszczyk's bound and is optimal up to the constant. It is existential: no efficient or online algorithm is given, so the algorithmic and online versions of the question remain open.

problems.name: Brannen's simplex conjecture for projection-body volume
problems.field: Convex geometry; projection bodies, reverse affine isoperimetric inequalities
problems.statement: For a convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ with projection body $\Pi K$ (support function $h_{\Pi K}(u)=\mathrm{vol}_{d-1}(\mathrm{proj}_{u^\perp}K)$), the ratio $R_d(K)=|\Pi K|/|K|^{d-1}$ is affine invariant. The simplex has $R_d=c_d=(d+1)d^d/d!$. Brannen (1996) conjectured that simplices maximize $R_d$ among all convex bodies, i.e. $|\Pi K|\le c_d|K|^{d-1}$. Is the simplex the maximizer of normalized projection-body volume in every dimension?
problems.posedBy: N. S. Brannen, Volumes of projection bodies, Mathematika 43 (1996)
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1: for $K=T_{10}\times T_{10}\subset\mathbb R^{20}$, $R_{20}(K)/c_{20}=121\binom{20}{10}/(21\cdot2^{20})>1$, so the simplex bound fails in dimension 20; iterating the product identity $R_{r+s}(A\times B)=R_r(A)R_s(B)$ gives $R_n(K_n)\ge\lambda^nc_n$ for some $\lambda>1$ and all large $n$. Priority: Feng, Hu, Liu and Xu (preprint, August 2026) already disproved the conjecture in every dimension $d\ge9$, and Chen et al. proved it in dimension 3; the paper cites both and presents its result as a direct product construction with an exact value. It does not determine the optimal upper constant or the maximizers.

problems.name: The Gaitsgory-Raskin full-support conjecture for restricted geometric Langlands in positive characteristic
problems.field: Geometric Langlands program; l-adic sheaves in positive characteristic
problems.statement: Let $X$ be a smooth projective connected curve over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, $G$ a connected reductive group, $\ell\ne p$. Gaitsgory and Raskin constructed, under the characteristic hypotheses of the restricted theory of Arinkin-Gaitsgory-Kazhdan-Raskin-Rozenblyum-Varshavsky, a $\mathrm{QCoh}(Y)$-linear equivalence from $\mathrm{Shv}_{\mathrm{Nilp}}(\mathrm{Bun}_G(X))$ onto $\mathrm{IndCoh}_{\mathrm{Nilp}}(Y')$ for an open-and-closed union $Y'$ of connected components of the restricted stack $Y=\mathrm{LS}^{\mathrm{restr}}_{\check G}(X)$, and proved $Y'=Y$ for $GL_n$. Their Conjecture 1.3.10 asserts that no component is missing. Is $Y'=Y$, so that the restricted Langlands functor is an equivalence onto all of $\mathrm{IndCoh}_{\mathrm{Nilp}}(Y)$?
problems.posedBy: Dennis Gaitsgory and Sam Raskin
problems.ageNote: Gaitsgory-Raskin, Geometric Langlands in positive characteristic from characteristic zero, arXiv:2508.02237 (2025), Conjecture 1.3.10, as cited by the manuscript.
problems.resultNote: Theorem (full support): under either regime, $Y'=Y$, so $\mathbb L^{\mathrm{restr}}_G:\mathrm{Shv}_{\mathrm{Nilp}}(\mathrm{Bun}_G(X))\to\mathrm{IndCoh}_{\mathrm{Nilp}}(Y)$ is a $\mathrm{QCoh}(Y)$-linear equivalence; a rational-coefficient form is also proved over $\overline{\mathbb F}_q$. Consequences: nonzero localized categories at every spectral component, the full arithmetic trace formula in the finite-field regime, and nonzero Hecke eigenobjects for every parameter. It does not remove the characteristic hypotheses, and does not assert bounded constructibility or perversity of eigenobjects (the three October 5 eigensheaf companions construct perverse tame eigensheaves in specific settings).

problems.name: The higher-dimensional Duke theorem for torus packets of totally real fields of prime degree at least five (with primitive quartic and sextic cases)
problems.field: Homogeneous dynamics; equidistribution of periodic torus orbits
problems.statement: Ideal classes of a totally real field $K$ of degree $n$ give compact orbits of the diagonal group $A_n$ on $X_n=\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb Z)\backslash\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb R)$, grouped into packets by local homothety type. Duke proved equidistribution for $n=2$; Einsiedler, Lindenstrauss, Michel and Venkatesh proved the cubic case and described the extension to higher prime degree as conditional on subconvexity; Lemke Oliver, Thorner and Zaman handled prime degree outside a sparse exceptional set of fields. For a fixed degree $n$ and discriminants tending to infinity, do the volume-weighted packet measures on $X_n$ converge to Haar probability measure, with no escape of mass?
problems.posedBy: Einsiedler, Lindenstrauss, Michel and Venkatesh (Distribution of periodic torus orbits and Duke's theorem for cubic fields, Annals of Math. 2011, Section 1.6.3), following Linnik and Duke
problems.ageNote: The manuscripts locate the higher-degree question in ELMV 2011, Section 1.6.3, building on ELMV 2009 (Duke Math. J.) and Duke 1988; Linnik's ergodic method goes back to the 1960s.
problems.resultNote: Principal Theorem 1.1: for each fixed prime $n\ge5$ and any totally real fields $K_i$ of degree $n$ with full lattices $M_i$ whose multiplier-order discriminant $D(M_i)\to\infty$, the packet measures converge weakly to Haar measure on $X_n$ with no escape of mass, for every local homothety type, nonmaximal orders of unbounded index and every field (no exceptional set). Companions: the same for Picard packets of arbitrary orders in primitive totally real quartic fields, and for ideal-class packets of maximal orders in primitive totally real sextic fields. Not shown: individual orbits, rates, composite degrees with proper intermediate fields, nonmaximal sextic orders.

problems.name: The Benjamini-Schramm nonuniqueness conjecture: p_c < p_u for bond percolation on nonamenable quasi-transitive graphs
problems.statement: Let $G$ be an infinite connected locally finite quasi-transitive graph and consider Bernoulli bond percolation with critical parameter $p_c(G)$ (infinite clusters appear) and uniqueness threshold $p_u(G)$ (the infinite cluster becomes unique almost surely). On a regular tree of degree at least three, $p_c<p_u=1$. Benjamini and Schramm (1996, Conjecture 6) conjectured that nonamenability alone always separates the two thresholds. It was known under extra hypotheses: planar one-ended transitive graphs, highly nonamenable or large-girth graphs, graphs with nonconstant harmonic Dirichlet functions (Gaboriau), Gromov hyperbolic and nonunimodular graphs (Hutchcroft), and Cayley graphs for some suitably chosen generating set. Hutchcroft further conjectured the stronger strict inequality $p_c<p_{2\to2}$ for the $\ell^2$ operator threshold. Is $p_c(G)<p_u(G)$ for every nonamenable quasi-transitive graph $G$, so that some interval of $p$ has infinitely many infinite clusters?
problems.posedBy: Itai Benjamini and Oded Schramm
problems.ageNote: Benjamini and Schramm, Electronic Communications in Probability 1 (1996), Conjecture 6, stated for site percolation and extended by them to bond percolation; Hutchcroft's operator-threshold form is from GAFA 29 (2019), Conjecture 6.1.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every infinite connected locally finite quasi-transitive graph with positive vertex isoperimetric constant, $\sup_{p<p_c}\|T_p\|_{2\to2}=\|T_{p_c}\|_{2\to2}<\infty$ and $p_c<p_{2\to2}\le p_u$; there are $p_c<p_1<p_2<1$ such that, in the uniform-label coupling, almost surely infinitely many infinite clusters exist simultaneously for all $p\in[p_1,p_2]$. Corollary 1.2 gives the same for every finite symmetric generating set of every nonamenable finitely generated group. Further consequences: the triangle condition at $p_c$, mean-field critical exponents, and exponential decay of connections below $p_{2\to2}$. It concerns bond percolation only; the site-percolation form of the conjecture and the related $p_u<1$ question for one-ended graphs are not addressed. Constants and the interval depend on $G$.

problems.name: The Ford-Konyagin-Luca conjecture: the prime factors of $p-1$ follow the Poisson-Dirichlet law
problems.field: Analytic number theory; smooth shifted primes
problems.statement: For a prime $p$, list the prime factors of $p-1$ with multiplicity in decreasing order $q_1(p)\ge q_2(p)\ge\cdots$ and set $V_j(p)=\log q_j(p)/\log(p-1)$. For a uniformly random integer the analogous normalized factor sizes converge to the Poisson-Dirichlet law $\mathrm{PD}(1)$ (Billingsley, Donnelly-Grimmett). Ford, Konyagin and Luca (2010, Section 6, Conjecture 5) conjectured the same for shifted primes. The first coordinate already contains the shifted-prime Dickman law stated by Granville, $\#\{p\le x:P^+(p-1)\le x^{1/u}\}\sim\pi(x)\rho(u)$ for fixed $u$; unconditionally only lower bounds of size $x/(\log x)^C$ for $P^+(p-1)\le x^{0.2844}$ were known (Baker-Harman, Lichtman), and the full law was known under Elliott-Halberstam (Bharadwaj-Rodgers). With $p$ uniform among primes up to $x$, does $(V_1(p),V_2(p),\ldots)$ converge in finite-dimensional distributions to $\mathrm{PD}(1)$ as $x\to\infty$?
problems.posedBy: Kevin Ford, Sergei Konyagin and Florian Luca (Prime chains and Pratt trees, GAFA 2010, Section 6, Conjecture 5)
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every $k$ and bounded continuous $F$ on $[0,1]^k$, the average of $F(V_1(p),\ldots,V_k(p))$ over primes $3\le p\le x$ tends to $\mathbb E F(L_1,\ldots,L_k)$ with $(L_j)\sim\mathrm{PD}(1)$, unconditionally and with equal weight on each prime. The manuscript notes this gives Granville's fixed-$u$ asymptotic $\#\{p\le x:P^+(p-1)\le x^{1/u}\}\sim\pi(x)\rho(u)$, so a positive proportion of primes have $x^{\varepsilon}$-smooth predecessors for each fixed $\varepsilon>0$. No error terms or uniformity as $u$ grows are claimed. The companion on $\mu(p-1)=1$ (infinitely many primes with $p-1$ squarefree with an even number of prime factors) is linked here, not cataloged, since it cites no posing source.

problems.name: Zauner's conjecture: at most three mutually unbiased bases in dimension six
problems.shortName: Mutually unbiased bases in dimension six
problems.field: Mutually unbiased bases; complex Hadamard matrices
problems.statement: Orthonormal bases $\mathcal B,\mathcal C$ of $\mathbb C^d$ are mutually unbiased if $|\langle b,c\rangle|^2=1/d$ for all $b\in\mathcal B$, $c\in\mathcal C$. Let $N(d)$ be the largest number of pairwise unbiased bases. Always $N(d)\le d+1$, with equality in prime-power dimensions (Ivanovic; Wootters-Fields), so $d=6$ is the first open case. Three bases exist in $\mathbb C^6$ from a tensor-product construction; numerical searches (Butterley-Hall, Brierley-Weigert) and restricted exclusions (Grassl; Jaming et al. for the Fourier family) found no fourth. Zauner conjectured in his 1991 diploma thesis that three is the maximum; Klappenecker and Rotteler state $N(6)=3$ as Conjecture 1. Is $N(6)=3$?
problems.posedBy: Gerhard Zauner (diploma thesis, Vienna, 1991); stated as Conjecture 1 by Klappenecker and Rotteler (2004)
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1 (computer-assisted): there are no four pairwise mutually unbiased orthonormal bases in $\mathbb C^6$, hence $N(6)=3$, the lower bound coming from the explicit tensor-product triple. The proof covers every second basis (an arbitrary complex Hadamard matrix) by certified phase balls and excludes two further bases in each by a clique search with rounding margins. It is conditional on the stated binary64 arithmetic and on the complete execution it documents. The companion paper gives an exact rational certificate only for $N(6)\le5$, and that weaker bound is what the release's Lean formalization proves.
