problems.name: The ordinary-double-point gap conjecture for normalized volumes of klt singularities
problems.statement: For a klt germ $x\in X$ of dimension $n$ with zero boundary, the normalized volume $\widehat{\mathrm{vol}}(x,X)=\inf_vA_X(v)^n\mathrm{vol}(v)$ over valuations centred at $x$ is at most $n^n$, with equality exactly at smooth points (Liu-Xu). Spotti and Sun, motivated by volume densities of tangent cones of Kahler-Einstein limits, conjectured that the ordinary double point comes next. It was known for surfaces (Li-Liu), threefolds (Liu-Xu) and local complete intersections (Liu), with a different sharp bound for toric germs (Moraga-Suss). Does every singular $n$-dimensional klt germ satisfy $\widehat{\mathrm{vol}}(x,X)\le2(n-1)^n$, with equality exactly for an ordinary double point?

problems.ageNote: Spotti-Sun, Pure Appl. Math. Q. 13 (2017), Conjectures 1.2 and 5.5 (arXiv 1705.00377); listed in Xu-Zhuang, Open problems in K-stability of Fano varieties (2026).
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for $n\ge2$ and a singular closed point of a normal complex algebraic $n$-fold with $K_X$ $\mathbb Q$-Cartier, klt with zero boundary, $\widehat{\mathrm{vol}}(x,X)\le2(n-1)^n$, with equality iff the germ is analytically an ordinary double point; the point need not be isolated. The companion proves dimension four (bound 162), the base case. Corollary 1.2 gives a strict anticanonical volume bound below $2n^n$ for singular K-semistable $\mathbb Q$-Fano $n$-folds, so $(-K_V)^n=2n^n$ off projective space only for the smooth quadric or $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^{n-1}$. By the Holevo-Schumacher-Westmoreland theorem its unassisted classical capacity is the regularized Holevo information $\lim_n\chi(\mathcal A^{\otimes n})/n$, and since Holevo additivity fails in general (Hastings) the one-use value need not be the answer. What is the classical capacity of $\mathcal A_{\gamma,
u}$ for all $\gamma,
u$, and does it equal the one-shot Holevo capacity?

problems.name: Parity is not in QAC0 (Moore's parity conjecture)
problems.field: Quantum circuit complexity; constant-depth lower bounds
problems.statement: $\mathrm{QAC}^0$ is the class of constant-depth quantum circuits on polynomially many qubits built from arbitrary one-qubit unitaries and Toffoli gates with unboundedly many controls, gates in a layer acting on disjoint qubits. Classically parity is not in $\mathrm{AC}^0$ (Furst-Saxe-Sipser, Ajtai, Hastad). Moore introduced these quantum classes in 1999 and related coherent parity to unbounded fanout; he conjectured that parity cannot be computed in $\mathrm{QAC}^0$. Prior lower bounds needed restrictions on the number of ancillas or on the entangling depth. Can a constant-depth quantum circuit of this kind, with polynomially many zero-initialized ancillas, compute the parity of $n$ input bits with bounded error?
problems.posedBy: Cristopher Moore (Quantum circuits: fanout, parity, and counting, arXiv quant-ph/9903046, 1999)
problems.resultNote: Claims: for every fixed depth $d$, every $c\ge1$ and every $0<\varepsilon\le1/2$, for all large $n$ no depth-$d$ circuit of one-qubit unitaries and unbounded-arity Toffoli gates on at most $n^c$ qubits, ancillas starting in $|0\rangle$ and one output qubit measured, computes parity with probability at least $1/2+\varepsilon$ on every input. Taking $\varepsilon=1/6$ gives bounded error $2/3$. The companion paper gives a second proof via regular trajectories and pruning; via Xu-Li reductions the same obstruction holds for strict majority. It does not cover circuits with intermediate measurements, postselection or primitive fanout gates, and gives no explicit size-depth tradeoff beyond polynomial size.

problems.name: Matiyasevich's single-fold conjecture: every r.e. set has a single-fold Diophantine representation
problems.statement: By the Davis-Putnam-Robinson-Matiyasevich theorem every recursively enumerable set $S\subseteq\mathbb N^n$ has a Diophantine representation: a polynomial $P$ with integer coefficients such that $a\in S$ iff $P(a,w)=0$ for some $w\in\mathbb N^m$. The representation is single-fold if such $w$ is unique when it exists, finite-fold if there are finitely many. Matiyasevich (1974) proved single-fold exponential Diophantine representations and posed the polynomial case, reducing it to a single-fold representation of exponentiation; the finite-fold conjecture is the weaker form. Does every recursively enumerable set have a single-fold Diophantine representation?
problems.posedBy: Yuri Matiyasevich
problems.ageNote: Matiyasevich, The existence of non-effectivizable estimates in the theory of exponential Diophantine equations, Zap. Nauchn. Sem. LOMI 40 (1974), Section 1; finite-fold form in Matiyasevich, Towards finite-fold Diophantine representations (2010); both cited by the manuscript.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: every r.e. $S\subseteq\mathbb N^n$, $n\ge1$, has a polynomial $P\in\mathbb Z[A_1..A_n,W_1..W_m]$ with $\#\{w\in\mathbb N^m:P(a,w)=0\}$ equal to 1 for $a\in S$ and 0 otherwise. Hence the finite-fold conjecture holds, and Diophantine solvability over $\mathbb N$ stays undecidable under an at-most-one-solution promise (Section 8). The construction bounds a Pell-type exponential with a cutoff from rational points on a rank-one elliptic curve. Witnesses range over $\mathbb N$; the paper does not claim the analogue over $\mathbb Z$ beyond what follows from it, nor any bound on degree or number of variables.

problems.name: The approximation threshold for metric $k$-median: is $1+2/e$ attainable?
problems.statement: In metric $k$-median, finite sets of clients $J$ and candidate facilities $F$ lie in a common metric space, and one opens at most $k$ facilities to minimize the total distance from clients to their nearest open facility. Approximating within any factor below $1+2/e\approx1.736$ is NP-hard in this candidate-facility model, by the Max-$k$-Coverage gap. Algorithms improved from the first constant factor (Charikar-Guha-Tardos-Shmoys) through $3+\varepsilon$ local search (Arya et al.), Li-Svensson's route past factor three, $2.675+\varepsilon$ (Byrka et al.) and $2.613$ (Gowda et al.) to $2+\varepsilon$ (Cohen-Addad et al., announced 2025). Is there, for every $\varepsilon>0$, a polynomial-time $(1+2/e+\varepsilon)$-approximation, so that $1+2/e$ is the exact approximation threshold?
problems.posedBy: Implicit in the 1+2/e hardness bound of Jain, Mahdian and Saberi (2002); the manuscript names no poser
problems.ageNote: The manuscript does not attribute the question; it cites the hardness through Anand-Lee (2024) and Feige (1998). Matching the 1+2/e lower bound has been a standard open question in approximation algorithms since that bound appeared around 2002, but that dating comes from the general literature, not from this manuscript, so yearPosed is left empty.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$, a deterministic algorithm running in time polynomial in the binary input length (the polynomial depends on $\varepsilon$) returns $S\subseteq F$ with $|S|\le k$ and cost at most $(1+2/e+\varepsilon)\mathrm{OPT}_k$, for arbitrary $k$ and arbitrary finite rational metrics with specified candidate facilities. Corollary 1.2: under $P\ne NP$, the infimum of polynomial-time approximation factors in this model is $1+2/e$, the lower bound being the known coverage gap. It does not give a $(1+2/e)$-approximation itself, does not settle the model where every client is a candidate facility ($F=J$), whose lower bound differs, and claims no practical running time. The companion proves a randomized $(2-\sigma)$-approximation for an absolute $\sigma>0$ by anchor recovery and bounded-price payment accounting.

problems.name: The Modified Integer Round-Up Conjecture for bin packing (Scheithauer-Terno)
problems.field: Bin packing and cutting stock; configuration LP integrality gap
problems.statement: In one-dimensional bin packing (cutting stock), the Gilmore-Gomory configuration linear program assigns nonnegative weights to feasible bin patterns and minimizes their total subject to covering the item demands; its value $LP(I)$ is a lower bound for the optimum number of bins $OPT(I)$. The integer round-up property $OPT(I)=\lceil LP(I)\rceil$ fails (Marcotte 1985-86), but all known instances satisfied $OPT(I)\le\lceil LP(I)\rceil+1$. Scheithauer and Terno (1995, 1997) investigated this modified bound, now known as the Modified Integer Round-Up Conjecture. Does every bin packing instance satisfy $OPT(I)\le\lceil LP(I)\rceil+1$?
problems.posedBy: Guntram Scheithauer and Johannes Terno
problems.ageNote: Scheithauer and Terno, Eur. J. Oper. Res. 84 (1995) and Oper. Res. Lett. 20 (1997), as cited by the manuscript, which calls the bound the Modified Integer Round-Up Conjecture.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every integer $c\ge0$ there are a finite rational instance $I$, every item larger than $1/6$ (so at most five items per bin), and an integer $B$ with $LP(I)=B$ and $OPT(I)>B+c$; the same LP value holds for the stronger formulation whose patterns are subsets of individual item copies. So the additive integrality gap of the configuration LP is unbounded and the Modified Integer Round-Up Conjecture is false. Not shown: a gap growing like $\log OPT$ in the instance size, matching the Hoberg-Rothvoss upper bound; the paper says it obtains no such lower bound.

problems.name: The hot spots conjecture for smooth simply connected planar domains
problems.shortName: Hot spots, smooth simply connected planar
problems.field: Spectral theory of the Neumann Laplacian
problems.statement: Rauch's hot spots problem (1975) asks whether an eigenfunction for the first positive Neumann eigenvalue $\mu_1(\Omega)$ of a bounded domain $\Omega$ attains its maximum and minimum only on the boundary. It fails in general: Burdzy and Werner (1999) gave a planar counterexample with two holes, and Burdzy (2005) one with a single hole. Burdzy conjectured that it holds for bounded simply connected planar domains; known cases include lip domains, triangles and symmetric convex domains. Does every first-positive Neumann eigenfunction on a bounded simply connected planar domain attain its extrema only on the boundary?
problems.posedBy: Krzysztof Burdzy (simply connected planar form); the hot spots problem is due to Jeffrey Rauch
problems.ageNote: Burdzy, The hot spots problem in planar domains with one hole, Duke Math. J. 129 (2005), Conjecture 1.2(ii), as cited by the manuscript. Rauch's original problem: Five problems, Lecture Notes in Math. 446 (1975).
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: on every bounded simply connected planar domain with $C^\infty$ boundary, every nonzero eigenfunction for the first positive Neumann eigenvalue has nonvanishing gradient in the interior, so its global extrema lie only on the boundary; this holds even when the eigenvalue is multiple and with no convexity or symmetry assumption. It does not treat nonsmooth (for example Lipschitz or polygonal) simply connected domains, domains with holes, or higher dimensions.

problems.name: Arnold's corank problem: is the Hessian corank of a hypersurface singularity an ambient topological invariant?
problems.field: Singularity theory; topological invariants of hypersurface germs
problems.statement: For a holomorphic germ $f:(\mathbb{C}^N,0)\to(\mathbb{C},0)$ with a critical point at the origin, let $\mathrm{corank}_0(f)=N-\mathrm{rank}_{\mathbb{C}}\mathrm{Hess}_0(f)$. Fernandes, Jelonek and Sampaio proved that the corank is preserved by ambient homeomorphisms in three complex variables, and Sampaio proved that its parity is an ambient topological invariant in every dimension. Arnold's question, as recorded by Sampaio (2026, Problem 1): if a homeomorphism germ of $(\mathbb{C}^N,0)$ carries $V(f)$ onto $V(g)$ for reduced holomorphic germs $f,g$ with critical points at the origin, must $\mathrm{corank}_0(f)=\mathrm{corank}_0(g)$?
problems.posedBy: V. I. Arnold, as stated in J. E. Sampaio, 'On the Arnold corank, the Zariski multiplicity, and the tangent Milnor fiber problems' (preprint, 2026), Problem 1
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites the question only through Sampaio's August 2026 preprint, which attributes it to Arnold. It gives no date for Arnold's original formulation, so the year is left blank.
problems.resultNote: The weighted homogeneous germs $f_1,f_2$ on $\mathbb{C}^N$ ($N>3$, divisible by eight) of the Zariski counterexample are ambiently homeomorphic, have isolated critical points and real coefficients, and have Hessian ranks $16E>0$ and $0$, so their coranks differ. Corank parity is preserved, as Sampaio's theorem requires. Nothing is said about corank in three variables (where it is invariant) or about a minimal dimension.

problems.name: The finite-temperature free energy of the spherical perceptron with bounded continuous potentials (Gyorgyi-Reimann continuous-RSB formula)
problems.statement: For $x$ uniform on the sphere of radius $\sqrt N$ in $\mathbb R^N$, $M=\lfloor\alpha N\rfloor$ standard Gaussian patterns and a single-pattern potential $\phi$, the pressure is $p_N=N^{-1}\log\int e^{\beta\sum_a\phi(g^a\cdot x/\sqrt N)}d\sigma_N(x)$. Gardner (1988) began the study of such storage volumes; Shcherbina-Tirozzi proved Gardner's replica-symmetric formula for nonnegative margins in a restricted regime. Gyorgyi and Reimann (2000) derived a continuous replica-symmetry-breaking formula for the finite-temperature model, which in general is not replica-symmetric and not a Gaussian spin glass. Does $p_N$ converge, for every density and temperature and nonconvex potentials, to that variational formula?
problems.posedBy: Geza Gyorgyi and Peter Reimann, Beyond storage capacity in a single model neuron: continuous replica symmetry breaking (J. Stat. Phys., 2000), after Elizabeth Gardner (1988)
problems.ageNote: Gardner's storage-volume problem dates to 1988; the precise finite-temperature formula the theorem matches is Gyorgyi-Reimann 2000, as the manuscript cites.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for all $\alpha,\beta>0$ and $\phi\in C_b(\mathbb R)$, $\mathbb Ep_N$ and $p_N$ (in probability) converge to $\inf_m\{\alpha V_{\beta\phi}(m)+S(m)\}$ over nondecreasing $m:[0,1]\to[0,1]$, with $V$ a Brownian stochastic-control value and $S$ the spherical entropy; this matches the Gyorgyi-Reimann continuous-RSB functional. Companions: the analogous formula for the Gaussian Ising perceptron with any bounded Borel log-potential at all densities and positive temperatures, and for spherical models with bi-orthogonally invariant disorder without outliers. Not shown: hard constraints or zero temperature (storage capacity), discontinuous potentials in the spherical case, or properties of the optimizer.

problems.name: Sogge's local smoothing conjecture for the wave equation in three spatial dimensions
problems.field: Harmonic analysis; dispersive and wave equations
problems.statement: For the half-wave propagator $e^{it\sqrt{-\Delta}}$ on $\mathbb R^n$, the sharp fixed-time estimate on $L^p$ loses $(n-1)|1/2-1/p|$ derivatives. Sogge (1991) conjectured that averaging over $t\in[1,2]$ gains almost $1/p$ of a derivative for $p\ge 2n/(n-1)$: $\|e^{it\sqrt{-\Delta}}f\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^n\times[1,2])}\le C\|f\|_{W^{\sigma,p}}$ for $\sigma>(n-1)(1/2-1/p)-1/p$, and $\sigma>0$ for $2<p\le 2n/(n-1)$. It implies the Bochner-Riesz conjecture and was proved for $n=2$ by Guth, Wang and Zhang (2020). In three spatial dimensions the critical exponent is $p=3$; Bourgain-Demeter decoupling gave the conjecture for $p\ge4$, Gan-He-Li-Wu for $p\ge10/3$, and at $p=3$ only $\sigma>1/12$ was known. Does the estimate hold in $\mathbb R^3$ for every $2<p<\infty$ and every $\sigma>\max\{0,1-3/p\}$, in particular at $p=3$ with every positive loss?
problems.posedBy: Christopher D. Sogge
problems.ageNote: Sogge, Propagation of singularities and maximal functions in the plane, Invent. Math. 104 (1991), Section 4, cited by the manuscript as the source of the higher-dimensional formulation.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every $\varepsilon>0$, $\|e^{it\sqrt{-\Delta}}f\|_{L^3(\mathbb R^3\times[1,2])}\le C_\varepsilon\|J^\varepsilon f\|_{L^3}$. With the $L^2$ and $L^\infty$-kernel endpoints, Corollary 10.6 gives the full strict range $2<p<\infty$, $\sigma>\max\{0,1-3/p\}$. Section 11, through Beltran-Hickman-Sogge, Tao and Wolff, derives the strict three-dimensional Bochner-Riesz range, maximal Bochner-Riesz bounds for $p\ge3$, the diagonal sphere restriction estimate $L^r(S^2)\to L^r(\mathbb R^3)$ for $r>3$, and the three-dimensional Kakeya maximal estimate. Not shown: the endpoint $\sigma=0$ at $p=3$, dimensions $n\ge4$, or the conjecture's general-$n$ form.
problems.aiRole: The release README says the results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model with a fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result, and that some outputs build on earlier model results. This result is not among the README's exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region). The manuscript is authored 'OpenAI' and names no human author. The manuscript uses two external published inputs, the planar Furstenberg theorem of Ren-Wang and the cone wave-envelope theorem of Guth-Wang-Zhang.

Checked here: Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 10.6 were read against Sogge's conjecture in dimension three; the stated range matches the conjectured strict range. The 160-page proof was not refereed. problems.name: The log abundance conjecture in characteristic zero (rational boundary, every dimension), with canonical nonvanishing
problems.statement: For a projective log canonical pair $(X,B)$ the abundance conjecture of the minimal model program asserts that if the log canonical divisor $K_X+B$ is nef then it is semiample: some positive multiple is generated by global sections, so numerical positivity defines a morphism. The companion nonvanishing conjecture asserts that a pseudo-effective canonical class on a smooth projective variety has a nonzero pluricanonical section. Abundance was known in dimension at most three (Miyaoka, Kawamata, Keel-Matsuki-McKernan) and in special cases beyond. Is every nef $\mathbb Q$-Cartier $K_X+B$ on a projective log canonical pair with effective rational boundary, over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, semiample?
problems.posedBy: Central conjecture of the minimal model program (Kawamata, Miyaoka, Reid and others); the manuscripts name no single poser and cite its threefold history
problems.ageNote: The manuscripts do not say who posed the conjecture or when. Its threefold cases were proved between 1988 and 1994 (Miyaoka, Kawamata, Keel-Matsuki-McKernan), and it has been a standing conjecture of the minimal model program since the 1980s.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for a normal projective lc pair $(X,B)$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, with $B$ effective rational and $K_X+B$ $\mathbb Q$-Cartier and nef, some positive Cartier multiple of $K_X+B$ is globally generated. The induction also gives good minimal models for lc pairs with pseudo-effective real adjoint and, over $\mathbb C$, canonical nonvanishing for smooth projective varieties in every dimension; consequences include rational slc abundance (Fujino-Gongyo) and finite generation of lc rings. Not shown: semiampleness with real boundaries, positive characteristic, or any bound on the multiple. The family's compact Kahler log abundance theorem assumes logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity (claimed in family 033) and is not part of this entry.
problems.claimIssueNote: The release contradicts itself on this claim. The 24 September manuscript's abstract states that the rational-boundary log abundance conjecture is proved in every dimension. An appendix of the release's own 5 October manuscript on compact Kahler fourfolds calls the same theorem "a positive conditional resolution of the log abundance conjecture. It is not an unconditional abundance theorem", resting on a logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity assumption that it says follows from a lemma elsewhere in the release. Until OpenAI clarifies which reading is meant, or a specialist checks the chain, the entry is Contested.

problems.name: The irrationality exponent of pi is 2
problems.statement: The irrationality exponent of an irrational $x$ is $\mu(x)=\sup\{\nu>0: 0<|x-p/q|<q^{-\nu}$ for infinitely many coprime $p,q$, $q\ge2\}$; Dirichlet's pigeonhole argument gives $\mu(x)\ge2$, and almost every real has $\mu=2$. For $\pi$ only finite upper bounds were known: Mahler (1953) gave $42$, Mignotte $20$, Hata about $8.016$, Salikhov about $7.606$, and Zeilberger and Zudilin about $7.103$. The expected value is $2$, recorded as the conjecture that for every $\varepsilon>0$, $|\pi-p/q|\ge q^{-2-\varepsilon}$ for all large $q$. Is $\mu(\pi)=2$?
problems.posedBy: Folklore conjecture; the manuscript cites its statement in Michel Waldschmidt, Open Diophantine problems, Moscow Math. J. 4 (2004), p. 265
problems.ageNote: The manuscript names no originator or year; it cites Waldschmidt's 2004 survey as the place the conjecture is recorded. The question of a finite exponent goes back at least to Mahler's 1953 bound, the earliest work the manuscript cites.
problems.resultNote:
Theorem 1.1: $\mu(\pi)=2$; for every $
u>2$ there is $Q(
u)$ with $|\pi-p/q|\ge q^{-
u}$ for all $p\in\mathbb Z$ and $q\ge Q(
u)$. Corollary: the Flint Hills series converges, and $\sum n^{-a}|\sin n|^{-b}$ converges iff $a>\max\{1,b\}$. The bound is NOT effective (no explicit $Q(
u)$), and it is NOT a bound of the form $c/q^2$: bounded partial quotients for $\pi$ are not claimed. The method is an interpolation-determinant argument, not an improvement of the integral constructions behind earlier numerical bounds.

This family has one manuscript, dated September 24, 2026. The manuscript is credited to 'OpenAI' alone and names no human author. The README's two exceptions to the fixed procedure (the Riemann zeta zero-free region work, whose Re(s) > 11/12 write-up was human-edited, and the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties) do not concern this family, so the result is presented as found and written up by the model. The README also cautions that unformalized results could have issues. OpenAI also released an abridged reasoning summary for this family (reasoning_traces/irrationality-exponent-of-pi.pdf).

No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 of the TeX source read against the conjecture as posed; it gives, for every real $

problems.name: The endpoint case of Carleson's pointwise convergence problem for the Schrodinger equation: a.e. convergence for data in H^{n/(2(n+1))}
problems.shortName: Endpoint of Carleson's Schrodinger convergence problem
problems.field: Harmonic analysis; dispersive equations and pointwise convergence
problems.statement: Carleson asked for which Sobolev exponents $s$ the free Schrodinger evolution $e^{it\Delta}f$ converges to $f$ almost everywhere as $t\to0$ for every $f\in H^s(\mathbb R^n)$. In one dimension the answer is $s\ge1/4$ (Carleson; Dahlberg-Kenig). Bourgain's 2016 counterexample showed that $s\ge n/(2(n+1))$ is necessary for $n\ge2$ but did not rule out equality; Du, Guth and Li (planar) and Du and Zhang ($n\ge3$) proved convergence for every $s>n/(2(n+1))$, leaving only the endpoint. Does $e^{it\Delta}f\to f$ almost everywhere for every $f\in H^{n/(2(n+1))}(\mathbb R^n)$, $n\ge2$ (in the plane, for $H^{1/3}$)?
problems.posedBy: Lennart Carleson (the convergence problem); the endpoint left open after Bourgain (2016), Du-Guth-Li (2017) and Du-Zhang (2019)
problems.ageNote: Carleson, Some analytic problems related to statistical mechanics (Lecture Notes in Math. 779, 1980), cited by the manuscripts. The endpoint became the remaining case only after Du-Guth-Li and Du-Zhang; the manuscripts cite no separate statement of the endpoint question.
problems.resultNote: Planar theorem: for every $f\in H^{1/3}(\mathbb R^2)$ there is a full-measure set $E_f$ on which the Gaussian-regularised evolution has a limit for every $0<t<1$ and converges to $f$ as $t\downarrow0$. Higher-dimensional theorem: the same for $f\in H^{n/(2(n+1))}(\mathbb R^n)$, every $n\ge3$. With Bourgain's necessary condition this gives the exact range $s\ge n/(2(n+1))$ for $n\ge2$. Not shown: the endpoint local $L^3$ maximal inequality in the plane, sharp $L^p$ maximal estimates at the endpoint in higher dimensions, or results for other dispersive equations or convergence along curves.
problems.aiRole: The release README says the vast majority of results were obtained with one fixed procedure using an unreleased internal OpenAI model, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result, and that some outputs build on earlier results produced by the models. This result is not among the README's exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region, whose write-up was human edited). The manuscripts are authored 'OpenAI' and name no human author. The family has two manuscripts dated September 24, 2026: the planar endpoint $H^{1/3}(\mathbb R^2)$ and the endpoint in every dimension $n\ge3$.

Checked here: the main theorems of both manuscripts were read against Carleson's problem and the endpoint left by Bourgain and Du-Zhang. The evolution is defined by taking the Gaussian-regularisation limit first, on one full-measure spatial set and for all $0<t<1$, which the papers state explicitly; this is a standard way to give meaning to $e^{it\Delta}f$ pointwise. problems.name: The Hovey-Strickland conjecture: the thick tensor ideals of dualizable K(n)-local spectra
problems.statement: Fix a prime $p$ and a height $n\ge1$, and let $\mathcal D_{(n,p)}$ be the homotopy category of dualizable $K(n)$-local spectra, with tensor product $L_{K(n)}(X\wedge Y)$. A thick tensor ideal is a full subcategory closed under retracts, cofiber sequences, suspensions and tensoring with every object. For $0\le k\le n$ the localization of a finite type-$k$ spectrum generates a thick tensor ideal $\mathcal D_k$, giving a chain $\mathcal D_0\supsetneq\mathcal D_1\supsetneq\cdots\supsetneq\mathcal D_n\supsetneq0$. By analogy with the Hopkins-Smith thick subcategory theorem for finite spectra, Hovey and Strickland (1999) conjectured that this chain is everything. Barthel, Heard and Naumann proved it at height two and showed it follows from Chai's invariant-ideal conjecture. For every prime and every height, are the thick tensor ideals of $\mathcal D_{(n,p)}$ exactly the $n+2$ ideals $\mathcal D_0,\ldots,\mathcal D_n,0$, so that the Balmer spectrum is a chain of $n+1$ points?
problems.posedBy: Mark Hovey and Neil Strickland (Morava K-theories and localisation, Mem. AMS 1999, Section 12); restated by Barthel, Heard and Naumann (2022)
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.2: for every prime $p$ and $n\ge1$ the thick tensor ideals of the dualizable $K(n)$-local category are exactly $\mathcal D_0\supsetneq\cdots\supsetneq\mathcal D_n\supsetneq\mathcal D_{n+1}=0$, so there are $n+2$ of them and each $\mathcal D_k$ does not depend on the chosen type-$k$ spectrum; a corollary identifies the Balmer spectrum with the $n+1$ proper members of the chain, with its specialization order. It is deduced from Theorem 1.1 (Chai's conjecture, a separate entry) by the known Barthel-Heard-Naumann implication. It concerns dualizable objects only and does not classify localizing or other subcategories of the whole $K(n)$-local category. Height two was already known.

problems.name: The Ball-Evans approximation problem in three dimensions: strong approximation of Sobolev homeomorphisms by diffeomorphisms
problems.field: Geometric function theory; Sobolev homeomorphisms and nonlinear elasticity
problems.statement: In nonlinear elasticity a deformation is a map between domains whose injectivity expresses non-interpenetration. Smooth approximation of a Sobolev map is elementary if injectivity is dropped, but convolution destroys it. Ball, attributing the question to Evans, asked whether a Sobolev homeomorphism $f\in W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R^n)$ can be approximated in the $W^{1,p}$ norm by diffeomorphisms (or piecewise affine homeomorphisms). In the plane this was proved for $1<p<\infty$ (Iwaniec-Kovalev-Onninen) and $p=1$ (Hencl-Pratelli); in dimensions $n\ge4$ it fails for $1\le p<\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ (Hencl-Vejnar, Campbell-Hencl-Tengvall). In dimension three: for bounded domains $\Omega,\Lambda\subset\mathbb R^3$ and $1\le p<\infty$, is every $W^{1,p}$ homeomorphism $f:\Omega\to\Lambda$ a strong $W^{1,p}$ limit of smooth diffeomorphisms onto $\Lambda$?
problems.posedBy: John M. Ball, attributing the question to Lawrence C. Evans
problems.ageNote: Ball, Singularities and computation of minimizers for variational problems, in Foundations of Computational Mathematics (Oxford, 1999), LMS Lecture Note Series 284 (2001), Section 3, cited by the manuscripts; Ball says the question is due to Evans, who may have raised it earlier.
problems.resultNote: Theorems: for nonempty bounded connected open $\Omega,\Lambda\subset\mathbb R^3$ and a homeomorphism $f\in W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ onto $\Lambda$, there are $C^\infty$ diffeomorphisms $f_j:\Omega\to\Lambda$ with $\|f_j-f\|_{W^{1,p}}\to0$; proved for $1\le p\le2$ in one manuscript and for all finite $p>2$ in the other. The method first builds onto locally bi-Lipschitz approximants with small Sobolev error, then smooths them with fine pointwise control using three-dimensional PL topology (Moise, Bing, Hamilton). It does not give convergence of inverses, approximation by piecewise affine maps with inverse control, or anything in dimensions $n\ge4$ for $p\ge\lfloor n/2\rfloor$.

The manuscripts are authored 'OpenAI' and name no human author. The family has two manuscripts dated September 24, 2026: one for $1\le p\le2$ and one for every finite $p>2$.
problems.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: the main theorems of both manuscripts were read against Ball's formulation. problems.name: The binary corrected Elliott conjecture for ordinary averages
problems.field: Analytic number theory; pretentious multiplicative functions
problems.statement: Elliott (1992) conjectured that correlations $\frac1N\sum_{n\le N}f_1(n+h_1)\cdots f_k(n+h_k)$ of multiplicative functions bounded by one tend to zero when one factor does not pretend to be a twisted character. Matomaki, Radziwill and Tao showed the original hypothesis is insufficient for complex functions and corrected it: with $D(f,\chi n^{it};N)^2=\sum_{p\le N}(1-\mathrm{Re}\,f(p)\overline{\chi(p)}p^{-it})/p$, require $\inf_{|t|\le N}D(f,\chi n^{it};N)\to\infty$ for every fixed Dirichlet character $\chi$. Tao proved the logarithmically averaged binary case, and Tao-Teravainen and Klurman-Mangerel-Teravainen proved it along most scales. For multiplicative $f_1,f_2:\mathbb{N}\to\{|z|\le1\}$ with one factor uniformly nonpretentious and fixed distinct $h_1,h_2$, does $\frac1N\sum_{n\le N}f_1(n+h_1)f_2(n+h_2)\to0$?
problems.posedBy: P. D. T. A. Elliott (Notas Soc. Mat. Chile, 1992); corrected form by Matomaki, Radziwill and Tao (2015)
problems.ageNote: Elliott's 1992 conjecture; the corrected nonpretentiousness hypothesis used here is from Matomaki-Radziwill-Tao (Algebra Number Theory 2015), which the paper cites as equivalent to its condition.
problems.resultNote: For multiplicative $f_1,f_2:\mathbb{N}\to\{|z|\le1\}$, at least one satisfying $\inf_{|t|\le N}D(f_j,\chi n^{it};N)\to\infty$ for every fixed Dirichlet character, and fixed distinct $h_1,h_2\ge0$: $\frac1N\sum_{n\le N}f_1(n+h_1)f_2(n+h_2)\to0$. Also for fixed nonproportional affine forms and in fixed residue classes. Functions may be complex and need not be completely multiplicative. Qualitative only, no rate; the $k$-point Elliott conjecture for $k\ge3$ is not addressed.

problems.name: The critical dimension of the one-phase Bernoulli free boundary problem: is it seven?
problems.statement: For nonnegative $v\in H^1(B)$ the one-phase Bernoulli (Alt-Caffarelli) energy is $J(v;B)=\int_B(|\nabla v|^2+\mathbf 1_{\{v>0\}})\,dx$. By Weiss's monotonicity formula and dimension reduction, the regularity of minimizing free boundaries is governed by the least dimension $d_*$ admitting a nonzero, nonflat, one-homogeneous global minimizer: free boundaries are smooth below $d_*$ and singular sets have dimension at most $n-d_*$. Caffarelli, Jerison and Kenig settled dimension three, Jerison and Savin (2015) proved flatness through dimension four, so $d_*\ge5$, and De Silva and Jerison (2009) constructed a nonflat minimizing cone in dimension seven, so $d_*\le7$, by analogy with the Simons cone for minimal surfaces. Is $d_*=7$, that is, is every one-homogeneous global minimizer in dimensions five and six flat?
problems.posedBy: Open after De Silva and Jerison (2009) and Jerison and Savin (2015); the manuscript names no single poser
problems.ageNote: The manuscript calls it 'the critical-dimension question whether d* = 7', citing De Silva-Jerison (J. Reine Angew. Math. 2009) for d* <= 7 and Jerison-Savin (GAFA 2015) for d* >= 5, but gives no posing reference; the question has been open in this form at least since 2009.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: every nonzero one-homogeneous global minimizer of the one-phase Bernoulli energy in $\mathbb R^d$, $1\le d\le6$, is flat, $u=(x\cdot e)_+$, and a nonflat one-homogeneous global minimizer exists in $\mathbb R^7$, so $d_*=7$. Corollary 1.2: the interior free boundary of a local minimizer in $\mathbb R^n$ is smooth for $n\le6$, its singular set is locally finite for $n=7$ and has Hausdorff dimension at most $n-7$ for $n\ge7$, sharp by products of the De Silva-Jerison cone. Method: a Hessian-shape test function and vector field on the spherical link, with an exactly verified polynomial inequality. Not shown: classification of stable but non-minimizing cones, two-phase or vector-valued versions, or rigidity of non-homogeneous entire stable solutions.

problems.name: The Euclidean-complete affine Bernstein problem in dimensions three through nine
problems.statement: Let $u$ be smooth with positive-definite Hessian on an open convex $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ and solve the affine maximal equation $U^{ij}w_{ij}=0$, $U^{ij}=\det(D^2u)(D^2u)^{-1}_{ij}$, $w=(\det D^2u)^{-(n+1)/(n+2)}$, the Euler equation of affine area. Chern asked whether an entire such surface ($n=2$) must be an elliptic paraboloid; Calabi proved it under Euclidean and affine completeness, and Trudinger and Wang proved the Euclidean-complete surface case in 2000, reduced higher dimensions to a uniform strict-convexity estimate, and exhibited a singular nonquadratic weak solution in dimension ten. For $n\ge3$, if the graph of $u$ is complete for the induced Euclidean metric, must $\Omega=\mathbb R^n$ and $u$ be quadratic, and in which dimensions?
problems.posedBy: Shiing-Shen Chern (Affine minimal hypersurfaces, 1977 seminar, published 1979) for surfaces; the higher-dimensional Euclidean-complete form follows Trudinger and Wang (Invent. Math. 2000)
problems.ageNote: Chern's question concerns surfaces and was posed at a 1977 seminar published in 1979. The manuscripts call the higher-dimensional statement the Euclidean-complete affine Bernstein conjecture without naming who first stated it for n >= 3.
problems.resultNote: Claims: for $3\le n\le9$, every smooth affine maximal graph with positive-definite Hessian over an open convex domain whose graph is complete for the induced Euclidean metric is entire and quadratic, so an elliptic paraboloid; no growth or affine-completeness assumption. Via Trudinger-Wang it extends to affine-complete immersed hypersurfaces. The companion constructs a smooth nonquadratic entire solution with positive-definite Hessian in dimension ten, so the range cannot extend to $n=10$. Dimensions $n\ge11$ are not addressed, and the dimension-ten example asserts no uniform Hessian bound or affine completeness.

The release README says the vast majority of results used one fixed procedure, averaging about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result; this result is not among the README's stated exceptions (the Riemann zeta zero-free region work and the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties). The manuscript is authored as OpenAI with no human author named. The dimension-ten counterexample is a separate manuscript dated 5 October 2026.

That is the headline claim of this entry. Not formalized: the affine-complete immersed-hypersurface corollary and the dimension-ten counterexample.

problems.name: Toda's Gepner conjecture for the quintic threefold
problems.field: Algebraic geometry; Bridgeland stability conditions on Calabi-Yau threefolds
problems.statement: Let $X\subset\mathbb P^4$ be a smooth complex quintic threefold and $\Phi=T_{\mathcal O_X}\circ(-\otimes\mathcal O_X(1))$, the composite of tensoring by the hyperplane bundle and the Seidel-Thomas spherical twist at $\mathcal O_X$, which satisfies $\Phi^5\simeq[2]$. Physics predicts a stability condition at the Gepner point of the stringy Kahler moduli space fixed by this symmetry. Toda (2013) conjectured, in normalized form, that there is a Bridgeland stability condition $\sigma=(Z,\mathcal P)$ on $D^b(\mathrm{Coh}\,X)$ with $Z(\Phi E)=e^{2\pi i/5}Z(E)$ and $\Phi\mathcal P(\varphi)=\mathcal P(\varphi+2/5)$, and reduced it to a strong Bogomolov-Gieseker type inequality. Does every smooth quintic threefold admit such a Gepner-type stability condition?
problems.posedBy: Yukinobu Toda
problems.ageNote: Toda, Gepner type stability conditions on graded matrix factorizations (arXiv 1302.6293, Conjecture 1.2) and Gepner point and strong Bogomolov-Gieseker inequality for quintic 3-folds (arXiv 1305.0345, Conjecture 3.1), as cited.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: every smooth complex quintic threefold has a numerical Bridgeland stability condition, with support property on $K_{\mathrm{num}}(X)_{\mathbb R}$, on which $\Phi$ acts by rotating the charge by $e^{2\pi i/5}$ and shifting phases by $2/5$, normalized by $Z(\mathcal O_x)=-1$. The construction is a double tilt starting at slope $-1/2$, refined to a periodic grid of aisles. It relies on Xu's 2026 inequality. It does not prove Toda's general strong Bogomolov-Gieseker conjecture, treat other Calabi-Yau hypersurfaces, or describe the full stability manifold near the Gepner point.

The principal manuscript (September 24, 2026) is self-contained apart from a cited inequality of Xu (arXiv 2511.21288v2); the companion on large-volume charges (same date) is a separate result.
problems.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 of the principal manuscript was read against Toda's conjecture; it gives a numerical Bridgeland stability condition with the support property on the full numerical Grothendieck group, $Z(\Phi E)=e^{2\pi i/5}Z(E)$, $\Phi\mathcal P(\varphi)=\mathcal P(\varphi+2/5)$ and $Z(\mathcal O_x)=-1$, on every smooth quintic, and identifies the charge with Toda's by uniqueness of the normalized eigenform. problems.name: Existence of minimal models and Mori fibre spaces for projective log canonical pairs, in generalized-pair form
problems.shortName: Minimal model existence for lc pairs
problems.statement: The minimal model conjecture in its existence form asserts that every projective log canonical pair $(X,B)$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero has a minimal model (a birational model with nef $K_Y+B_Y$ and no worse discrepancies) when $K_X+B$ is pseudo-effective, and a Mori fibre space otherwise. Birkar-Cascini-Hacon-McKernan proved this for klt pairs with big boundary or big adjoint; the general case was open in dimension at least five, and for generalized pairs (Birkar-Zhang) carrying a fixed nef part. Does every projective (generalized) log canonical $\mathbb Q$-pair admit a minimal model or a Mori fibre space?
problems.posedBy: Central conjecture of the minimal model program; the manuscript cites its statement as Conjecture 1.1 of Gongyo (2011); generalized pairs of Birkar and Zhang
problems.ageNote: The conjecture is part of the minimal model program from the 1980s (Mori, Kawamata, Shokurov and others); the manuscript names no single poser and cites Gongyo's 2011 manuscript for the precise statement and Han-Li (2022) for the generalized-pair framework. No year is given because the sources do not fix one.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for a projective generalized lc $\mathbb Q$-pair $(X,B+M)$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero there is a birational map $X\dashrightarrow Y$ extracting no divisors, with $(Y,B_Y+M_Y)$ generalized lc and log discrepancies not decreasing (strictly on contracted divisors), such that $K_Y+B_Y+M_Y$ is nef if $K_X+B+M$ is pseudo-effective, and otherwise $Y$ has a Mori fibre space structure with relative Picard number one. With $M=0$ this gives the ordinary lc case. Companion: smooth projective varieties with $\kappa_\sigma(K_X)=1$ have $\mathbb Q$-factorial terminal minimal models. Not shown: termination of arbitrary flip sequences, real coefficients, abundance (claimed in a separate release paper), or Q-factorial models in general.

The manuscripts are authored 'OpenAI' and name no human author. The principal manuscript and the numerical-dimension-one companion are both dated September 24, 2026. The release's log abundance manuscript (already in the catalog) uses this paper's ordinary-pair corollary.

problems.name: The equivariant cohomological Hikita conjecture for quiver gauge theories
problems.field: Geometric representation theory; symplectic duality; Coulomb branches
problems.statement: Hikita conjectured that for a symplectic dual pair the cohomology ring of the symplectic resolution on one side is the coordinate ring of the scheme-theoretic fixed locus of a torus on the other, proving it for Hilbert schemes of points and some type A examples. For a quiver gauge theory the Higgs side is a Nakajima quiver variety $X$ and the dual is the Braverman-Finkelberg-Nakajima Coulomb branch $Y$. The equivariant form (Nakajima, recorded by Kamnitzer-Tingley-Webster-Weekes-Yacobi, formulated by Dumanski-Krylov) asks for compatibility with the tautological coefficient maps from $H^*_{G\times F}(\mathrm{pt})$. Is $H^*_F(X;\mathbb C)\cong\mathbb C[Y^\nu_{\mathfrak f}]$ as graded algebras over the common coefficient ring, for every quiver?
problems.posedBy: Tatsuyuki Hikita (arXiv:1501.02430, IMRN 2017); equivariant form in Kamnitzer-Tingley-Webster-Weekes-Yacobi (2019), Conj. 8.9-8.10; form proved: Dumanski-Krylov (2025), Conj. 2.1
problems.ageNote: Hikita's paper was posted in January 2015 and published in 2017. The quiver-gauge equivariant formulation the manuscript proves is that of Dumanski-Krylov (2025).
problems.resultNote: Claims the equivariant cohomological Hikita conjecture for all quiver gauge theories with regular stability: the flavor-equivariant cohomology of the Nakajima variety is canonically the coordinate ring of the scheme-theoretic stability-cocharacter fixed locus of the flavor-deformed Coulomb branch, including the empty case. It does NOT prove the quantized Hikita statement, nor extend to arbitrary reductive gauge groups, where Hikita-type identifications can fail, nor treat non-regular stability.

problems.name: Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture for abstract elementary classes
problems.statement: Morley proved that a countable first-order theory categorical in one uncountable cardinal is categorical in all of them. Shelah's abstract elementary classes (AECs) generalise elementary classes to nonelementary settings such as $L_{\omega_1,\omega}$ sentences, without compactness. Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture asks for an analogue: for each infinite cardinal $\lambda$ there should be a threshold $\mu(\lambda)$ such that every AEC $K$ with $LS(K)\le\lambda$ that is categorical in some cardinal $\ge\mu(\lambda)$ is categorical in every cardinal $\ge\mu(\lambda)$. Prior proofs needed amalgamation, tameness, a successor starting cardinal, large cardinals or weak GCH. Is eventual categoricity provable in ZFC for all AECs?
problems.posedBy: Saharon Shelah
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites Shelah, Classification Theory for Abstract Elementary Classes (2009), Conjecture N.4.2, and Boney-Vasey (2015). The conjecture is older than that book: the companion notes Shelah introduced AECs in the mid-1970s with these categoricity questions, but the release gives no earlier dated statement.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.2: for every infinite cardinal $\lambda$ there is $\mu(\lambda)\ge\lambda$ such that every AEC $K$ with $LS(K)\le\lambda$ categorical in some $\kappa\ge\mu(\lambda)$ is categorical in every $\kappa'\ge\mu(\lambda)$; equivalently (Theorem 1.3) an AEC categorical in unboundedly many cardinals is categorical on a tail. It applies to $L_{\omega_1,\omega}$ sentences in countable languages. It gives no explicit value for $\mu(\lambda)$; the prescribed $\beth_{\omega_1}$ threshold for $L_{\omega_1,\omega}$ and the Hanf threshold for AECs are left separate (the companion refutes the latter under CH).

problems.name: The Lane-Emden conjecture for elliptic systems, with its Henon-weighted extension
problems.statement: The Lane-Emden system is $-\Delta u=v^p$, $-\Delta v=u^q$ in $\mathbb R^n$ with $p,q>0$. The Lane-Emden conjecture asserts that it has no positive classical entire solution in the subcritical region $\frac1{p+1}+\frac1{q+1}>\frac{n-2}n$, with no symmetry or decay assumption. It was proved for $n\le2$, for $n=3$ (Serrin-Zou; Polacik-Quittner-Souplet) and $n=4$ (Souplet), and in partial ranges for $n\ge5$. Phan (2012, Conjecture C) posed the weighted Henon-Lane-Emden form $-\Delta u=|x|^Av^p$, $-\Delta v=|x|^Bu^q$ for $A,B>-2$, with subcritical region $\frac{n+A}{p+1}+\frac{n+B}{q+1}>n-2$, and Huang and Zou stated it for all real weights with solutions continuous at the origin. Is there no positive entire solution throughout the subcritical region, in every dimension?
problems.posedBy: Lane-Emden conjecture: Liouville literature of the 1990s (Mitidieri 1993, 1996; Serrin and Zou 1996); weighted form: Phan (2012), Conjecture C; Huang and Zou (2026), Conjecture B
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites Mitidieri (1993, 1996), Serrin-Zou (1996) and Souplet's 'proof of the Lane-Emden conjecture in four space dimensions' (2009) but does not say who first stated the unweighted conjecture; Phan's weighted Conjecture C dates from 2012 (arXiv 2011).
problems.resultNote: Claims Theorem 1.1: for every $n\ge2$, $p,q>0$ and $A,B\in\mathbb R$ with $\frac{n+A}{p+1}+\frac{n+B}{q+1}>n-2$, the Henon-Lane-Emden system has no positive solution continuous at the origin and $C^2$ elsewhere, with no condition at infinity. Corollary 1.2 is the unweighted Lane-Emden conjecture; with Bidaut-Veron and Giacomini's radial existence theorem this gives Phan's Conjecture C in full for $n\ge3$, $A,B>-2$, and Huang-Zou's Conjecture B. It does NOT classify solutions on the critical hyperbola beyond the cited radial existence, and treats only positive (not sign-changing) solutions.

problems.name: The scalar-curvature extension conjecture for Ricci flow in all dimensions
problems.statement: A smooth Ricci flow $\partial_tg=-2\mathrm{Ric}$ on a closed manifold extends past a finite time unless the full curvature becomes unbounded (Hamilton), and a Ricci bound suffices (Sesum). The scalar-curvature extension conjecture asks whether scalar curvature alone detects singularities: is it true that every finite-time singularity of a Ricci flow on a closed manifold of dimension at least four has unbounded scalar curvature, i.e. does $\sup_{M\times[0,T)}|R|<\infty$ always allow the flow to be extended past $T$?
problems.posedBy: Stated as open in R. H. Bamler, Convergence of Ricci flows with bounded scalar curvature, Ann. of Math. 188 (2018), p. 756; known cases surveyed by C. Li and Y. Li (2026)
problems.ageNote: The manuscripts cite the conjecture from Bamler (2018) and a 2026 survey without naming who first posed it or when; it was known for Type I flows (Enders-Muller-Topping 2011) and Kahler-Ricci flow (Zhang 2010).
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for some $q\ge10$ there is a smooth Ricci flow on the closed manifold $S^2\times S^{q+1}$ with $\sup|R|<\infty$ and $\max_M|\mathrm{Rm}|\to\infty$ at the finite maximal time; a corollary gives two-sided power-law curvature blowup with arbitrarily large exponents in one fixed dimension. This refutes the unrestricted all-dimensions conjecture. It relies on Stolarski's construction and gives no explicit dimension; it does not touch dimension four, which the companion proves true.

problems.name: The Hellinger conjecture for Boolean functions under product noise
problems.statement: Let $X$ be uniform on $\{-1,1\}^n$, let $T_\rho$ be the noise operator with correlation $\rho\in[-1,1]$, and write $H(t)=\sqrt{1-t^2}$. Anantharam, Bogdanov, Chakrabarti, Jayram and Nair (2017) conjectured that for every Boolean $f$ with mean $m$, $H(m)-\mathbb E\,H(T_\rho f)\le1-\sqrt{1-\rho^2}$, with equality for dictators: a single coordinate maximizes the loss of Hellinger affinity. They showed it implies the Courtade-Kumar conjecture. Known results included a Gaussian-isoperimetric lower bound (Chen-Nair) and the sharp balanced low-noise consequence (Durcik-Ivanisvili-Roos-Xie). Does the Hellinger inequality hold for every Boolean function, of any bias, and every $\rho$?
problems.posedBy: Venkat Anantharam, Andrej Bogdanov, Amit Chakrabarti, T. S. Jayram and Chandra Nair (ITA Workshop manuscript, February 2017)
problems.resultNote: Claims Theorem 1.1: for every $n\ge1$, every $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ with $m=\mathbb E f$ and every $\rho\in[-1,1]$, $\sqrt{1-m^2}-\mathbb E\sqrt{1-(T_\rho f)^2}\le1-\sqrt{1-\rho^2}$, with equality for signed coordinates. By the Anantharam et al. implication it reproves the Courtade-Kumar bound (Corollary 8.1). It does NOT treat non-Boolean (soft) functions or non-uniform inputs, and its proof depends on computer-checked arithmetic certificates.

problems.name: The scalar-curvature extension conjecture for Ricci flow in dimension four
problems.statement: A smooth Ricci flow on a closed manifold can stop only if the full curvature blows up. Bamler and Zhang developed heat-kernel and compactness theory for flows with bounded scalar curvature and proved smooth extension in dimension four when $H_2(M;\mathbb F)=0$ for all fields; Simon continued such flows through orbifold limits. In dimension four: if a smooth Ricci flow on a closed four-manifold has uniformly bounded scalar curvature on $[0,T)$ with $T<\infty$, does it extend smoothly on the same manifold past $T$?
problems.posedBy: Stated as open in R. H. Bamler, Ann. of Math. 188 (2018), p. 756, with the four-dimensional theory of Bamler-Zhang (2017, 2019) and M. Simon (2020)
problems.ageNote: The manuscripts do not say when or by whom the dimension-four case was first posed; Bamler-Zhang's partial result (Adv. Math. 2017) shows it was open by then.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: a smooth Ricci flow on a closed four-manifold with $\sup_{M\times[0,T)}|R|<\infty$, $T<\infty$, extends smoothly past $T$; Corollary: at a finite maximal time $\limsup\max R=+\infty$. This removes the $H_2$ hypothesis of Bamler-Zhang and gives smooth continuation rather than an orbifold flow. The companion proves $E=o(M)$ for the renormalized Einstein-Hilbert functional on degenerating trees of Ricci-flat spaces. It is specific to dimension four; in high dimension the family's other paper shows the statement is false.

problems.name: Lichter and Schweitzer's question: does witnessed symmetric choice strictly increase the expressive power of CPT with counting?
problems.statement: Choiceless polynomial time with counting (CPT) computes invariantly with hereditarily finite sets over the input atoms and cannot choose an element of a set merely because it is nonempty. Lichter and Schweitzer introduced the extension CPT+WSC by witnessed symmetric choice: a program may pick an element of an orbit provided it constructs automorphisms certifying that the choice is symmetric, so the answer stays isomorphism invariant. In Section 7 of their paper they asked whether this extension is strictly more expressive than CPT itself. Is there a Boolean query on finite structures definable in CPT+WSC but not in CPT with counting?
problems.posedBy: Moritz Lichter and Pascal Schweitzer
problems.ageNote: Lichter and Schweitzer, Choiceless Polynomial Time with Witnessed Symmetric Choice (LICS 2022; arXiv 2205.14003, version 3, 2023), Section 7, cited by the manuscript.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: over a vocabulary of eight binary relations there is a CPT+WSC sentence with a single WSC operator that returns a Boolean value on every finite structure and whose true-model class is not defined by any CPT sentence, even with counting and unbounded set rank; so CPT+WSC is strictly more expressive than CPT in Lichter and Schweitzer's sense. Not shown: whether CPT+WSC captures polynomial time, or the effect of nested WSC operators, both of which the paper leaves open.

problems.name: Milne's rationality conjecture for abelian varieties
problems.field: Arithmetic geometry: Hodge classes, reduction and rational Tate classes
problems.statement: Let $A$ be an abelian variety of dimension $d$ over $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ with good reduction $A_0$ at a $p$-adic place, and $\gamma$ a rational Hodge class in $H^{2r}(A(\mathbb C),\mathbb Q(r))$. Deligne's absolute-Hodge theorem gives compatible specializations of $\gamma$ to $\ell$-adic cohomology of $A_0$ for $\ell\ne p$ and to crystalline cohomology, but the reduction may acquire divisors that do not lift. Milne conjectured that the specialized class nevertheless behaves rationally, which he showed equivalent (for CM abelian varieties) to the existence of a good theory of rational Tate classes. For every list of divisors $D_1,\dots,D_{d-r}$ on $A_0$, is the intersection number of the specialized $\gamma$ with $D_1\cdots D_{d-r}$ one and the same rational number in every $\ell$-adic and in the crystalline realization?
problems.posedBy: J. S. Milne (weak form in his 2000 Langlands-Rapoport notes; pairing form in 2007 AIM notes and Conjecture 4.1 of Rational Tate classes, Mosc. Math. J. 2009)
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites a weak-rationality formulation in Milne's April 2000 notes (Conjecture 6.1(A)) and the pairing formulation in his July 2007 AIM notes and his 2009 paper (Conjecture 4.1). Year is the earliest cited form.
problems.resultNote: Claims Theorem 1.1: for every abelian variety over $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ with good reduction at a $p$-adic place, every residue characteristic $p$ including $2$, every rational Hodge class $\gamma$ of codimension $r$ and every divisors $D_1,\dots,D_{d-r}$ on the reduction, the $\ell$-adic traces ($\ell\ne p$) and the crystalline trace of $\gamma_0\cdot D_1\cdots D_{d-r}$ equal one rational number. Also claims each specialized Hodge class lies in one fixed good theory of rational Tate classes, and (using the CM Hodge theorem) is represented by a rational algebraic cycle in all realizations. It does not prove the Hodge or Tate conjecture for general abelian varieties.

problems.name: Derandomization of logarithmic space: is L = RL = BPL?
problems.statement: $\mathsf L$ is the class of languages decided in deterministic logarithmic space. $\mathsf{RL}$ allows a polynomial-time logarithmic-space machine fresh random bits with one-sided error (acceptance probability $0$ on no-inputs, at least $1/2$ on yes-inputs), and $\mathsf{BPL}$ allows two-sided bounded error ($\le1/3$ versus $\ge2/3$). Aleliunas, Karp, Lipton, Lovasz and Rackoff, after giving a randomized logspace algorithm for undirected connectivity, asked whether polynomial-time randomized logarithmic space can be simulated in deterministic logarithmic space. The best unconditional results before this work were Saks-Zhou space $O(\log^{3/2}n)$, improved by Hoza to $O(\log^{3/2}n/\sqrt{\log\log n})$, and Nisan's simultaneous polynomial time with $O(\log^2n)$ space. Is $\mathsf L=\mathsf{RL}=\mathsf{BPL}$?
problems.posedBy: R. Aleliunas, R. M. Karp, R. J. Lipton, L. Lovasz and C. Rackoff (1979)
problems.ageNote: The manuscript credits Aleliunas, Karp, Lipton, Lovasz and Rackoff (FOCS 1979) with asking the question explicitly; Gill (1977) had earlier set up the theory of probabilistic machines.
problems.resultNote: Claims $\mathsf L=\mathsf{RL}=\mathsf{BPL}$: every language decided with bounded one-sided or two-sided error by a randomized machine with polynomial worst-case running time and $O(\log n)$ space is decided by a deterministic $O(\log n)$-space machine. Quantitatively, acceptance probabilities can be approximated to within $2^{-q}$ in space $O(\log(n+2)+q)$ and time $(n+2)^{O(1)}2^{O(q)}$. The method builds a hierarchy of copies of the configuration graph with a shared finite random environment and evaluates a family of $O(\log n)$-bit estimators, more than three quarters of them accurate, by exhaustive enumeration. It does not give a pseudorandom generator with logarithmic seed, and it does not address randomized logspace without a polynomial time bound.
problems.aiRole: The release README says the manuscripts were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model, which was posed some 4,000 open research problems during an evaluation, with the vast majority of results obtained by one fixed procedure averaging about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute each. This manuscript is not among the README's named exceptions. It is credited to OpenAI with no human author named.
problems.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Theorem 1.1 was read against the posed question and states the full equality L = RL = BPL for the standard model (polynomial worst-case running time on every random tape, logarithmic space counting all live counters). Its statement was read here: for finite transition-table machines over binary words, with read-only input heads, binary work tapes, one coin bit per step and space at most $c\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil$ on every coin tape, the classes L, RL (polynomial clock, $\ge1/2$ versus $0$) and BPL ($\ge2/3$ versus $\le1/3$) satisfy L = RL and RL = BPL. The paper concerns polynomial-time randomized logspace; it does not claim that randomized logspace machines without a time bound are derandomized.

problems.name: Hoering's conjecture: tangent-bundle summands on rationally connected manifolds are integrable
problems.field: Algebraic geometry; rationally connected varieties, foliations
problems.statement: Let $X$ be a smooth rationally connected projective complex manifold with a holomorphic splitting $T_X=E_1\oplus E_2$ into positive-rank subbundles. Hoering (2007) proved that if one summand is integrable then $X\cong X_1\times X_2$ compatibly, and conjectured (2008, Conjecture 1.2) that at least one summand is always integrable; Campana-Peternell had settled small ranks on Fano manifolds, and Hoering (2026, Conjecture 1.5) states that both summands are integrable in the smooth rationally connected case, after proving it for Fano type. Is every summand of such a splitting integrable, so that $X$ is a compatible product?
problems.posedBy: A. Hoering, The structure of uniruled manifolds with split tangent bundle, Osaka J. Math. 45 (2008), Conjecture 1.2; both-summand form: Hoering, arXiv:2602.15427 (2026), Conjecture 1.5
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: on a smooth connected rationally connected projective manifold of dimension at least two, both summands of every holomorphic splitting $T_X=E_1\oplus E_2$ into positive-rank subbundles are integrable. Corollary 1.2 (with Hoering's 2007 product theorem): $X\cong X_1\times X_2$ with $E_i=\mathrm{pr}_i^*T_{X_i}$. Smoothness is needed (Hoering 2026 gives a singular counterexample); splittings with more than two summands are not treated.

problems.name: The Eisenbud-Green-Harris conjecture over fields of characteristic zero
problems.statement: Let $S=k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ be a standard graded polynomial ring over a field, let $2\le a_1\le\cdots\le a_c$, and let $I$ be a homogeneous ideal containing a regular sequence $f_1,\ldots,f_c$ with $\deg f_i=a_i$. Eisenbud, Green and Harris, from their work on higher Castelnuovo theory, proposed that the pure powers $x_1^{a_1},\ldots,x_c^{a_c}$ can replace the regular sequence without changing the Hilbert function: there should be a monomial ideal containing $(x_1^{a_1},\ldots,x_c^{a_c})$, indeed a lex-plus-powers ideal, with the same Hilbert function as $I$. Known cases required fast-growing degrees or regular sequences of special form. Does every such $I$ have the Hilbert function of a lex-plus-powers ideal?
problems.posedBy: David Eisenbud, Mark Green and Joe Harris, Higher Castelnuovo theory, Asterisque 218 (1993), Section 4
problems.ageNote: The conjecture is usually stated over an arbitrary field; this entry covers characteristic zero, which is all the manuscripts claim.
problems.resultNote: Claims the Eisenbud-Green-Harris conjecture over every field of characteristic zero, for homogeneous regular sequences of any positive length with all degrees at least two and with no growth condition on the degrees, via commuting division-coefficient linear forms whose ordered monomials form a basis of the whole polynomial algebra. It does NOT treat positive characteristic. The Betti-number strengthening (lex-plus-powers) is the companion's result, listed separately.

problems.name: The Unique Games Conjecture
problems.statement: A Unique Games instance is a graph with a finite label set $K$ and, on each edge, a permutation of $K$; a labeling satisfies an edge when the label at one endpoint is the image of the other endpoint's label under that permutation. Khot (2002) conjectured that for every $\varepsilon,\delta>0$ there is a finite alphabet size $q=q(\varepsilon,\delta)$ such that it is NP-hard to distinguish instances over $q$ labels in which a $1-\varepsilon$ fraction of the constraints can be satisfied from instances in which at most a $\delta$ fraction can. Under this hypothesis, optimal inapproximability was known for Max-Cut (the Goemans-Williamson ratio), Vertex Cover (factor $2$) and many other problems, but only conditionally. Is the Unique Games Conjecture true?
problems.posedBy: Subhash Khot, On the Power of Unique 2-Prover 1-Round Games, STOC 2002
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every fixed $\varepsilon,\delta\in(0,1/2)$ there are $s\ge1$ and a deterministic polynomial-time reduction from 3SAT to explicit unweighted, simple bipartite Unique Games over $K=\mathbb F_2^s$ whose constraints are translations $a(v)=a(u)+c_e$, with value at least $1-\varepsilon$ on satisfiable formulas and at most $\delta$ on unsatisfiable ones. This is the conjecture in its usual edge-value form. The route keeps the Barak-Kothari-Steurer degree-two matrix shortcode and its Khot-Minzer-Safra inverse theorem and changes the noise through a nonlinear map to push completeness to $1-\varepsilon$. Section 7 transfers known UG-hardness reductions (cut, covering, CSP, ordering, deletion, clustering) to NP-hardness; those reductions are credited to their authors. Companion manuscripts give direct NP-hardness proofs for Max-Cut beyond $\alpha_{GW}$, Vertex Cover below factor $2$, and every constant factor for Min-UnCut and directed feedback vertex set.

problems.name: The Sandier-Serfaty conjecture: the triangular lattice minimizes planar Coulomb renormalized energy
problems.field: Coulomb gases; renormalized energy of Ginzburg-Landau vortex patterns
problems.statement: Sandier and Serfaty introduced a renormalized energy $W$ for infinite configurations of planar point charges against a uniform neutralizing background, defined through curl-free fields $E$ with $\operatorname{div}E=2\pi(\nu-m)$, the logarithmic self-energy removed and energy taken per unit area. It governs microscopic vortex patterns in the Ginzburg-Landau model and limits of two-dimensional Coulomb gases. They proved that a minimum exists, that it is approximated by periodic fields, and that among Bravais lattices the triangular lattice is optimal (Theorems 1 and 2 of their 2012 paper). Their Conjecture 1 asks: is the triangular lattice the minimizer of $W$ over the full admissible class of fields, not only among lattices?
problems.posedBy: Etienne Sandier and Sylvia Serfaty (Conjecture 1, Comm. Math. Phys. 313, 2012)
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every admissible curl-free field with unit background, $W(E)\ge W(E_\triangle)$, and $\inf W=W(E_\triangle)$ is finite, with no separation, periodicity or Voronoi assumption on the competitor. Theorem 1.2 gives the finite version: on every square torus with $n\ge2$ points the renormalized energy is at least $nW(E_\triangle)$. The proof builds one trial potential from Voronoi sectors on a minimizing torus configuration, with an exact identity leaving a nonnegative square, plus interval-arithmetic estimates. It does not classify minimizers (compact changes keep the energy per area) and does not treat the Riesz or higher-dimensional cases.

problems.name: The Solomon-Yau least-volume conjecture for minimal hypersurfaces of round spheres
problems.field: Minimal hypersurfaces in spheres; volume gaps
problems.statement: The equator is the least-volume closed minimal hypersurface of the unit sphere $S^{m+1}$. The minimal Clifford products $S^k(\sqrt{k/m})\times S^{m-k}(\sqrt{(m-k)/m})$, $1\le k<m$, are the natural next examples; let $a_m$ be the least of their volumes. Cheng, Li and Yau (1984) proved a dimension-dependent volume gap above the equator, and for $m=2$ the sharp bound $2\pi^2$ follows from the Marques-Neves proof of the Willmore conjecture. Yau's problem list (Problem 31) asks for the next volume level, and Ge and Li (2021, Conjecture 1.12(ii)) state it as the Solomon-Yau conjecture. For every $m\ge2$, does every closed minimal hypersurface of $S^{m+1}$ that is not totally geodesic have volume at least $a_m$?
problems.posedBy: S.-T. Yau, Open problems in geometry (1994), Problem 31; formulated as the Solomon-Yau conjecture by J. Ge and F. Li (2021, Conjecture 1.12(ii))
problems.ageNote: 1994 is the year of the Yau problem list as cited by the manuscript; the name credits B. Solomon as well, without a separate citation in the manuscript.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for $m\ge2$, a closed connected smooth minimal immersion $F:M^m\to S^{m+1}$ with non-totally-geodesic image has $\mathrm{Vol}(M,F^*g)\ge a_m$, attained by a minimizing Clifford product. Intermediate results: $\int_\Sigma|A|^2\ge m|\Sigma|$ for closed embedded non-equatorial minimal hypersurfaces (the lower-bound part of Perdomo's conjecture, also in Nifa 2026) and Clifford rigidity at index $m+3$. It does not classify hypersurfaces at volume $a_m$ beyond attainment, and says nothing about higher codimension or the next volume levels.

problems.name: Hadwiger's Conjecture
problems.statement: For a graph $G$ let $h(G)$, the Hadwiger number, be the largest $t$ such that $K_t$ is a minor of $G$. Hadwiger (1943) conjectured that every graph with no $K_{t+1}$ minor is $t$-colourable, that is, $\chi(G)\le h(G)$. It was known for $t\le5$ (Hadwiger and Dirac for $t=3$, Wagner plus the Four Colour Theorem for $t=4$, Robertson-Seymour-Thomas for $t=5$). The special case of graphs with independence number at most two (equivalently, every such $m$-vertex graph has a $K_{\lceil m/2\rceil}$ minor, Plummer-Stiebitz-Toft) and the fractional weakening $\chi_f(G)\le h(G)$ discussed by Reed and Seymour (1998) were also open. Does every finite graph satisfy $\chi(G)\le h(G)$?
problems.posedBy: Hugo Hadwiger, Uber eine Klassifikation der Streckenkomplexe, Vierteljahrsschr. Naturforsch. Ges. Zurich 88 (1943); fractional weakening discussed by Reed and Seymour (1998)
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there are arbitrarily large $m$ and $m$-vertex graphs with $\alpha(G)\le2$ and connected-matching number below $m/100$. With the counting bound $h(G)\le(|V(G)|+4\,\mathrm{cm}(G)+2)/3$, Corollary 1.2 gives $h(G)<26m/75+2/3<m/2\le\chi_f(G)\le\chi(G)$. So Hadwiger's conjecture fails, already in the case $\alpha\le2$ and even for fractional colouring, with $\chi/h$ above about $1.44$ in the limit. The graphs are complements of a triangle-free hole relation built from tensor frames over $\mathbb F_2$, so $\alpha\le2$; the four-hole conflicts that kill large connected matchings are forced by a distribution theorem and a container argument. It does not say anything about small $t$, and it does not refute linear bounds $\chi\le C\,h$, which the companion list-colouring paper proves.

problems.name: Constant-competitive single-sample prophet inequalities on general matroids
problems.field: Online algorithms; prophet inequalities and matroid secretary problems
problems.statement: In a matroid prophet inequality, independent nonnegative values $V_e$ on the elements of a known matroid $M$ arrive one at a time and an online rule must irrevocably accept or reject each, keeping the accepted set independent; it is compared with $\mathbb E[\mathrm{OPT}_M(V)]$. With known distributions, Kleinberg and Weinberg (2012) achieve 1/2. Azar, Kleinberg and Weinberg (2014) introduced the limited-information model in which the rule only gets one independent sample from each unknown distribution, and related it to order-oblivious matroid secretary algorithms. For general matroids only a doubly logarithmic loss in the rank was known with one sample (Feldman-Svensson-Zenklusen), and constant guarantees needed polylogarithmically many samples (Fu et al. 2024). Is there a single-sample rule achieving a constant fraction of the expected offline optimum on every matroid?
problems.posedBy: Azar, Kleinberg and Weinberg (SODA 2014) introduced single-sample prophet inequalities; Fu, Lu, Tang, Wu, Wu and Zhang (EC 2024) describe the general-matroid single-sample question as open
problems.ageNote: The manuscript does not quote an explicit statement of the question. 2014 is the Azar-Kleinberg-Weinberg framework it cites; the abstract of Fu et al. (2024, also cited) records that no constant-factor single-sample algorithm was known for general matroids and ties the question to the matroid secretary conjecture.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there is a measurable online rule, independent of the value laws, which for every finite matroid and every independent family of samples $S_e$ and values $V_e$ with common laws and $\mathbb E[\mathrm{OPT}_M(V)]<\infty$ accepts an independent set with expected value at least $2^{-310}\mathbb E[\mathrm{OPT}_M(V)]$, against an adversary that chooses the order after seeing samples, values and the full random seed (the proof gives $2^{-293}$). A corollary gives a constant-competitive matroid secretary rule against adversarial reordering after a random observation prefix. The constant is tiny and no efficient implementation is asserted. Recent preprints (Singla 2026, Huang 2026) settle the random-order matroid secretary problem; the paper notes those keep uniformly random arrivals and do not give this result.

problems.name: The higher-dimensional Erdos distinct-distances conjecture
problems.statement: For a finite set $P\subset\mathbb R^d$ let $\Delta(P)=\{|p-q|:p\ne q\in P\}$. Erdos introduced the distinct-distances problem in 1946; the integer grid $\{1,\ldots,t\}^d$ shows that $n$ points can determine only $O(n^{2/d})$ distances when $d\ge3$. Known lower bounds fell short of this exponent: $n^{0.5643}$ and $n^{2/d-2/(d(d+2))}$ (Solymosi-Vu), $n^{3/5}$ up to logarithms in $\mathbb R^3$ via Guth-Katz, and $n^{2/3-o(1)}$ in $\mathbb R^3$ (Tidor-Yu-Zakharov). For every fixed $d\ge3$, is there $c_d>0$ such that every set of $n\ge2$ points in $\mathbb R^d$ determines at least $c_dn^{2/d}$ distinct distances?
problems.posedBy: Paul Erdos (1946, 'On sets of distances of n points'); the higher-dimensional form as recorded by Bardwell-Evans-Sheffer and Tidor-Yu-Zakharov
problems.ageNote: The manuscript says Erdos introduced the problem in 1946 and cites Bardwell-Evans-Sheffer (2019) and Tidor-Yu-Zakharov (2026) for the higher-dimensional conjecture; it does not quote the higher-dimensional form from the 1946 paper itself.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every integer $d\ge3$ there is $c_d>0$ such that every set of $n\ge2$ distinct points in $\mathbb R^d$ determines at least $c_dn^{2/d}$ distinct distances, matching the integer grid up to the constant. No dependence of $c_d$ on $d$ is made explicit, nothing is claimed for pinned distances (many distances from one point), and the planar problem, whose conjectured order is $n/\sqrt{\log n}$, is untouched beyond reusing the Guth-Katz bound. Priority: Aksoy Yazici earlier claimed the same constant-factor bound in all dimensions $d\ge3$, but withdrew the manuscript because a step was wrong; it is not an opposite claim.

problems.name: Zarankiewicz's crossing-number conjecture (Turan's brick factory problem)
problems.statement: Turan's brick factory problem (1944) asks for the least number of crossings in a plane drawing of the complete bipartite graph $K_{m,n}$, crossings counted as points with edges drawn as simple arcs. Zarankiewicz (1954/55) gave a drawing with $\lfloor\frac m2\rfloor\lfloor\frac{m-1}2\rfloor\lfloor\frac n2\rfloor\lfloor\frac{n-1}2\rfloor$ crossings and a proof of optimality that turned out to contain a gap, leaving the formula as a conjecture. Kleitman proved it when $\min(m,n)\le6$, Woodall checked $K_{7,7}$ and $K_{7,9}$, and flag algebras gave about $0.91$ of the value asymptotically. Is $\mathrm{cr}(K_{m,n})=\lfloor\frac m2\rfloor\lfloor\frac{m-1}2\rfloor\lfloor\frac n2\rfloor\lfloor\frac{n-1}2\rfloor$ for all positive $m,n$?
problems.posedBy: Paul Turan (brick factory problem, 1944, recounted in 1977); formula and flawed proof by Kazimierz Zarankiewicz (Fund. Math. 41, 1954/55)
problems.ageNote: Turan's 1977 note dates the problem to his 1944 labour-camp brickyard. Zarankiewicz's paper is cited by the manuscript as 1955 (Fund. Math. volume 41); the gap in his argument made the formula a conjecture.
problems.resultNote: Claims $\mathrm{cr}(K_{m,n})=\lfloor\frac m2\rfloor\lfloor\frac{m-1}2\rfloor\lfloor\frac n2\rfloor\lfloor\frac{n-1}2\rfloor$ for all positive $m,n$. The lower bound comes from a linear-algebra inequality $\sum_{i,j}\dim(U_i\cap V_j)\le\lfloor m^2/4\rfloor N$ for subspaces with $U_i\cap V_i=0$, proved by interpolation, applied through signed intersections of cycles; Zarankiewicz's drawing gives the upper bound. Crossings are counted as points. It does NOT address rectilinear, pair or odd crossing numbers of $K_{m,n}$.

problems.name: Banach's problem: a probability-preserving transformation with simple Lebesgue spectrum
problems.field: Ergodic theory; spectral theory of measure-preserving maps
problems.statement: For an invertible measure-preserving transformation $T$ of a probability space, the Koopman operator $U_Tg=g\circ T$ is unitary on $L^2$ and leaves the constants invariant. Banach's problem, in its probability-preserving form, asks whether some $T$ has simple Lebesgue spectrum on the orthogonal complement $L^2_0$ of the constants: equivalently, whether there is $f\in L^2_0$ whose iterates $\{f\circ T^n\}_{n\in\mathbb Z}$ form an orthonormal basis of $L^2_0$. Rokhlin (1949) asked for ergodic automorphisms with simple, or at least finite-multiplicity, Lebesgue spectrum. Known constructions gave Lebesgue components, finite-measure flows, simple non-Lebesgue spectrum, or infinite-measure examples, but not this. Does such a probability-preserving transformation exist?
problems.posedBy: Stefan Banach (question recorded by Ulam); the probability-space form was asked by V. A. Rokhlin
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites Rokhlin (1949, Section 4, no. 7) for the probability-space question and Ulam's 1960 collection (Section 6, p. 76) for the question attributed to Banach, which it describes as a distinct real-line formulation. The date of Banach's own question is not given.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there are a $C^\infty$ volume-preserving diffeomorphism $T$ of $\mathbb T^3$ and a real $f\in L^2_0(\mathbb T^3)$ such that $\{f\circ T^n\}_{n\in\mathbb Z}$ is an orthonormal basis of $L^2_0$; hence $T$ is ergodic and $U_T$ on $L^2_0$ is unitarily equivalent to multiplication by $w$ on $L^2(S^1)$. Mixing, zero entropy and zero Lyapunov exponents follow; mixing of all orders uses a separate multiple-mixing manuscript. The manuscript states this is distinct from the historical real-line question attributed to Banach and does not address that formulation; $f$ is only $L^2$, not smooth.

problems.name: Hochster's small Cohen-Macaulay module conjecture for complete local domains
problems.statement: A small (maximal) Cohen-Macaulay module over a Noetherian local ring $(R,\mathfrak m)$ is a nonzero finitely generated module $M$ with $\mathrm{depth}\,M=\dim R$. Hochster conjectured in the early 1970s that every complete Noetherian local domain has one. It holds in dimension at most two, and in some graded positive-characteristic cases in dimension three; big Cohen-Macaulay modules and algebras exist in all characteristics, but they are not finitely generated, and the existence question was open even for local rings of affine three-dimensional domains over algebraically closed fields. Does every complete Noetherian local domain admit a small Cohen-Macaulay module?
problems.posedBy: Melvin Hochster

problems.name: Naor's sublinear-dimension question for finite subsets of Lp, 1 < p < infinity, p not 2
problems.statement: The Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma embeds every $n$-point subset of Hilbert space into $O(\log n)$ dimensions with distortion $1+\varepsilon$, and Johnson and Lindenstrauss (1984, Problem 3) asked what analogues hold in other Banach spaces. In $L_1$ polynomial dimension is necessary (Brinkman-Charikar), and Ball's exact bound for $L_p$ is $\binom n2$ coordinates. Naor (ICM 2018) remarked that for no fixed $p\in[1,\infty)\setminus\{2\}$ was it even known whether every $n$-point subset of $\ell_p$ embeds with bounded distortion into a normed space of dimension $o(n)$. For fixed $p\ne2$ and distortion $D$, can every $n$-point subset of $L_p$ be embedded with distortion $D$ in dimension $o(n)$?
problems.posedBy: Assaf Naor (after William B. Johnson and Joram Lindenstrauss)
problems.ageNote: Naor, Metric dimension reduction: a snapshot of the Ribe program, Proc. ICM 2018, remark after Question 13; the underlying question is Johnson-Lindenstrauss (1984), Problem 3.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for fixed $1<p<\infty$, $p\ne2$, and $D>1$, every $n$-point subset of any $L_p$ embeds with distortion $D$ into $\ell_p^d$ (same exponent, coordinate target, nonlinear map) with $d\le\exp(C_{p,D}(\log n)^{\gamma(p)})=n^{o(1)}$, where $\gamma(p)=2-p$ for $p<2$ and $1-2/p$ for $p>2$; exact embeddings need dimension of order $n^2$. This answers the $o(n)$ question for every $p\in(1,\infty)\setminus\{2\}$. Not shown: $p=1$; Naor's Question 13 itself ($O(\log n)$ dimension in some normed space), which Naor-Ren's 2026 lower bound already excludes for $\ell_p^d$ targets when $p>2$; optimal exponents; an efficient algorithm.
