problems.name: A power saving over the Spencer-Szemerédi-Trotter n^(4/3) bound for planar unit distances (Erdős Problem 90)
problems.field: Combinatorial geometry; unit distances and incidences
problems.statement: Let $u(n)$ be the largest number of pairs at distance exactly $1$ among $n$ points of the Euclidean plane. Erdős introduced the problem in 1946, showed $u(n)\ge n^{1+c/\log\log n}$ and conjectured $u(n)=n^{1+o(1)}$ (erdosproblems.com Problem 90). Spencer, Szemerédi and Trotter proved $u(n)=O(n^{4/3})$ in 1984, and no better exponent was known; Valtr's metric with $n^{4/3}$ unit pairs shows that an improvement must use a special feature of the Euclidean metric, as the problem record notes. In 2026 an OpenAI construction disproved Erdős's conjecture with $u(n)\ge n^{1+\varepsilon}$ for infinitely many $n$ (Sawin: exponent $1.0141$). Can the upper exponent $4/3$ be lowered by a fixed amount: is $u(n)=O(n^{4/3-\delta})$ for some absolute $\delta>0$?
problems.posedBy: Paul Erdős (problem, 1946); the 4/3 upper bound is due to Spencer, Szemerédi and Trotter (1984)
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites Erdős (Amer. Math. Monthly 1946) for the problem and Spencer-Szemerédi-Trotter (1984) for the exponent 4/3, and phrases its result as answering whether that exponent can be lowered, without a separate posing reference. The erdosproblems.com record of Problem 90 names O(n^(4/3)) as the best known upper bound.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there are absolute constants $0<C<\infty$ and $1\le\beta<4/3$ such that every set of $n$ points in the Euclidean plane has at most $Cn^\beta$ unordered pairs at distance $1$, for every $n$. This is the first improvement of the 1984 exponent $4/3$. It leaves a gap to the lower bound $n^{1.0141}$ (Sawin) from the 2026 disproof of Erdős's $n^{1+o(1)}$ conjecture, and $\delta=4/3-\beta$ is not made explicit. Not addressed: distinct distances, higher dimensions, or other norms (for Valtr's metric $4/3$ is sharp).

problems.name: The classification of closed Einstein four-manifolds with positive sectional curvature
problems.field: Riemannian geometry; Einstein metrics in dimension four
problems.statement: A Riemannian metric is Einstein if $\mathrm{Ric}=\lambda g$. The round $S^4$, the round $\mathbb{RP}^4$ and the Fubini-Study $\mathbb{CP}^2$ are closed Einstein four-manifolds with strictly positive sectional curvature. Yang (2000, Conjecture 1) conjectured that these are the only ones. Earlier results needed extra hypotheses: Berger's strict quarter pinching (1961), quantitative pinching bounds of Yang, Costa and Cao-Tran, Gursky-LeBrun's nonzero positive-definite intersection form, and in 2026 topological conditions of Cheng ($\chi\le3$) and Gursky-Malchiodi ($2\chi-3|\tau|\le4$). problems.name: The Nakayama conjecture on dominant dimension
problems.field: Representation theory of algebras; homological conjectures
problems.statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a finite-dimensional algebra over a field with minimal injective resolution $0\to\Lambda\to I^0\to I^1\to\cdots$. Its dominant dimension is infinite when every $I^j$ is projective. The classical Nakayama conjecture asserts that infinite dominant dimension forces $\Lambda$ to be self-injective. Its relatives are the generalized Nakayama conjecture of Auslander and Reiten (every indecomposable injective occurs as a summand of some $I^j$), the strong Nakayama conjecture (a module $V$ with $\mathrm{Ext}^i(V,\Lambda)=0$ for all $i\ge0$ is zero), the Auslander-Gorenstein conjecture and the Wakamatsu tilting conjecture; the finitistic dimension conjecture implies the classical one. Must a finite-dimensional algebra of infinite dominant dimension be self-injective?
problems.posedBy: Tadasi Nakayama (classical Nakayama conjecture); formulations recalled from Y. Zhang (2018) in the manuscript
problems.ageNote: The manuscript does not cite Nakayama's original paper. It recalls the formulations from Zhang (Algebra Colloquium 2018) and cites Mueller (1968) for the dominant-dimension connection; the conjecture is usually dated to Nakayama in the late 1950s, which the curator should confirm from the original.
problems.resultNote: Claims Corollary 1.2: for the symmetric pair $(A,M)$ of the Tachikawa counterexample and every field extension $K$ of $\mathbb F_2(q,H_1,H_2)$, the finite-dimensional algebra $\Gamma_K=\mathrm{End}(A_K\oplus M_K)^{op}$ has all injective terms projective but infinite self-injective dimension, has a nonzero simple $S$ with $\mathrm{Ext}^i(S,\Gamma_K)=0$ for all $i\ge0$, and has a projective-injective Wakamatsu tilting module that is not tilting. Hence the classical, generalized and strong Nakayama conjectures, the Auslander-Gorenstein conjecture and the Wakamatsu tilting conjecture all fail. Corollary 1.3: $\Gamma_K$ has infinite little and big finitistic dimension. It does NOT give characteristic-zero examples.

The manuscript is credited to OpenAI with no human author named. The Nakayama-type counterexamples are Corollary 1.2 of the Tachikawa manuscript, obtained from its symmetric counterexample through the classical Mueller correspondence between pairs (A, M) and algebras of large dominant dimension.

problems.name: The Blaschke conjecture: Blaschke manifolds are compact rank-one symmetric spaces
problems.field: Riemannian geometry; manifolds all of whose geodesics are closed
problems.statement: A connected closed Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$ of positive dimension is a Blaschke manifold if its injectivity radius equals its diameter, so every unit-speed geodesic minimizes up to the diameter. Round spheres, the real, complex and quaternionic projective spaces and the Cayley plane with their standard metrics are Blaschke. Blaschke posed the problem for surfaces (settled by Green, 1963); the sphere and real projective cases were settled by Berger, Kazdan, Weinstein and Yang, and Bott-Samelson theory fixes the cohomology type, but the metric question was open for the complex, quaternionic and Cayley types. Is every Blaschke manifold isometric, up to scaling, to a compact rank-one symmetric space?
problems.posedBy: Wilhelm Blaschke (surfaces); general metric form in Arthur Besse's monograph (1978)
problems.ageNote: Blaschke's Vorlesungen uber Differentialgeometrie I (1921) for surfaces; the higher-dimensional metric conjecture is as described in Besse, Manifolds all of whose geodesics are closed (1978), with McKay's 2016 progress summary, all cited by the manuscript.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: if $(M,g)$ is connected, closed, smooth, of positive dimension, with $\mathrm{inj}(M,g)=\mathrm{diam}(M,g)$, then $(M,g)$ is isometric up to scale to a round sphere, a standard real, complex or quaternionic projective space, or the Cayley plane. Theorem 1.2 gives $\mathrm{Vol}(M,g)\ge\mathrm{Vol}(M_0,g_0)$ against the model at equal diameter, with equality only for isometry; the upper bound in quaternionic dimension $4r$, $r\ge2$, is proved from characteristic classes and the geodesic space. It does not treat the weaker Besse-type questions on manifolds all of whose geodesics are closed without the Blaschke condition (SC or P-manifolds in general).

problems.name: The Falconer distance conjecture
problems.statement: For $E\subset\mathbb R^d$ let $\Delta(E)=\{|x-y|:x,y\in E\}$ be its distance set. Falconer (1985) showed that $\dim_H E>(d+1)/2$ forces $\Delta(E)$ to have positive Lebesgue measure, and lattice-type examples show the threshold cannot go below $d/2$. Later thresholds were $4/3$ in the plane (Wolff), $d/2+1/3$ (Erdogan), $9/5$ in $\mathbb R^3$ and further improvements via decoupling (Du, Guth, Ou, Wang, Wilson, Zhang; Du, Zhang), and $5/4$ in the plane for pinned distances (Guth, Iosevich, Ou, Wang). Does every compact $E\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$, with $\dim_H E>d/2$ have $\mathcal L^1(\Delta(E))>0$?
problems.posedBy: Kenneth Falconer, On the Hausdorff dimensions of distance sets, Mathematika 32 (1985)
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every integer $d\ge2$ and every compact $E\subset\mathbb R^d$ with $\dim_H E>d/2$, $\mathcal L^1(\Delta(E))>0$. No regularity beyond the strict dimension bound is assumed. The paper does NOT treat the endpoint $\dim_H E=d/2$, does NOT prove a pinned version (some $y$ with $\mathcal L^1(\Delta_y(E))>0$) at the threshold $d/2$. It states that it uses no decoupling theorem and no earlier distance theorem at an improved threshold; it does use the Orponen-Shmerkin incidence theorem.

problems.name: The finitistic dimension conjecture for finite-dimensional algebras
problems.field: Representation theory of finite-dimensional algebras; homological algebra
problems.statement: For a finite-dimensional algebra $A$ over a field, the little finitistic dimension is $\mathrm{findim}\,A=\sup\{\mathrm{pd}_AN: N\text{ finitely generated},\ \mathrm{pd}_AN<\infty\}$. The finitistic dimension conjecture, publicized by Bass, asserts that $\mathrm{findim}\,A<\infty$ for every finite-dimensional (more generally, Artin) algebra. It was proved for monomial algebras, radical-cube-zero algebras and representation dimension at most three (Igusa-Todorov), and it implies several other homological conjectures; Huisgen-Zimmermann showed the little and big dimensions can differ but both stayed finite in all examples. Is the little finitistic dimension of every finite-dimensional algebra finite?
problems.posedBy: Hyman Bass (publicized the finitistic dimension questions)
problems.ageNote: The manuscript says the finitistic-dimension questions 'were publicized by Bass in 1960' (Bass, Finitistic dimension and a homological generalization of semi-primary rings, Trans. AMS 1960).
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there is a finite-dimensional complex algebra $A$ with, for each $m\ge1$, a finite-dimensional left module $N_m$ with $2m-2\le\mathrm{pd}\,N_m<\infty$; so $\mathrm{findim}\,A=\infty$ and the big finitistic dimension is infinite too, refuting the conjecture for Artin algebras. By Rickard's theorem injective left $A$-modules do not generate the derived category. Corollary (left-right asymmetry): an algebra $\Lambda$ with both finitistic dimensions infinite on the left and zero on the right. The construction passes through a finitely presented group algebra with Abels-type central involutions. A companion OpenAI manuscript (Tachikawa family) independently gives characteristic-two examples.

problems.name: Sinai's conjecture: positive metric entropy of the standard map for a positive-measure set of parameters
problems.statement: The standard map $f_k(x,y)=(x+y+k\sin(2\pi x),\,y+k\sin(2\pi x))$ on $\mathbb T^2$ preserves area $m$ and was introduced by Chirikov as a model of conservative chaos. For large $k$ it has hyperbolic sets (Duarte), full-dimension transitive sets for residual parameters (Gorodetski) and positive topological entropy (Oliveira), but also elliptic islands, and none of this gives positive area. Sinai's conjecture, in the formulation of Berger and Turaev (2019, Conjecture 0.4), asks: is the metric entropy $h_m(f_k)$, equivalently a positive Lyapunov exponent on positive area, positive for a set of parameters $k$ of positive Lebesgue measure?
problems.posedBy: Yakov Sinai; the manuscript cites the formulation of P. Berger and D. Turaev, On Herman's positive entropy conjecture, Adv. Math. 349 (2019), Conjecture 0.4
problems.ageNote: The manuscript attributes the conjecture to Sinai but cites no work of Sinai or year for it; it cites Berger and Turaev (2019) for the formulation and Obata (2021) for the large-parameter form. The standard map itself is cited from Chirikov (1979).
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there is $k_0>0$ with $h_m(f_k)>0$ for every $k\ge k_0$; equivalently, by Pesin's formula, the top Lyapunov exponent is positive on a set of positive area. Corollary 1.2: a positive-area ergodic component with nonzero exponents that splits into finitely many cyclic Bernoulli pieces. It does NOT claim ergodicity of area, positive exponents almost everywhere, a uniform lower bound on the entropy, or any explicit $k_0$, and says nothing about small or moderate $k$.

problems.name: The free group factor isomorphism problem
problems.field: Operator algebras: II_1 factors and free probability
problems.statement: For a discrete group $G$ let $L(G)=\lambda(G)''$ be its group von Neumann algebra on $\ell^2(G)$, and let $\mathbb F_n$ be the free group on $n$ generators. Murray and von Neumann showed the free group factors are not hyperfinite but could not distinguish their ranks. Voiculescu, Radulescu and Dykema built interpolated factors $L(\mathbb F_r)$, $1<r\le\infty$, and proved they are either all isomorphic or pairwise non-isomorphic. Are $L(\mathbb F_m)$ and $L(\mathbb F_n)$ isomorphic for distinct $m,n\ge 2$?
problems.posedBy: Richard V. Kadison, as credited in Dykema (1994); the factors go back to Murray and von Neumann (1943)

With the classical interpolated-factor dichotomy, all $L(\mathbb F_r)$, $1<r\le\infty$, are isomorphic and their fundamental group is $\mathbb R_{>0}$. It also shows free entropy dimension depends on the generating tuple. It does not identify $L(\mathbb F_2)$ with other non-free group factors.

problems.name: Talagrand's discrete convexity conjecture
problems.field: Probabilistic combinatorics; Bernoulli product measures and covers
problems.statement: Let $\mu_p$ be the product Bernoulli measure on subsets of $[N]$. A family $\mathcal A$ is $p$-small if there are sets $I$ with $\sum p^{|I|}\le1/2$ such that every member of $\mathcal A$ contains one of them. For a family $\mathcal D$ and an integer $k$, let $E_k(\mathcal D)$ be the sets contained in no union of $k$ members of $\mathcal D$. By analogy with his Gaussian convexity question, Talagrand (2010, Conjecture 7.1; also Research Problem 13.3.2 in his 2021 book) conjectured that a fixed number of members of a sufficiently likely family covers everything outside a $p$-small family. Is there a universal integer $k$ such that $\mu_p(\mathcal D)\ge1-1/k$ implies that $E_k(\mathcal D)$ is $p$-small, for every $N$, every $p\in(0,1)$ and every family $\mathcal D$?
problems.posedBy: Michel Talagrand (Conjecture 7.1, STOC 2010; Research Problem 13.3.2, Upper and Lower Bounds for Stochastic Processes, 2nd ed., 2021)
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: with $k=2^{75}$, for every $N\ge1$, $p\in(0,1)$ and $\mathcal D\subseteq2^{[N]}$, $\mu_p(\mathcal D)\ge1-1/k$ implies $E_k(\mathcal D)$ is $p$-small. Consequences: a containment cover for large values of positive selector processes (recovering Park-Pham's theorem), and with Li's fractional result and the companion rounding theorem, $E_2(\mathcal D)$ is $(p/C)$-small when $\mu_p(\mathcal D)>1/2$. Earlier, Hua-Song-Tudose derived a discrete statement with three unions at density $p^C$ and Park one with two unions at a $\log\log(1/p)$ loss. The constant $k$ is far from optimal and the Gaussian convexity question is a different problem.

problems.name: Goldfeld's conjecture on analytic ranks of quadratic twists
problems.field: Arithmetic of elliptic curves; arithmetic statistics
problems.statement: For an elliptic curve $E/\mathbb{Q}$ and squarefree $d$ let $E^{(d)}$ be the quadratic twist and $a(E^{(d)})=\mathrm{ord}_{s=1}L(E^{(d)},s)$ its analytic rank. Goldfeld (1979, Conjecture B) conjectured that the average analytic rank over the twist family is $1/2$; the density form predicts that analytic ranks 0 and 1 each occur for half of all twists. Known before: positive proportions for special curves (James, Vatsal, Kriz-Li for curves with a rational 3-isogeny), conditional means under GRH (Heath-Brown, Fiorilli), and Smith's theorem that 2-power Selmer coranks 0 and 1 each have density 1/2, giving Goldfeld's conjecture under BSD. For every $E/\mathbb{Q}$, do analytic ranks 0 and 1 each have density $1/2$ among the twists, and does the mean analytic rank tend to $1/2$?
problems.posedBy: Dorian Goldfeld, Conjectures on elliptic curves over quadratic fields, Number Theory Carbondale 1979, LNM 751, p. 113, Conjecture (B)
problems.resultNote: Density paper: for every $E/\mathbb{Q}$ and $j\in\{0,1\}$, the proportion of squarefree $0<|d|\le X$ with $a(E^{(d)})=j$ tends to $1/2$; on a density-one set analytic and Mordell-Weil ranks agree and Sha is finite. The main new input is the 2-converse: if the $2^\infty$-Selmer corank is 0 or 1 it equals the analytic and Mordell-Weil ranks and Sha is finite. Mean paper: $\frac{1}{\#\mathcal D(Y)}\sum_{d}a(E^{(d)})\to1/2$, via a tail bound on high-rank twists, plus algebraic-rank moments. Both use signed squarefree twists ordered by $|d|$, not Goldfeld's discriminant ordering; no higher analytic-rank moments are claimed.

problems.name: The cotype-cotype conjecture: finite cotype of a Banach space and its dual implies K-convexity (approximation property case)
problems.field: Banach space geometry; Rademacher type and cotype, K-convexity
problems.statement: A Banach space $X$ is $K$-convex if the Rademacher projections on $L_2(\{-1,1\}^s;X)$ are uniformly bounded; by Maurey-Pisier and Pisier this is equivalent to nontrivial Rademacher type. If $X$ is $K$-convex then $X$ and $X^*$ have finite cotype. Pisier (1980-81) proved the converse when $X$ has the bounded approximation property and the cotype exponents $q,r$ of $X,X^*$ satisfy a restriction, and asked whether the restriction can be removed (Remark 2(iii)). Without any approximation hypothesis the converse fails (Pisier 1983). Szarek and Tomczak-Jaegermann (2009) call this the cotype-cotype conjecture, and Gupta, Misra and Ray (2025, Conjecture 1.5) state the BAP form. If $X$ has the (bounded) approximation property and both $X$ and $X^*$ have finite cotype, with arbitrary exponents, must $X$ be $K$-convex?
problems.posedBy: G. Pisier, Seminaire d'analyse fonctionnelle 1980-81, expose VII, Remark 2(iii); named the cotype-cotype conjecture by Szarek and Tomczak-Jaegermann (2009)
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: a nonzero real Banach space $X$ with the approximation property is $K$-convex if and only if $C_q(X)<\infty$ and $C_r(X^*)<\infty$ for some $q,r\in[2,\infty)$, possibly different; equivalently such $X$ has nontrivial Rademacher type. Corollary 1.2 makes the bound on $K(X)$ uniform in the cotype data and gives dimension-free metric-entropy duality for the corresponding convex bodies; a further consequence settles a Gupta-Misra-Ray tensor-norm conjecture (their Conjecture 1.4) under AP. Real scalars only; constants are existential. It does not address spaces failing AP, where the statement is false.

problems.name: The Toms-Winter conjecture: strict comparison implies Jiang-Su stability for simple nuclear C*-algebras
problems.field: Operator algebras; regularity in the Elliott classification program
problems.statement: For simple separable unital infinite-dimensional nuclear C*-algebras $A$, the Toms-Winter conjecture asserts the equivalence of three regularity properties: finite nuclear dimension, Jiang-Su stability $A\cong A\otimes\mathcal Z$, and strict comparison of positive elements by traces. Winter and Castillejos-Evington-Tikuisis-White-Winter proved finite nuclear dimension equivalent to $\mathcal Z$-stability, and Rordam proved that $\mathcal Z$-stability gives strict comparison. The remaining implication, strict comparison implies $\mathcal Z$-stability, was known only under conditions on the tracial boundary (finitely many extreme traces, compact finite-dimensional boundary, Lin's condition) or with uniform property $\Gamma$. Does strict comparison imply $\mathcal Z$-stability for every simple separable nuclear non-elementary C*-algebra?
problems.posedBy: Andrew Toms and Wilhelm Winter
problems.ageNote: The release cites Winter-Zacharias, The nuclear dimension of C*-algebras (Adv. Math. 2010), Conjecture 9.3, and Schafhauser-Tikuisis-White's 99 problems (Conjecture 5, Problem XVIII). The conjecture circulated in Toms and Winter's work a few years earlier.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: strict comparison implies $A\cong A\otimes\mathcal Z$ for every separable simple nuclear non-elementary $A$, unital or not. More generally (Theorem 1.2) every separable nuclear algebra whose Cuntz semigroup is almost unperforated and fully almost divisible is $\mathcal Z$-stable, which answers the implication (iii) to (ii) of the nonsimple Toms-Winter problem (STW Problem LXXV) and the abstract Cuntz-semigroup question (STW Problem XXVI). Separability and nuclearity remain hypotheses; nonnuclear and non-separable algebras are not treated.

problems.name: Sidorenko's conjecture
problems.statement: For finite simple graphs $H$ and $G$, let $t(H,G)$ be the probability that a uniformly random map $V(H)\to V(G)$ is a homomorphism, and $p(G)=2|E(G)|/|V(G)|^2$ the edge density. Sidorenko conjectured that every bipartite graph $H$ with at least one edge satisfies $t(H,G)\ge p(G)^{|E(H)|}$ for every $G$: a random graph of the same density minimises the number of copies of $H$. It was known for trees, even cycles, complete bipartite graphs, hypercubes, graphs with a vertex complete to the other side (Conlon-Fox-Sudakov), weakly norming graphs, tree-arrangeable graphs and many other classes. Does every bipartite graph satisfy Sidorenko's inequality?
problems.posedBy: Alexander Sidorenko, Inequalities for functionals generated by bipartite graphs (Diskret. Mat., 1991) and A correlation inequality for bipartite graphs (Graphs Combin., 1993)
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites Sidorenko's 1991 and 1993 papers for the conjecture and places its roots in the supersaturation questions of Erdos, Lovasz, Spencer and Simonovits (1979 to 1984); the form with injective copies is often credited to Erdos and Simonovits.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for the explicit bipartite incidence graph $H$ of 22 triples on 13 points ($35$ vertices, $66$ edges, connected, degrees 4 to 6 on one side and 3 on the other) there is a finite simple graph $G$ with an edge and $t(H,G)<p(G)^{66}$. Corollaries: tensor powers make $t(H,F)/p(F)^{66}$ arbitrarily small, and blow-ups give a fixed deficit for injective copies at a positive limiting density. Not given: an explicit host graph, the smallest counterexample, or which other bipartite graphs fail.

problems.name: Universal optimality of the triangular lattice in the plane (Cohn-Kumar)
problems.shortName: Universal optimality of the triangular lattice
problems.field: Discrete geometry; energy minimization and universal optimality
problems.statement: For a locally finite configuration $\mathcal C\subset\mathbb R^2$ of density one and a potential $g$, the energy per point is the lower limit of $N_R^{-1}\sum_{x\ne y\in\mathcal C\cap B_R}g(|x-y|^2)$. Among lattices of covolume one the triangular lattice minimizes inverse-power sums (Rankin, Cassels, Ennola, Diananda) and Gaussian theta sums (Montgomery 1988), but these say nothing about non-lattice competitors. Cohn and Kumar (2007, Conjecture 9.4) conjectured that the triangular lattice, like $E_8$ and the Leech lattice, is universally optimal, with sharp Fourier auxiliary functions certifying it; Cohn, Kumar, Miller, Radchenko and Viazovska proved the analogue in dimensions 8 and 24. Does the triangular lattice of covolume one minimize energy per point among all density-one planar configurations, for every completely monotone function $g$ of squared distance?
problems.posedBy: Henry Cohn and Abhinav Kumar (Conjecture 9.4, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 2007)
problems.ageNote: The lattice-only form goes back to Rankin (1953) and Cassels (1959); the conjecture against all configurations is Cohn-Kumar 2007, as cited by the manuscript.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: the density-one triangular lattice $A$ minimizes the lower energy per point $E_g$ among all locally finite planar configurations of centered-disk density one, for every nonnegative smooth completely monotone $g$ of squared distance, including Gaussians and all inverse powers, with infinite energies allowed and no separation assumption. The proof builds sharp radial Schwartz minorants $f_\alpha\le e^{-\pi\alpha|x|^2}$ with $\widehat f_\alpha\ge0$ touching at all nonzero lattice and dual-lattice points, and integrates over Gaussians. Section 8 transfers this, following Petrache-Serfaty, to triangular minimality of the logarithmic and Riesz $0<s<2$ renormalized (jellium) energies. It does not give a sharp auxiliary function for every mixed potential, does not classify minimizers, and does not treat other dimensions.

problems.name: The group-ring Determinant Conjecture (Luck)
problems.field: L2-invariants; Fuglede-Kadison determinants over group von Neumann algebras
problems.statement: For a discrete group $G$ and a matrix $A$ over $\mathbb Z[G]$, let $T_A$ act on $\ell^2(G)^n$ by the regular representation and let $\mu_A$ be the spectral measure of $T_A^*T_A$ with respect to the group trace. A nonsingular integer matrix has $|\det|\ge1$; the Determinant Conjecture (Luck 2002, Conjecture 13.2) asks for the analogue $\int_{(0,\infty)}\log t\,d\mu_A(t)\ge0$, which for invertible $A$ says the Fuglede-Kadison determinant is at least $1$. It was known for amenable groups (Schick) and sofic groups (Elek-Szabo), and underlies approximation and torsion results for $L^2$-invariants. Does the Determinant Conjecture hold for every group?
problems.posedBy: Wolfgang Luck, L2-Invariants: Theory and Applications to Geometry and K-Theory (2002), Conjecture 13.2
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: a finitely generated group $G_D$, $n\ge1$ and $A\in M_n(\mathbb Z[G_D])$, invertible over $\mathbb Q[G_D]$ with bounded inverse, whose Fuglede-Kadison determinant lies strictly between $0$ and $1$; the log integral is finite and negative. The group is nonsofic by Elek-Szabo. It disproves the unrestricted conjecture only; it says nothing about torsion-free groups, groups satisfying the Atiyah conjecture, or the determinant approximation conjecture, and it relies on the characteristic-two direct-finiteness counterexample.

problems.name: The Kadison-Kaplansky Projection Conjecture
problems.statement: For a torsion-free discrete group $H$, let $C_r^*(H)$ be its reduced group $C^*$-algebra. The Kadison-Kaplansky conjecture asserts that $C_r^*(H)$ contains no projections other than $0$ and $1$. Pimsner and Voiculescu proved it for free groups, and it follows from surjectivity of the coefficient-free Baum-Connes map, so it holds for amenable and hyperbolic groups. Does every torsion-free discrete group have a projectionless reduced $C^*$-algebra?

problems.name: The LeBrun-Salamon conjecture: positive quaternionic-Kahler manifolds and contact Fano manifolds are homogeneous
problems.field: Differential and algebraic geometry; quaternionic-Kahler and contact Fano
problems.statement: A Riemannian manifold of dimension $4m$, $m\ge2$, is quaternionic-Kahler if its holonomy lies in $Sp(m)Sp(1)$; it is positive if its scalar curvature is positive. Wolf showed that the compact symmetric examples (the Wolf spaces) correspond to the adjoint varieties of simple complex Lie algebras, and Salamon's twistor construction attaches to every closed positive quaternionic-Kahler manifold a complex contact Fano manifold. LeBrun and Salamon proved finiteness and strong rigidity results and conjectured that the symmetric examples are the only ones. The algebraic form, the contact-Fano homogeneity conjecture, asks the same of every smooth complex projective contact Fano manifold, which should be an adjoint variety $\mathbb P(\mathcal O_{\min}(\mathfrak g))$. Known cases covered real dimension 8, 12 and 16 and low complex dimensions, or required extra hypotheses (reductive automorphism group, nonnegative sectional curvature). Is every closed connected positive quaternionic-Kahler manifold of dimension at least 8 a Wolf space, and is every contact Fano manifold an adjoint variety?
problems.posedBy: Claude LeBrun and Simon Salamon
problems.ageNote: LeBrun and Salamon, Strong rigidity of positive quaternion-Kahler manifolds, Invent. Math. 118 (1994), cited by the manuscript as the setting of the homogeneity conjecture; the general algebraic formulation is cited from Buczynski (Doc. Math. 2010, Conjecture 1.1).
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: every smooth connected complex projective contact Fano manifold $(X,F)$ of dimension $2n+1$, $n\ge1$, is contact-isomorphic to the adjoint variety $Y_{\mathfrak g}$ of a simple complex Lie algebra, with $L\simeq\mathcal O(1)|_{Y_{\mathfrak g}}$. Corollaries: every such manifold is Kahler-Einstein; every smooth projective contact manifold with $b_2=1$ is an adjoint variety and with $b_2\ge2$ is $\mathbb P(T^*Z)$ (via Kebekus-Peternell-Sommese-Wisniewski and Demailly); every closed connected positive quaternionic-Kahler manifold of real dimension $4m\ge8$ satisfies $\nabla Rm=0$ and is homothetic to a Wolf space. It says nothing about negative or zero scalar curvature, about noncompact or incomplete metrics, or about compact Kahler contact manifolds that are not projective beyond the jet criterion it states.

problems.name: Almost everywhere convergence of Fourier series in L log L
problems.shortName: Fourier convergence in L log L
problems.field: Harmonic analysis; pointwise convergence of Fourier series
problems.statement: For an integrable function $f$ on the circle $\mathbb T$ let $S_Nf(x)=\sum_{|k|\le N}\widehat f(k)e^{ikx}$. Carleson (1966) proved $S_Nf\to f$ almost everywhere for $f\in L^2$, Hunt (1968) extended this to $L^p$, $p>1$, and Kolmogorov (1923) gave an integrable function whose Fourier series diverges almost everywhere. Between these, convergence was known in $L\log L\log\log L$ (Sjolin 1969), in $L\log L\log\log\log L$ (Antonov 1996) and in the quasi-Banach space $\mathrm{QA}$ of Arias de Reyna. Does $S_Nf(x)\to f(x)$ for almost every $x$, along the full sequence $N=0,1,2,\ldots$, for every $f$ in the Orlicz class $L\log L(\mathbb T)=\{f:\int|f|\log(2+|f|)<\infty\}$?
problems.posedBy: Classical question after Carleson, Hunt, Sjolin and Antonov; stated as Conjecture 1 (with a weak-L1 maximal formulation) by Victor Lie (2017)
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites no first posing. The earliest explicit statement it cites is V. Lie, Pointwise convergence of Fourier series (I), JEMS 19 (2017), Definition 1.1 and Conjecture 1. The question is implicit in the work it lists from Sjolin (1969) and Antonov (1996) onward; the original posing date is not given in the literature read here.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every complex-valued $f\in L\log L(\mathbb T)$ there is a null set $N_f$ with $\lim_{N\to\infty}S_Nf(x)=f(x)$ for $x\notin N_f$, along the full sequence. The key estimate is a good-set bound $\int_{\{M\rho\le e^{4h}\}}\sup_N|S_N\rho|\le Cd$ for bounded densities of height $e^d$, summed over height layers. The paper also deduces a weak-$L^1$ maximal inequality in Luxemburg norm. It does not address spaces strictly between $L\log L$ and $L^1$ (where Konyagin's divergence results apply below $L\sqrt{\log L}$), nor lacunary or higher-dimensional analogues.

The manuscript (September 23, 2026) has no companion in the release.

problems.name: Beauville's splitting conjecture for two integrable summands
problems.field: Complex and Kahler geometry; split tangent bundles and foliations
problems.statement: Let $X$ be a compact Kahler manifold with a holomorphic splitting $T_X=\bigoplus_i E_i$ such that partial sums of the summands are integrable. Beauville (2000, Section 2.3) conjectured that the universal cover of $X$ then splits as a product $\prod Y_i$ compatibly with the decomposition, and proved it for Kahler-Einstein manifolds and surfaces. Later work covered line-bundle summands with integrable complement (Brunella-Pereira-Touzet), Hermitian-flat summands (Pereira-Touzet, Druel-Pereira-Pym-Touzet) and foliations with a compact leaf of finite holonomy. For two summands the hypothesis is that both are integrable. If $T_X=E_1\oplus E_2$ with both summands integrable of positive rank, is the universal cover a compatible product $Y_1\times Y_2$?
problems.posedBy: A. Beauville, Complex manifolds with split tangent bundle, in Complex Analysis and Algebraic Geometry (de Gruyter 2000), Section 2.3
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: if a compact connected Kahler manifold has $T_X=E_1\oplus E_2$ with both summands integrable holomorphic subbundles of positive rank, its universal cover is biholomorphic to $Y_1\times Y_2$ (connected, simply connected) with $d\Phi(\pi^*E_i)=\mathrm{pr}_i^*T_{Y_i}$. Corollary: non-uniruled projective manifolds with a two-summand splitting (integrability by Hoering 2007). It does not treat three or more summands, gives no finite-cover product, and assumes integrability (automatic integrability is the companion entry, for rationally connected manifolds).

The manuscript is authored as OpenAI with no human author named. A Lean formalization accompanies it (Comparator challenge KahlerSplitting, listed in lean/formalization.yaml).

problems.name: Is the worst-case translative covering density of convex bodies linear in the dimension?
problems.field: Discrete and convex geometry; translative and lattice coverings
problems.statement: For a convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^n$ let $\theta_T(K)$ be the least density of a covering of $\mathbb R^n$ by translates of $K$. Rogers (1957) proved $\theta_T(K)\le n\log n+n\log\log n+5n$ for every convex body, and lower bounds of order $n$ are known for balls. Naszodi recorded the question whether a universal linear bound holds: is there an absolute constant $C$ with $\theta_T(K)\le Cn$ for every convex body in every dimension? Equivalently, what is the order of the worst-case covering density in dimension $n$?
problems.posedBy: M. Naszodi, Flavors of Translative Coverings, New Trends in Intuitive Geometry, Bolyai Soc. Math. Stud. 27 (2018), Section 3 (arXiv 1603.04481)
problems.ageNote: Recorded in Naszodi's survey, arXiv 1603.04481 (2016), published 2018; the manuscript does not say who first asked it. Rogers' n log n upper bound dates from 1957.
problems.resultNote: Translative paper, Theorem 1.1: for absolute $c>0$ and all large $n$ there is a centrally symmetric convex body (even a rational polytope) with $\theta_T(K_n)>cn\log n$, so no universal linear bound exists; with Rogers' bound the worst-case order is $n\log n$. It extends the lattice lower bound of Li and Liu (2026) to arbitrary translative coverings. The companion proves every convex body has a single-lattice covering of density at most $Cn\log n$, removing the $(\log\log n)^{O(1)}$ loss of Li-Liu, so the lattice supremum also has order $n\log n$. Constants are not optimized; Euclidean balls are not treated.

problems.name: Fujita's freeness conjecture
problems.statement: Let $X$ be a smooth complex projective variety of dimension $n$, $K_X$ its canonical bundle and $L$ an ample line bundle. Fujita conjectured that $K_X+mL$ is globally generated for every $m\ge n+1$ (and very ample for $m\ge n+2$); the bound is sharp for $(\mathbb P^n,\mathcal O(1))$. Known: curves by Riemann-Roch, surfaces by Reider, dimensions 3, 4, 5 by Ein-Lazarsfeld, Kawamata and Ye-Zhu; in general Angehrn-Siu's quadratic bound $m\ge(n^2+n+2)/2$, later improved to $n(\log\log n+2.34)$ by Ghidelli-Lacini and to about $1.776n$ by Han. Is $K_X+(n+1)L$ globally generated for every smooth projective $X$ of every dimension $n$ and every ample $L$?
problems.posedBy: Takao Fujita, On polarized manifolds whose adjoint bundles are not semipositive, Algebraic Geometry, Sendai 1985, Adv. Stud. Pure Math. 10 (1987)
problems.ageNote: The cited source is the proceedings of the 1985 Sendai conference, published in 1987; the conjecture is often dated to the 1985 meeting.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every smooth connected complex projective variety $X$ of dimension $n\ge1$ and every ample line bundle $L$, $K_X+(n+1)L$ is generated by global sections; hence $K_X+mL$ is globally generated for all $m\ge n+1$, even when $L$ itself is not. The bound is sharp. The method minimises an exponential average of normalised section orders over bases and weighted monomial valuations, then lifts sections with Fujita's discrepancy-and-vanishing mechanism. It does not prove the very-ampleness conjecture ($m\ge n+2$) or point separation.

problems.name: The (B)-conjecture for even log-concave measures: log-concavity of t -> mu(e^t K)
problems.statement: Let $\mu$ be an even log-concave measure on $\mathbb R^n$ and $K$ an origin-symmetric convex body. The (B)-conjecture asks whether $t\mapsto\mu(e^tK)$ is log-concave on $\mathbb R$. Cordero-Erausquin, Fradelizi and Maurey (2004) proved it for the Gaussian measure, and the question for general even log-concave measures remained open; Saroglou (2016) showed that the logarithmic Brunn-Minkowski inequality in a given dimension implies it for every even log-concave density in that dimension. Is $t\mapsto\mu(e^tK)$ log-concave for every even log-concave measure $\mu$ and every origin-symmetric convex body $K$?
problems.posedBy: Not named in the manuscript; it cites Cordero-Erausquin, Fradelizi and Maurey (2004) for the conjecture's Gaussian case
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites Cordero-Erausquin, Fradelizi and Maurey, J. Funct. Anal. 214 (2004), whose title already names the (B)-conjecture, and Saroglou (Mathematika 2016) for the transfer; it does not say who first posed it or when. The wider literature attributes the Gaussian question to Banaszczyk.
problems.resultNote: Corollary 8.1: for every $n\ge1$, every even log-concave Radon measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb R^n$ (finite or infinite total mass, possibly supported on a subspace) and origin-symmetric convex bodies $K,L$, the log-Brunn-Minkowski inequality holds for $\mu$; taking $L$ a dilate of $K$ gives log-concavity of $t\mapsto\mu(e^tK)$. This is the scalar-dilation form; the stronger diagonal (B)-property for general linear dilations is not claimed except where Saroglou's equivalence for cubes applies.

problems.name: Explicit depth-three circuit lower bounds beyond the square-root exponent
problems.statement: For a Boolean function $f$ on $\{0,1\}^n$, let $S_3(f)$ be the least number of gates in an unbounded fan-in OR-AND-OR (depth-three) circuit computing $f$. Hastad's switching lemma gives $S_3(\text{parity})=2^{\Theta(\sqrt n)}$, and Paturi-Pudlak-Zane's bound $\Omega(n^{1/4}2^{\sqrt n})$ is tight for parity; all lower bounds for explicit functions remained of the form $2^{c\sqrt n}$ for a constant $c$. Hastad, Jukna and Pudlak asked for an explicit function needing $2^{n^{1/2+\varepsilon}}$ gates, and Gurumukhani-Paturi-Pudlak-Saks-Talebanfard discuss as open the weaker goal of a superconstant multiple of $\sqrt n$ in the exponent. Is there an explicit function, for instance a language in polynomial time, with $S_3(f_n)\ge 2^{\omega(\sqrt n)}$?
problems.posedBy: Discussed as open by Gurumukhani, Paturi, Pudlak, Saks and Talebanfard (CCC 2024); Hastad, Jukna and Pudlak (1995) posed the stronger 2^(n^(1/2+eps)) problem
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites GPPST (CCC 2024, Section 1.1) for this open problem and notes it is weaker than Hastad-Jukna-Pudlak's 1995 Problem 2. The square-root barrier itself dates from Hastad's 1986 parity bound, so the question is older than its 2024 citation; the year here is the earliest posing the manuscript gives for exactly this question.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there is a language $L$ decidable by a deterministic Turing machine in time $C(n+1)^a$ whose $n$-bit membership functions satisfy $\log_2 S_3(f_n)/\sqrt n\to\infty$, counting all gates of OR-AND-OR circuits with no fan-in restriction. The language and machine are fixed before the constant $A$. It does not give a fixed exponent $n^{1/2+\varepsilon}$ (Hastad-Jukna-Pudlak's problem stays open), says nothing about AND-OR-AND circuits beyond what duality gives for the complement, and nothing about depth above three or Valiant's $2^{\omega(n/\log\log n)}$ threshold.

problems.name: The complete Crouzeix conjecture: the numerical range is a complete 2-spectral set
problems.field: Matrix analysis; numerical range and spectral sets
problems.statement: For $A\in M_n(\mathbb C)$ with numerical range $W(A)=\{x^*Ax:\|x\|=1\}$ and a matrix polynomial $P(z)=\sum_{j=0}^d B_jz^j$ with $B_j\in M_m(\mathbb C)$, put $P[A]=\sum_j A^j\otimes B_j$. Crouzeix conjectured in 2004 that $\|p(A)\|\le2\max_{W(A)}|p|$ for scalar polynomials (the case $m=1$), and in 2007 proved the complete bound with constant 11.08; Crouzeix and Palencia lowered the complete constant to $1+\sqrt2$. The complete conjecture asks for the constant 2 uniformly in $m$, $n$ and $d$, that is, that $W(A)$ is a complete 2-spectral set. Does $\|P[A]\|\le2\sup_{z\in W(A)}\|P(z)\|$ hold for all such $A$ and $P$?
problems.posedBy: Michel Crouzeix (scalar form 2004; complete form as named in the later literature)
problems.ageNote: The manuscripts date the scalar question to Crouzeix 2004 and his complete bound 11.08 to 2007, and cite Ohag, Czyz and Virtanen (2026) for the name 'complete Crouzeix conjecture', but do not say when the complete form was first stated as a conjecture. Year left blank.
problems.resultNote: Shown: for every bounded operator $A$ on any complex Hilbert space (no separability assumed) and every matrix polynomial $P$, $\|P[A]\|\le2\sup_{W(A)}\|P\|$, with 2 sharp; the same bound holds for finite matrix-valued functions holomorphic near $\overline{W(A)}$ and for rational functions with poles outside it. For a matrix and an admissible convex domain containing $W(A)$, an optimal similarity with condition number at most 2 makes the conformal image contractive, with one positive boundary density representing all matrix-valued analytic evaluations. It contains the scalar Crouzeix theorem as the case $m=1$.

The principal manuscript (September 23, 2026) gives a structural proof via an optimal similarity and a common positive boundary density; a second manuscript (September 26, 2026) gives a separate direct proof of the finite-matrix inequality. The manuscripts cite the scalar proofs of Jin, of Lorist and Schwenninger, and of Luo.

problems.name: The Kakeya maximal conjecture in three dimensions
problems.statement: For $\omega\in S^2$ and $0<\delta<1$ let $K_\delta f(\omega)$ be the supremum, over unit tubes of radius $\delta$ in direction $\omega$, of the average of $|f|$ on the tube. The Kakeya maximal conjecture in $\mathbb R^n$ asks that $\|K_\delta f\|_{L^n(S^{n-1})}\le C_\varepsilon\delta^{-\varepsilon}\|f\|_{L^n(\mathbb R^n)}$ for every $\varepsilon>0$; it implies the Kakeya set conjecture. In $\mathbb R^3$ Wang and Zahl proved the set conjecture in 2025, but their union estimate carries a density power $\lambda^{K(\varepsilon)}$ where the maximal bound needs $\lambda^3$, a gap stated after their theorem. Does the Kakeya maximal estimate hold in $\mathbb R^3$ for every $\varepsilon>0$?
problems.posedBy: Maximal form of the Kakeya conjecture (Cordoba, Bourgain); the manuscripts cite the formulations of Katz and Tao (2002) and Zahl's 2025 survey, Conjecture 1.3''
problems.ageNote: The manuscripts do not attribute the maximal conjecture to one poser or year. The earliest sources they cite for the maximal formulation are Cordoba's planar maximal estimates (1977) and Bourgain's higher-dimensional work (1991).
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $C_\varepsilon$ such that $\|K_\delta f\|_{L^3(S^2)}\le C_\varepsilon\delta^{-\varepsilon}\|f\|_{L^3(\mathbb R^3)}$ for all $0<\delta<1$ and $f\in L^3(\mathbb R^3)$. This is the $n=3$ case of the maximal conjecture; it strengthens the Wang-Zahl set theorem by getting the cubic dependence on shading density. The paper also derives Nikodym maximal and local curved Kakeya estimates by cited transfers. It does not treat dimension four or higher for the maximal operator; the four-dimensional Hausdorff case is a separate entry. The same release's local smoothing result in three dimensions (family 079, entry local-smoothing-conjecture-r3) also yields this Kakeya maximal estimate, by the established Bochner-Riesz to restriction to Kakeya chain in its Section 11.1.

problems.name: Gaussian free field limit of the six-vertex height function throughout the regime a = b = 1, 0 < c <= 2
problems.field: Statistical mechanics; six-vertex model and random surfaces
problems.statement: In the square-lattice six-vertex model with weights $a=b=1$ and $c>0$, the ice rule makes the arrows a height function $h$ on faces. The Coulomb-gas picture predicts that in the critical range $|\Delta|\le1$, $\Delta=1-c^2/2$ (that is $0<c\le2$), the rescaled height converges to a multiple of the Gaussian free field; Di Francesco, Saleur and Zuber (1987) gave the Gaussian action for $1<c<2$ with squared multiplier $1/\arcsin(c/2)$ in unit height steps. Rigorous results covered the free-fermion point $c=\sqrt2$ (Kenyon), perturbations of it, logarithmic delocalization for $1\le c\le2$, and a GFF theorem for $\sqrt3\le c\le2$. Does the height function converge to $\sigma(c)$ times the Gaussian free field, with $\sigma(c)^2=1/\arcsin(c/2)$, for every $c\in(0,2]$?
problems.posedBy: Coulomb-gas prediction; the manuscript cites P. di Francesco, H. Saleur and J.-B. Zuber (J. Stat. Phys. 1987) for the Gaussian action and coupling
problems.ageNote: The Gaussian description belongs to the Coulomb-gas approach of the 1970s and 1980s; the manuscript cites DFSZ 1987 for the precise prediction in $1<c<2$ and states that its formula agrees with the proved multiplier. Physical predictions stated precisely in print count as posed.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for each $c\in(0,2]$ the balanced-torus plane law exists and $h(\cdot/\delta)$ converges to $\sigma(c)\Gamma$, $\sigma(c)^2=2/\arccos(1-c^2/2)=1/\arcsin(c/2)$, with Green kernel $-(2\pi)^{-1}\log|x-y|$, jointly on finite-energy mass-zero test measures, in $B^\alpha_{p,q}$ and $W^{\alpha,p}$ restriction spaces for $-1<\alpha<0$, and with Wick-type limits of increment moments. Priority: Duminil-Copin, Kozlowski, Lammers and Manolescu had proved this for $\sqrt3\le c\le2$. Not shown: other slopes or Gibbs states, anisotropic $a\ne b$, or the regime $c>2$.

problems.name: Lech's multiplicity conjecture
problems.statement: For a nonzero Noetherian local ring $(A,\mathfrak a)$ of dimension $d$, the Hilbert-Samuel multiplicity is $e(A)=\lim_N d!\,\ell_A(A/\mathfrak a^N)/N^d$. Lech (1960) proved the inequality below when the source has dimension at most two and in complete-intersection cases; Ma proved it in equal characteristic for dimension three, for standard graded sources over perfect fields, and a bound $e(R)\le\max\{1,d!/2^d\}e(S)$. Lech asked whether multiplicity can decrease under flat maps. If $(R,\mathfrak m)\to(S,\mathfrak n)$ is a flat local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings, is $e(R)\le e(S)$?
problems.posedBy: Christer Lech, Note on multiplicities of ideals, Ark. Mat. 4 (1960); Inequalities related to certain couples of local rings, Acta Math. 112 (1964)
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every flat local homomorphism $(R,\mathfrak m)\to(S,\mathfrak n)$ of nonzero Noetherian local rings, $e(R)\le e(S)$, in all dimensions and characteristics. The key input is a uniform lower bound on the zeroth homology of finite free complexes with entries in high powers of a parameter ideal, valid for generalized length functions, applied with Frobenius perfection in characteristic $p$ and perfectoid lengths in mixed characteristic. The paper does not claim the stronger Iyengar-Ma-Walker conjecture for all complete local rings, only its complete-domain characteristic-$p$ case.

problems.name: The K(pi,1) conjecture for Artin groups of finite rank
problems.statement: For a Coxeter matrix $M$ on a finite set $S$, the Artin group $A_M$ is the fundamental group of the quotient of the complexified hyperplane complement of the Coxeter group $W$ by $W$, and of the finite Salvetti complex $X(W,S)$, which has one cell per spherical subset of $S$. Deligne (1972) proved asphericity when $W$ is finite; Charney-Davis proved the FC and dimension-two cases, Paolini-Salvetti the affine case, Huang-Przytycki dimension three. The $K(\pi,1)$ conjecture, attributed to Arnol'd, Brieskorn, Pham and Thom and listed as Problem 1 in Charney's Artin-group problem list, asserts asphericity in general. Is the Salvetti complex (equivalently the hyperplane-complement quotient) a $K(A_M,1)$ for every Coxeter matrix?
problems.posedBy: Attributed to Arnol'd, Brieskorn, Pham and Thom; stated in Brieskorn's Bourbaki seminar (LNM 317, 1973); Problem 1 in R. Charney, Problems related to Artin groups
problems.ageNote: The manuscript cites Brieskorn's Seminaire Bourbaki expose (1971/72, published 1973, Section 2) for the question and Paolini for the conventional attribution to Arnol'd, Brieskorn, Pham and Thom; it gives no earlier date.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every Coxeter matrix on a finite set, with arbitrary finite or infinite labels and connected or disconnected diagrams, the universal cover of the full Salvetti complex $X(W,S)$ is contractible, so $\pi_n(X)=0$ for $n\ge2$. The proof contracts the poset of spherical cosets by a well-ordered vertex filtration, using a framed zigzag-algebra braid action whose layer multiplicities define a harmonic height. Consequences recorded: torsion-freeness, the center $Z(A)\cong\mathbb Z^k$, and Dobrinskaya's monoid equivalence. Infinite rank is not covered.

problems.name: Erdos's question on the maximum modulus of real Littlewood polynomials: is it at least (1 + c) sqrt(N)?
problems.field: Littlewood polynomials; extremal problems on the unit circle
problems.statement: For signs $\epsilon_k\in\{-1,1\}$ let $P(z)=\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\epsilon_k z^k$. Parseval gives $\|P\|_{L^2(|z|=1)}=\sqrt N$, so $\max_{|z|=1}|P(z)|\ge\sqrt N$. Erdos asked whether this is far from sharp: is there an absolute constant $c>0$ with $\max_{|z|=1}|P(z)|\ge(1+c)\sqrt N$ for every such polynomial of large length? The analogue for complex unimodular coefficients was refuted by Kahane's ultraflat polynomials (1980); the Rudin-Shapiro polynomials give $O(\sqrt N)$ and Balister et al. gave two-sided flatness up to constants, but the constant $1+c$ for real signs stayed open. Is $\liminf_N \min_{\epsilon}\max_{|z|=1}|P(z)|/\sqrt N>1$?
problems.posedBy: Paul Erdos
problems.ageNote: Erdos, Some unsolved problems, Michigan Math. J. 4 (1957), Problem 22, as cited by the manuscript; also Hayman-Lingham, Research problems in function theory, Problems 4.13 and 4.31.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: $\min_{\epsilon}\max_{|z|=1}|\sum_{k<N}\epsilon_k z^k|=(1+o(1))\sqrt N$ as $N\to\infty$ through all integers, so no constant $c>0$ as in Erdos's question exists. The construction relaxes to real coefficients in $[-1,1]$ with small defect, using sampled quadratic-phase modes and a hypergraph interval packing, then rounds to signs by a Lovett-Meka partial-coloring argument. It is existential and gives no rate. The principal paper gives no uniform lower bound; the October 5 companions add $|P|\ge\sqrt N/16$ and then full two-sided ultraflatness $(1\pm\epsilon)\sqrt N$ at every large length.
problems.claimIssueNote: This result conflicts with published claims. Preprints by el Abdalaoui (arXiv:1609.03435 and two others) claim the opposite, that such flat polynomials do not exist; the release's manuscript argues in its Appendix A that those arguments have specific gaps. Until the conflict is settled in public, the entry is Contested.

problems.name: Simon's Problem 2: pure-point spectrum for the two-dimensional Anderson model at every disorder
problems.statement: Let $H=\Delta+v$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}^2)$, with nearest-neighbor hopping and independent site potentials $v_x$ uniform on $[-h,h]$. The scaling theory of Abrahams, Anderson, Licciardello and Ramakrishnan (1979) predicts no metallic behavior in two dimensions, at any disorder. Rigorous localization was known only at large disorder or at extreme energies (Frohlich-Spencer, Frohlich-Martinelli-Scoppola-Spencer, Aizenman-Molchanov) and near the band edge (Ding-Smart). Simon's Problem 2 asks: for every $h>0$, does $H$ almost surely have pure-point spectrum throughout its spectrum?
problems.posedBy: Barry Simon (Problem 2 in 'Schrodinger operators in the twenty-first century'), formalizing the two-dimensional localization conjecture of Abrahams, Anderson, Licciardello and Ramakrishnan
problems.ageNote: The physical prediction dates from 1979 (Abrahams et al.); the 2000 date is Simon's mathematical formulation, which the manuscript cites as the problem.
problems.resultNote: For each fixed $h>0$, the operator $H_v=\Delta+v$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}^2)$ with iid $v_x$ uniform on $[-h,h]$ almost surely has pure-point spectral type with a complete orthonormal eigenbasis, spectrum $[-4-h,4+h]$ and dense eigenvalues. The null set may depend on $h$. Not shown: one event for all $h$, bounds uniform in energy, exponential decay of eigenfunctions, dynamical localization, or other single-site laws such as Bernoulli.

problems.name: Global classical solutions of the 3D relativistic Vlasov-Maxwell system for large data
problems.statement: The relativistic Vlasov-Maxwell system couples a particle density $f(t,x,v)\ge0$ on $\mathbb R^3_x\times\mathbb R^3_v$, transported by $\partial_tf+\hat v\cdot\nabla_xf+(E+\hat v\times B)\cdot\nabla_vf=0$ with $\hat v=v/\sqrt{1+|v|^2}$, to Maxwell's equations with charge and current densities computed from $f$. Wollman proved local existence of classical solutions, DiPerna and Lions global weak solutions, and Glassey and Strauss showed that a classical solution continues as long as its momentum support stays bounded and proved global existence for small (dilute) data. Global classical existence was known only under smallness, symmetry or reduced dimension. For arbitrary smooth, compactly supported particle data and smooth finite-energy fields satisfying the constraints, does the classical solution exist for all time?
problems.posedBy: Classical open problem framed by R. Glassey and W. Strauss (1986 continuation criterion); no single poser named in the manuscript
problems.ageNote: The manuscript calls this the large-data global classical regularity problem and traces it through Wollman (1984), Glassey and Strauss (1986, 1987) and DiPerna and Lions (1989), but cites no paper that states it as an open problem. It has been open at least since Glassey and Strauss's 1986 criterion; yearPosed is left blank.
problems.resultNote: Claims that every smooth admissible datum ($f_0\in C_c^\infty$, $f_0\ge0$, fields in $C_b^\infty\cap L^2$ satisfying $\nabla\cdot E_0=\rho_{f_0}$, $\nabla\cdot B_0=0$) generates a unique global classical solution of the one-species relativistic Vlasov-Maxwell system in three dimensions, smooth on every $[0,T]$ with compact phase-space support there. The key estimate controls the signed momentum impulse along characteristics, integrating the retarded force along source trajectories before taking absolute values, which rules out momentum blow-up and lets the Glassey-Strauss criterion apply. It treats one species without background charge; it does not give uniform-in-time momentum bounds (the support may grow with $T$) or asymptotic behaviour, and it does not cover the non-relativistic or multi-species systems explicitly.

problems.name: Gromov's codimension-two Urysohn width conjecture for positive scalar curvature, with the macroscopic dimension conjecture for universal covers
problems.field: Scalar curvature; Urysohn width and macroscopic dimension
problems.statement: For a metric space $X$ the Urysohn $d$-width $\mathrm{UW}_d(X)$ is the infimum, over continuous maps $f:X\to K$ to simplicial complexes of dimension at most $d$, of $\sup_y\operatorname{diam}f^{-1}(y)$. Gromov proposed that positive scalar curvature collapses two dimensions at the curvature scale: a complete Riemannian $n$-manifold with $\mathrm{Scal}\ge1$ should map to an $(n-2)$-dimensional polyhedron with all point inverses of diameter bounded by a constant depending only on $n$, and the universal cover of a closed manifold with positive scalar curvature should have macroscopic dimension at most $n-2$. Known: closed and complete three-manifolds (Gromov-Lawson, Liokumovich-Maximo, Liokumovich-Wang), spin cases under the Strong Novikov Conjecture (Bolotov, Bolotov-Dranishnikov), and the aspherical consequence in dimensions four and five (Chodosh-Li, Gromov). Is $\mathrm{UW}_{n-2}(M)\le C_n$ for every complete $n$-manifold with $\mathrm{Scal}\ge1$?
problems.posedBy: Mikhael Gromov (Large Riemannian manifolds, 1986, Section 2.A(c); Positive curvature, macroscopic dimension, spectral gaps and higher signatures, 1996, Section 2 1/2; A dozen problems, 2017)
problems.ageNote: The spectral companion dates the quantitative formulation to Gromov 1986, Section 2.A(c); the principal manuscript cites the 1996 macroscopic-dimension paper and Gromov's 2017 problem list (filling-radius Conjecture A-minus).
problems.resultNote: Principal manuscript, Theorem 1.1: for every $n\ge4$ there is $C_n$ such that every connected complete boundaryless Riemannian $n$-manifold with $\mathrm{Scal}\ge1$ admits a continuous map to a simplicial complex of dimension at most $n-2$ whose entire fibers have diameter at most $C_n$; no orientability, spin, compactness or bounded-geometry assumption. problems.name: Marrakchi's relative bicentralizer conjecture
problems.field: Operator algebras; type III von Neumann algebras, bicentralizers
problems.statement: Connes asked whether the bicentralizer of a faithful normal state on a type $\mathrm{III}_1$ factor with separable predual is always trivial; Haagerup settled the amenable case. Ando, Haagerup, Houdayer and Marrakchi built a relative bicentralizer and its flow for expected inclusions. Marrakchi formulated the relative bicentralizer conjecture and proved that, for separable preduals, it is equivalent to: for every inclusion $N\subset M$ of von Neumann algebras with separable preduals and a faithful normal conditional expectation, there is an expected amenable subalgebra $P\subset N$ with $P'\cap c(M)=N'\cap c(M)$, where $c(M)$ is the continuous core. Is the relative bicentralizer conjecture true?
problems.posedBy: A. Marrakchi, Kadison's problem for type III subfactors and the bicentralizer conjecture, Invent. Math. 239 (2025), Conjecture C (arXiv 2308.15163)
problems.ageNote: Posed in the arXiv preprint 2308.15163 (2023), published in Invent. Math. in 2025. The absolute problem it generalizes goes back to Connes (1980s).
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every unital inclusion $N\subset M$ with separable preduals and a faithful normal conditional expectation there are an amenable $P\subset N$ and an expectation $N\to P$ with $P'\cap c(M)=N'\cap c(M)$; with Marrakchi's Theorem D this is the relative bicentralizer conjecture, including arbitrary centers and types, and gives an expected MASA corollary relevant to Kadison's problem for subfactors. Along the way it reproves Connes' bicentralizer conjecture for separable type $\mathrm{III}_1$ factors; priority for that absolute case belongs to Houdayer and Marrakchi (arXiv 2609.11462, 10 Sep 2026), whose statement has no separability assumption. The companion gives a second absolute proof via bounded recovery. Non-separable preduals are not treated.

problems.name: The Lipman-Zariski conjecture in characteristic zero
problems.field: Algebraic geometry; singularities and derivation modules
problems.statement: On a smooth complex variety of dimension $d$ the tangent sheaf is locally free of rank $d$. Lipman (1965), following a question of Zariski, proved that local freeness of the derivation module forces normality and asked for the converse of smoothness: if $A$ is a finitely generated integral $\mathbb C$-algebra and $\mathrm{Der}_{\mathbb C}(A)$ is locally free, is $A$ regular? It was known for hypersurfaces, local complete intersections, graded rings, isolated singularities in dimension at least three, klt and log canonical spaces, and several classes of normal surface singularities, but the surface case was open. Is every complex algebraic variety with locally free tangent sheaf nonsingular?
problems.posedBy: Joseph Lipman, after Oscar Zariski
problems.ageNote: Lipman, Free derivation modules on algebraic varieties, Amer. J. Math. 87 (1965), as cited by the manuscript; the attribution to Zariski is in the conjecture's standard name, not stated in the manuscript.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there are a finitely generated normal integral $\mathbb C$-algebra $A$ of dimension two and a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ with $\mathrm{Der}_{\mathbb C}(A)\cong A^{\oplus2}$ and $A_{\mathfrak m}$ not regular; the surface can be smooth away from that point. By Jorder's theorem no local tangent frame there commutes. The paper also answers negatively, in characteristic zero, the derivation-blowup question of Barajas, Chavez-Martinez and Romano-Velazquez (2026, Question 1). It does not address higher-dimensional non-isolated cases left open by earlier results or give a counterexample with a commuting frame (impossible by Jorder).

problems.name: Cardy's formula for critical Poisson-Voronoi percolation (annealed crossing part of Schramm's Problem 2.12)
problems.statement: In critical planar Voronoi percolation, the cells of a Poisson point process of intensity $\varepsilon^{-2}$ are coloured black or white independently with probability $1/2$. Cardy predicted, and Smirnov proved for site percolation on the triangular lattice, that crossing probabilities of a conformal quadrilateral converge to Cardy's hypergeometric function of its conformal modulus. Schramm (ICM 2006, Problem 2.12) asked for the corresponding conformal-invariance theorem for Voronoi percolation. Do the crossing probabilities of critical Poisson-Voronoi percolation in a Jordan quadrilateral converge to Cardy's formula, and is the scaling limit conformally invariant?
problems.posedBy: Oded Schramm
problems.ageNote: Schramm, Proceedings of the ICM 2006 (Madrid), Problem 2.12, as cited by the manuscript; Benjamini and Schramm had earlier studied conformal invariance of Voronoi percolation (1998).
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every bounded Jordan domain with four marked boundary points, the annealed probability of a black crossing in critical Poisson-Voronoi percolation converges to Cardy's function $F(x)$ of the conformal cross-ratio $x$. A corollary gives a quenched $L^2$ limit for fixed rectangles. The companions prove that the expected number of pivotal cells for a unit-square crossing is asymptotic to $c\,\varepsilon^{-3/4}$ and that conditional near-critical crossing-threshold laws for rational polygonal quads converge in probability over tessellations to the triangular-lattice law. Not shown: convergence of interfaces to SLE(6) or the full conformal invariance of Schramm's problem.

problems.name: The Linear List Hadwiger Conjecture
problems.statement: Kawarabayashi and Mohar (2007, Conjecture 1.3) proposed a linear relaxation of Hadwiger's conjecture for list colouring: there is an absolute constant $C$ such that every graph with no $K_t$ minor is $Ct$-choosable. Degeneracy gives $O(t\sqrt{\log t})$; the best list bounds before this work were superlinear (for example Postle's $O(t(\log\log t)^6)$), and $K_t$-minor-free graphs can have list chromatic number close to $2t$, so $C=1$ is impossible. Even the ordinary-colouring version, $\chi(G)=O(h(G))$, was open. Is there an absolute constant $C$ with $\chi_\ell(G)\le C\,h(G)$ for every graph $G$?
problems.posedBy: Ken-ichi Kawarabayashi and Bojan Mohar, A relaxed Hadwiger's conjecture for list colorings, J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 97 (2007), Conjecture 1.3
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there is an absolute integer $C\ge1$ such that every finite nonempty simple graph satisfies $\chi_\ell(G)\le C\,h(G)$; Corollary 1.2 gives the ordinary linear Hadwiger bound $\chi(G)\le C\,h(G)$. The constant is not computed or optimised and must be at least $2$ by Steiner's examples. The proof shows $K_t$-minor-free graphs on at most $t^{11/10}$ vertices are $Lt$-choosable and then lifts this to all orders through Postle-style separability and a three-district recursion. It does not give $C$ close to $1$ or $2$.

problems.name: The amenability problem for Thompson's group F (Geoghegan's conjecture)
problems.statement: Thompson's group $F$ is the group, under composition, of increasing piecewise linear homeomorphisms of $[0,1]$ with finitely many pieces, dyadic rational breakpoints and slopes in $2^{\mathbb Z}$. A discrete group is amenable if its bounded real functions carry a positive normalized left-invariant mean. $F$ has no nonabelian free subgroup (Brin-Squier), so the free-subgroup obstruction does not apply, yet it is not elementary amenable. Geoghegan conjectured in 1979 that $F$ is not amenable. Is Thompson's group $F$ nonamenable?
problems.posedBy: Ross Geoghegan (1979), as recorded by J. W. Cannon, W. J. Floyd and W. R. Parry, Introductory notes on Richard Thompson's groups (Enseign. Math., 1996), p. 227
problems.ageNote: Complete claims in both directions have appeared and been withdrawn or disputed (Shavgulidze 2009 for amenability, with errors identified by Moore; Moore's own withdrawn claim; Akhmedov 2021 for nonamenability), as the manuscript recounts.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: Thompson's group $F$ is not amenable. The proof finds a fixed finite set $S\subset F$ and $b>0$ with $|hA\triangle A|\ge b|A|$ for some $h\in S$, for every nonempty finite $A\subset F$, so no Folner sets exist. It converts approximate invariance of finite averages into an approximate fixed point of a Lipschitz self-map of a Hilbert ball, contradicting a Benyamini-Sternfeld displacement map that the paper constructs explicitly. It confirms Geoghegan's conjecture. The formal version gives no explicit expansion constant for a standard generating set, and the paper does not address other questions about $F$ such as its exact isoperimetric profile.

problems.name: The Shafarevich conjecture on holomorphic convexity of universal covers
problems.field: Complex algebraic geometry; universal covers and fundamental groups
problems.statement: Shafarevich asked whether the universal cover of a complete algebraic variety is holomorphically convex. In the usual smooth projective formulation: for every smooth connected projective complex variety $X$, is the universal cover $\widetilde X$, with the lifted complex structure, holomorphically convex, i.e. is the holomorphic hull $\{v:|g(v)|\le\sup_K|g|\ \forall g\in\mathcal O(\widetilde X)\}$ of every compact $K$ compact? A direct form for varieties with large fundamental group (Kollar) asks whether $\widetilde X$ is Stein when it contains no positive-dimensional compact analytic subvariety. The conjecture was proved for elliptic surfaces, for virtually nilpotent fundamental groups, and for fundamental groups with a faithful linear representation (Eyssidieux-Katzarkov-Pantev-Ramachandran). Does it hold in general?
problems.posedBy: Igor Shafarevich
problems.ageNote: The surface manuscript cites Shafarevich's Basic Algebraic Geometry (1974, p. 407) via Lasell-Ramachandran; the fourfold manuscript cites Kollar (1995) for the large-fundamental-group formulation.
problems.resultNote: Surface manuscript, Theorem 1.1: a smooth connected projective complex surface $X$ containing a connected nodal curve $Z_0$ with smooth rational components such that $\pi_1(Z_0)\to\pi_1(X)$ has infinite image; a component of its preimage in $\widetilde X$ is a closed noncompact union of compact rational curves, so hulls are noncompact and $\widetilde X$ is not holomorphically convex. By the linear Shafarevich theorem $\pi_1(X)$ has no faithful finite-dimensional complex representation. Fourfold manuscript, Theorem 1.1: a smooth projective fourfold with large fundamental group (no positive-dimensional compact subvariety in $\widetilde X$) whose universal cover is not Stein, hence not holomorphically convex; this disproves the large-fundamental-group form as well. Neither paper addresses quasi-projective or Kahler variants beyond these.

problems.name: GOE bulk universality for random regular graphs of fixed degree
problems.shortName: GOE bulk universality, random regular graphs
problems.field: Random matrix theory; spectra of sparse random graphs
problems.statement: Let $A$ be the adjacency matrix of a uniform random $d$-regular graph on $n$ vertices with $d\ge3$ fixed. Its eigenvalue density tends to the Kesten-McKay law, and Jakobson, Miller, Rivin and Rudnick predicted, with numerical evidence, that the local eigenvalue statistics in the bulk are those of the Gaussian Orthogonal Ensemble. Bulk universality was proved for growing degrees (Bauerschmidt-Huang-Knowles-Yau; Bourgade-Huang for $(\log n)^{24}\ll d\le n^{1/2}$), and edge universality at fixed degree (Huang-McKenzie-Yau). Bourgade and Huang state the fixed-degree case as Conjecture 2.11. For fixed $d\ge3$ and fixed bulk energy, does the unfolded eigenvalue point process converge to the GOE bulk process?
problems.posedBy: Dmitry Jakobson, Stephen D. Miller, Igor Rivin and Zeev Rudnick, Eigenvalue spacings for regular graphs, IMA Vol. 109 (1999); stated as Conjecture 2.11 by Bourgade and Huang (arXiv:2607.07617, 2026)
problems.resultNote: Claims fixed-energy GOE bulk universality of the full microscopic eigenvalue point process for uniform random $d$-regular graphs, every fixed $d\ge3$ including cubic graphs, at every energy in the open Kesten-McKay bulk. The companion extends this to sufficiently weak fixed iid uniform diagonal disorder on compact subintervals of the clean band. It does NOT address the spectral edges (already known), energy-averaged spacing statistics in the original JMRR form beyond what the point-process limit implies, or strong disorder.

problems.name: Talagrand's conjecture that fractional and integral expectation thresholds agree up to a constant
problems.statement: For an increasing family $\mathcal F$ of subsets of a finite set $X$, call $\mathcal F$ $p$-small if some family $\mathcal G$ with every member of $\mathcal F$ containing a member of $\mathcal G$ has $\sum_{S\in\mathcal G}p^{|S|}\le1/2$; the expectation threshold $q(\mathcal F)$ is the largest such $p$. The fractional expectation threshold $q_f(\mathcal F)$ allows instead weights $g(S)\in[0,1]$ with $\sum_{S\subseteq H}g(S)\ge1$ for $H\in\mathcal F$ and $\sum_S g(S)p^{|S|}\le1/2$, so $q\le q_f$. Frankston-Kahn-Narayanan-Park and Park-Pham proved the Kahn-Kalai comparisons with the threshold $p_c$; special cases of Talagrand's comparison were known for weights on singletons, pairs, cliques and bounded-size sets. Talagrand (2010, Conjecture 6.3) asked: is there a universal constant $L$ with $q_f(\mathcal F)\le L\,q(\mathcal F)$ for every increasing family?
problems.posedBy: Michel Talagrand (Conjecture 6.3, 'Are many small sets explicitly small?', STOC 2010)
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: $q_f(\mathcal F)\le25\cdot512^4\,q(\mathcal F)$ for every finite nonempty $X$ and nonempty proper increasing $\mathcal F\subseteq2^X$, independently of $|X|$, the sizes of minimal members and the support of the fractional cover; equivalently every fractional cover of cost at most $1/2$ at $r$ rounds to an integral cover of cost at most $1/2$ at $r/(25\cdot512^4)$. Previously the best general loss was of order $\log\log|X|$ (Fischer-Person with Pham). The constant is explicit but not optimized.

problems.name: Katok's entropy rigidity conjecture in dimension at least three
problems.field: Smooth dynamics; geodesic flows in negative curvature
problems.statement: Let $(M,g)$ be a closed connected Riemannian manifold with strictly negative sectional curvature and geodesic flow $\phi_t$ on the unit tangent bundle. The variational principle gives $h_{m_L}(\phi_1)\le h_{top}(\phi_1)$, where $m_L$ is normalized Liouville measure. Katok (1982) proved for surfaces that equality forces constant curvature, and proved the higher-dimensional statement within the conformal class of a locally symmetric metric; later work gave only local rigidity near real or complex hyperbolic metrics. Katok conjectured that in every dimension equality of the Liouville entropy and the topological entropy characterizes locally symmetric metrics. Does $h_{m_L}=h_{top}$ hold for a negatively curved closed manifold only when $g$ is locally symmetric?
problems.posedBy: Anatole Katok
problems.ageNote: Katok, Entropy and closed geodesics, Ergodic Theory Dynam. Systems 2 (1982), p. 347, cited by the manuscript as the formulation; the surface case is proved there.
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for a closed connected smooth Riemannian manifold of dimension $n\ge3$ with strictly negative sectional curvature, normalized Liouville measure has maximal entropy for the geodesic flow if and only if the metric is locally symmetric (real, complex, quaternionic or Cayley hyperbolic, any scale). When the metric is not locally symmetric, the measure of maximal entropy and Liouville measure are mutually singular. It does not treat nonpositive curvature, Anosov geodesic flows without negative curvature, or the related volume-entropy (Besson-Courtois-Gallot) setting.

problems.name: The Colin de Verdiere Chromatic Conjecture
problems.statement: Colin de Verdiere (1990) introduced the graph invariant $\mu(G)$: the maximum nullity of a real symmetric matrix that is negative on edges, zero on non-edges, has exactly one negative eigenvalue and satisfies the Strong Arnold Property. It characterizes outerplanar ($\mu\le2$), planar ($\mu\le3$) and linklessly embeddable ($\mu\le4$) graphs. He conjectured that $\chi(G)\le\mu(G)+1$ for every graph; since $h(G)\le\mu(G)+1$, this is implied by Hadwiger's conjecture, and it holds when $\mu(G)\le4$. Does every finite graph satisfy $\chi(G)\le\mu(G)+1$?
problems.posedBy: Yves Colin de Verdiere, Sur un nouvel invariant des graphes et un critere de planarite, J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 50 (1990)
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there are graphs of arbitrarily large order with $\alpha(G)\le2$ and $\mu(G)+1<|V(G)|/2\le\chi(G)$; the fractional chromatic number also exceeds $\mu(G)+1$. The proof shows every well-signed matrix on the graph with one negative eigenvalue has rank above $|V(G)|/2+1$, without using the Strong Arnold Property, so the Lovasz-Schrijver parameter $\kappa$ also satisfies $\kappa(G)+1<|V(G)|/2$. Since $h\le\mu+1$, these graphs also violate Hadwiger's inequality, by a route independent of the connected-matching companion. Nothing is claimed for small $\mu$.

problems.name: The degenerate Arnold conjecture: critical-number and rational cup-length lower bounds for Hamiltonian fixed points
problems.field: Symplectic topology; Hamiltonian fixed points, Arnold conjecture
problems.statement: Arnold asked whether a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism $\phi$ of a closed symplectic manifold $M$ must have at least as many geometrically distinct fixed points as a smooth function on $M$ has critical points. Without nondegeneracy assumptions this is the critical-number bound $\#\mathrm{Fix}(\phi)\ge\mathrm{Crit}(M)$, with the weaker rational cup-length form $\#\mathrm{Fix}(\phi)\ge\mathrm{cuplength}(M;\mathbb Q)$ (unit included). These are known on tori and $\mathbb{CP}^n$, and when $[\omega]$ and $c_1$ vanish on $\pi_2(M)$ (Rudyak-Oprea). Do the critical-number and cup-length bounds hold for every Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of every closed symplectic manifold?
problems.posedBy: V. I. Arnold, First steps in symplectic topology, Russian Math. Surveys 41 (1986); recorded as Conjectures 1.4 and 1.6 in R. Golovko, On variants of Arnold conjecture, Arch. Math. (Brno) 56 (2020)
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: on the complex quadric threefold there is a smooth Hamiltonian diffeomorphism with exactly three fixed points, at least one degenerate, while every smooth function has at least four critical points and the rational cup length is four; this disproves both unrestricted degenerate bounds, and contractibility conditions cannot rescue them. The construction composes a Hamiltonian involution fixing $Q^2\cong S^2\times S^2$ with a short invariant flow, using a three-critical-point function on $S^2\times S^2$. The count three is sharp by Gong (2025). It says nothing against the nondegenerate homological (Floer) bounds. Jiao (arXiv, 27 Sep 2026, after this paper) independently reports a two-fixed-point example on $S^2\times S^2$.
problems.claimIssueNote: The release says: 'Ma [Theorem 1.5] asserted that the minimum number of fixed points over all Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms always equals Crit(M). Theorem 1.1 contradicts that assertion' (degenerate paper) and 'Ma's preprint asserts that the minimum number of fixed points of a nondegenerate Hamiltonian diffeomorphism always equals the ordinary Morse number ... Theorem 1.1 contradicts that unrestricted assertion' (Morse-number paper). The other side: R. Ma, Proofs on Arnold conjectures, arXiv 0808.0613v7 (2013), Theorem 1.5, claims these lower bounds hold in general. Ma's preprint is unpublished; no referee has ruled between them.

problems.name: The strong hyperkahler SYZ conjecture
problems.field: Complex and algebraic geometry; hyperkahler manifolds, Lagrangian fibrations
problems.statement: Let $X$ be a compact irreducible holomorphic symplectic (hyperkahler) Kahler manifold of dimension $2n$ with Beauville-Bogomolov-Fujiki form $q$. A nonzero class $c_1(L)$ that is nef and isotropic, $q(c_1(L))=0$, has numerical dimension $n$, and should come from a Lagrangian fibration $X\to B$ with $\dim B=n$. This was known for all known deformation types (Bayer-Macri, Markman, Yoshioka, Mongardi-Rapagnetta, Mongardi-Onorati, with Soldatenkov-Verbitsky's deformation theorem), and Verbitsky proved nonvanishing under a semipositive metric. Is every holomorphic line bundle $L$ on such an $X$ with $c_1(L)\ne0$ nef and isotropic semiample?
problems.posedBy: Misha Verbitsky (GAFA 2010, Conjecture 1.7); earlier nef-isotropic forms in Hassett-Tschinkel (2001, Remark 3.12) and Sawon (2003, Conjecture 4.1)
problems.ageNote: Year of Hassett-Tschinkel's Remark 3.12, the earliest explicit nef-isotropic semiampleness formulation the manuscript cites; the 'strong' form with this name is Verbitsky's Conjecture 1.7 (2010).
problems.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: if $c_1(L)\ne0$, $c_1(L)$ is in the closure of the Kahler cone and $q_X(c_1(L))=0$, then $L$ is semiample: some $L^m\simeq f^*A$ for a surjective connected-fibre map $f:X\to B$ onto a normal projective $n$-dimensional $B$ with $A$ ample, every fibre component Lagrangian of dimension $n$. Corollary 1.2: in each dimension there are finitely many deformation types with $b_2\ge5$. Corollary 1.3 (projective $X$, via the companion): $B\simeq\mathbb P^n$. Not shown: existence of a nef isotropic class on a given $X$, or anything for $b_2\le4$ in the finiteness corollary.
